sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Fear Aura (Su): A pit fiend can radiate a 20-foot-radius fear aura as a free action. A creature in the area must succeed on a DC 27 Will save or be affected as though by a fear spell (caster level 18th). A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same pit fiend's aura for 24 hours. Other devils are immune to the aura. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Disease — Devil Chills (Su): A creature struck by a pit fiend's bite attack must succeed on a DC 27 Fortitude save or be infected with a vile disease known as devil chills (incubation period 1d4 days, damage 1d4 Str). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 27, initial damage 1d6 Con, secondary damage death. The save DC is Constitution-based. The poison is delivered by the pit fiend's bite.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a pit fiend must hit with its tail slap attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Constrict (Ex): A pit fiend deals 2d8+26 points of damage with a successful grapple check.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—blasphemy (DC 25), create undead, fireball (DC 21), greater dispel magic, greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), invisibility, magic circle against good, mass hold monster (DC 27), persistent image (DC 23), power word stun, unholy aura (DC 26); 1/day—meteor swarm (DC 27). Caster level 18th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Wish (Sp): Once per year a pit fiend can use wish as the spell (caster level 20th). Pit fiends are notorious for granting such a wish only on terms that ruin the one who asked.

Summon Devil (Sp): Twice per day a pit fiend can automatically summon 2 lemures, bone devils, or bearded devils, or 1 erinyes, horned devil, or ice devil. This ability is the equivalent of an 8th-level spell.

Regeneration 5 (Ex): A pit fiend recovers from wounds at a supernatural rate, closing 5 points of injury each round and never dying from ordinary damage. It takes normal damage from good-aligned silvered weapons, and from spells or effects with the good descriptor.

See in Darkness (Su): A pit fiend can see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell.

Aligned Weapons (Ex): A pit fiend's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Size and Appearance: A pit fiend often wraps its wings around itself like a grotesque cloak, and appears wreathed in flames. It stands 12 feet tall and weighs 800 pounds.

lore.summary: Hounds out of the ordered hells: rust-red or coal-black, shoulder-high to a man's belt, with ember eyes and smoke leaking from their jaws. Devils keep them as watchdogs and hunting packs, and so do wizards who ought to know better. Where you find one, look at once for the rest — they seldom hunt alone, and they are already circling.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a heavy hound, taller at the shoulder than a mastiff and much weightier than it looks.
Durability: No hardier than a big dog. Once you have your hands on one it dies like a dog.
Defenses: Fire cannot touch them — not their own, not a torch, not a wizard's.
Speed: Fast. Faster than a man over open ground, and utterly tireless on a trail.
Might: Jaws that scorch as they close, and a cone of flame breathed out again and again through a fight, never spent for long.
Mind: Dull, but not stupid. They cannot speak at all, though they understand the devils' tongue well enough to take orders and keep them.
Disposition: Disciplined and patient. They ring their quarry in silence — they move far quieter than a beast that size has any right to — then start it with fire and drive it onto the waiting jaws. They do not lose a trail, and they do not give up a hunt.
Bane: Cold. Frost pains them worse than it pains a man, and one good blast of it breaks a pack's nerve as surely as its bodies. Past that they are only dogs, and dogs can be met with a spear.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They circle wide and quiet until the ring is closed, then one or two open with fire from the flank to panic the quarry and drive it toward the rest. If it stands instead of running, the whole pack closes at once and bites, and every bite burns. Whatever flees, they follow — by scent, all night if need be, and they are still behind you at dawn.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Frost. Any frost. A flask of it is worth more here than a second sword.
• Count the eyes in the dark before you charge. There is never only the one pair.
• The great black ones the archdevils breed for war are the same beast grown to the size of a horse. Do not mistake the two at dusk.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing to say, and no mouth to say it with. They take orders in the devils' tongue and nothing else moves them; I have tried commands, meat, and the name of their master. They ignored the meat. Kill them, then go and find whoever whistled them up — that one may talk.

sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Breath Weapon (Su): 10-foot cone, once every 2d4 rounds, damage 2d6 fire, Reflex DC 13 half. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Fiery Bite (Su): A hell hound deals an extra 1d6 points of fire damage every time it bites an opponent, as if its bite were a flaming weapon.

Scent (Ex): A hell hound can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell, normally noticing creatures within 30 feet.

Aligned Weapons (Ex): A hell hound's natural weapons are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Skills: Hell hounds have a +5 racial bonus on Hide and Move Silently checks. *They also receive a +8 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent, due to their keen sense of smell.

Pack Tactics: Hell hounds are efficient hunters. A favorite pack tactic is to surround prey quietly, then attack with one or two hounds, driving it toward the rest with their fiery breath. If the prey doesn't run, the pack closes in. Hell hounds track fleeing prey relentlessly. A typical hell hound stands 4-1/2 feet high at the shoulder and weighs 120 pounds. Hell hounds do not speak, but understand Infernal.

Note: Nessian Warhound: The greatest of the breed are the Nessian warhounds, coal-black mastiffs the size of draft horses, often fitted with shirts of infernal chainmail (Large, Challenge Rating 9). Their bite deals 2d6+12/19–20 plus 1d8 fire, and their breath weapon is a 10-foot cone of 3d6 fire (Reflex DC 21 half). They run in packs alongside ordinary hell hounds.

lore.summary: A barrel of living rock standing on three thick legs, with three arms, three eyes set about its crown, and a wide toothed mouth atop its head. It swims through solid stone as a fish swims through water and leaves no hole behind it. It eats gems and precious metal and nothing else. You will meet one on the deep roads, coming up beneath a miner's cart.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — squat and rock-hided, near as wide as it is tall, and heavier than a horse.
Durability: Hard as the stone it swims in, and about as willing to give ground.
Defenses: Fire and frost do nothing to it, lightning little. Its hide turns edges and points aside with contempt. It cannot be flanked, for those eyes ring its head and watch every quarter at once, and it feels every footfall through the rock.
Speed: Ponderous on its feet, but it glides through stone and earth as easily as you walk a road, leaving neither tunnel nor ripple nor sound.
Might: A great mouth that bites through a shield, and three raking claws besides. It smells coin and gemstone on you from across a chamber.
Mind: As shrewd as an ordinary man, and it speaks — the trade-tongue and the language of the earth both.
Disposition: Indifferent to flesh, which it cannot digest, and hostile only over food or property. Hungry ones on this side of the world grow bold, for ore and gemstone are far scarcer here than at home.
Bane: A mace or a hammer; blades and arrows are wasted on that hide. It cannot pass through metal, so a grille or a plated door will pen it. And the charm that shifts earth flings it clear of the stone and leaves it reeling.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lies just beneath the floor and lets you walk over it, then rises out of the stone at your side and bites before you have turned. Claws follow while you find your footing. If it tires of you, or you of it, it simply sinks back into the wall and is gone — and a xorn that has gone is not fled, only waiting somewhere you are not looking.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Carry a purse of poor gems on any deep road. Cheaper than a funeral.
• Hammer, not sword. Its hide laughs at edges.
• If one is talking to you, another is under your feet. Get off the stone floor before you haggle.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The best bargain on the deep roads. It wants your rings, not your ribs. I have bought passage from three of them with a handful of poor garnets and got an escort thrown in. Watch only for the old trick: while one talks terms, its fellows lie waiting under the floor about you. Pay quickly, and civilly.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar, Earth)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), burrow 20 ft.
Armor Class: 24 (+14 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 24
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+10
Attack: Bite +10 melee (4d6+3)
Full Attack: Bite +10 melee (4d6+3) and 3 claws +8 melee (1d4+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: All-around vision, earth glide, damage reduction 5/bludgeoning, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to cold and fire, resistance to electricity 10, tremorsense 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 10, Con 15, Int 10, Wis 11, Cha 10
Skills: Hide +10, Intimidate +10, Knowledge (dungeoneering) +10, Listen +10, Move Silently +10, Search +10, Spot +10, Survival +10 (+12 following tracks or underground)
Feats: Cleave (bonus), Multiattack, Power Attack, Toughness
Environment: Elemental Plane of Earth
Organization: Solitary, pair, or cluster (3–5)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 8–14 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Earth Glide (Ex): A xorn can glide through stone, dirt, or almost any other sort of earth except metal as easily as a fish swims through water. Its burrowing leaves behind no tunnel or hole, nor does it create any ripple or other sign of its presence. A move earth spell cast on an area containing a burrowing xorn flings the xorn back 30 feet, stunning the creature for 1 round unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Fortitude save.

All-Around Vision (Ex): A xorn's symmetrically placed eyes allow it to look in any direction, providing a +4 racial bonus on Spot and Search checks. A xorn can't be flanked.

Tremorsense (Ex): A xorn is sensitive to vibrations in the ground and automatically pinpoints the location of anything in contact with the ground within 60 feet.

Appetite (Ex): Xorns do not attack fleshly beings except to defend themselves or their property, since they cannot digest meat. They are indifferent to creatures of the Material Plane — with the sole exception of anyone carrying a significant amount of precious metals or minerals, which xorns eat. They can smell such food up to 20 feet away, and can be quite aggressive when seeking it.

Ambush from Stone: A xorn's favorite mode of attack is to wait just beneath a stone surface until a foe comes within reach, then emerge suddenly. Groups of xorns often send one of their number to the surface to negotiate for food while the remainder position themselves for a surprise attack. Xorns speak Common and Terran.

Note: Minor and Elder Xorns: The rows above describe the average xorn, about 5 feet tall and wide and weighing some 600 pounds. Minor xorns are Small (about 3 feet tall and wide, 120 pounds), Challenge Rating 3, AC 23, Str 15, and attack with a bite (2d8+2) and 3 claws (1d3+1). Elder xorns are Large (about 8 feet tall and wide, 9,000 pounds), Challenge Rating 8, AC 25, Str 25, reach 10 ft., and attack with a bite (4d8+7) and 3 claws (1d6+3). All three share earth glide, all-around vision, tremorsense 60 ft., and damage reduction 5/bludgeoning.

lore.summary: Gaunt leather-skinned assassins of the Abyss, sent where a quieter murder is wanted than a horde can manage. A rank red jelly weeps constantly from their hides. I have found their work in locked towers and sealed camps — throats opened, doors untouched, and good blades left pitted and smoking on the floor beside the dead.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man's height and a man's shape, but starved-hound gaunt, with a long skull swept back into a single horn.
Durability: Hardy out of all proportion to that frame; it soaks punishment that would fell a strong man twice over.
Defenses: Horn-tough hide that turns common steel, and a coat of corrosive slime over all of it. Lightning does nothing to it and venom less than nothing; acid, frost and flame are all half-swallowed. Magic finds it a little harder to grip than it ought.
Speed: Walks at a man's pace, but climbs like a spider and moves in perfect silence.
Might: Two raking claws and a bite, and it knows exactly where to put them — it opens a man who has not seen it coming.
Mind: Sharp, literate and patient. It picks locks, wears disguises, reads a trail, and speaks mind to mind without opening its mouth.
Disposition: Cruel and methodical. It kills whoever looks most dangerous first, then takes its time with whatever is left standing.
Bane: Cold iron or a blessed edge cuts it; every other metal is wasted effort. Its slime eats whatever touches it, so keep to the reach of a spear and never lay hands on it. Flame and frost it shrugs off — but raw sound it has no armour against at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens from hiding against whoever looks most dangerous, drawing darkness about itself and stepping out of it with claws already moving. It strips protective wards with a word, sees through invisibility as plainly as daylight, and when the odds turn it calls another of its kind out of the dark or simply steps away between one heartbeat and the next. Strike it bare-handed and its slime takes the skin off your knuckles; strike it with a fine blade and the blade comes back eaten.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron, or bless the steel. Everything else comes back pitted and useless.
• Never put a bare hand on one. My knuckles still show where I did.
• It talks first only when it reckons you worth more alive than dead. That is not comfort.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I bargained with one in a bell-tower at Corrieth. It answered mind to mind, courteous as a clerk, and named its price: a name. I gave it one I thought harmless. The man was dead inside the month. The babau kept its side and let me walk out. It always costs.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Chaotic, Demon, Extraplanar, Evil)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 19 (+1 Dex, +8 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+12
Attack: Claw +12 melee (1d6+5)
Full Attack: 2 claws +12 melee (1d6+5) and bite +7 melee (1d6+2)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Sneak attack +2d6, spell-like abilities, summon demon
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/cold iron or good, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to electricity and poison, protective slime, resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and fire 10, spell resistance 14, telepathy 100 ft.
Saves: Fort +10, Ref +6, Will +6
Abilities: Str 21, Dex 12, Con 20, Int 14, Wis 13, Cha 16
Skills: Climb +15, Disable Device +12, Disguise +13, Escape Artist +11, Hide +19, Listen +19, Move Silently +19, Open Lock +11, Search +20, Sleight of Hand +11, Survival +1 (+3 following tracks), Use Rope +1 (+3 with bindings)
Feats: Cleave, Multiattack, Power Attack
Environment: A chaotic evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary or gang (3-6)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Always chaotic evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 8-14 levels (Large); 15-21 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Sneak Attack (Ex): A babau can make a sneak attack like a rogue, dealing an extra 2d6 points of damage whenever a foe is denied his or her Dexterity bonus, or when the babau is flanking.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will - darkness, dispel magic, see invisibility, greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only). Caster level 7th.

Protective Slime (Su): A slimy red jelly coats the babau's skin. Any weapon that touches it takes 1d8 points of acid damage from the corrosive goo, and the weapon's hardness does not reduce this damage. A magic weapon may attempt a DC 18 Reflex save to avoid taking this damage. A creature who strikes the babau with an unarmed attack, unarmed strike, touch spell, or natural weapon takes this damage as well but can negate the damage with a DC 18 Reflex save. The save DCs are Constitution-based.

Summon Demon (Sp): Once per day a babau can attempt to summon 1 babau with a 40% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 3rd-level spell.

Skills: Babaus have a +8 racial bonus on Hide, Listen, Move Silently, and Search checks.

Demon Traits: Demons are immune to electricity and poison, and have resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and fire 10. Most share the ability to summon others of their kind, though they are often reluctant to use that power until in obvious peril. Except where otherwise noted, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic, and communicate by telepathy. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: A demon that hunts demons: a spined arachnid with a body the bulk of a plough-horse and legs that span a cart-road. It walks between worlds at its own whim, and where it passes in the Abyss the lesser fiends go quiet. On our side of the veil it hunts whatever it finds, which means us. It serves no lord and it takes no treasure.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a body the size of a plough-horse carried on legs that span a cart-road, heavier than a loaded waggon.
Durability: Vast and thick-shelled. It takes an appalling amount of killing and knows it.
Defenses: Chitin plate over knotted muscle, turning any steel that has not been blessed. Mark well what it lacks: it is no true fiend of the Abyssal breed, so lightning burns it, venom sickens it, and it carries no ward against spellcraft whatever.
Speed: Faster over open ground than a running man, and it goes up a sheer wall as readily as it crosses a floor.
Might: Fangs that punch through plate and two claws that, landing together, tear a harness apart at the seams. It smells blood on the wind and follows it for days.
Mind: Dull-witted the way a hunting dog is dull-witted — no scholar, but no fool afield. It understands the Abyssal tongue perfectly and will not answer in it.
Disposition: It attacks anything it sees. There is nothing else in it to appeal to.
Bane: Only a blessed or good-aligned edge bites; cold iron and silver are thrown away here, whatever your armourer told you. But it has no ward against spellcraft and no immunity to lightning or venom, so the spellcaster in your company is worth the whole shield-wall. And fight it stripped — what harness you wear it will pull off you in pieces.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fixes on one of you, usually whoever it reached first, and works at that one alone, throwing great gouts of web to pin the rest out of the fight. It tears at armour with both claws until the harness comes apart at the buckles, then bites. If the fight sours it bites once more and withdraws, content to let the venom eat the life out of a man over the following hours. It steps between worlds to come and to go, so a wounded one is not a finished one.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bless the steel. Cold iron does nothing — that is a true demon's weakness, and this thing is not one.
• No ward against magic on this one. Let the spellcaster work freely for once in her life.
• Leave the good harness at camp. It strips it off you anyway and you fight the rest of it half-naked.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is no talk here. It understands the Abyssal tongue — I tried it, on a ledge above the Vault of Sighs, hands open and empty and my voice steady — and it came for me all the same. It hears you perfectly well. It simply does not care. Speak afterward, over the carcass, if you must speak.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Outsider (Chaotic, Extraplanar, Evil)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), climb 20 ft.
Armor Class: 22 (-2 size, +1 Dex, +13 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 21
Base Attack/Grapple: +12/+29

Full Attack: Bite +19 melee (2d6+9 plus poison) and 2 claws +14 melee (2d4+4); or web +11 ranged
Space/Reach: 15 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison, rend armor, web
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/good, darkvision 60 ft., plane shift, scent, telepathy 100 ft.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 24, initial damage 1d6 Con, secondary damage 2d6 Con. Bebilith venom is highly perishable, losing its potency and becoming inert, foul-smelling goo almost as soon as it comes into contact with air. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Rend Armor (Ex): If a bebilith hits with both claw attacks, it pulls apart any armor worn by its foe. This attack deals 4d6+18 points of damage to the opponent's armor. Creatures not wearing armor are unaffected by this special attack. Armor that takes more damage than it can withstand is destroyed outright. Damaged armor may be repaired with a successful Craft (armorsmithing) check.

Web (Ex): A bebilith can throw a web up to four times per day. This is similar to an attack with a net but has a maximum range of 30 feet, with a range increment of 10 feet. This attack is effective against targets of up to Gargantuan size. The web anchors the target in place, allowing no movement. An entangled creature can escape with a DC 24 Escape Artist check or burst the web with a DC 24 Strength check. The check DCs are Constitution-based. The web withstands 14 points of damage before parting, and has hardness 0. There is a 75% chance that the webbing will not burn if any sort of fire is applied to it (check each round).

Plane Shift (Su): This ability affects only the bebilith. It is otherwise similar to the spell (caster level 12th).

Skills: A bebilith has mottled coloration that gives it a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks.

Aligned Natural Weapons (Ex): A bebilith's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Note that the bebilith does not carry the Demon subtype and lacks the usual demonic immunity to electricity and resistance to acid, cold, and fire; its only listed defence against magic is damage reduction 10/good. Bebiliths understand but do not speak Abyssal, and use telepathy to communicate silently with one another.

lore.summary: The runt of the Abyss and its most numerous creature: a squat potbellied thing with a slack face and small mean eyes, bred to be spent. Dretches come in crowds, driven forward by their betters, and they die in crowds without anyone much minding. They cannot utter a word aloud, yet they will beg you, silently, from inside your own skull.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — waist-high, wide as a barrel, and a good deal heavier than it looks.
Durability: Tougher than its size promises, though nothing you would call stout.
Defenses: Rubbery hide that plain steel bounces off; cold iron or a blessed edge is the whole answer. Lightning and venom do nothing to it, and frost, flame and acid are blunted. It carries no ward against spellcraft at all.
Speed: Slow. Slower than a man walking briskly, and it never improves upon that.
Might: Two clumsy claws and a bite, feeble enough on their own. In a mob it is another matter entirely.
Mind: Dim as cattle. It cannot speak aloud whatever, and it reaches into your thoughts only if you already carry the Abyssal tongue.
Disposition: Cowardly to its marrow. It runs at the first blood unless something worse than you is standing behind it.
Bane: Cold iron or a blessed edge, and nothing else will serve. Beyond that it is slow, stupid and wide open to any spell you care to throw. Break the greater fiend driving the mob and the mob scatters — their terror of their masters is the only thing in them stronger than their terror of dying.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It shuffles forward because the thing behind it frightens it more than you do, claws and bites badly, and calls another of itself up out of the dark to even the odds. Given a moment it vomits a cloud of stinking vapour to leave you retching and helpless, or throws a wave of raw dread at whoever in your line looks least steady. Alone it runs. In a crowd it drowns you by sheer weight of bodies, and there are always more coming up behind.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron even for the runt. A plain blade turns on it and you will feel a fool.
• Hold your breath and back out of the cloud. The vapour does the killing, not the dretch.
• Kill whatever is driving them and you will not have to kill them at all.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: The only demon that will grovel. One clutched my boot in the ruins under Ghast Fen and begged, mind to mind, for its life; I let it go for the name of the thing commanding it. The name was true. It then went and told that thing precisely where I stood. It fears the next one up far more than it fears you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day - scare (DC 12), stinking cloud (DC 13). Caster level 2nd. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Summon Demon (Sp): Once per day a dretch can attempt to summon another dretch with a 35% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 1st-level spell.

Telepathy (Su): Dretches cannot speak, but can communicate telepathically with creatures within 100 feet that speak Abyssal.

Demon Traits: Demons are immune to electricity and poison, and have resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and fire 10. Most share the ability to summon others of their kind, though they are often reluctant to use that power until in obvious peril. Except where otherwise noted, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic, and communicate by telepathy. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: The tempter of the Abyss, and the most dangerous fiend a careful man is likely to meet, because it opens with an offer rather than a claw. Dog-headed, russet to pitch black, with violet eyes and two great crab's pincers set above a pair of ordinary hands. Once in a turning of the moon it can grant a mortal a true wish. It always delivers. It never ends well.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — better than twice a tall man's height, and heavier than a team of draught horses.
Durability: Immense. It is generally the hardest thing to kill in whatever room it has chosen to enter.
Defenses: Armour-plate hide that turns any steel not blessed. Lightning and venom are nothing to it; frost, flame and acid are blunted. Spellcraft slides off it badly, and it sees through every illusion, invisibility and disguise you own without the least effort.
Speed: Covers ground faster than a running man, and can step from where it stands to anywhere it has a mind to be.
Might: Two pincers that catch a man and keep him, two clawed hands besides, and a bite. Once a pincer closes you do not get free by strength.
Mind: Clever, well-read and enormously persuasive. It reads a man's wants faster than the man can put a name to them.
Disposition: It would far rather buy you than fight you, and only fights once the buying has plainly failed — and then it fights with real spite.
Bane: Only a blessed or good-aligned weapon bites; cold iron and silver are wasted here. Its ward against spellcraft is formidable, so trust blessed steel over any spellbook. But the true bane is the offer itself: refuse it early and you have taken away the better half of its strength.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It talks first, and when talk fails it turns the ground and the air against you — a hammer-blow of raw chaos, a wash of unholy blight, a single word that stops a man's mind mid-thought. It sows confusion so your own line turns upon itself, throws up a crowd of false selves to soak your blows, and hauls whole chambers sideways so that your footing becomes a fall. Then it wades in, catches the wounded up in a pincer, and finishes them at its leisure.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The offer is genuine. That is the trap — it delivers exactly, and the delivering ruins you.
• Blessed steel only. Cold iron is for its lesser kin and it knows the difference.
• Do not bother hiding from it. It has seen you the whole while and it always has.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Every hunter I respect has spoken with one, and every one of them paid. Mine wanted a chapel unroofed before winter and offered me a life back in trade. I said no and walked out, and it let me, because a refusal amuses it and it has patience to spare. It is still waiting. Say no early, say it once, explain nothing.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Saves: Fort +18, Ref +8, Will +11

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a glabrezu must hit a Medium or smaller opponent with a pincer attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will - chaos hammer (DC 19), confusion (DC 19), dispel magic, mirror image, reverse gravity (DC 22), greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), unholy blight (DC 19); 1/day - power word stun. Caster level 14th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Wish (Sp): Once per month, a glabrezu can fulfill a wish for a mortal humanoid. The demon can use this ability to offer a mortal whatever he or she desires - but unless the wish is used to create pain and suffering in the world, the glabrezu demands either terrible evil acts or great sacrifice as compensation.

Summon Demon (Sp): Once per day a glabrezu can attempt to summon 4d10 dretches or 1d2 vrocks with a 50% chance of success, or another glabrezu with a 20% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 4th-level spell.

True Seeing (Su): Glabrezu continuously use true seeing as the spell (caster level 14th).

Skills: Glabrezu have a +8 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Demon Traits: Demons are immune to electricity and poison, and have resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and fire 10. Most share the ability to summon others of their kind, though they are often reluctant to use that power until in obvious peril. Except where otherwise noted, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic, and communicate by telepathy. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: A great toad reared up on its hind legs, warty and wet and taller than a man, though it goes on all fours when it pleases. Hezrous are the Abyss's shock troops: they go in first, they enjoy it, and they carry their best weapon in their skin — a reek that empties a man's stomach and leaves him useless. Where a cellar smells of rotten pond-water, turn back.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a toad's bulk stood upright, half again a tall man's height and several times his weight.
Durability: Prodigiously tough. Squat, dense, and very hard indeed to put down for good.
Defenses: Thick warty hide that plain steel will not part; only a blessed edge tells. Lightning and venom are nothing to it, frost, flame and acid are blunted, and spellcraft finds it hard to take hold.
Speed: A man's walking pace and no better, upright or on all fours. But it can turn itself to vapour and drift where it likes.
Might: A bite that takes an arm off and two raking claws; if both claws land it has you fast, and a thing that heavy does not let go.
Mind: Cunning enough to know its business, but with no patience for schemes. It wants the melee and it wants it now.
Disposition: Eager, brutal and pleased with itself. It wades into the thickest part of a fight on purpose.
Bane: A blessed or good-aligned weapon; cold iron and silver do nothing whatever. The stench is a venom, so anyone proof against poison walks through it untouched and everyone else fights at spear-length or upwind. And it is slow. Make it come to you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens with a word of blasphemy that drops the weak where they stand, then closes as fast as its bulk allows, because it wants you inside the reek. Near it men vomit and cannot lift a shield. It follows with hammer-blows of chaos or a wash of unholy blight, bites, and takes hold with both claws — and once it has hold you stay held until it has finished. If the fight sours it goes to vapour and drifts clear, or calls up a crowd of lesser demons to bleed you while it mends.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Stopper your nose if it pleases you. It will not help. Proof against poison or nothing.
• Spears. Long ones. Anything that keeps you out of its arms and out of its stink.
• It is slower than you are. Stop trying to out-fight it and start out-walking it.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It will talk, mind to mind, and it is no fool. But it wants the fight more than anything you can offer. I traded words with one across a flooded gallery in the Deep Marches and it agreed to let us pass. It let us pass, then followed and took the rearmost man within the hour. A demon's word lasts exactly as long as it amuses it.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will - chaos hammer (DC 18), greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), unholy blight (DC 18); 3/day - blasphemy (DC 21), gaseous form. Caster level 13th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Any living creature (except other demons) within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 24 Fortitude save or be nauseated for as long as it remains within the affected area and for 1d4 rounds afterward. Creatures that successfully save are sickened for as long as they remain in the area. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same hezrou's stench for 24 hours. A delay poison or neutralize poison spell removes either condition from one creature. Creatures that have immunity to poison are unaffected, and creatures resistant to poison receive their normal bonus on their saving throws. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Most share the ability to summon others of their kind, though they are often reluctant to use that power until in obvious peril. Except where otherwise noted, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic, and communicate by telepathy. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: Serpent below the waist, six-armed woman above, hung about with bangles and stolen jewels. The marilith is a general of the Abyss and thinks like one: she reads the ground, the light and your marching order before ever she draws. I have met two — one commanding a siege, one hunting alone in the burnt hills.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — she rears taller than a mounted man, and her coiled length would fill a barn's width.
Durability: Tremendous. She will bleed the whole afternoon and fight the whole afternoon.
Defenses: Plated hide beneath the jewellery that turns common steel aside, and spells fail against her as often as they take. Lightning and poison do nothing whatever; acid, cold and flame all come off blunted. She sees truly and always — no invisibility, no illusion, no worn face fools her.
Speed: Swift over open ground and never once off balance; the tail carries her sideways as easily as forward.
Might: Six arms, six longswords, and every stroke lands with a general's timing. The tail alone takes a horse off its feet and crushes what it catches, and a man caught in the coils goes limp and stays limp.
Mind: Brilliant. She plans campaigns, and she also thinks quicker in the moment than any captain I ever served under.
Disposition: Vain, proud and hungry for battle. She will not decline a fight, which is the only honest thing about her.
Bane: Her hide turns everything but a blade that is both cold iron and blessed — one or the other alone is a wasted purse. Fight her in a corridor where only a pair of arms can reach you, and go at her vanity: she will accept a duel she ought to refuse.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She does not charge. She hangs back, reads the ground, then picks the one holding your line together and puts three swords through him. A wall of turning blades to cut the room in half; your own weapon plucked out of your grip from across the hall; an image of her set where you will waste your arrows on it. All the while the coils are closing on whoever came too near, and what they take does not wake again while she holds it. If the fight turns against her she calls worse things up from home to buy her the time.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron alone will not do. Blessed steel alone will not do. It must be both. I ruined a good sword learning it.
• She sees through invisibility, always. Do not spend your one good trick on hiding from her.
• Take a doorway. Six arms want room; a doorway gives her two.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have spoken with her twice and paid both times. She will talk — she loves an audience — and she keeps every word of a bargain in exactly the shape that hurts most. The first cost me a name I had sworn to keep. The second cost me a man. Talk to learn her plan; never trust her terms.

They see in the dark out to 60 feet and communicate by telepathy out to 100 feet with any creature that has a language. Most can summon others of their kind. Except where noted otherwise, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: A boar's head on an ape's bulk, obscenely fat, with wings that have no business lifting it — and yet it flies. Nalfeshnees are the judges of the Abyss, sorting the arriving dead and gloating over the sentence. They hold plain fighting beneath their office, right up until the blood-lust takes them, which is always sooner than they claim.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a bloated ape's frame under a boar's head, taller than a barn door and heavier than a bull.
Durability: Immense. It soaks punishment the way a bog soaks rain.
Defenses: Hide that common steel scarcely troubles, and a great deal of spellcraft simply slides off it. Lightning and poison are wasted; acid, cold and flame all bite less than they ought. It sees every truth continually — no disguise, no invisibility, no illusion holds in front of it.
Speed: Ponderous afoot and clumsy in the air, but it does fly, and it will not be outrun on level ground for long.
Might: A bite that takes an arm off at the shoulder, claws behind it, and the weight to shove a shield wall apart and walk through the gap.
Mind: Far sharper than most things you will ever face. It is a judge by trade and an arrogant one, and it will lecture you throughout.
Disposition: Contemptuous. Fighting is beneath its dignity until the blood-lust rises, and then it is worse than the creatures it commands.
Bane: Only a blessed weapon truly bites it; cold iron buys you nothing here. When rainbow colours begin crawling over its hide you have a single breath before they burst — spend that breath getting out of the light, for it leaves a man standing helpless in his own worst imaginings. And it is slow, on the ground and in the air both. Its own kind are untouched by the light; you are not.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens by kindling its nimbus — colours playing across the fat of it — and a moment later the light bursts wide and leaves everyone in reach stupefied by visions of what they fear most. Then it walks among the helpless and bites. Failing that, it strips a mind bare with a word, hauls lightning down out of the sky, drags a man's pace down to wading, or unpicks whatever wards you spent the morning setting. When it tires of the labour it summons vultures and toads of the Abyss to finish the work while it watches.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Blessed steel or nothing. Cold iron is a wasted purse against this one.
• When the colours start crawling on its hide, move. You have a breath, no more, and the light spreads wide.
• It is fat, slow and proud. Take the high ground and make it climb; it resents that more than it resents you.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It will talk gladly — it is a judge, and judges love the sound of judging. I stood before one and argued my case the better part of an hour and walked out whole, which is not the same as unhurt. It took my testimony and it used it. Address it as a court, flatter the office, and concede nothing at all.

One round later they burst in a 60-foot radius. Any creature within this area must succeed on a DC 22 Will save or be dazed for 1d10 rounds as visions of its worst fears hound it. lore.summary: A hand-tall horror of horns, bat-wings and a barbed tail, the quasit binds itself to warlocks and wicked wizards as a familiar and spends its service sneering at the master. It is a coward, a liar and an inveterate gossip — and now and again it may ask the powers below a straight question and be answered truly.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — it would perch on your forearm, and it will, if you allow it.
Durability: Frail. One solid blow finishes it; the difficulty is entirely in landing one, for its hurts knit shut while you watch.
Defenses: Common steel slides off the little wretch. Poison does nothing to it and fire troubles it hardly at all. It goes unseen whenever it pleases, and wears the shape of a bat, a toad, a wolf or a great crawling centipede as the mood takes it.
Speed: Slow on its feet and faultless on the wing — it flies like a swift, not like a hawk.
Might: Next to none. The claws scarcely break skin, but they carry a venom that leaves a swordsman's hands clumsy and then useless.
Mind: Ordinary wit wedded to extraordinary malice. It has the common tongue and the Abyssal one, and it cannot stop talking.
Disposition: Sly and cowardly. It fights from ambush, and the instant the fight turns it flings a wave of terror behind it and is gone.
Bane: Cold iron or a blessed edge — either serves, and either ends it quickly. Mark this: it is not truly of the demon host, whatever it claims. Storm and lightning burn it as they burn you, where they do nothing at all to the great ones. In alternate shape its venom is left behind with its own body.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It never opens honestly. It arrives unseen, or wearing the shape of some harmless little beast, gets inside your reach and rakes with poisoned claws — the venom takes the hands first, so your grip goes before your legs do. Then it is aloft and invisible again, waiting for you to relax. Press it hard and it lashes out a wave of raw fear to cover its flight and does not come back until it has thought of something worse.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron or holy steel and it dies fast. It is only the hitting that is hard.
• Mind your grip. The venom takes the hands before anything else — lash your shield arm on before it starts.
• It is no true tanar'ri, whatever it tells you. A storm-charm hurts it, where the same charm is nothing to a marilith.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: The chattiest thing in the Abyss and the least trustworthy in it. I traded one a bottle of decent wine for the name of the man who paid for a friend's death, and it told me true — then went and told him I was coming. Ask plain questions. Assume every answer is repeated elsewhere before nightfall.

sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 13, initial damage 1d4 Dex, secondary damage 2d4 Dex. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—detect good, detect magic, and invisibility (self only); 1/day—cause fear (as the spell, except that its area is a 30-foot radius from the quasit, save DC 11). Caster level 6th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Commune (Sp): Once per week a quasit can use commune to ask six questions. The ability otherwise works as the spell (caster level 12th).

Alternate Form (Su): A quasit can assume other forms at will as a standard action. This ability functions as a polymorph spell cast on itself (caster level 12th), except that a quasit is not healed by changing form, and any individual quasit can assume only one or two forms no larger than Medium. Each quasit can assume one or two forms from the following list: bat, Small or Medium monstrous centipede, toad, and wolf. A quasit in alternate form loses its poison attack.

Tanar'ri Traits (Partial): The quasit is a demon in temperament but does not carry the full demon subtype, and its defenses are narrower than a true tanar'ri's: it is immune to poison and has resistance 10 against fire only — no immunity to electricity and no acid or cold resistance. It sees in the dark out to 60 feet and mends itself steadily with fast healing 2. Quasits speak Common and Abyssal. A quasit's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: In her own shape she is a winged, horned woman; in yours, she is whoever you would most like to meet. The succubus is a demon of temptation and she does not fight — she arranges. She appears as a rescued captive, a grateful widow, a fellow traveller on a bad road, and she can hold that face as long as the work requires.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a woman's height and build, until you notice the wings behind her.
Durability: Slight. She is no soldier, and once you have her cornered she goes down about as easily as the shape she is wearing.
Defenses: Her hide is harder than it looks and a great deal of magic simply refuses to touch her. Lightning and poison do nothing; acid, cold and flame come off blunted. Cornered, she steps sideways out of the world altogether, or is simply elsewhere between one breath and the next, and she can wear any human or elvish face she pleases.
Speed: Quick afoot and quicker on the wing — but her real speed is in leaving, and she leaves before you have decided to stop her.
Might: Claws, if you force her to them, and she is ashamed of needing them. Her true weapon is a kiss, and what it takes out of a man is not put back by a night's sleep.
Mind: Clever, patient and a superb liar. Every tongue ever spoken is plain to her, and she is reading your intent while you are still choosing your words.
Disposition: She has no appetite for battle whatever. She wants you alone, willing, and grateful. Everything before that is groundwork.
Bane: Cold iron or a blessed edge, either one, and there is little enough beneath the hide. Her ruin is being named: true sight strips the borrowed face off her, and once she is named aloud the whole approach collapses and she flees. Never let her separate one of you. And never accept the second kiss — the first kiss is what asks for it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She does not fight, if she is given any choice at all. Her first move is a friend's face and your own name in her mouth; her second is a suggestion so reasonable that you make it yourself and thank her for the company; her third is setting your own people against one another while she stands back. Cornered, she reads what you mean to do, throws a charm over the strongest of you, kisses whoever she can lay hands on, and steps out of the world entirely. If she truly needs muscle she whistles up a vulture-demon and leaves it to the butchery.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron or holy steel — either serves. Reaching her at all is the whole of the problem.
• The kiss asks for a second kiss. That request is the working. If you catch yourself agreeing, you have already lost.
• Never let her get one of you alone. The weeping prisoner in the cell is the oldest trap on the road, and it still works.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Understand this before anything else: with her the conversation is the attack. There is no talking to a succubus, only being talked to. I did it once, knowingly, for information, warded and with a friend gripping my collar — and I still gave more than I got, and some part of me did not come back. Speak to her through another man, or not at all.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.body:
Energy Drain (Su): A succubus drains energy from a mortal it lures into some act of passion, or by simply planting a kiss on the victim. If the target is not willing to be kissed, the succubus must start a grapple, which provokes an attack of opportunity. The succubus's kiss or embrace bestows one negative level. The kiss also has the effect of a suggestion spell, asking the victim to accept another kiss from the succubus. The victim must succeed on a DC 21 Will save to negate the effect of the suggestion. The DC is 21 for the Fortitude save to remove a negative level. These save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—charm monster (DC 22), detect good, detect thoughts (DC 20), ethereal jaunt (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), polymorph (humanoid form only, no limit on duration), suggestion (DC 21), greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only). Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Summon Demon (Sp): Once per day a succubus can attempt to summon 1 vrock with a 30% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 3rd-level spell.

Tongues (Su): A succubus has a permanent tongues ability (as the spell, caster level 12th). Succubi usually use verbal communication with mortals.

Change Shape (Su): A succubus can assume the form of any Small or Medium humanoid, and can maintain the deception indefinitely. While using her polymorph change shape ability, a succubus gains a +10 circumstance bonus on Disguise checks.

Skills: Succubi have a +8 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Tanar'ri Traits: Demons of the tanar'ri sort share a common template. They are immune to electricity and poison, and have resistance 10 against acid, cold, and fire. They see in the dark out to 60 feet and communicate by telepathy out to 100 feet with any creature that has a language. Most can summon others of their kind. Except where noted otherwise, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: A vulture's head on a brawler's frame, taller than a cave bear, stinking of carrion and mould. Vrocks are the rank and file of the Abyssal hosts: cruel, unruly, and so fond of a fight that they take on odds which kill them. Where one comes down, expect a flock — and a flock is far worse than the sum of them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a head and a half above a tall man, with the reach to match.
Durability: Very hard indeed to put down. It goes on tearing at you long after it ought to have folded.
Defenses: Common steel makes little impression on it, and spells fail against it more often than they land. Lightning and poison do it no harm at all; acid, cold and flame all come off dulled.
Speed: It prances on the ground and it is superb in the air — it drops on you, tears, and lifts away again before you have swung.
Might: Two great claws, a rending beak, and clawed feet it brings into play by half-flying at your chest. It fights with all of them at once and does not tire.
Mind: Sharp enough to lay a plan and far too excitable to keep to one. It boasts well and bargains badly.
Disposition: Vicious and undisciplined. It loves the fighting more than the winning, which is the only mercy in the whole creature.
Bane: Only a blessed weapon cuts it properly — cold iron is no use whatever here. Its spores die under holy water or a blessing, and nothing else in your pack will touch them. And if you see a ring of them join hands and start to dance, kill any one dancer you can reach: the dance dies with him, and it will not harm its own kind, only you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes out of the air feet-first, all claws and beak, and while it is on you it puffs a cloud of grey spores that settle into the skin and keep growing there for the rest of the fight and well beyond. Now and then it opens that beak and shrieks, and every man in the room who is not a demon stands rigid. It splits itself into a crowd of reflections to waste your arrows, snatches your weapon out of your hand from across the hall, and summons grovelling lesser demons by the armful to foul your legs. Where several fight together they will break off entirely, join hands and dance — and if they are allowed to finish, the wave that comes off that dance kills everything in the hall that is not one of them.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Blessed steel. Cold iron does nothing to this one — I have watched a good man try it to the end.
• Carry holy water, and not for the demon. It kills the spores in your skin; nothing else in the pack will.
• If they form a ring and start dancing, drop one dancer — any one, fast. Otherwise the whole hall goes.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: You can talk to a vrock much as you can talk to a drunk mercenary — it will answer, boast, and then come at you anyway because it grew bored of answering. I bought an hour from one with a cask of brandy and the name of a rival it hated. It kept the hour honestly. It came back the following night.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.body:

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Dance of Ruin (Su): To use this ability, a group of at least three vrocks must join hands in a circle, dancing wildly and chanting. At the end of 3 rounds of dancing, a wave of crackling energy flashes outward in a 100-foot radius. All creatures except for demons within the radius take 20d6 points of damage (Reflex DC 18 half). Stunning, paralyzing, or slaying one of the vrocks stops the dance. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—mirror image, telekinesis (DC 18), greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only); 1/day—heroism. Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spores (Ex): A vrock can release masses of spores from its body once every 3 rounds as a free action. The spores automatically deal 1d8 points of damage to all creatures adjacent to the vrock. They then penetrate the skin and grow, dealing an additional 1d4 points of damage each round for 10 rounds. At the end of this time, the victim is covered with a tangle of viny growths. (The vines are harmless and wither away in 1d4 days.) A delay poison spell stops the spores' growth for its duration. Bless, neutralize poison, or remove disease kills the spores, as does sprinkling the victim with a vial of holy water.

Stunning Screech (Su): Once per hour a vrock can emit a piercing screech. All creatures except for demons within a 30-foot radius must succeed on a DC 22 Fortitude save or be stunned for 1 round. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Summon Demon (Sp): Once per day a vrock can attempt to summon 2d10 dretches or another vrock with a 35% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 3rd-level spell.

Skills: Vrocks have a +8 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Tanar'ri Traits: Demons of the tanar'ri sort share a common template. They are immune to electricity and poison, and have resistance 10 against acid, cold, and fire. They see in the dark out to 60 feet and communicate by telepathy out to 100 feet with any creature that has a language. Most can summon others of their kind. Except where noted otherwise, demons speak Abyssal, Celestial, and Draconic. A demon's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: Hell sets the hamatula to guard what it would rather was not found — a vault, a gate, a name. Every span of it is spike and hook, and it likes nothing better than to fold a man against its chest and let its own body do the killing. I met one in a sealed crypt beneath Karrat, patient as the stone it stood on.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall man's height, but every inch of it is barb.
Durability: Immensely hard to kill; it shrugs off wounds that would finish a lesser fiend outright.
Defenses: Flame and venom pass through it as through smoke, and frost and acid barely bite. Its hide turns any blade that is not blessed. It sees in the deepest dark, and hostile spellwork slides off it as often as not.
Speed: Walks at a man's pace and no faster; no wings, no burrowing. But it steps from place to place by will alone when the chase bores it.
Might: Terrible strength. Its claws open armour, and once it has hold of you it drags you onto its own spines and works you against them.
Mind: Shrewd and disciplined — a jailer's mind rather than a general's. It speaks into your skull without opening its mouth, and it is a patient talker.
Disposition: A sentinel. It does not wander and does not hunt; it waits at its post and kills whatever crosses the line drawn for it.
Bane: Blessed arms cut it where silver and cold iron will not; nothing else a mortal carries does honest work. And never grapple it — the barbs are the trap, not the claws. Fight it with a spear or polearm from beyond arm's length and its hide cannot repay you at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It closes at once, claws foremost, and the mere touch plants a terror in a man that has sent better soldiers than you running onto the spikes of its fellows. Those who stand it seizes and folds against itself, impaling them again and again on its own body. Foes who keep their distance it pins with a binding word, blinds with a false image, or scorches with lances of fire; if the fight turns it calls a stroke of hellish law down on the lot of you. Cornered, it summons its kind, or steps away entire and reappears at your back.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never grapple it, never let it grapple you. Use a spear — the barbs cannot reach a long haft.
• Fire is wasted breath. Frost and acid nearly so. Bring something blessed or bring nothing.
• Ask what it guards, not what it will permit. Doorkeepers can sometimes be walked around.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I bargained with a hamatula for passage through the door it kept. It agreed, and it let me by — then stood aside while the thing beyond took my two companions, for our terms had said nothing of what lay past the threshold. It kept every word and meant none of them.

sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Barbed devils eagerly fight with their claws, trying to impale their opponents. They use hold person to immobilize those who avoid their hug attacks. A barbed devil’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. A barbed devil is about 7 feet tall and weighs about 300 pounds.

Fear (Su): A creature hit by a barbed devil must succeed on a DC 20 Will save or be affected as though by fear (caster level 9th). Whether or not the save is successful, that creature cannot be affected by that same barbed devil’s fear ability for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Impale (Ex): A barbed devil deals 3d8+9 points of piercing damage to a grabbed opponent with a successful grapple check.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a barbed devil must hit with a claw attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can impale the opponent on its barbed body.

Barbed Defense (Su): Any creature striking a barbed devil with handheld weapons or natural weapons takes 1d8+6 points of piercing and slashing damage from the devil’s barbs. Note that weapons with exceptional reach, such as longspears, do not endanger their users in this way.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), hold person (DC 16), major image (DC 17), scorching ray (2 rays only). 1/day—order’s wrath (DC 18), unholy blight (DC 18). Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day a barbed devil can attempt to summon 1d6 bearded devils or another barbed devil with a 35% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 4th-level spell.

Baatezu Traits: Devils are fiends native to lawful evil-aligned planes. Most devils share the following traits: immunity to fire and poison; resistance to acid 10 and cold 10; see in darkness, letting them see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell; the ability to summon others of their kind (chance of success and type noted in each entry); and telepathy. Except where noted otherwise, devils speak Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Many are surrounded by a fear aura, used to break up powerful groups and defeat opponents piecemeal, and those with spell-like abilities lean on illusions — a favourite trick is conjuring illusory reinforcements, so foes can never be sure which of the devils joining the fray are real.

lore.summary: The footsoldier of Hell, and it wants nothing from you but the fight. A barbazu comes shoulder to shoulder with its fellows, sawtoothed glaive levelled, its writhing beard of wire already reaching. They are stupid, eager and wholly without fear, and they work themselves into a red frenzy that carries them over the bodies of their own rank.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall soldier's build under scaled hide, and light on its feet for all that.
Durability: Tough as a veteran. It will take a great deal of honest hacking.
Defenses: Fire and venom cannot touch it; frost and acid scarcely trouble it. It sees in utter darkness and shrugs off a fair share of wizardry.
Speed: Faster afoot than a man in mail, and it loves to run you down. It can step home to Hell at will, though it rarely stoops to.
Might: Strong, and stronger still once the frenzy takes it. Its glaive strikes from a haft's length and leaves a cut that will not close.
Mind: Dull. It takes orders and relishes them, and there is very little else behind the eyes.
Disposition: Aggressive past all sense. It loves the fight for its own sake, never withdraws, and cannot be frightened off.
Bane: Silvered steel or blessed arms bite it; plain iron does half the work at twice the cost. Its wits are the true seam — feint it, split it from its rank, and it will chase you alone into whatever you have laid out for it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It levels the glaive and comes on, striking from a haft's length before you can close. Every cut it lands bleeds on and on and refuses the healer's craft — a man patched three times over will still empty himself into his boots. Get inside its reach and it takes you with both claws and lashes that wire beard across your face; the filth in it brings a wasting chill that eats the strength out of a man over days. Twice in a fight it can whip itself into a frenzy and simply stop caring what you do to it, and it will bellow up a tide of lesser fiends to bury whatever is left of your line.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Its glaive-cuts will not close on their own. Carry a surgeon's kit and a steady hand — prayer alone often fails on that wound.
• The beard carries a wasting chill. Wash the cuts, and watch your wounded for days after.
• Silvered or blessed. Plain steel does half the work and takes twice the time.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I have tried it. Twice. It does not want your gold, your name or your surrender — it wants the fight, and the officer who owns it has told it nothing worth hearing. The only word a barbazu keeps is the one its captain gave it. Kill it before it levels the glaive.

sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Bearded devils are aggressive and love to fight. They revel in their battle frenzy, spreading mayhem among their foes. A bearded devil’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Every bearded devil carries a sawtoothed glaive; it stands 6 feet tall and weighs about 225 pounds.

Infernal Wound (Su): The damage a bearded devil deals with its glaive causes a persistent wound. An injured creature takes 2 additional points of damage each round. The wound does not heal naturally and resists healing spells. The continuing bleeding can be stopped by a DC 16 Heal check, a cure spell, or a heal spell. However, a character attempting to cast a cure spell or a heal spell on a creature damaged by a bearded devil’s glaive must succeed on a DC 16 caster level check, or the spell has no effect on the injured character. A successful Heal check automatically stops the continuing bleeding as well as restoring some of the damage dealt. The infernal wound is a supernatural ability of the bearded devil, not of the weapon. The check DC is Constitution-based.

Beard (Ex): If a bearded devil hits a single opponent with both claw attacks, it automatically hits with its beard. The affected creature takes 1d8+2 points of damage and must succeed on a DC 16 Fortitude save or be infected with a vile disease known as devil chills (incubation period 1d4 days, damage 1d4 Str). Damage is dealt each day until the afflicted creature succeeds on three consecutive Fortitude saves, the disease is cured magically, or the creature dies. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Battle Frenzy (Ex): Twice per day, a bearded devil can work itself into a battle frenzy similar to the barbarian’s rage (+4 Strength, +4 Constitution, +2 morale bonus on Will saves, –2 AC penalty). The frenzy lasts for 6 rounds, and the bearded devil suffers no ill effects afterward.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only). Caster level 12th.

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day a bearded devil can attempt to summon 2d10 lemures with a 50% chance of success, or another bearded devil with a 35% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 3rd-level spell.

Baatezu Traits: Devils are fiends native to lawful evil-aligned planes. Most devils share the following traits: immunity to fire and poison; resistance to acid 10 and cold 10; see in darkness, letting them see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell; the ability to summon others of their kind (chance of success and type noted in each entry); and telepathy. Except where noted otherwise, devils speak Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Many are surrounded by a fear aura, used to break up powerful groups and defeat opponents piecemeal, and those with spell-like abilities lean on illusions — a favourite trick is conjuring illusory reinforcements, so foes can never be sure which of the devils joining the fray are real.

lore.summary: Hell's inquisitor: a gaunt, stooping thing of dry bone and stretched hide, tall as a barn door, with a scorpion's tail curled up over its shoulder. Osyluths police the other devils and take an ugly pleasure in the work; where one walks, its own kind cringe. I have met them on battlefields, in gaols, and once in a magistrate's chamber.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — head and shoulders above a tall man even with the stoop, and it reaches further than you think.
Durability: Very hard to put down, for all that it looks like a picked carcass.
Defenses: Fire and venom mean nothing to it, frost and acid little. Blades that are not blessed slide from its hide. It sees in the blackest dark, and a good deal of magic fails against it outright.
Speed: Quick on the ground and quicker in the air, for it flies at a thought. Worse, it can nail the road shut behind you — no stepping away, no calling for help.
Might: Strong. It bites, rakes with both claws and drives that tail-sting home in the same breath; the venom withers the strength out of your arms until you cannot lift a shield.
Mind: Clever and cold — a questioner's mind. It reads a man quickly, remembers everything, and lies well.
Disposition: It hates every living thing, its own kind included, and enjoys the hating. It fights to break you rather than merely to kill you.
Bane: Only blessed arms bite through its hide; silver and cold iron are wasted here. It fights by a pattern — walls of ice to cut your band apart, then the sting on the stragglers. Break the ice early, keep restorative draughts on your strongest arm, and it has little left but spite.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Dread rolls off it in a tight ring and the men nearest break first. It throws up walls of ice to halve your band, goes unseen, and works the stragglers with bite, claws and always the tail. The venom is the whole point: it wants you weak enough to question. If you mean to leave by magic it seals the space shut before it strikes. When the fight sours it drags a tide of lesser fiends out of Hell to hold you while it recovers its temper, then comes back at the wounded.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Its sting steals your strength, not your blood. Your strongest fighter drops first — plan the order.
• It shuts the road before it strikes. If you intend to leave by magic, leave early.
• Blessed steel only. Silver and cold iron will not answer here.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: The only devil I have held a true conversation with. It questioned me an hour and answered three of mine, all of them honestly and all of them useless. It keeps its word to the letter and hunts the gap in your phrasing while you are still speaking. Bring a lawyer's care or keep your mouth shut.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Bone devils hate all other creatures and attack ruthlessly. They freely use wall of ice to keep the enemy divided. A bone devil’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Bone devils stand about 9 feet tall and weigh about 500 pounds.

Fear Aura (Su): Bone devils can radiate a 5-foot-radius fear aura as a free action. Affected creatures must succeed on a DC 17 Will save or be affected as though by a fear spell (caster level 7th). A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same bone devil’s aura for 24 hours. Other devils are immune to the aura. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 20, initial damage 1d6 Str, secondary damage 2d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), dimensional anchor, fly, invisibility (self only), major image (DC 15), wall of ice. Caster level 12th. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day a bone devil can attempt to summon 2d10 lemures with a 50% chance of success, or another bone devil with a 35% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 4th-level spell.

Baatezu Traits: Devils are fiends native to lawful evil-aligned planes. Most devils share the following traits: immunity to fire and poison; resistance to acid 10 and cold 10; see in darkness, letting them see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell; the ability to summon others of their kind (chance of success and type noted in each entry); and telepathy. Except where noted otherwise, devils speak Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Many are surrounded by a fear aura, used to break up powerful groups and defeat opponents piecemeal, and those with spell-like abilities lean on illusions — a favourite trick is conjuring illusory reinforcements, so foes can never be sure which of the devils joining the fray are real.

lore.summary: A kyton wears chains instead of clothing, and the chains are alive when it wills them so. It is a torturer by trade and a smith by craft, forging its own links in the deep prisons of Hell. Mark this well: it is not proof against fire as its cousins are. I have never heard of one called to a bargain — only to a cell. They come in mobs.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a man's size and shape beneath the iron, and a good deal heavier than it looks.
Durability: Sturdy, and worse, it knits shut while you cut. Hack a limb away and it grows another before the night is out; hand the piece back and it seats itself instantly.
Defenses: Cold cannot harm it at all. But do not mistake it for the rest of its house — fire burns a kyton, and poison works on it, neither of which is true of its cousins. Its wounds close on their own unless the blade was silvered or blessed. It sees in the dark, and turns aside a fair share of spellwork.
Speed: Walks at a man's pace. It cannot fly, cannot step between places, and cannot outrun you — but it climbs its own chains as easily as a stair, and fights from up there.
Might: Strong enough in the arm, though the chains are its real weight. It can wake several at once within a short throw, stretch them out long and make them sprout barbs — every chain in the room becomes its limb, including the one on your wrist.
Mind: Dull and cruel, with one genuine gift: metalwork. It speaks the tongue of Hell and common speech besides, and it will use both on you.
Disposition: It does not want your death quickly. It wants you held, and it has all the time there is.
Bane: Silvered or blessed arms both serve — they cut it and stop the wound closing. Fire, useless against other devils, is welcome here, and so is poison. Then strip the room: a strong will can wrench a chain back out of its grip, and iron it cannot reach is iron it cannot use.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lifts its face and wears the features of someone you buried, or someone you hated, and the shock costs you your aim. Then the chains come — the two in its hands and more off the walls, lengthened and barbed, striking from every angle at once while the kyton climbs a link out of your reach. It does not retreat, does not tire and does not bargain for its life. Cut it and it closes over, unless your steel is silvered or blessed.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Not like the others: fire hurts it. Bring a torch and use it without shame.
• Silvered or blessed, or your cuts seal before you can swing again.
• Fight it in a bare room. Every chain, hook and manacle within a short throw becomes its arm.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I spoke to one. It answered in plain common speech, politely, and asked how long I thought I could scream. There is no bargain in a kyton — it wants nothing you can offer and nothing you can withhold. It has a smith's patience and a butcher's appetite. Do not open with words.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar, Lawful)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 20 (+2 Dex, +8 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +8/+10
Attack: Chain +10 melee (2d4+2/19–20)
Full Attack: 2 chains +10 melee (2d4+2/19–20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft. (10 ft. with chains)
Special Attacks: Dancing chains, unnerving gaze
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/silver or good, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to cold, regeneration 2, spell resistance 18
