sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Kytons are humanlike devils, wrapped in chains instead of clothing. A chain devil is 6 feet tall and weighs about 300 pounds, chains included. It attacks by flailing away with the spiked chains that serve as its clothing, armor, and weapons. A chain devil’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Chain devils speak Infernal and Common.

Dancing Chains (Su): A chain devil’s most awesome attack is its ability to control up to four chains within 20 feet as a standard action, making the chains dance or move as it wishes. In addition, a chain devil can increase these chains’ length by up to 15 feet and cause them to sprout razor-edged barbs. These chains attack as effectively as the devil itself. If a chain is in another creature’s possession, the creature can attempt a DC 15 Will save to break the chain devil’s power over that chain. If the save is successful, the kyton cannot attempt to control that particular chain again for 24 hours or until the chain leaves the creature’s possession. The save DC is Charisma-based. A chain devil can climb chains it controls at its normal speed without making Climb checks.

Unnerving Gaze (Su): Range 30 ft., Will DC 15 negates. A chain devil can make its face resemble one of an opponent’s departed loved ones or bitter enemies. Those who fail their saves take a –2 penalty on attack rolls for 1d3 rounds. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Regeneration (Ex): Chain devils take normal damage from silvered weapons, good-aligned weapons, and spells or effects with the good descriptor. A chain devil that loses a piece of its body regrows it in 2d6×10 minutes. Holding the severed member against the stump enables it to reattach instantly.

Skills: Chain devils have a +8 racial bonus on Craft checks involving metalwork.

Baatezu Traits: The kyton does not share the usual devil package. Its own entry gives immunity to cold rather than immunity to fire and poison, and lists no acid or cold resistance, no see in darkness and no telepathy — it relies instead on darkvision 60 ft., damage reduction 5/silver or good, regeneration 2, and spell resistance 18, and it speaks Infernal and Common rather than the Infernal, Celestial and Draconic of most devils. Like all its lawful evil kin it is native to a lawful evil-aligned plane and its weapons count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: Beautiful, winged, and a finer shot than any archer I have known. The erinyes hunts alone, taking contracts on the souls of oath-breakers, and she is not fussy about whether you count yourself one. She sees through every disguise, glamour and cloak of invisibility as plainly as through window glass. Expect her above you, and expect the first arrow to be burning.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — the frame of a comely woman or man, with broad dark wings that spoil the illusion at once.
Durability: Hardy. She takes a beating far better than that frame suggests.
Defenses: Fire and venom cannot touch her, frost and acid scarcely. Blades that are not blessed do half their work. She sees in the dark, sees through every lie of the eye without pausing to look, and much magic slides off her entirely.
Speed: Afoot, no swifter than you. Aloft, quick and beautifully handled — and she will not come down for you.
Might: Stronger than her look by a wide margin. She draws a burning bow that punches clean through mail, and carries a longsword she is entirely willing to use.
Mind: Sharp, worldly and well read. She speaks the tongue of Hell, the tongue of Heaven and the tongue of dragons, and can put words straight into your head besides.
Disposition: Professional. She is a huntress under contract; she will talk before, during and after the killing, and none of it kindly meant.
Bane: Only blessed arms cut her properly — silver and cold iron are wasted. She fights at range and loathes being closed with: get under her, break the sky between you, force the sword into her hand and most of what makes her deadly is gone. And watch for the rope.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She opens by charming one of yours, turning a friend into your problem, then rises out of reach and rains fire-fletched arrows down faster than you will care to count. Any man who breaks toward her meets a hurled rope that binds him fast; she lifts him, carries him high and lets go, and that is the end of him. Pressed, she calls up lesser fiends to hold the ground while she keeps shooting, or lays a stroke of unholy blight across your line. Cornered at last she draws steel, and she is no worse with it than with the bow.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• She will not land. Bring bows, slings or a way up, or you are only a target.
• Her arrows burn. A ward against fire blunts half of every shaft.
• Never let her get the rope on you. She drops what she catches.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: She talked with me a whole night on a rooftop in Sarn, and I liked her, which is the danger. We struck terms: she would not shoot me. She kept them exactly, and cut the rope I was hanging from instead. I have not walked right since. Bargain only in words you would sign your name beneath.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Erinyes prefer to engage in combat from a distance. They use charm monster to distract or disorganize their opponents, then rain down fiery arrows from above. An erinyes’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Unlike other devils, erinyes appear attractive to humans, resembling very comely women or men; an erinyes stands about 6 feet tall and weighs about 150 pounds, and speaks Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic.

Entangle (Ex): Each erinyes carries a stout rope some 50 feet long that entangles opponents of any size as an animate rope spell (caster level 16th). An erinyes can hurl its rope 30 feet with no range penalty. Typically, an erinyes entangles a foe, lifts it into the air, and drops it from a great height.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), charm monster (DC 19), minor image (DC 17), unholy blight (DC 19). Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

True Seeing (Su): Erinyes continuously use true seeing, as the spell (caster level 14th).

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day an erinyes can attempt to summon 2d10 lemures or 1d4 bearded devils with a 50% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 3rd-level spell.

Baatezu Traits: Devils are fiends native to lawful evil-aligned planes. Most devils share the following traits: immunity to fire and poison; resistance to acid 10 and cold 10; see in darkness, letting them see perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell; the ability to summon others of their kind (chance of success and type noted in each entry); and telepathy. Except where noted otherwise, devils speak Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Many are surrounded by a fear aura, used to break up powerful groups and defeat opponents piecemeal, and those with spell-like abilities lean on illusions — a favourite trick is conjuring illusory reinforcements, so foes can never be sure which of the devils joining the fray are real.

lore.summary: Hell keeps hounds; it also keeps cats. The bezekira is a great lion of the lower planes, and the cruelty of it is this — in honest daylight you cannot see it at all. Only in the dark does it show, a faint burning outline padding between the trees. It is sent up from Hell to hunt what Hell wants hunted, and it does not stop.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a lion's bulk, longer than a tall man and heavier than a warhorse.
Durability: Solid meat and bone beneath the glow; it bleeds and it dies as a beast does, though it takes a deal of killing.
Defenses: Blessed steel bites it and little else does. Spells break upon it as often as not, and flame troubles it hardly at all.
Speed: Swift as any hunting lion, sure-footed on rock and roof-slate alike, and it climbs and swims besides.
Might: Raking claws and a jaw that takes hold and will not let go; once it has borne you down it rakes with the hind feet until you stop moving.
Mind: As clever as a common man, and it speaks skull to skull without ever opening that mouth.
Disposition: A servant, not a savage. It hunts on an errand, and it will let quarry it was not sent for walk past untouched.
Bane: Only weapons blessed with good will cut it — plain steel is turned and silver is wasted, and cold iron does nothing to any devil. Douse your lanterns: in ordinary dark it burns as an outline and cannot hide. Conjured darkness smothers even that, so never let it have the summoned night.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It stalks unseen by the light of your own torches, tracking by scent for days if need be, then charges the flank in one leap — both claws and a bite that closes on a limb. Having taken hold it drags you down and rakes with the hind claws while your fellows are still turning about. If the fight sours it withdraws, circles, and comes again from the other side.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Put out every light you carry. It sees you regardless, but at least you can see the shape of it.
• It is sent, not turned loose. Ask whose errand it runs — sometimes the answer buys you the road.
• Blessed edges only. I emptied a quiver of good plain silver into one and got nothing for it but a nearer cat.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks into the skull, and speaks well. I have bargained with one twice, both times for passage. It kept my words exactly and my meaning not at all — I asked to pass unhurt, and it let me pass and ate the mule. Say what you mean, then say it again narrower.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a hellcat must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can rake.

Pounce (Ex): If a hellcat charges, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): Attack bonus +13 melee, damage 1d8+3.

Invisible in Light (Ex): A hellcat is invisible in any area lit well enough for a human to see. In a darkened area, it shows up as a faintly glowing outline visible up to 30 feet away (60 feet if the viewer has low-light vision). Magical darkness smothers the glow and conceals the outline. Though its appearance suggests it is incorporeal, a hellcat has a solid body and can be harmed by physical attacks.

Baatezu Traits: A hellcat is a devil, but it does not carry the full devil template. Its own entry grants damage reduction 5/good, darkvision 60 ft., scent, resistance to fire 10 (not immunity), and spell resistance 19; it has no immunity to fire or poison and no acid or cold resistance. It uses a natural telepathy out to 100 feet to communicate with other hellcats and with those it encounters. Its natural weapons, and any weapons it wields, count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Skills: Hellcats have a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Move Silently checks.

lore.summary: The cornugon is a captain of Hell — a horned, bat-winged brute of iron discipline that drills the lesser ranks and answers only to the dukes above it. Where one stands, a mob of lemures and a file of bearded devils is never far behind. It fights with a spiked chain longer than any sane weapon's reach, and it does not retreat.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a broad, winged thing half again the height of a tall man, and heavy with muscle.
Durability: Fearfully tough, and worse than tough: cut it and the cut knits shut while you watch.
Defenses: Fire and venom do nothing to it, acid and cold barely more. Most spells break upon it, and it sees plainly through any dark, conjured or natural.
Speed: Ground-slow for its size, but it flies steadily, and it can step across the world at a thought when it wishes to leave.
Might: The chain reaches farther than you expect, and any blow of it may leave a man standing stunned and useless; claws and jaws follow, and the tail opens a wound that keeps bleeding and fights off healing.
Mind: Clever, disciplined and a practised liar. It reads a battle line at a glance and goes straight for whoever matters most.
Disposition: Bold to the edge of arrogance. It rarely retreats even against odds, and it will call up lesser devils to pin you while it works.
Bane: Nothing but a weapon that is silvered and blessed together will cut it, and only such a weapon or holy magic stops the flesh from knitting — one property alone is a wasted arm, and cold iron is useless against all devils. Its aura of dread reaches only a little way; stand off and your nerve stays yours.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at a distance with dread, with flung fire and with lightning, then closes on the chain — singling out whoever it judges most dangerous and hammering that one senseless before turning to the next. Claws, bite and the bleeding tail follow. It sunders good weapons on purpose, calls up whatever help it can, and holds its ground long past the point where anything sane would run.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silvered and blessed, both, on the same blade. Either alone is an expensive way to annoy it.
• Its dread carries only a short way. Fight at the length of its chain and your men keep their courage.
• What the tail opens will not close on its own. Bring someone who can force a healing through, or bring a stretcher.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I bargained with a cornugon once, for a name. It gave me the name — and gave the same name to the men hunting me, having promised only to tell it me, not to keep it close. Deal with a captain of Hell and you get precisely what you said aloud. Nothing beside it.

sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: At will—dispel chaos (DC 21), dispel good (DC 21), magic circle against good, greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), persistent image (DC 21); 3/day—fireball (DC 19), lightning bolt (DC 19). Caster level 15th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Fear Aura (Su): A horned devil can radiate a 5-foot-radius fear aura as a free action. A creature in the area must succeed on a DC 23 Will save or be affected as though by a fear spell (caster level 15th). A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same horned devil's aura for 24 hours. Other devils are immune to the aura. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Stun (Su): Whenever a horned devil hits with a spiked chain attack, the opponent must succeed on a DC 27 Fortitude save or be stunned for 1d4 rounds. The save DC is Strength-based. This ability is a function of the horned devil, not of the spiked chain.

Infernal Wound (Su): The damage a horned devil deals with its tail attack causes a persistent wound. An injured creature takes 2 additional points of damage each round. The wound does not close naturally and resists healing spells. The continuing bleed can be stopped by a DC 24 Heal check, a cure spell, or a heal spell. However, a character attempting to cast a cure spell or a heal spell on a creature damaged by a horned devil's tail must succeed on a DC 24 caster level check, or the spell has no effect on the injured character. A successful Heal check automatically stops the continuing bleed as well as mending some of the damage. The check DC is Constitution-based.

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day a horned devil can attempt to summon 2d10 lemures or 1d6 bearded devils with a 50% chance of success, 1d6 barbed devils with a 35% chance of success, or another horned devil with a 20% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 6th-level spell.

Regeneration (Ex): Regeneration 5. A horned devil takes normal damage from good-aligned silvered weapons, and from spells or effects with the good descriptor; damage from anything else closes back up almost as fast as it is dealt.

Baatezu Traits: As a devil, a horned devil has immunity to fire and poison, resistance to acid 10 and cold 10, and see in darkness (it sees perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell). It has darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 28, damage reduction 10/good and silver, and telepathy out to 100 feet, and it speaks Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Its natural weapons, and any weapons it wields, count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: The gelugon is a devil built like an upright insect — chitin plate, working mandibles, a whipping segmented tail — and it governs the frozen reaches of Hell where the fire gives out. It is as cold as its country and it plans in lifetimes. You do not stumble upon one. It has been expecting you for some while.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — an upright, chitin-plated insect taller than any man, with a lashing segmented tail.
Durability: Very hard to put down, and it seals shut nearly as fast as you open it unless the blade is blessed.
Defenses: Fire and venom cannot touch it, and cold and acid scarcely — for all the ice it wears, it is a thing of Hell's furnace beneath. Most magic breaks upon it and it sees in any darkness.
Speed: Quick afoot for its bulk, and it takes to the air whenever it pleases.
Might: A great spear whose every strike drives a numbing cold into the limbs and slows a man to wading; the lashing tail does the same, and claws and jaws follow behind.
Mind: Brilliant and cold — the sharpest thing you are likely to meet below short of a duke, and learned in half the crafts there are.
Disposition: It fights only when a fight serves its purpose, and it judges that shrewdly. Losing, it steps out of the world rather than die on your terms.
Bane: Only a blessed weapon cuts it, and only blessing or holy magic keeps the cut open — silver is wasted here, unlike on its horned brothers, and cold iron is wasted on all devils. Its dread reaches only a little way. Fire is no use whatever; cold does grudging work at best.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It measures you first, then throws walls and storms of ice to break your line and pen you where it wants you, and steps in with the spear. Every hit puts the numbing cold in a man, and a slowed man is soon a dead one. It calls up lemures and bearded devils to hold your flanks, keeps an unholy ward about itself, and throws up false images to draw your arrows. If the reckoning turns, it vanishes and returns with a better plan.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Blessed steel, not silver. Silver is for the horned ones — here it is dead weight.
• The spear takes the quickness out of whoever it touches. Rotate your front rank before a man goes stiff.
• It withdraws when it is losing, and it remembers faces. Finish it or leave the country.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Of all the devils this one is worth the talking to — patient, genuinely learned, and it will hear an offer to its end. It is also finding the loose thread in your wording while it listens. I offered one a season's service for a road through the ice. It took the season. It never said which season.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Fear Aura (Su): An ice devil can radiate a 10-foot-radius fear aura as a free action. A creature in the area must succeed on a DC 22 Will save or be affected as though by a fear spell (caster level 13th). A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same ice devil's aura for 24 hours. Other devils are immune to the aura. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Slow (Su): A hit from an ice devil's tail or spear induces numbing cold. The opponent must succeed on a DC 23 Fortitude save or be affected as though by a slow spell for 1d6 rounds. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—cone of cold (DC 20), fly, ice storm (DC 19), greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only), persistent image (DC 20), unholy aura (DC 23), wall of ice (DC 19). Caster level 13th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Summon Devil (Sp): Once per day an ice devil can attempt to summon 2d10 lemures or 1d6 bearded devils, 2d4 bone devils with a 50% chance of success, or another ice devil with a 20% chance of success. This ability is the equivalent of a 4th-level spell.

Regeneration (Ex): Regeneration 5. An ice devil takes normal damage from good-aligned weapons and from spells or effects with the good descriptor; damage from anything else knits closed almost as fast as it is dealt.

Baatezu Traits: As a devil, an ice devil has immunity to fire and poison — despite its frozen aspect — along with resistance to acid 10 and cold 10, and see in darkness (it sees perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell). It has darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 25, damage reduction 10/good, and telepathy out to 100 feet, and it speaks Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic. Its natural weapons, and any weapons it wields, count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: Small, red and endlessly reasonable, the imp is Hell's clerk and Hell's spy. It fastens itself to a wizard or a petty lord, makes itself useful, and keeps a private ledger of every favour done. Most are met perched on a shoulder in some draughty tower — or never met at all, since it would far rather watch you as a raven or a rat.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — no bigger than a cat, and lighter than it looks.
Durability: Frail. One honest blow finishes it. Leave it be for a moment, though, and its hurts close by themselves.
Defenses: Silvered or blessed steel cuts it; anything less slides away. Venom cannot harm it, flame troubles it little, and it goes unseen whenever it cares to.
Speed: Ground-bound and slow afoot, but on the wing it is faultless — it turns in its own length and is gone.
Might: Little enough. The tail carries a sting whose poison takes the quickness out of a man's hands, and a man who cannot grip his sword is a man it can afford to fight.
Mind: As sharp as a clerk and far better read. It flatters, it bargains, and it can slip a suggestion into your head that feels like your own good idea.
Disposition: Craven and patient. It will not stand and trade blows, but it will gladly sting a sleeping man and be a raven again before he wakes.
Bane: Silvered or blessed steel is the only thing that touches it, and cold iron nothing — but it is a fragile creature, and one true blow settles it. Cut off the retreat first: it flees unseen and on the wing, and it can borrow the shape of a spider, a raven, a rat or a boar.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only from ambush and only while winning. It comes unseen or wearing another shape, stings once, and flies out of reach; if the sting lands and your hands go clumsy, it comes back for the rest. Cornered, it talks — pleading, offering, flattering — and it will keep talking exactly as long as it takes for something to distract you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver, or a blessing. A dagger will do — it dies as easily as a cat.
• Whatever it agrees to, make it say the whole of it aloud. The gap in the wording is where it lives.
• If a raven watches you eat two nights running, it is not a raven.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: The most conversable devil there is and the most expensive. I have traded with imps four times and come away poorer each time. It answers honestly and to the letter — ask a question with any slack in it and the slack is the whole of your loss. Fix the price, then fix the wording.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Tiny Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar, Lawful)
Initiative: +3
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 50 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 20 (+2 size, +3 Dex, +5 natural), touch 15, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/–5
Attack: Sting +8 melee (1d4 plus poison)
Full Attack: Sting +8 melee (1d4 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 2-1/2 ft./0 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Alternate form, damage reduction 5/good or silver, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 2, immunity to poison, resistance to fire 5
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +6, Will +4
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 17, Con 10, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 14
Skills: Diplomacy +8, Hide +17, Knowledge (any one) +6, Listen +7, Move Silently +9, Search +6, Spellcraft +6, Spot +7, Survival +1 (+3 following tracks)
Feats: Dodge, Weapon Finesse
Environment: A lawful evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 4–6 racial levels (Tiny)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 13, initial damage 1d4 Dex, secondary damage 2d4 Dex. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—detect good, detect magic, invisibility (self only); 1/day—suggestion (DC 15). Caster level 6th. The save DC is Charisma-based. Once per week an imp can use commune to ask six questions; the ability otherwise works as the spell (caster level 12th).

Alternate Form (Su): An imp can assume other forms at will as a standard action. This ability functions as a polymorph spell cast on itself (caster level 12th), except that an imp does not mend its injuries by changing form, and an individual imp can assume only one or two forms no larger than Medium. Each imp can assume one or two forms from the following list: Small or Medium monstrous spider, raven, rat, and boar.

Baatezu Traits: An imp is a devil, but its own entry replaces most of the family template: it has immunity to poison and resistance to fire 5 rather than the usual fire immunity, and no acid or cold resistance and no see in darkness. It keeps damage reduction 5/good or silver, darkvision 60 ft., and fast healing 2. Its natural weapons, and any weapons it wields, count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. It speaks Infernal, Celestial, and Draconic, and may serve as an improved familiar.

lore.summary: The lowest thing in Hell and by far the most numerous — a slumped lump of molten flesh in the rough shape of a man, its half-made face forever weeping. It cannot think and it cannot speak. It has no will of its own at all, only what a greater devil pushes into it, and greater devils push them forward in mobs, up any stair, into any spear.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a dripping, sagging shape about the height of a short man.
Durability: Soft and slow, and it comes apart readily enough. One of them was never the trouble.
Defenses: Fire cannot burn it and venom cannot touch it; cold and acid bother it little. It sees through any darkness. Nothing you say, sing or conjure at its mind will land, for there is no mind there to land upon.
Speed: A shambling walk. You can outpace one at a stroll; you cannot outpace a corridor packed with them.
Might: Two clumsy claws and no craft whatever behind them. The danger is in the counting, not the skill.
Mind: None. It is mindless in the plainest sense — it does not think, cannot speak, cannot be frightened, charmed, tricked, or reasoned with in any tongue.
Disposition: It surges at whatever living thing it meets and claws until it is destroyed, or until another devil tells it silently to stop. Nothing else will halt it.
Bane: Silvered or blessed steel opens it and common steel does not; cold iron is useless, as against all devils. It is slow, and it is stupid — take a doorway, a bridge or a stair and let them come to you one at a time.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: There are no tactics here to speak of. It walks at the nearest living thing and claws at it. It does not flank, does not flee, does not tire and cannot be made afraid. A mob of them exists to hold you in place while something with a mind decides what is to be done with you — so mind less what shambles at you and more what stands quietly behind it, giving the orders no one can hear.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• No mind means no fear, no charm, no bluff, no bargain. Nothing you say lands. Swing.
• Fight in a doorway. In the open they simply fold around you and press.
• A silvered or blessed edge, and a heavy one. You will be hacking for a good long while.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Do not waste the breath. There is nothing inside it to hear you — no words, no wit, no fear, not even appetite. I have shouted, offered, threatened and prayed at them and got the same wet reaching every time. Talk instead to whatever devil is driving the mob. That one can hear you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar, Lawful)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 14 (+4 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+2
Attack: Claw +2 melee (1d4)
Full Attack: 2 claws +2 melee (1d4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/good or silver, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to fire and poison, mindless, resistance to acid 10 and cold 10, see in darkness
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +3
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 10, Con 10, Int —, Wis 11, Cha 5
Skills: —
Feats: —
Environment: A lawful evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary, pair, gang (3–5), swarm (6–15), or mob (10–40)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 3–6 racial levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Mindless (Ex): Immunity to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects). Lemures are mindless and cannot communicate, but they are sensitive to telepathic messages from other devils, typically obeying a devil's mental commands. Only such a command, or their complete destruction, will make them stop clawing at whatever they meet.

Baatezu Traits: As a devil, a lemure has immunity to fire and poison, resistance to acid 10 and cold 10, and see in darkness (it sees perfectly in darkness of any kind, even that created by a deeper darkness spell). It has darkvision 60 ft. and damage reduction 5/good or silver, but no spell resistance and no telepathy of its own — it only receives the sendings of greater devils, and speaks no language at all. Its natural weapons, and any weapons it wields, count as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

lore.summary: A hound-sized thing of the deep tunnels, tan along the belly and rust-red across the back, waving a pair of feathered antennae before it like a blind man's hands. It smells iron the way a wolf smells blood, and it comes at a run. It wants no flesh — only your gear, crumbled to red dust and licked up off the floor.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — the bulk of a big hound, low and broad, with a long paddle of a tail.
Durability: Sturdier than the beast looks, though it dies like any animal once you find something to hit it with that isn't steel.
Defenses: A plated hide of no great thickness. It trusts to its legs and to the ruin of your weapons, not to armour of its own.
Speed: Quicker than a man in mail, and tireless — it will follow you across half a mountain while you still carry iron.
Might: Feeble jaws, hardly worth the name. The peril is the antennae: a brush of them and good steel falls to powder where it stands — breastplate first, then shield, then every smaller piece you carry. Enchanted metal sometimes holds. More often it does not.
Mind: Beast-witted. It knows hunger, and it knows iron, and there is nothing else in there.
Disposition: Not malicious in the least. It is a grazing animal, and you are the pasture.
Bane: It cannot want what it cannot smell — wood, stone, bone, horn and leather leave it indifferent, and it will abandon a chase to eat a heap of rust you dropped behind you. It favours plain iron and steel over gold and silver. Fight it with anything but metal: a steel blade that wounds it corrodes on the instant, so the very blow that lands costs you the sword.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It scents metal from a good way off, dashes straight at the largest piece — your breastplate, always — then the shield, then buckles, blade and buckle-tongues. It is relentless while anything intact remains, but it will break off the moment there is a fresh meal of red dust to devour. The bite is an afterthought and barely worth guarding against.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• A pouch of nails. Throw them down the passage, walk the other way, keep your mail.
• Never parry with steel — the blade dies with the blow. Staff, club, or a spellcaster's hands.
• Do not run from it wearing the thing it wants. It is faster than you and it never tires.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing behind those antennae to bargain with; it hears no words in any tongue I own. The whole conversation is conducted in iron. Cast a spare spearhead into the dark and walk away — I have kept my harness three times over with a handful of horseshoe nails.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor beast, and a ruinous one

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration
Initiative: +3
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (+3 Dex, +5 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+3
Attack: Antennae touch +3 melee (rust)
Full Attack: Antennae touch +3 melee (rust) and bite –2 melee (1d3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Rust
Special Qualities: Darkvision, scent
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +4, Will +5
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 17, Con 13, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 8
Skills: Listen +7, Spot +7
Feats: Alertness, Track
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary or pair
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 6–8 levels (Medium); 9–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Rust (Ex): A rust monster that makes a successful touch attack with its antennae causes the target metal to corrode, falling to pieces and becoming useless immediately. The touch can destroy up to a 10-foot cube of metal instantly. Magic armor and weapons, and other magic items made of metal, must succeed on a DC 17 Reflex save or be dissolved. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +4 racial bonus. A metal weapon that deals damage to a rust monster corrodes immediately. Wooden, stone, and other nonmetallic weapons are unaffected.

Scent (Ex): A rust monster can scent a metal object from up to 90 feet away. When it detects one, it dashes toward the source and attempts to strike it with its antennae. It targets the largest metal object available, striking first at armor, then at shields and smaller items, and prefers ferrous metals (steel or iron) over precious metals such as gold or silver — though it will devour the latter if given the opportunity.

lore.summary: A chest nobody carted in. A door in a wall that has no other side. A stout bed standing in a room where no one has slept in an age. The mimic is a great slow lump of hard flesh that has learned the shapes men trust, and it waits in old vaults and deep halls, still as furniture, until a hand comes near enough to glue itself to.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a wide, immensely heavy mass, near always wearing the shape of some solid piece of furniture.
Durability: Thickly made and slow to kill; it takes a deal of honest hewing.
Defenses: A hard, rough body beneath whatever paint it is showing you, and acid runs off it like water off slate — flasks and burning spittle are wasted here.
Speed: Wretched. It crawls. It cannot chase and it knows it, which is why it waits.
Might: Two heavy pseudopods that fall like sacks of wet sand, and a grip that crushes what it holds. Its whole surface runs with a glue that seizes anything touching it — hands, boots, and the sword you struck it with.
Mind: As sharp as a common man's, and it speaks the common tongue plainly when it cares to.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor kind. Hungry, and fond of coin, and quite willing to let you live if you make it worth the trouble.
Bane: Slow beyond all remedy — step back out of its reach and it can do nothing whatever but talk. Strong spirits dissolve the glue. And it cannot alter its bulk, only its shape, so mistrust the chest too fat for the door it stands behind, or the wardrobe standing where no dust-ring marks the floor.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It holds perfectly still until you are within reach, then lashes out with a pseudopod that sticks fast where it lands and squeezes. Weapons that strike it are held in the slime; men held against it are crushed against it. It fights out of hunger and greed, not malice, and will haggle in the middle of the brawl — it does not fight to the death if it can extort treasure or a meal instead.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Pay it. Salt pork, coin, anything. Cheaper than an arm.
• Carry a flask of the harshest spirit you can buy. It eats the glue, and it warms you after.
• Count the furniture against the dust. The piece with no dust-ring is the piece that walked in.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks, and it is greedy rather than wicked — that is a door, if you use it. I bought passage from one that had eaten the door out of a barrow, with a sack of salt pork and the rings off my left hand. But it will talk to you while it holds you. Never open a bargain from inside its reach.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable ambusher

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Aberration (Shapechanger)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 10 ft. (2 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (–1 size, +1 Dex, +5 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+13
Attack: Slam +9 melee (1d8+4)
Full Attack: 2 slams +9 melee (1d8+4)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Adhesive, crush
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to acid, mimic shape
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +6
Abilities: Str 19, Dex 12, Con 17, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 10
Skills: Climb +9, Disguise +13, Listen +8, Spot +8
Feats: Alertness, Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Focus (slam)
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: 1/10th coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 8–10 levels (Large); 11–21 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Adhesive (Ex): A mimic exudes a thick slime that acts as a powerful adhesive, holding fast any creatures or items that touch it. An adhesive-covered mimic automatically grapples any creature it hits with its slam attack. Opponents so grappled cannot get free while the mimic is alive without removing the adhesive first. A weapon that strikes an adhesive-coated mimic is stuck fast unless the wielder succeeds on a DC 16 Reflex save. A successful DC 16 Strength check is needed to pry it off. Strong alcohol dissolves the adhesive, but the mimic still can grapple normally. A mimic can dissolve its adhesive at will, and the substance breaks down 5 rounds after the creature dies.

Crush (Ex): A mimic deals 1d8+4 points of damage with a successful grapple check.

Mimic Shape (Ex): A mimic can assume the general shape of any object that fills roughly 150 cubic feet (5 feet by 5 feet by 6 feet), such as a massive chest, a stout bed, or a wide door frame. The creature cannot substantially alter its size, though. A mimic’s body is hard and has a rough texture, no matter what appearance it might present. Anyone who examines the mimic can detect the ruse with a successful Spot check opposed by the mimic’s Disguise check. Of course, by this time it is generally far too late.

Skills: A mimic has a +8 racial bonus on Disguise checks.

lore.summary: A wet heap of eyes and mouths that flows rather than walks, forever talking and never once saying anything. It is not wicked; it is thirsty, and it thirsts after the blood of thinking creatures above all. Look for it in sumps and drowned galleries beneath the earth, where its babble comes rolling up the tunnel long before the thing itself arrives.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a low spreading mound no higher than a man's waist, though it slumps and slides to fill whatever holds it.
Durability: Hardy out of all proportion to its bulk. There is a great deal of it and no part of it is vital.
Defenses: Formless — no wound is a mortal wound, and it cannot be caught out of position or taken from behind. Points and edges sink in and accomplish very little.
Speed: A crawl on land, and a far better swimmer than you are. Do not let it reach water while you are still in it.
Might: Half a dozen mouths on stalks of raw flesh that bite, latch, and drink; a spat gobbet of acid that burns and blinds; and the strength to fold a man bodily into itself and eat him from every side at once.
Mind: Dim, but not empty. It can shape the common tongue and near never chooses to.
Disposition: Neither evil nor reasoning. A gabbling appetite that never stops.
Bane: Bring a hammer or a stout staff — crushing tells on it where cuts and thrusts do not. Stop your ears against the gibbering, for the babble scrambles a man into striking his own fellows. Anyone born without eyes is spared its blinding spittle, though not the burning. And it softens stone underfoot into a mire, so never stand where it wishes you to stand.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It begins its gabble the instant it sees something edible, and those who cannot shut it out turn on the men beside them. Then the spittle, to burn and blind whoever looks most dangerous, and then the mouths — biting, fastening on, drinking the blood out of whatever they hold. Once enough of them have hold of a man it folds him in whole and the freed mouths go looking for the next. All the while the floor turns to porridge beneath the rest of you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Wax in the ears before you round the corner. The babble turns your own line against you.
• Hammers and staves. Points and edges only make it wetter.
• Stand on ground you brought with you — a plank, a shield laid flat. It turns stone to mire.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Words go in and come back out as slop. It has the common tongue somewhere in all those mouths — I once heard my own name given back to me in a dead friend's voice — but there is nobody in there to mean it. Do not listen for sense in the babble. Listening is precisely how it takes you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable horror

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration
Initiative: +1
Speed: 10 ft. (2 squares), swim 20 ft.
Armor Class: 19 (+1 Dex, +8 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+3
Attack: Bite +4 melee (1) or spittle +4 ranged touch (1d4 acid plus blindness)
Full Attack: 6 bites +4 melee (1) and spittle +4 ranged touch (1d4 acid plus blindness)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Gibbering, spittle, improved grab, swallow whole, blood drain, engulf, ground manipulation
Special Qualities: Amorphous, damage reduction 5/bludgeoning, darkvision 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +4, Will +5
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 13, Con 22, Int 4, Wis 13, Cha 13
Skills: Listen +4, Spot +9, Swim +8
Feats: Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Finesse
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 5–12 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Gibbering (Su): As soon as a mouther spots something edible, it begins a constant gibbering as a free action. All creatures (other than mouthers) within a 60-foot spread must succeed on a DC 13 Will save or be affected as though by a confusion spell for 1d2 rounds. This is a sonic mind-affecting compulsion effect. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected by the same gibbering mouther’s gibbering for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spittle (Ex): As a free action every round, a gibbering mouther fires a stream of spittle at one opponent within 30 feet. The mouther makes a ranged touch attack; if it hits, it deals 1d4 points of acid damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 18 Fortitude save or be blinded for 1d4 rounds. Eyeless creatures are immune to the blinding effect, but are still subject to the acid damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a gibbering mouther must hit a Medium or smaller foe with a bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Swallow Whole (Ex): The gibbering mouther can attempt to swallow a grappled opponent of Medium or smaller size by making a successful grapple check. (The gibbering mouther doesn’t actually “swallow” the opponent — it engulfs it within its amorphous form — but the effect is essentially the same.) Once inside, the gibbering mouther can use its blood drain ability. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by dealing 5 points of damage to the gibbering mouther (same AC). The gibbering mouther’s body can hold 1 Medium, 2 Small, 8 Tiny, 32 Diminutive, or 128 Fine creatures.

Blood Drain (Ex): On a successful grapple check after grabbing, that mouth attaches to the opponent. It automatically deals bite damage and drains blood, dealing 1 point of Constitution damage each round. A mouth can be ripped off (dealing 1 point of damage) with a DC 12 Strength check, or severed by a successful sunder attempt — 2 points of damage destroy a mouth. A severed mouth continues to bite and drain blood for 1d4 rounds after such an attack. A creature whose Constitution is reduced to 0 is killed. A swallowed opponent automatically takes 1d4 points of Constitution damage each round.

Engulf (Ex): A gibbering mouther can try to engulf a Medium or smaller opponent grabbed by three or more mouths. The opponent must succeed on a DC 14 Reflex save or fall and be engulfed. In the next round, the mouther makes twelve bite attacks instead of six (each with a +4 attack bonus). An engulfed creature cannot attack the mouther from within. The previously attached mouths are now free to attack others. The save DC is Strength-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Ground Manipulation (Su): At will, as a standard action, a gibbering mouther can cause stone and earth in all adjacent squares to become a morass akin to quicksand. Softening earth, sand, or the like takes 1 round, while stone takes 2 rounds. Anyone other than the mouther in that area must take a move-equivalent action to avoid becoming mired (treat as being pinned).

Amorphous (Ex): A gibbering mouther is not subject to critical hits. It cannot be flanked.

Skills: Thanks to their multiple eyes, gibbering mouthers have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks. A gibbering mouther has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It always can choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: A dark rubbery worm as long as a tall man, four barbed tentacles wreathing a small hooked beak, its hide the exact colour of the stone it lies against. It coils in a shadow beside any tunnel where things pass often, takes whatever moves within reach, and drags the body off to eat somewhere quieter. Pale-bellied, silent, and almost never seen first.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a coiled worm about as long as a tall man is high, and heavier than it looks.
Durability: Not greatly stout in itself. The difficulty is landing a blow that counts at all.
Defenses: That rubbery body sheds honest steel; plain blades and arrows slide from it as from a wet sail. Arms with some enchantment in them bite as they should — and so do the grick's own tentacles, which is worth remembering.
Speed: Brisk on the flat, and just as easy going up a sheer wall or along a ceiling.
Might: Four lashing tentacles studded with barbs, all coming at once. The beak is small and weak against so much body, and is not the danger.
Mind: Barely above an animal. It knows its hunting place and its hunger and nothing beyond.
Disposition: Attacks when hungry or crowded, never for spite. Even a cluster of them will not act together — each takes the nearest thing and hauls it away alone.
Bane: Common steel is near useless — you need an enchanted arm or a spell, or you will hack at it all evening. Beyond that it is a fragile, easily discouraged creature: it never presses a losing fight, and it will take dead meat over a live opponent every time.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lies motionless in the rock-shadow beside a well-used passage, invisible until it moves, and when something comes within reach all four tentacles arrive together. It does not press a losing fight and has no wish to finish you — the instant it has a body it can shift, it takes that and goes back to its lair to eat at leisure. Where there are several, each does this on its own account, which is a mercy.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Ordinary steel slides off. Bring an enchanted arm, or bring a spellcaster.
• It hides flat against bare rock and you will not see it. Watch the shadows at chest height.
• Drop a haunch of meat and back away. It would far rather drag than fight.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing to say to a grick. I have tried on four occasions in three tongues and been answered by the beak each time. It is a beast at a snare, and you deal with it as with any beast — bait it off with carrion, or kill it with something it can actually feel.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril, badly underestimated

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration
Initiative: +2
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), climb 20 ft.
Armor Class: 16 (+2 Dex, +4 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+3
Attack: Tentacle +3 melee (1d4+2)
Full Attack: 4 tentacles +3 melee (1d4+2); bite –2 melee (1d3+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/magic, darkvision 60 ft., scent
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +2, Will +5
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 14, Con 11, Int 3, Wis 14, Cha 5
Skills: Climb +10, Hide +3*, Listen +6, Spot +6
Feats: Alertness, Track (bonus feat)
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary or cluster (2–4)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 3–4 levels (Medium); 5–6 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Damage Reduction 10/magic (Ex): A grick’s rubbery body seems to shed blows of any kind; only magic weapons overcome its damage reduction. A grick’s own natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Ambush Tactics: Gricks attack when hungry or threatened. They hunt by holing up near high-traffic areas, using their natural coloration to blend into convenient shadows. When prey — virtually anything that moves — ventures near, they lash out with their tentacles. Their jaws are relatively small and weak compared to their body mass, so rather than consume a kill immediately, a grick normally drags its victim back to its lair to be eaten at its leisure. Multiple gricks do not fight in concert; each attacks the prey closest to it and breaks off the fight as soon as it can drag dead or unconscious prey away.

Skills: A grick has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened. *Their coloration affords gricks a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks when in natural rocky areas.

lore.summary: A gangling thing that hops on a single leg, with four long arms and a clutch of stalked eyes, and half of it never quite here. It walks the empty space beside the world, steps out of the air at your elbow, lifts the ring from your hand or the wand from your belt, and is gone before the shout. What it takes it hoards in a burrow, purely to look at.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — tall, spindly, and awkward-looking, which is a lie its victims pay for.
Durability: Slight. It has no wish to stand and take blows, and could not if it wished.
Defenses: None to speak of but absence. It steps sideways out of the world as easily as you step over a puddle, and your blade closes on nothing. It can pass clean through a wall to do it.
Speed: Very quick afoot, and quicker still to act — it has moved before you have finished deciding to.
Might: Almost none. A weak bite, given only to make you look at the wrong hand. Its true weapon is fingers you never feel.
Mind: Simple, but far from stupid — a magpie's cunning. It does not speak, in any tongue at all.
Disposition: A thief, not a killer. It wants the bright thing and nothing else, and it flees the moment it is hurt.
Bane: It sees magic wherever magic is, and goes straight for it — so an enchantment is the leash by which you lead it. Any number of simple ruses blunt its attack: a false purse, a decoy on a cord, gear lashed shut instead of hanging loose. Wound it once and it will not come back for a second helping.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It prowls unseen, often straight through the stone, until it has chosen its mark. Then it is beside you for a heartbeat — a bite to pull your eye one way, a hand to your belt the other — and it is out of the world again with the best thing you owned. It will not trade blows for long. Hurt it and it runs, and it does not return.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Lash your pouches shut and keep the good pieces under your shirt. Loose things walk.
• It smells enchantment. Leave a cheap charmed trinket out where it can see it, and it takes that instead.
• It will not kill you. Chasing it will — it goes through walls and you do not.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It has no words, but it deals. I have swapped with the same one twice — a bright brass astrolabe laid on a stone, then three steps back, and my sister's ring came out of the air where it had been. It understands a bargain and nothing whatever about keeping one. Show, never hand over.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor nuisance with costly tastes

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration
Initiative: +8
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (+4 Dex, +3 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+3
Attack: Bite +3 melee (1d4)
Full Attack: Bite +3 melee (1d4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., detect magic, ethereal jaunt
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 18, Con 11, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 10
Skills: Listen +9, Sleight of Hand +12, Spot +9
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: No coins; standard goods; double items
Advancement: 6–7 levels (Medium); 8–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Detect Magic (Su): Ethereal filchers can detect magic as the spell (caster level 5th) at will.

Ethereal Jaunt (Su): An ethereal filcher can shift from the Ethereal Plane to the Material Plane as part of any move action, and shift back again as a free action. It can remain on the Ethereal Plane for 1 round before returning to the Material Plane. The ability is otherwise identical with the ethereal jaunt spell (caster level 15th).

Thieving Tactics: An ethereal filcher prowls about, using its ethereal jaunt ability to move about unseen and often through solid objects. Upon locating a likely mark, it shifts to the Material Plane, attempting to catch its victim unaware. The creature attempts to seize an item, then retreats quickly back to the Ethereal Plane. It is not above delivering a bite to distract its target. Once it secures a trinket, it scurries back to its lair to admire its prize. When badly wounded, a filcher escapes rather than continuing the fight. Any number of simple ruses can blunt a filcher’s attack.

Skills: Ethereal filchers have a +8 racial bonus on Sleight of Hand checks, and a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

lore.summary: It hunts on the far side of the world's skin. A long blue-violet thing on stout legs, with three jaws that open outward like a flower, it steps from empty air, tears once at whatever stands nearest, and is gone before the blood has finished falling. Look for it where the veil wears thin: barrow-roads, ruined shrines, the deep places men have worn through with too much magic.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — shoulder-high to a big hound, and rather longer than a man laid out.
Durability: Middling. A lean hunter with no great armour of flesh, and it knows it.
Defenses: Its hide turns a little, but absence is its true shield: it simply is not there when the blow lands.
Speed: Swift afoot, and swifter still in leaving. Stepping sideways out of the world costs it nothing at all.
Might: One bite, given whole and hard, from three jaws that shut together like a trap.
Mind: Dull — a beast's cunning and no words in any tongue I know, only a thin whine that rises and falls with its pace and its hurts.
Disposition: A predator and nothing else. It takes no treasure, holds no grudge, and knows you only as meat that wandered near a thin place.
Bane: It must become solid to bite, and in that instant it is only a beast — ready your points and let it arrive on them. It wears no armour of magic, so plain steel serves. Wound it in earnest and it quits for its own plane and does not come back.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It listens from the grey and picks the straggler, then comes solid at your back to catch you unready. One bite, and it is gone again before you have finished turning. It will do this over and again while its luck holds, choosing a new side each time so that you never learn where to look. Cost it enough blood, though, and it breaks off entirely and goes home; it has no interest in dying for a meal.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight back to back. It always comes for the man facing away.
• Set your spears and wait. Swinging at it is swinging at air.
• You need not kill it. You need only make it expensive, and it leaves.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None to be had. It speaks nothing, understands nothing, and is away again before a greeting is finished. I once addressed one in five tongues, calling at empty air like a fool. The air bit me. Set your guard, put a wall you trust at your back, and let the beast come onto your point.

sections.body: Minor — A minor menace

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Ethereal Jaunt (Su): An ethereal marauder can shift from the Ethereal Plane to the Material Plane as a free action, and shift back again as a move action. The ability is otherwise identical with the ethereal jaunt spell (caster level 15th).

Skills: Ethereal marauders have a +2 racial bonus on Listen, Move Silently, and Spot checks.

Hunting Pattern: Once a marauder locates prey, it shifts to the Material Plane to attack, attempting to catch its victim flat-footed. The creature bites its victim, then retreats quickly back to the Ethereal Plane. When badly hurt or wounded, a marauder escapes to its home plane rather than continuing the fight.

lore.summary: Beneath the world lives a curious thing shaped like nothing much at all: a low spreading slick of flesh, swirled with colours that serve it for eyes and ears. A phasm may wear any shape it has seen — a coin on a stair, a hound, a captain of the guard — and changes chiefly for the pleasure of changing. Met alone, in old deep halls, and generally already watching you.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — in its own shape a broad low disc of flesh no taller than a footstool, and far heavier than it looks.
Durability: Stubborn out of all proportion to its softness. It endures a great deal and complains about none of it.
Defenses: Formless: no front, no back, no vital spot to find and none to flank. Poison, sleep, palsy, stunning and the shaping magics all slide off it, and it shrugs aside what would fell a stouter thing.
Speed: Unhurried in its own shape — but it can put on something swift the moment it would rather be elsewhere.
Might: Feeble of arm; the slap of a pseudopod is nothing. Its strength is borrowed, for it becomes the most fearsome creature it has ever seen and fights with that shape's gifts.
Mind: Sharp, well-read and endlessly curious. It studies, it makes things with its hands when it has hands, it remembers, and it lies beautifully when the mood takes it.
Disposition: Whimsical and wholly its own master — as apt to greet you, flee you or fall upon you as the fancy strikes. It loves a joke and is not always careful whom the joke lands on.
Bane: Curiosity, and boredom. It would sooner have a story than a meal, and it tires of a fight that stops being interesting. Its own limbs are weak, so deny it the moment it needs to put on a fiercer shape. No hide of its turns a blade — plain steel serves, no silver, no blessing, no enchantment needed.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only when it elects to, and it elects badly for you: it puts on the worst thing it has ever met and comes at you wearing that. Formless underneath, it cannot be flanked nor struck in any vital place, and every foot on the floor tells it where you stand, so surprise is not on offer. Hurt it in earnest and it becomes something fleet — a bird, a hare, a running man — and is simply gone, bearing no grudge afterward.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Talk first. It is the one thing down there that would rather hear you than eat you.
• Never call its bluff twice. The first time it laughs; the second it puts on teeth.
• The chair was not a chair. Sit down slowly in strange rooms.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The pleasantest company on the deep roads. Mine wore my own face to see whether I would laugh; I laughed, and we were friends by morning. Bring news, riddles, and some object it has never handled. It lies for sport and never for malice, and keeps any bargain it thought amusing to strike. Speak plainly — it hears you in the mind before you finish.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Skills: Bluff +20, Climb +7, Craft (any one) +12, Diplomacy +12, Disguise +20 (+22 acting)*, Intimidate +4, Knowledge (any one) +18, Listen +12, Spot +12, Survival +8

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Alternate Form (Su): A phasm can assume any form of Large size or smaller as a standard action. This ability functions as a polymorph spell cast on itself (caster level 15th), except that the phasm gains no healing from changing form. A phasm can remain in its alternate form until it chooses to assume a new one or return to its natural form.

Amorphous (Ex): A phasm in its natural form has immunity to poison, sleep, paralysis, polymorph, and stunning effects. It is not subject to critical hits and, having no clear front or back, cannot be flanked.

Resilient (Ex): A phasm has a +4 racial bonus on Fortitude and Reflex saves (included in the statistics block).

Tremorsense (Ex): A phasm can automatically sense the location of anything within 60 feet that is in contact with the ground, so long as it is touching the ground itself.

Skills: *When using shapechange, a phasm gains a +10 circumstance bonus on Disguise checks.

Temperament: When faced with potential danger, a phasm is equally likely to retreat, parley, or attack, as its fancy strikes. If pursued or harassed, a phasm transforms into the most fearsome creature it knows and attacks. When seriously hurt, it changes to some fast or agile form and tries to escape. Phasms can speak Common but prefer telepathic communication.

lore.summary: Slaves, and bred for it. Long ago the aboleths took men and unmade them across generations into these hunched, scaled, fish-eyed things — amphibious, obedient, and made to keep the drowned halls of their masters. You find them in lightless sumps and flooded undercaverns, never singly, and never far from the thing that owns them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a man's height and a man's weight, but hunched, and wrong at every joint.
Durability: Hardy enough. No better than a seasoned soldier and no worse.
Defenses: A scaled hide worth a little and nothing beyond it. No weapon is barred from it and no spell slides off.
Speed: Shambling and slow on dry stone; in water it moves faster than anything you can do in mail.
Might: Strong out of all keeping with its frame. The bite is the real weapon — jaws that take a limb — with claws to hold you steady while it works, and raking hind feet besides once it has you in the water.
Mind: As clever as a common man, which is precisely what makes it dangerous. It lays ambushes, keeps proper watches, and understands what it is doing.
Disposition: Cruel, orderly, and utterly owned. It obeys, it reports, and it does not break ranks to save itself.
Bane: Dry land. Ashore it is slow and clumsy, and blind to half of what its ears and eyes manage beneath the surface. Ordinary steel is enough — it has no hide that turns a blade and no charm that answers one.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They come from below, in broods, in black water where their senses beat yours. One drags a man in and the rest close on him; in the water they bite, hold and rake with the hind feet all at once, and no man in mail survives being held under. Ashore they are far less — they wade out only when ordered — and they fight shoulder to shoulder in ranks, because they were bred to obey rather than to think of themselves.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight them ashore or not at all. In the water you are the slower animal.
• Count the ripples, not the heads. They never come as few as they look.
• Whatever they promise, their master has promised nothing.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: They speak the water-tongue and will answer you in it, politely — and every word carried back to their master. I bought passage from a brood once with nothing but news; they kept the bargain to the letter, then took me at the next ford on new orders. Talk if you must, but know you are talking to the thing behind them.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration (Aquatic)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), swim 40 ft.
Armor Class: 13 (+1 Dex, +2 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+5
Attack: Bite +5 melee (2d6+4)
Full Attack: Bite +5 melee (2d6+4) and 2 claws +0 melee (1d4+2)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Rake 1d6+2
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., amphibious
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +1, Will +3
Abilities: Str 19, Dex 13, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 10, Cha 6
Skills: Hide +6*, Listen +7*, Move Silently +6, Spot +7*, Swim +12
Feats: Alertness
Environment: Underground
Organization: Brood (2–5) or pack (6–15)
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Usually lawful evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 3–4 levels (Medium); 5–6 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Rake (Ex): Attack bonus +0 melee, damage 1d6+2. A skum also gains two rake attacks when it attacks while swimming.

Skills: *Skum have a +4 racial bonus on Hide, Listen, and Spot checks underwater. A skum has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Amphibious (Ex): A skum breathes water and air alike, and fights as readily on land as in the deep. It is about the same height and weight as a human. Skum speak Aquan.

lore.summary: A soft lamp bobbing over black water, the colour of a candle or a drowned moon. Inside that light sits a mind — patient, cruel, and long practised. It walks travellers off the causeway into the sucking places, then hangs above them while they go under, and drinks the terror as a man drinks wine. Temperate fens and marshes; the friendliest-looking thing in them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — a globe of soft light no bigger than a helm, and a good deal lighter than one.
Durability: Little enough. The whole trouble is landing anything on it at all.
Defenses: It drifts aside from every stroke and every arrow; I have watched good archers empty their quivers into a bog. Nearly all spellcraft passes clean through it, and when startled it snuffs its glow and is gone from sight entirely.
Speed: It flies where it likes and turns within its own width. You will not chase it, and you cannot outrun it.
Might: Feeble — it could not lift a dagger. It touches you instead, and the touch is lightning.
Mind: Keen, and it speaks: the common tongue and the speech of the air both, in a voice made by shivering its own body. It has no mouth. The sound comes from everywhere at once.
Disposition: Malice for its own sake. It wants you frightened, then lost, then drowning, and it wants to watch it happen.
Bane: Two things reach it: the unerring darts of magic, which cannot miss and are not turned aside, and the spell that shuts a creature inside a maze of its own. Beyond those, bring rope, a sounding-pole, and the discipline not to follow a light off the path.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It scarcely fights at all. It shows itself as a lantern at a comfortable distance and drifts off whenever you close, always toward worse footing — reed beds, sink-holes, a channel that wears the look of a path. Only when the mire has hold of you does it come down and touch, and each touch is a stroke of lightning, and it is in no hurry whatever. Threaten it in earnest and it puts out its light and becomes simply unfindable.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never step off the path for a light. Not for a lantern, not for a voice, not for a crying child.
• Rope every man to the line before you enter the fen. Every man, every time.
• If it goes dark, it has not left. Back out the way you came, slowly.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It will talk, and that is the horror of it. Mine had a woman's voice and no mouth to make it. It asked after my mother by name, told me how long the last man had taken to go under, and wondered aloud whether I would be quicker. It answers honestly. It asks only one thing of you: that you come a little closer.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Aberration (Air)
Initiative: +13
Speed: Fly 50 ft. (perfect) (10 squares)
Armor Class: 29 (+1 size, +9 Dex, +9 deflection), touch 29, flat-footed 20
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/–3

Full Attack: Shock +16 melee touch (2d8 electricity)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to magic, natural invisibility
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +12, Will +9
Abilities: Str 1, Dex 29, Con 10, Int 15, Wis 16, Cha 12
Skills: Bluff +13, Diplomacy +3, Disguise +1 (+3 acting), Intimidate +3, Listen +17, Search +14, Spot +17, Survival +3 (+5 following tracks)
Feats: Alertness, Blind-Fight, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Weapon Finesse (B)
