Organization: Solitary, pair, or string (3–4)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 10–18 levels (Small)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Immunity to Magic (Ex): A will-o'-wisp is immune to most spells or spell-like abilities that allow spell resistance, except magic missile and maze.

Natural Invisibility (Ex): A startled or frightened will-o'-wisp can extinguish its glow, effectively becoming invisible as the spell.

Shock (Ex): Will-o'-wisps usually avoid combat. They prefer to confuse and bewilder adventurers, luring them into morasses or other hazardous places. When they are forced to fight, they loose small electrical shocks, which act as melee touch attacks at +16 and deal 2d8 points of electricity damage.

Glow and Voice: A will-o'-wisp's body is a globe of spongy material about 1 foot across and weighing about 3 pounds, and its glowing body sheds as much light as a torch. They can be yellow, white, green, or blue, and are easily mistaken for lanterns. Will-o'-wisps speak Common and Auran; they have no vocal apparatus but can vibrate to create a voice with a ghostly sound.

lore.summary: Look up. In the old halls a choker lies flattened against the vaulting above an archway or a stairhead — a squat grey body with two absurdly long rubbery arms, and spined pads that hold it to bare stone as easily as you hold a cup. It takes the last man in the file by the throat, quietly, and the rest of you walk on a while before anyone thinks to count.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — no heavier than a hound, with arms far longer than anything that size has business owning.
Durability: Slight. Once it is off the ceiling and in front of you it does not last long.
Defenses: Rubbery and quick, and that is the whole of it. Steel serves; no silver, no blessing, no enchantment wanted.
Speed: Unnaturally quick — it acts twice in the time you act once, and it goes up sheer stone as easily as you walk a road.
Might: Stronger than its frame allows. It reaches from beyond your sword's length, takes the throat, and crushes.
Mind: Dull, but not witless. It has the underfolk's tongue after a fashion, chooses its ambush spots with real judgement, and never fails to pick the straggler.
Disposition: Vicious, greedy, and solitary. It hunts alone, kills for the eating, and keeps whatever its meals were carrying.
Bane: It fights from above and from behind; deny it both and it is a feeble thing. A man in its grip can neither shout nor speak a word of magic, so the fight is decided by whoever is watching the rear. Bring light to the ceiling.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits at a pinch-point — an arch, a well-mouth, the head of a stair — pressed flat to the stone above, and lets most of the party pass beneath. Then it reaches down for the last man's neck, takes hold and hauls him upward, crushing as it goes. It strikes and shifts in the same ugly breath, faster than it has any right to be. Its victim can neither cry out nor speak a spell. Lose it the grip and it flees along the ceiling.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Eyes up in old halls. It is always above the arch, never beside it.
• The last man in the file is the bait. Rotate him, and never let him be your youngest.
• It reaches farther than you do. Step in past its arms; do not lean in at them.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is none. It has words — the underfolk's tongue, badly — and it uses them for nothing whatever. I called up to one at Hallow Deep for the better part of an hour; it waited me out and took my torchbearer as we filed away. Do not negotiate with a ceiling. Put a light on it and kill it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Aberration
Initiative: +6
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), climb 10 ft.
Armor Class: 17 (+1 size, +2 Dex, +4 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+5
Attack: Tentacle +6 melee (1d3+3)
Full Attack: 2 tentacles +6 melee (1d3+3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, constrict 1d3+3
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., quickness
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +4
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 14, Con 13, Int 4, Wis 13, Cha 7
Skills: Climb +13, Hide +10, Move Silently +6
Feats: Improved Initiative (B), Lightning Reflexes, Stealthy
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 4–6 levels (Small); 7–12 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Constrict (Ex): A choker deals 1d3+3 points of damage with a successful grapple check against a Large or smaller creature. Because it seizes its victim by the neck, a creature in the choker's grasp cannot speak or cast spells with verbal components.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a choker must hit a Large or smaller opponent with a tentacle attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict. Chokers receive a +4 racial bonus on grapple checks, which is already included in the statistics block.

Quickness (Su): Although not particularly dexterous, a choker is supernaturally quick. It can take an extra standard action or move action during its turn each round.

Skills: A choker has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on Climb checks, even if rushed or threatened.

Ambush Habits: A choker likes to perch near the ceiling, often at intersections, archways, wells, or staircases, and reach down to attack its prey. Its hands and feet have spiny pads that help it grip almost any surface. A choker attacks creatures of almost any size, but prefers lone prey of its size or larger. If one is very hungry, it may attack a group, but it waits to grab the last creature in line. Chokers speak Undercommon.

lore.summary: A pale greenish thing like a vast toothed centipede, walking the walls and hanging from the vaulting, with a crown of eight soft tentacles about its head and two eyes on stalks above them. It stinks of the grave, and you will smell it long before you see it. It prefers the dead — but a living man who cannot move is near enough the same thing to its way of thinking.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer than a horse and nearly as heavy, though most of that length is body and legs.
Durability: Not much. It is a soft thing under all that length, and it dies quickly once you can reach it.
Defenses: Nothing worth the name. Common steel opens it. Its whole protection is that you cannot move by the time you are close enough to try.
Speed: Brisk on the flat, and it takes a sheer wall or a ceiling without slowing. Expect it from the roof.
Might: Weak jaws — the bite is almost an afterthought. The tentacles are the whole of it: one touch and the limb goes dead, and enough touches leave you lying still and wide awake while it begins.
Mind: None to speak of. A hunger with a good nose on it.
Disposition: Scavenger before hunter. It follows the smell of dead things, and a battlefield or a charnel pit will draw one from a long way off.
Bane: Fragile, and its jaws are feeble; the danger is only ever the tentacles. Fight it with reach and stand well apart, so one man going stiff does not lose you the line. Whatever wards a man against palsy is worth more here than any armour.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hunts by smell and comes along the wall or the ceiling, dropping into the middle of a marching line. It lashes with all eight tentacles at once, seeking any bare skin, and every touch that lands leaves the limb — and shortly the man — dead weight and helpless. It does not stop to finish those still standing; it works down the line laying men out, and only then settles to feed on whoever fell first, awake and watching it work.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Spears and polearms. Anything that ends at your fist will end you.
• Never stand shoulder to shoulder. One sweep takes the whole rank otherwise.
• It smells the dead. Do not camp downwind of a battlefield, and bury your kills deep.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None. There is nothing in it to talk to — no words, no cunning, only appetite and a good nose. I have coaxed one off a road with a dead mule, and that is the nearest thing to conversation it offers. If you have no mule, you had better have spears.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Aberration
Initiative: +2
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), climb 15 ft.
Armor Class: 17 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +6 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+8
Attack: Tentacle +3 melee (paralysis)
Full Attack: 8 tentacles +3 melee (paralysis) and bite –2 melee (1d4+1)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Paralysis
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., scent
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +5
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 1, Wis 15, Cha 6
Skills: Climb +12, Listen +6, Spot +6
Feats: Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Track
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary, pair, or cluster (3–5)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 4–6 levels (Large); 7–9 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Paralysis (Ex): Those hit by a carrion crawler's tentacle attack must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 2d4 rounds. The tentacles themselves deal no damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Scent (Ex): A carrion crawler has a highly developed sense of smell and can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track carrion by scent. It follows the reek of death through miles of tunnel.

Skills: A carrion crawler has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened. It uses this to travel along ceilings and drop on prey from above.

Feeding Habits: A carrion crawler is a pale yellow-green, centipede-like scavenger some 9 to 10 feet long and 500 pounds in weight, with eight tentacles springing from the sides of its head and two eye stalks above them. It lashes with the tentacles until something goes rigid, then bites at leisure. Nests hold a single crawler or a cluster of up to five.

lore.summary: Made, not born. A hand-sized thing of clay, ash and mandrake root, quickened with a measure of its maker's own blood and given leathery wings. It flies errands above a wizard's tower, and all it sees, its master sees. Meet one on the road and you have already met the man who sent it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — it sits comfortably in a cupped hand, and would rather perch than stand.
Durability: Frail as a small bird. One honest blow ends it — though breaking it wounds the maker, wherever in the world he happens to be sitting.
Defenses: None to speak of, save the virtues of a made thing: no breath to stop, no blood to poison, no pain, no fear, and nothing you can say to its mind that it will heed.
Speed: Slow and lurching afoot; swift and neatly agile on the wing.
Might: Almost none at all. Its whole strength is a small venomous bite.
Mind: As sharp as its maker and no sharper, for it thinks with his thoughts. It cannot utter a word aloud, yet it hears and understands every word of yours.
Disposition: Obedient past all sense. It has no wants of its own — only orders, which it follows to the letter and to its own ruin.
Bane: It must land upon you to bite, and it is soft — a gauntlet, a cloak or a stick will do. Better still, deal with the wizard: kill the master and the servant melts to a pool of ichor of its own accord.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits above and behind, drops onto a shoulder or the nape of a neck, and bites. The venom does not kill; it drops a man into a dead sleep where he stands, and sleep in the wrong company is the same as dying. It has no interest in a stand-up fight, keeps to the air when it can, and breaks off the moment its errand is done or its master calls it home.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It cannot speak. It listens perfectly. Assume the wizard is standing right behind it.
• The bite is sleep, not death. Which is small comfort — I woke stripped of everything but my boots.
• Break it and the maker feels the blow. Fine leverage, and a fine way to earn an enemy for life.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: You are never truly speaking to the homunculus. It has no voice to answer with. But say your piece slowly and plainly and know the wizard hears every syllable through its ears. I once bargained a truce standing in an empty lane, talking to a thing the size of a cat. Mind that the same trick lets him count your blades.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Tiny Construct
Initiative: +2
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 50 ft. (good)
Armor Class: 14 (+2 Dex, +2 size), touch 14, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/–8
Attack: Bite +2 melee (1d4–1 plus poison)
Full Attack: Bite +2 melee (1d4–1 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 2-1/2 ft./0 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison
Special Qualities: Construct traits, darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +4, Will +1
Abilities: Str 8, Dex 15, Con —, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 7
Skills: Hide +14, Listen +4, Spot +4
Feats: Lightning Reflexes
Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Any (same as creator)
Treasure: None
Advancement: 3–6 levels of construct (Tiny)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 13, initial damage sleep for 1 minute, secondary damage sleep for another 5d6 minutes. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus. Homunculi land on their victims and bite with their venomous fangs.

Telepathic Link (Su): A homunculus cannot speak, but the process of creating one links it telepathically with its creator. It knows what its master knows and can convey to him or her everything it sees and hears, out to a distance of 1,500 feet. A homunculus never travels beyond this range willingly, though it can be removed forcibly; if this occurs, the creature does everything in its power to regain contact with its master. An attack that destroys a homunculus deals 2d10 points of damage to its master. If the creature's master is slain, the homunculus also dies, and its body swiftly melts away into a pool of ichor.

Construct Traits: A construct has no Constitution score and is never fatigued or exhausted. It is immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and necromancy effects, and to any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, ability drain or energy drain, and cannot be raised or resurrected. It cannot heal damage on its own, though it can often be repaired. It has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision, and it does not eat, sleep or breathe. A homunculus, unusually for a construct, is not mindless: it has an Intelligence score of 10 and shares its creator's alignment and basic nature.

Construction: A homunculus is shaped from a mixture of clay, ashes, mandrake root, spring water, and one pint of the creator's own blood. The materials cost 50 gp. The master may assemble the body or hire someone else to do the job; creating the body requires a DC 12 Craft (sculpting) check or a DC 12 Craft (pottery) check. After the body is sculpted, it is animated through an extended magical ritual that requires a specially prepared laboratory or workroom, similar to an alchemist's laboratory and costing 500 gp to establish. A larger and more capable homunculus can be created, but each additional level of the creature adds 2,000 gp to the cost. Requires Craft Construct, arcane eye, mirror image, mending, and a caster of at least 4th level; Price — (never sold); Cost 1,050 gp + 78 XP.

lore.summary: Not a beast at all, but a spell wearing furniture. A rope, a carpet, a chair, a ladder, a great bronze idol — any object may be woken and set walking at you, and it comes without hatred, without haste and without stopping. Whatever it was before it moved is exactly what it is now: cord, cloth, oak, stone, iron.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: As big as whatever was woken — a stool, a wardrobe, a wagon, a temple door, the colossus in the market square.
Durability: It keeps the toughness of its own substance and nothing more. Cloth tears, cord parts, oak splits, bronze simply laughs at you.
Defenses: A made thing entire: no breath, no blood, no fear, nothing to sicken, charm or strike dead. Nothing you can do to a mind will touch it, because there is no mind in it.
Speed: It lurches if it has no legs, strides if it has two, scuttles quick as a spider if it has many, and a wheeled thing will run down a horse. Wooden pieces float and swim, a rope climbs, and a carpet flies — badly.
Might: A plain crushing blow, weighted by whatever it is made of. A big hard one simply walks over you and keeps walking.
Mind: None whatever. It is a tool holding a purpose that was never its own.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor angry nor eager. It does exactly as the animator bade it, without question, and it never tires and never breathes.
Bane: Fight the material, not the shape — an axe for the wardrobe, a hammer for the statue, shears for the tapestry. And it has no wit at all: lead it onto a stair, a rotted floor or the lip of a pit and it will follow you straight down.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only as its animator directed, in a straight line and no cleverer than the order it was given. Sheets and tapestries go for the face, wrapping the head and blinding a man while the rest of the household batters him; ropes, vines and rugs coil round and crush; anything large and hard enough tramples what it walks over. It cannot be bluffed, taunted, drawn off or made to reconsider.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bring the right tool, not your good sword. An axe for wood, a hammer for stone. Steel just chips.
• The carpet goes for the head. Cut your way out of it fast or you fight the rest of the room blind.
• It follows without looking. Back over a pit or a rotten stair and let the floor do the work.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nobody home. I have tried — greeted a striding wardrobe in three tongues while it walked me the length of a corridor, and got no more from it than I would from the wall. The only conversation worth having is with the hand that woke the thing, and that hand is usually in the next room.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Construct
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares); 30 ft. legs, 40 ft. multiple legs, 60 ft. wheels
Armor Class: 14 (–1 size, +5 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+10
Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d8+4)
Full Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d8+4)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft. (long); 10 ft./10 ft. (tall)
Special Attacks: See text (blind, constrict or trample, depending on the object's form)
Special Qualities: Construct traits, darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, hardness of the original object; also see text
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +1, Will –4
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 10, Con —, Int —, Wis 1, Cha 1
Skills: —
Feats: —
Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 3 (Large; other sizes range from 1/2 to 10 — see text)
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: —

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Other Sizes: Any object of any size may be woken, and the rows above describe the Large reference form. Tiny: Challenge Rating 1/2, AC 14 (touch 14), slam +1 melee (1d3–1), Str 8, Dex 14, speed 40 ft.; Small: Challenge Rating 1, AC 14 (touch 12), slam +1 melee (1d4), Str 10, Dex 12, speed 30 ft.; Medium: Challenge Rating 2, AC 14 (touch 10), slam +2 melee (1d6+1), Str 12, speed 30 ft.; Large: Challenge Rating 3, AC 14 (touch 9), slam +5 melee (1d8+4), Str 16, speed 20 ft.; Huge: Challenge Rating 5, AC 13 (touch 7), slam +9 melee (2d6+7), Str 20, Dex 8, speed 20 ft., space 15 ft.; Gargantuan: Challenge Rating 7, AC 12 (touch 4), slam +15 melee (2d8+10), Str 24, Dex 6, speed 10 ft., space 20 ft.; Colossal: Challenge Rating 10, AC 11 (touch –1), slam +25 melee (4d6+13), Str 28, Dex 4, speed 10 ft., space 30 ft. Organization runs Group (4) for Tiny objects, Pair for Small, and Solitary from Medium upward.

Blind (Ex): A sheetlike animated object such as a carpet or tapestry can grapple an opponent up to three sizes larger than itself. The object makes a normal grapple check; if it wins, it wraps itself around the opponent's head, causing that creature to be blinded until it is removed.

Constrict (Ex): A flexible animated object such as a rope, vine, or rug deals damage equal to its slam damage value plus 1-1/2 times its Strength bonus with a successful grapple check against a creature up to one size larger than itself. An object of at least Large size can make constriction attacks against multiple creatures at once, if they all are at least two sizes smaller than the object and can fit under it.

Trample (Ex): An animated object of at least Large size and with a hardness of at least 10 can trample creatures two or more sizes smaller than itself, dealing damage equal to the object's slam damage plus 1-1/2 times its Strength bonus. Opponents who do not make attacks of opportunity against the object can attempt Reflex saves (DC 10 + half the object's construct level total + the object's Strength modifier) to halve the damage.

Hardness (Ex): An animated object has the same hardness it had before it was animated — a wooden table remains as tough as wood, a bronze statue as tough as bronze, a rope as soft as rope.

Improved Speed (Ex): The base land speeds given assume that an animated object lurches, rocks, or slithers along. Objects with two legs (statues, ladders) or a similar shape that allows faster movement have a +10-foot bonus to speed; objects with multiple legs (tables, chairs) have a +20-foot bonus; wheeled objects have a +40-foot bonus. Objects might have additional modes of movement: a wooden object can float and has a swim speed equal to half its land speed, a rope or similar sinuous object has a climb speed equal to half its land speed, and a sheetlike object can fly (clumsy maneuverability) at half its normal speed.

Construct Traits: A construct has no Constitution score and is never fatigued or exhausted. It is immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and necromancy effects, and to any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, ability drain or energy drain, and cannot be raised or resurrected. It cannot heal damage on its own, though it can often be repaired. It has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision, and it does not eat, sleep or breathe. An animated object is mindless — it has no Intelligence score and cannot be reasoned with, only commanded by the animator.

Combat: Animated objects fight only as directed by the animator. They follow orders without question and to the best of their abilities. Since they do not need to breathe and never tire, they can be extremely capable minions. An animated object can have one or more of the special abilities above, depending on its form.

lore.summary: A demon lord's hunting hound, if a hound were an iron spider with a body the size of an ox and legs that span a hall. It is built for one purpose and given one name — a thief, a runaway slave, a stolen ring — and from the moment it is loosed it knows precisely where that thing stands, on any world, and walks toward it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — an ox's bulk carried high on four legs longer than a man is tall.
Durability: Appalling. Plated all over in horn and metal, and what you do manage to open closes again while you watch.
Defenses: A made thing of another world: nothing to poison, nothing to frighten, nothing to charm, no breath to stop and no blood to spill. It does not tire and it does not slow.
Speed: Faster than a thing that size has any right to be. It runs down a horse over open ground and keeps the pace all day.
Might: Four sweeping claws, and jaws that take a grown man up whole and carry him off. Worse are the eyes: fire, frost, the lightning, and a stare that leaves a man standing as stone forever.
Mind: None. It cannot be reasoned with, tricked, bribed or insulted, because there is nobody inside to hear it.
Disposition: It wants one thing only. Stand between it and that thing and it will remove you without malice; step aside and it may well walk past you as though you were a post.
Bane: Its errand is its leash. It has one quarry and will not be turned aside — so if you are not the quarry, get out of the road. If you are, run for somewhere it cannot follow, or take the errand back from the one who set it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes at a run, rakes with four claws and looses a ray from one eye each moment — flame, then frost, then lightning, then the stone-stare — cycling through them as each comes ready, striking with claws all the while. When it has what it came for it bites, holds the prize fast in its jaws, and simply leaves the field. It has no tactic beyond this and has never needed one.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Learn who it wants before you draw. If it is not you, you are only furniture standing in its road.
• Fire, frost, lightning, stone — it works through them in turn. Count the order and you know what is coming.
• Cut it and watch the cut close over. You will not outlast it. Break it, or leave.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I have never got a word out of one and I have stopped trying. There is no mind behind those eyes, only the errand. The conversation you actually want is with whoever named the quarry, and that means treating with a prince of the Abyss — its own kind of dying. If it has not come for you, stand aside and hold your tongue.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Construct (Extraplanar)
Initiative: +3
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares)
Armor Class: 21 (–2 size, +3 Dex, +10 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+25
Attack: Claw +15 melee (2d6+10) and eye ray +8 ranged touch
Full Attack: 4 claws +15 melee (2d6+10) and bite +10 melee (1d8+5) and eye ray +8 ranged touch
Space/Reach: 15 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Eye rays, find target, improved grab
Special Qualities: Construct traits, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 5, low-light vision
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +6, Will +3
Abilities: Str 31, Dex 17, Con —, Int —, Wis 11, Cha 1
Skills: —
Feats: —
Environment: A chaotic evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 11
Alignment: Always chaotic evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 11–15 levels of construct (Huge); 16–30 levels of construct (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Eye Rays (Su): A retriever's eyes can produce four different magical rays with a range of 100 feet. Each round, it can fire one ray as a free action. A particular ray is usable only once every 4 rounds. A retriever can fire an eye ray in the same round that it makes physical attacks. The save DC for all rays is 18, and is Dexterity-based. The four eye effects are: Fire — deals 12d6 points of fire damage to the target (Reflex half); Cold — deals 12d6 points of cold damage (Reflex half); Electricity — deals 12d6 points of electricity damage (Reflex half); Petrification — the target must succeed on a Fortitude save or turn to stone permanently.

Find Target (Sp): When ordered to find an item or a creature, a retriever does so unerringly, as though guided by discern location. The being giving the order must have seen (or must have an item belonging to) the creature to be found, or must have touched the object to be located. This ability is the equivalent of an 8th-level spell.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a retriever must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and grips the opponent fast in its mouth. This is the method by which it usually “retrieves” things.

Construct Traits: A construct has no Constitution score and is never fatigued or exhausted. It is immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and necromancy effects, and to any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, ability drain or energy drain, and cannot be raised or resurrected. It cannot heal damage on its own, though it can often be repaired. It has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision, and it does not eat, sleep or breathe. A retriever is mindless — it has no Intelligence score, obeys only the demon lord who built it, and cannot be bargained with, frightened or talked down.

Fast Healing 5 (Ex): A retriever repairs itself as it moves, mending 5 points of damage each round so long as it is not yet destroyed. Fast healing does not restore damage dealt by effects that a construct cannot repair, and it does not allow the retriever to regrow or reattach lost parts.

Combat: Retrievers attack with four claws, but their eye rays are far more deadly. A retriever has a body the size of an ox, with legs spanning more than 14 feet, and weighs about 6,500 pounds. It specializes in recovering lost or desired objects, runaway slaves, and enemies, and bringing them back to its master.

lore.summary: A black horse out of an evil plane, mane and tail streaming fire, hooves that leave the grass burning behind them. It is no beast: it is a fiend that has chosen the shape of a mount, and it carries only riders it judges worthy of the honour. Met on a night road, in a stink of hot sulphur, at the gallop.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — the frame and weight of a light warhorse, and it bears a rider as readily.
Durability: Hardy and thickly muscled. It takes far more punishment than any horse of this world, and shows no sign of feeling it.
Defenses: Its own smoke is its armour: past a few paces you are swinging at a shadow in a cloud, while the smoke troubles its sight not at all. Beyond that it steps sideways into the ether or out into the astral whenever it pleases, and is simply gone.
Speed: Tireless at the gallop, and swifter still on the wing. No wall, no river and no plane of existence will hold it.
Might: Burning hooves that set alight whatever they strike, and a hard bite besides. Its blows carry a wickedness of their own, and cut through guards that would turn honest steel.
Mind: Clever as a man and a great deal colder. It follows what is said around it, weighs the speaker, and remembers.
Disposition: Evil without any hurry about it. It serves willingly, for reasons of its own, and it loathes being straddled by anyone it has not consented to carry.
Bane: Close with it. At a distance its smoke blinds you and screens it wholly from a bowman, but at arm's length the cloud thins and you can see what you are hitting. It wears no charmed hide — plain good steel bites it as it would any living horse.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It charges, rears and hammers down with burning hooves, biting as it comes, and snorts a cone of hot sulphurous smoke that leaves men coughing, half-blinded and wild in their aim for a good while after. It fights happily with a rider on its back. When the odds turn against it, it steps clean out of the world and returns at a moment of its own choosing — generally the worst one available to you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it close. Far off you are swinging at smoke; at the length of your arm the cloud thins.
• Everything those hooves touch catches light. Take the fight out of the barn before it takes the barn.
• It leaves the world when it is losing and comes back when you are asleep. Finish it or move camp.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I spoke with one on a bridge, once, and it heard me out. It follows speech and it has its own pride, though I have never heard one answer in words — it bargains by standing still, or by not standing still. Offer it what its rider cannot: a better master, or a road home. Then keep watching the hooves.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), fly 90 ft. (good)
Armor Class: 24 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +13 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 22
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+14
Attack: Hoof +9 melee (1d8+4 plus 1d4 fire)
Full Attack: 2 hooves +9 melee (1d8+4 plus 1d4 fire) and bite +4 melee (1d8+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Flaming hooves, smoke
Special Qualities: Astral projection, darkvision 60 ft., etherealness
Saves: Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +6
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 13, Wis 13, Cha 12
Skills: Concentration +12, Diplomacy +3, Intimidate +10, Knowledge (the planes) +10, Listen +12, Move Silently +11, Search +10, Sense Motive +10, Spot +12, Survival +10 (+12 on other planes and following tracks)
Feats: Alertness, Improved Initiative, Run
Environment: An evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 7–10 levels of outsider (Large); 11–18 levels of outsider (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Flaming Hooves (Su): A blow from a nightmare's hooves sets combustible materials alight. Each hoof deals an extra 1d4 points of fire damage.

Smoke (Su): During the excitement of battle, a nightmare snorts and neighs with rage. This snorting fills a 15-foot cone with a hot, sulfurous smoke that chokes and blinds opponents. Anyone in the cone must succeed on a DC 16 Fortitude save or take a –2 penalty on all attack and damage rolls until 1d6 minutes after leaving the cone. The cone lasts 1 round, and the nightmare uses it once as a free action during its turn each round. The save DC is Constitution-based. Because of the smoke it gives off, a nightmare has concealment against creatures 5 feet away and total concealment against creatures 10 feet or farther away. The smoke does not obscure the nightmare's own vision at all.

Astral Projection and Etherealness (Su): These abilities function just like the spells of the same names (caster level 20th); a nightmare can use either at will. It steps out of the world when pressed and returns where it pleases.

Evil-Aligned Weapons: A nightmare's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Carrying a Rider: A nightmare can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also fight unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. A nightmare is about the size of a light war horse. Carrying capacity: a light load is up to 300 pounds; a medium load 301–600 pounds; and a heavy load 601–900 pounds.

Cauchemar: The greatest of the breed, a cauchemar is a Huge outsider with Challenge Rating 11, AC 26 (touch 10), 2 hooves +23 melee (2d6+10 plus 1d4 fire) and a bite +18 melee (2d6+5), Str 31, Dex 14, Con 24, Int 16, Wis 12, Cha 12, and the same flaming hooves, smoke, astral projection and etherealness. It is found on neutral evil planes.

lore.summary: The tiger-faced fiend that lives as a lord. Born out of the warm marshes, it walks into a city wearing a borrowed human face, buys land, gives feasts, judges disputes — and reads the mind of every guest at its table. Look at its true shape and you will see a tiger's head, and hands set on backwards, the palms turned the wrong way.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no taller and no heavier than the man whose place it has quietly taken.
Durability: Sturdy, but nothing extraordinary. If you can wound it at all, it dies much as a mortal thing does.
Defenses: Here is the whole trouble. Common weapons slide off it as though it were water, and sorcery withers before it lands. It wears another's face at will; no unbinding will strip the shape, only true sight shows the tiger beneath, and death alone brings the real face back.
Speed: Quick on its feet, and quicker still to be elsewhere. It does not remain in a fight it did not arrange.
Might: Claws and a tiger's bite, which it holds beneath its dignity to use. Its true armoury is sorcery — charms, whispered suggestions, illusions to split a party, bolts of raw force, unseen mail, invisibility, and the swiftness to work them all at once.
Mind: Brilliant, patient, urbane, and reading you the entire time. It knows what you fear before you have finished naming it to yourself.
Disposition: Lawful and utterly wicked. It keeps its word to the letter, and it drafts the letter with great care.
Bane: A blessed crossbow bolt. Nothing else I ever carried would bite — the point must be piercing and hallowed both at once, or it is no better than a thrown cup. Bless the bolts before you knock at the door.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It thinks open battle ignoble and avoids it. It reads your thoughts, wears a face you trust, and opens with a charm or a suggestion murmured in a friend's voice, or an illusion to scatter your fellows down separate corridors. Pressed, it hastens itself, raises unseen mail, and works from behind invisibility. Losing, it becomes a servant, a guardsman, your own captain — and walks out through the door past you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bless the bolts. A hallowed piercing shot is the only thing I have seen so much as mark one.
• It hears your thoughts across the table. Rehearse a dull thought and think it very hard.
• The hands are on backwards. Watch how a lord takes his cup — in a crowded hall it is the only tell.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk, by all means — it dearly loves to talk, and it will host you handsomely while you do. I dined a whole season with one that went by the name of a marquis, and left with what I came for. But it hears your thoughts across the board, so carry in your head only what you would say aloud. It keeps every promise it makes. Each one cost me.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Native)
Initiative: +2
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 21 (+2 Dex, +9 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+8
Attack: Claw +8 melee (1d4+1)
Full Attack: 2 claws +8 melee (1d4+1) and bite +3 melee (1d6)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Detect thoughts, spells
Special Qualities: Change shape, damage reduction 15/good and piercing, darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 27
Saves: Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +6
Abilities: Str 12, Dex 14, Con 16, Int 13, Wis 13, Cha 17
Skills: Bluff +17*, Concentration +13, Diplomacy +7, Disguise +17 (+19 acting)*, Intimidate +5, Listen +13, Move Silently +13, Perform (oratory) +13, Sense Motive +11, Spellcraft +11, Spot +11
Feats: Alertness, Combat Casting, Dodge
Environment: Warm marshes
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 10
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: Standard coins; double goods; standard items
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Detect Thoughts (Su): A rakshasa can continuously use detect thoughts as the spell (caster level 18th; Will DC 15 negates). It can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spells: A rakshasa casts spells as a 7th-level sorcerer. Typical Sorcerer Spells Known (6/7/7/5 per day; save DC 13 + spell level): 0 — detect magic, light, mage hand, message, read magic, resistance, touch of fatigue; 1st — charm person, mage armor, magic missile, shield, silent image; 2nd — bear's endurance, invisibility, acid arrow; 3rd — haste, suggestion.

Change Shape (Su): A rakshasa can assume any humanoid form, or revert to its own form, as a standard action. In humanoid form, a rakshasa loses its claw and bite attacks (although it often equips itself with weapons and armor instead). A rakshasa remains in one form until it chooses to assume a new one. A change in form cannot be dispelled, but the rakshasa reverts to its natural form when killed. A true seeing spell reveals its natural form.

Damage Reduction and Spell Resistance: A rakshasa has damage reduction 15/good and piercing — a blessed piercing weapon, the classic being a crossbow bolt blessed by a cleric, cuts through where ordinary steel does not — and spell resistance 27, high enough that most spellcasters who meet one simply fail to touch it.

Skills: A rakshasa has a +4 racial bonus on Bluff and Disguise checks. *When using change shape, a rakshasa gains an additional +10 circumstance bonus on Disguise checks. If reading an opponent's mind, its circumstance bonus on Bluff and Disguise checks increases by a further +4.

Combat and Appearance: In close combat, which a rakshasa disdains as ignoble, it employs its sharp claws and powerful bite; whenever possible it uses its other abilities to make such encounters unnecessary. A closer look at a rakshasa reveals that the palms of its hands are where the backs of the hands would be on a human. A rakshasa is about the same height and weight as a human, and rakshasas speak Common, Infernal, and Undercommon.

lore.summary: Half goblin, half wolf, and wholly a fiend of the orderly hells. A barghest comes up out of an evil plane to walk among goblin camps in a borrowed shape — a lean wolf, a squat chieftain — and it eats not merely flesh but the life inside it. Every such meal swells it. Whelps pass for wolves; the old ones go bluish, then blue, with eyes that kindle orange when they are pleased.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no bigger than a large wolf, and lighter than you would credit for the strength in it.
Durability: Stouter than the wolf it apes, but no marvel of endurance; a determined line puts it down.
Defenses: Its hide turns honest steel. Enchanted arms bite it plainly, and its own jaws count as enchanted for the same purpose — do not think your warded skin will keep it out.
Speed: Walks at a man's pace and no faster, yet it flickers in and out of the world, floats where there is no floor, and steps through a door that is not there. It is never where you swung.
Might: Jaws and claws in every shape it wears, and a wolf's weight behind them — but it has no stomach for a straight fight and knows it.
Mind: Clever as a courtier and far better at lying. It has the goblin tongue, the worg's growl, and the speech of devils, and it uses all three.
Disposition: Lawful and evil in even measure: it keeps every bargain it strikes and means every cruelty written into one.
Bane: Enchanted steel, silvered or no — plain iron slides off, a charmed blade goes in. Beyond that, its own cowardice: it fights from ambush or not at all, and pressed in the open it will bargain or bolt.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It never opens with its teeth. First comes a weight of despair laid over your whole company, or a charm dropped on whoever is holding the line, so that friend turns to the fiend's side; then it works round the flanks, keeping well clear of your strongest arm. It fades and reappears, floats above a shield wall, and vanishes across the room when the fight turns. When a man of yours falls, it will stop fighting altogether to crouch and feed — and what it feeds upon cannot be called back by any priest you can afford.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Blessed or enchanted steel, or you are only combing its fur.
• It will bargain, and it will keep the bargain. Read every word twice before you shake on it.
• Do not leave your dead on the field. What it eats, no priest brings back.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Words work here, which is the trouble. I have bargained with three, in Goblin and in the devils' speech, and got true passage from every one — and every one had already sold me to someone else. Talk, but talk with your dead carried and your terms narrow.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar, Lawful, Shapechanger)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (+2 Dex, +6 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+9
Attack: Bite +9 melee (1d6+3)
Full Attack: Bite +9 melee (1d6+3) and 2 claws +4 melee (1d4+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities, feed
Special Qualities: Change shape, damage reduction 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft., scent
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +7
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 15, Con 13, Int 14, Wis 14, Cha 14
Skills: Bluff +11, Diplomacy +6, Disguise +2 (+4 acting), Hide +11*, Intimidate +13, Jump +12, Listen +11, Move Silently +10, Search +11, Sense Motive +11, Spot +11, Survival +11 (+13 following tracks)
Feats: Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative, Track
Environment: An evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary or pack (3–6)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: Double standard
Advancement: Special — a barghest grows by feeding (see below)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Overcoming Damage Reduction (Ex): A barghest’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Its natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—blink, levitate, misdirection (DC 14), rage (DC 15); 1/day—charm monster (DC 16), crushing despair (DC 16), dimension door. Caster level equals the barghest’s level (6th for the typical barghest). The save DCs are Charisma-based. Barghests open a fight with crushing despair and charm monster to keep opponents off balance, and try to stay away from the enemy’s main strength.

Feed (Su): When a barghest slays a humanoid opponent, it can feed on the corpse, devouring both flesh and life force, as a full-round action. Feeding destroys the victim’s body and prevents any form of raising or resurrection that requires part of the corpse. There is a 50% chance that a wish, miracle, or true resurrection spell can restore a devoured victim to life. Check once for each destroyed creature. If the check fails, the creature cannot be brought back to life by mortal magic. A barghest advances in power by consuming corpses in this fashion: for every three suitable corpses it devours, it grows one step stronger, and its Strength, Constitution, and natural armor each increase by +1. Its attack bonus and saves improve as normal for an outsider of its new standing, and it gains skill points, feats, and ability score improvements normally. A barghest only advances by consuming the corpses of creatures whose levels are equal to or greater than its own current total.

Change Shape (Su): A barghest can assume the shape of a goblin or a wolf as a standard action. In goblin form, a barghest cannot use its natural weapons but can wield weapons and wear armor. In wolf form, a barghest loses its claw attacks but retains its bite attack.

Pass Without Trace (Ex): A barghest in wolf form can use pass without trace (as the spell) as a free action.

Greater Barghest: A barghest that reaches the ninth step of advancement through feeding immediately becomes a greater barghest upon completion of the act. A greater barghest is a Large outsider of Challenge Rating 5, with Armor Class 20 (touch 11, flat-footed 18), speed 40 ft., base attack/grapple +9/+18, bite +13 melee (1d8+5) and 2 claws +8 melee (1d6+2), 10 ft. reach, damage reduction 10/magic, saves Fort +9, Ref +8, Will +10, and Str 20, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 18, Wis 18, Cha 18. It changes shape into a goblinlike creature of Large size (about 8 feet tall and 400 pounds) or a dire wolf; in goblin form it cannot use its natural weapons but can wield weapons and wear armor, and in dire wolf form it loses its claw attacks but retains its bite. In addition to the spell-like abilities all barghests possess it gains at will—invisibility sphere; 1/day—mass bull’s strength, mass enlarge person, with a save DC of 14 + spell level. Occasionally a greater barghest wields a magic two-handed weapon instead of its claws, attacking at +13/+8 and biting at +8 each round. A greater barghest can reach a maximum of eighteen steps of advancement through feeding.

Skills: *A barghest in wolf form gains a +4 circumstance bonus on Hide checks. Barghests speak Goblin, Worg, and Infernal.

lore.summary: A black hound out of an evil plane, lean as famine, that runs on air as readily as on earth. Yeth hounds hunt only after dark, in pairs or in packs, coursing above the hedgerows on a moonless night and giving voice as they come. Every farm on a moor road has a name for that sound. They are met where some fiend or wicked lord keeps kennels — and never, ever by daylight.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — stands to a grown man's waist at the shoulder and weighs about what a small pony does.
Durability: Slight for all its ferocity. One good stroke that lands ends the hound.
Defenses: Its flesh shrugs off honest steel; silver parts it like wet cloth. Nothing else it carries will save it.
Speed: Fast on the ground and faster in the air, and it flies well — it can quit the air or take to it as swiftly as you might blink, so it will not stay pinned.
Might: One dreadful bite, and with the same lunge it sweeps your legs from under you. A pack tumbles a man and finishes the work on the ground.
Mind: Dull-witted, as fiends go. It understands the devils' tongue well enough to take an order, but it has no voice to answer in any speech at all.
Disposition: Always evil and always nocturnal. It hunts for meat, and it hunts as much for the terror it raises on the way.
Bane: Silver, before anything else in your pack. And the sun — mark the wording, for men get this wrong: the light does not burn it or weaken it. It simply fears the sun, hunts only at night, and will never venture out in daylight even if its life depends upon it. Hold out till dawn and you have won without a blow.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It gives voice first, always — a bay that carries over a whole valley and sends everything living, save other fiends, running blind with panic. Then the pack comes out of the dark air, low and quick, biting to knock a man off his feet and worrying him where he lies while the rest circle back overhead. They break off before dawn without fail, whatever the state of the fight, and they take their wounded with them.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver. If you have none, you have brought nothing.
• The bay only takes you once a night — stand the first, and after that it is only noise.
• Never break off and run for it. Keep your line together till the sky greys and they leave of their own accord.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, though I tried it twice. I have the devils' speech and the hounds plainly understand it — the ears turn, the head cocks — but they have no voice to answer with and no wish for one. The conversation you want is with whoever keeps the kennel. Talk to the master; kill the dogs.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar, Evil)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), fly 60 ft. (good)
Armor Class: 20 (+2 Dex, +8 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+6
Attack: Bite +6 melee (1d8+4)
Full Attack: Bite +6 melee (1d8+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Bay, trip
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/silver, darkvision 60 ft., flight, scent
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 15, Con 15, Int 6, Wis 14, Cha 10
Skills: Listen +11, Spot +11, Search +7, Survival +11 (+13 following tracks)*
Feats: Improved Initiative, Track
Environment: An evil-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pack (6–11)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 4–6 levels (Medium); 7–9 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Bay (Su): When a yeth hound howls or barks, all creatures except other evil outsiders within a 300-foot spread must succeed on a DC 11 Will save or become panicked for 2d4 rounds. This is a sonic mind-affecting fear effect. Whether or not the save is successful, an affected creature is immune to the same hound’s bay for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Trip (Ex): A yeth hound that hits with its bite attack can attempt to trip the opponent (+3 check modifier) as a free action without making a touch attack or provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react to trip the yeth hound.

Flight (Su): A yeth hound can cease or resume flight as a free action.

Fear of the Sun: The SRD gives yeth hounds no formal sunlight powerlessness ability; the restriction is stated in the creature’s combat text, in these words: “Yeth hounds hunt only at night. They fear the sun and never venture out in daylight, even if their lives depend on it.”

Overcoming Damage Reduction (Ex): A yeth hound’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. The hound itself is reduced by silver: damage reduction 10/silver.

Skills: *A yeth hound has a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent. A yeth hound stands 5 feet tall at the shoulder and weighs about 400 pounds. Yeth hounds cannot speak, but understand Infernal.

lore.summary: Red-hided, four-armed, and patient beyond a soldier's patience, the xill wait in the ether beside our roads and rooms, watching through the veil until something soft-bodied wanders past. They step through, take a living host, and step back. They come for bodies rather than for coin, and a raiding gang works with the order and silence of drilled troops.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a little shorter than a man and much lighter, with four arms off a narrow trunk.
Durability: About as hard to fell as a good soldier. Toughness is not what keeps it alive.
Defenses: No hide worth the name — plain steel bites it cleanly — but a great deal of your spellwork simply slides off it unfelt, and while it is fading back toward the ether your blows begin to pass through empty air.
Speed: Swift afoot and a superb tumbler. It arrives out of nothing in an eyeblink, but going home is slow: it fades for a long, helpless while, and cannot stir a limb the whole time.
Might: Four limbs, all working — a blade in each of two hands with two claws left free to seize you, or all four sets of claws, or two bows drawn at once. The claws are for holding. The bite is the killing part, and it draws no blood.
Mind: Ordinary wits, drilled discipline, the devils' tongue. Some of them are cultured, and will speak with you rather than at you.
Disposition: Lawful evil and quite cold about it. It does not hate you; it wants a warm place to lay eggs.
Bane: It needs no silver, no blessing, no enchantment to hurt — honest steel does the whole job; only your spells are apt to fail. And catch it in the act of fading home: for those long moments it cannot move at all, and it is yours for the taking.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: A gang lies out in the ether and lets you walk past, then comes through all at once from three sides. One or two press the strongest of you and then go on the defensive, tumbling clear, while the others work the flanks. They grapple with the free claws — and the moment they have you held, the bite comes, and it does no hurt at all, which is the horror of it: the venom locks a body rigid for hours. Then they carry the stiff, waking body off through the veil, lay eggs in it, and leave. The young come out in a season, from the inside.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The bite that does not hurt is the one to fear. Break the grapple before the jaws come.
• If a friend went stiff and came back whole, he did not come back whole. Find a priest who can purge plague, or a very steady hand with a knife, and do it that week.
• When one starts to blur and go thin, that is not escape — that is a held target. Put everything into it.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have spoken with one, in the devils' tongue, across a campfire it had no need to sit at. It was courteous, curious, and perfectly honest that it meant to use one of us later. They keep terms while terms serve them. Never sleep in the same country as an agreement with a xill.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar)
Initiative: +7
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 20 (+3 Dex, +7 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+7
Attack: Short sword +7 melee (1d6+2/19–20) or claw +7 melee (1d4+2) or longbow +8 ranged (1d8/×3)
Full Attack: 2 short swords +5 melee (1d6+2/19–20, 1d6+1/19–20) and 2 claws +5 melee (1d4+1); or 4 claws +5 melee (1d4+2, 1d4+1); or 2 longbows +4 ranged (1d8/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Implant, improved grab, paralysis
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., planewalk, spell resistance 21
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +5
Abilities: Str 15, Dex 16, Con 15, Int 12, Wis 12, Cha 11
Skills: Balance +13, Climb +10, Diplomacy +2, Escape Artist +11, Intimidate +8, Listen +9, Move Silently +11, Sense Motive +8, Spot +9, Tumble +11, Use Rope +3 (+5 with bindings)
Feats: Improved Initiative, Multiattack (bonus), Multiweapon Fighting
Environment: Ethereal Plane
Organization: Solitary or gang (2–5)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 6–8 levels (Medium); 9–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Planewalk (Su): These planar travelers like to slip between the folds of space to attack enemies as though from thin air. They can cross from the Ethereal Plane with a move action but take 2 rounds to cross back, during which time they are immobile. As a xill fades away, it becomes harder to hit: opponents have a 20% miss chance in the first round and a 50% miss chance in the second. A xill can planewalk with a willing or helpless creature.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a xill must hit with one or more claw attacks. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. It receives a +2 bonus on the grapple check for each claw that hits. If it wins the grapple check and maintains the hold in the next round, it automatically bites the foe at that time. The bite deals no damage but injects a paralyzing venom.

Paralysis (Ex): Those bitten by a xill must succeed on a DC 14 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 1d4 hours. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Implant (Ex): As a standard action, a xill can lay eggs inside a paralyzed creature. The young emerge about 90 days later, literally devouring the host from inside. A remove disease spell rids a victim of the egg, as does a DC 25 Heal check. If the check fails, the healer can try again, but each attempt (successful or not) deals 1d4 points of damage to the patient.

Tactics: Xills are dangerous opponents, attacking with all four limbs. More civilized ones use weapons, usually fighting with two at a time so as to leave two claws free for grab attacks. Xills typically lie in wait on the Ethereal Plane for suitable prey to happen by, then ambush it using their planewalk ability. They make full use of their Tumble skill in combat: usually, one or two distract physically powerful enemies by attacking, then assume a defensive stance while their fellows maneuver to advantage. A xill stands 4 to 5 feet tall and weighs about 100 pounds. Xills speak Infernal.

lore.summary: A quilled hound-thing bred where chaos and evil hold the ground, longer than a horse and heavier, with a ruff of black spines along its neck. Howlers run in gangs and packs, climb sheer walls like cats, and are met most often with a demon on the back of one — they are broken to the saddle, though it takes a hard trainer and a friendly beast to do it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer than a warhorse and a good deal heavier, yet built and moving like a hound.
Durability: Solidly made and stubborn to put down, for all that it is a coward.
Defenses: None to speak of. No hide that turns a blade, no ward against spellcraft. It lives on speed and on numbers alone.
Speed: Very fast — faster than a good horse, and it climbs a wall or a ceiling as readily as it runs. It charges, races clear, and charges again before you have set your feet.
Might: A terrible bite for its size, and as it bites it thrashes the quills of its neck into whatever is nearest.
Mind: Reckoned dim, and reckoned wrong — it is cleverer than it looks. It understands the demons' tongue, but it speaks nothing at all: only howling, which no man and no spell has yet unravelled.
Disposition: Chaotic, cruel and cowardly together. It will not face you alone, and it very seldom comes alone.
Bane: Plain steel serves — it needs no silver and no blessing — and its nerve is the real weakness: break the pack or kill the rider and the rest scatter. Mind the quills, which snap off in the wound; every one left in you spoils your aim, your footing and your luck until it is cut out, and cutting it out costs blood.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They come in a gang, never singly if it can be helped: a charge out of the dark, a bite and a thrashing of spines as they pass, then away and round for another run before you can close. They keep to the walls and the ceilings of a cave and drop on the rearmost. As for the howling — hunters get this backwards. It does the beast no good whatever in the melee. It is a slow poison: a full hour in earshot of it, and again for every hour after, wears the wits and the will out of a man. It is the price of camping within earshot, not the opening of a fight.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Quills first, wounds second. Cut them out that night or you will fight the next day half-drunk.
• Never camp inside earshot. It is the hours, not the moment, that hollow you out.
• Kill the rider and the mounts lose heart. Kill one mount and the pack often loses heart too.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never with the beast. It has wit enough to understand a demon's order, and I have tried Abyssal on one from a ledge, but nothing in that howling answers to a tongue — no charm of mine has ever made sense of it. If there is a rider, the rider is your conversation. Otherwise, bows.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Chaotic, Evil, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +7
Speed: 60 ft. (12 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (–1 size, +3 Dex, +5 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+15
Attack: Bite +10 melee (2d8+5)
Full Attack: Bite +10 melee (2d8+5) and 1d4 quills +5 melee (1d6+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Quills, howl
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +8, Will +7
Abilities: Str 21, Dex 17, Con 15, Int 6, Wis 14, Cha 8
Skills: Climb +14, Hide +8, Listen +13, Move Silently +12, Search +7, Spot +13, Survival +2 (+4 following tracks)
Feats: Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative
Environment: A chaotic-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary, gang (2–4), or pack (6–10)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always chaotic evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 7–9 levels (Large); 11–18 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Quills (Ex): A howler’s neck bristles with long quills. While biting, the creature thrashes about, striking with 1d4 of them. An opponent hit by a howler’s quill attack must succeed on a DC 16 Reflex save or have the quill break off in his or her flesh. Lodged quills impose a –1 penalty on attacks, saves, and checks per quill. The save DC is Dexterity-based. A quill can be removed safely with a DC 20 Heal check; otherwise, removing a quill deals an extra 1d6 points of damage.

Howl (Ex): All beings other than outsiders that hear the creature’s howling for an hour or longer are subject to its effect, though it does not help the howler in combat. Anyone within hearing range of a howler for a full hour must succeed on a DC 12 Will save or take 1 point of Wisdom damage. The save DC is Charisma-based. The save must be repeated for each hour of exposure. This is a sonic mind-affecting effect.

Overcoming Damage Reduction (Ex): A howler’s natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Howlers attack in groups, for they are cowardly and cruel; they prefer to charge into combat, race out, and then charge in again.

Training a Howler: Although intelligent, a howler requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. To be trained, a howler must have a friendly attitude toward the trainer (this can be achieved through a successful Diplomacy check). Training a friendly howler requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a howler requires an exotic saddle. A howler can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a howler is up to 460 pounds; a medium load, 461–920 pounds; and a heavy load, 921–1,380 pounds. A howler can drag 6,900 pounds. A howler is about 8 feet long and weighs about 2,000 pounds. Although surprisingly intelligent, howlers do not speak—they only howl; if there is a language within the howls, even spells cannot decipher it. Howlers understand Abyssal.

lore.summary: A ball of steady white light, no larger than a hooded lantern, that drifts and darts on a thought and never once sets down. It is the least of Heaven's servants and by far the gladdest: a scout, a runner of errands, a lamp for travellers gone astray. Only its death puts the glow out, though it can dim itself to hide.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — a hovering sphere of light about the size of a helm, with no body to speak of.
Durability: Slight. There is little there to break, and what there is breaks quickly.
Defenses: Honest steel washes off it, and so does most enchanted steel; it takes a warded blade of wicked make to truly bite. Lightning cannot touch it, nor can any stare that turns men to stone, and venom scarcely troubles it.
Speed: Flies swiftly and turns on the instant, perfect in the air; it can also step from one place to another as easily as you would blink.
Might: It has no hands and no strength at all. It fights with lances of light that pierce hide, ward and warding alike — no toughness of skin turns those aside.
Mind: Simple and cheerful; the plainest wit in all the heavenly ranks, and the most willing. It will speak whatever tongue you speak, without being asked.
Disposition: Lawful and good without exception, and it can neither lie to you nor be bought. It scouts, carries word, blesses tired arms, and lights the road for the lost.
Bane: What its enemies carry: a fiend's blade, wicked and enchanted both. Otherwise its frailty is the whole of it — and it will not abandon a charge, so the cruel bait it to its death by threatening whoever it guards.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It keeps its distance and hovers just near enough to bring you inside the righteous dread that hangs about an angered archon, then it burns you with paired rays of light — and no armour, hide or warding turns those. It picks one foe and worries at that one until it drops, then chooses the next. It will not close, and it will not run while there is anyone behind it to guard.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It cannot lie. Ask plainly and you get the truth, plainly.
• Its light burns through any hide. Do not stand behind cover you trust and gloat.
• Feed it nothing, pay it nothing. Point it at something wicked instead — that is its wage.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Talk to every one you meet. They are glad of the company and glad of the work, and they know every road on the plane you are standing on. One lit my camp through a night of ghouls in the Grey Fen and asked nothing but that I bury what I killed. I did.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor power, and no enemy of mine

Those who fail take a -2 penalty on attacks, AC and saves for 24 hours or until they successfully hit the archon that generated the aura. A creature that has resisted or broken the effect cannot be affected again by the same archon's aura for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based and includes a +2 racial bonus. lore.summary: A well-made man's body beneath a hound's head, walking upright, sometimes mailed and sometimes bare, and able to fold itself down into any dog or wolf that ever ran. Soldiers of the lawful heavens: they patrol the marches of good country, follow evil by its stink, and keep watch over roads no mortal lord has ever thought to pay for.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a broad, deep-chested man in build, with the head of a great hound.
Durability: Hard-wearing as a veteran soldier, and it heals faster than we do.
Defenses: Only a wicked weapon leaves a lasting wound; ordinary arms and honest blades slide off. Lightning does nothing, stone-gazes do nothing, poison barely troubles it, and hostile magic often simply fails to find it.
Speed: Runs down a horse over broken ground, and can be gone from the field and standing somewhere else before you have drawn breath.
Might: Strong-armed. It bites, it slams, and when it takes a greatsword to a thing the sword strikes as something holy and lawful, so no fiend's hide keeps it out.
Mind: Plain-spoken and shrewd rather than learned. It speaks every tongue there is, knows evil by scent, and never once mistook a wolf's track for a warg's.
Disposition: Lawful and good, dutiful, and better company on a long march than most men. It will not lie, will not lie in wait for the innocent, and will not leave a wounded stranger to follow a trail.
Bane: What its enemies carry: black weapons of fiendish make — nothing else scars it. The seam is its honour. It will not strike first, will not break a truce, and will turn from your throat to a child's cry every time.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes at you straight, as a soldier does, because it thinks the crooked way beneath it. The righteous dread about it takes the heart out of anyone who means it harm before the first blow lands. It bites and hammers with a free hand, or takes up a greatsword when the enemy is armoured, and it steps across the field at will to reach whoever most needs killing or most needs shielding. It fights to end the fight, never to prolong it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• In dog shape it can pass anywhere. That grey wolfhound at the crossroads may be judging you.
• It knows evil by smell. If it will not sit at your fire, look hard at whoever else is sitting there.
• Ask it to hunt with you, not for you. Say what the quarry has done. It will decide, and its decision is final.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The best friend this trade ever gave me. Coram walked at my shoulder in wolfhound shape for the whole of one long winter, took the far side of every door, and never once asked what was in it for him. When he was recalled he did not say goodbye — that is not their way — but he left his greatsword leaning by my fire, and I have it still.

sections.body: Formidable — A formidable ally

lore.summary: A winged herald in bright harness, bearing a silver trumpet longer than a man's arm. Trumpet archons proclaim judgements, carry the words of powers who do not travel, and stand as arbiters where mortals cannot agree between themselves. The horn is instrument and sword at once, and its music is the loveliest sound I have heard, and the most dangerous.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall, fair, winged figure, no larger than a big man.
Durability: Very tough indeed; it takes a war's worth of punishment and keeps its feet.
Defenses: Wicked weapons alone leave a mark, and hostile spells fail against it more often than they take hold. Lightning cannot harm it, no gaze turns it to stone, and venom is near enough wasted.
Speed: Swift afoot and swifter on the wing, and it can cross to any place it wishes between one word and the next.
Might: The trumpet becomes a keen greatsword at a thought, and it swings that sword like a captain who has done nothing else for an age. It also prays down the whole armoury of a high priest — smiting, blade-walls, banishings, and healing for its own.
Mind: Learned, courteous and exact. It speaks every tongue, weighs both sides, and remembers what was said word for word.
Disposition: Lawful and good, formal in bearing, and unbribable. It comes to deliver a message or a judgement, not to make friends, but it will hear you out in full.
Bane: What its enemies carry: weapons of true wickedness — nothing else keeps a wound on it. Its own seam is ceremony: it announces itself, it warns before it strikes, and it must finish the errand it was sent with before it will attend to anything else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It would rather not brawl at all. It opens at a distance with prayers — smitings, walls of blades, a word of banishment for anything that does not belong here — and returns to its duty the moment the matter is settled. Press it into a longer fight and it sounds the trumpet: everyone in earshot but its own kind is struck rigid with awe, and then the horn is a sword in its hands and it comes down on you from the air with the dread of Heaven hanging about it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• When it lifts the horn, be somewhere else. Awe holds you still while the sword finds you.
• Never touch the trumpet. Stolen, it is a lump of dead metal, and the owner always comes for it.
• Hear the message out. It was sent to say a thing; nothing else happens until it has said it.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Address it as you would a king's herald and you will be heard fairly. I once stood a hearing before one over a lammasu I had wrongly marked as quarry and very nearly loosed upon, spoke straight, and was let go with a rebuke I still feel. Do not flatter it and do not haggle. State the truth and abide by the finding.

lore.summary: A tall, comely, winged being of some good heaven, sent down to shepherd mortals worth the shepherding. Devas walk our roads in borrowed faces — a pilgrim, a beggar, a quiet soldier in the back of the column — and you learn what you were speaking with only long afterwards. It carries a heavy mace, and a hatred of evil entirely without malice.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — half again the height of a tall man, and heavier than the wings suggest.
Durability: Immensely hardy. Little short of a siege will trouble it.
Defenses: Only weapons of wicked make wound it at all. Acid runs off, cold cannot reach it, no gaze turns it to stone, fire and lightning are shrugged aside, and most spells simply break against it. It is hard to catch off guard and near impossible to flank.
Speed: Faster on foot than a running horse, and faster still in the air, with fine control.
Might: The mace hits like a falling beam; take two of its blows in a breath and you are left standing witless. Beyond that it commands words that scour the wicked, walls of blades, dispelling, and healing enough to raise a dying man off the field.
Mind: Keen and kindly and utterly unfoolable. It hears a lie the moment it is spoken, sees the unseen, and speaks whatever tongue you were raised in.
Disposition: Good, and honourable past our understanding — it will not lie, cheat or steal, whatever the cost. It guards mortals it judges worth guarding, and mostly it does so unseen.
Bane: What its enemies carry: fiendish arms — nothing honest marks it. The seam is its mercy and its truthfulness: it hears every falsehood you tell, but it will also stop to save a man you have wounded, and the wicked have long used that against it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not hang back. It comes into reach gladly and works with the mace, and if it lands twice in one breath the second blow leaves you rooted and gaping. Around it hangs a warding that blunts every wicked stroke and turns aside the lesser spells of evil folk entirely. It scours the field with words of holiness, walls the ground with blades, plucks curses and diseases off its allies, and heals the ones still worth healing. It never fights for sport, and it stops the instant the matter is settled.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not lie to it. Not a small one, not a kind one. It hears every word for what it is.
• It may already be walking with you wearing another face. Behave accordingly.
• Its warding shelters everyone standing close. If one fights beside you, stay near it.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Always talk, and talk straight — it can do nothing else itself. One judged me on a moor after I had put down a couatl that turned out to be no monster at all. It heard my whole miserable account, mended my arm, told me plainly what I owed, and left. I paid it. That page is elsewhere in this book.

Protective Aura (Su): Against attacks made or effects created by evil creatures, this ability provides a +4 deflection bonus to AC and a +4 resistance bonus on saving throws to anyone within 20 feet of the angel.
