Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

lore.summary: Bald, jade-skinned, a head and shoulders above any man, wings the colour of storm-cloud, a greatsword held in both hands: a planetar is a captain of the heavenly hosts and looks the part. They are sent where a war must be won rather than a soul saved, and they see through every disguise, lie and buried snare the moment they set eyes upon it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — towering, broad, and reaching well past a spear's length with that sword.
Durability: Grievous wounds knit shut while you watch. Only wicked weapons and truly evil magic leave anything behind.
Defenses: A warding hangs about it that turns the strokes and spells of evil creatures aside. Acid and cold do nothing, no gaze petrifies it, fire and lightning are shrugged off, venom scarcely troubles it, and most sorcery simply fails against it.
Speed: Ordinary on the ground, splendid in the air, and it can shift itself between worlds at need.
Might: Enormously strong, and the greatsword strikes as a holy thing, so no fiend's hide keeps it out. Behind that stands the prayer-craft of an archpriest: fire from the sky, walls of blades, a word that stuns, the ground itself broken, and the dead called back to answer questions or to live again.
Mind: Brilliant and grave. Every disguise fails before it, every lie is heard as a lie, every hidden pit and tripwire shows plain, and it speaks all tongues.
Disposition: Good and implacable, a soldier by vocation. It takes particular joy in killing fiends. It will not lie, cheat or steal, and it will not be turned from an errand by anything you can offer it.
Bane: What its enemies carry: blades of black make and spells of true wickedness — nothing else keeps a wound on it, for the rest close as fast as you cut. The seam is its office: it is a soldier, it fights the greater evil first, and it will hold to a given word even when breaking it would win the field.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: For all the prayers it commands, a planetar prefers to wade in with the greatsword, and it hunts fiends through a battle by preference. It opens with fire called down or a wall of blades laid across the line, stuns whoever is worst with a single spoken word, then closes. Its warding shelters every good soul near it while blunting the strokes of the wicked. Wounds you deal will close before you have set your feet again, and it does not tire.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cut it all you like; the cuts close. Only wicked steel or a truly evil working leaves a mark.
• It sees every disguise and every buried snare. Do not bother with either.
• If one is on the field, so is a fiend somewhere. Find that, and you have found what it came for.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: You may speak with one, but understand you are addressing a general in the middle of a campaign. Be brief, be truthful, and say what you know that it does not. I gave one the count of the gnolls holding a ford on the Ashen March; it thanked me by name, told me to go home, and I went home.

lore.summary: Once, at the mouth of a ruined temple, I saw a solar, and I have spent the years since failing to write the sentence that holds it. Half again a tall man's height, winged in white fire, its voice arriving in the chest before it reaches the ear. Greatest of the angels, it keeps the good planes and comes down into the world only where the stakes are the world.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — half again a tall man's height and broad with it, yet it moves as though it weighed nothing at all.
Durability: Wounds knit while you watch them. Nothing I have ever carried would have marked it for longer than a breath.
Defenses: Acid, killing cold and the petrifying gaze cannot touch it; lightning and fire barely warm it; spells slide off it like rain off slate. About it hangs a ward of grace that turns wicked work aside from the angel and from everyone standing near.
Speed: Swift afoot, and in the air faster and steadier than any hawk I have watched.
Might: A great blessed sword that it looses from the hand to fight on alone, hewing where it wills; a bow that shapes for each drawing an arrow made to slay the thing aimed at; and the prayers of the highest priest besides, up to the granting of wishes.
Mind: Wiser and better read than any sage I have sat with. It will not lie, nor cheat, nor steal — not from restraint, but because that is simply what it is.
Disposition: It has no interest in you unless you stand between it and some great evil. Then its interest is entire.
Bane: Its enemies carry blades of a make beyond any mortal forge, evil in their grain, and curses of that same black kind; only those stop the knitting of its flesh. No man has such a thing. What a man has instead is this: it will not strike first, and it will hear you out. Do not mistake either for weakness.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights as a general and a swordsman at once. It sees you truly from the first — through darkness, disguise, invisibility and every lie you offer — and it opens at distance, loosing arrows that are made to kill whatever they are pointed at, or throwing up walls of blades across the ground you meant to cross. Then the sword comes off its hand and goes to work by itself while the angel calls down earthquake, smiting light, or a single spoken word that stuns, blinds or simply stops the heart. It heals its own and raises the fallen mid-battle. It does not tire, it does not blunder, and it does not need to press: whatever you cut is closed again before you have set your feet.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It sees through every lie, every disguise, every trick of invisibility. Save your breath and tell it the truth.
• It will not lie to you either. If a solar says a thing is so, write it down and act upon it.
• If one has come down into the world, the trouble is far larger than you are. Ask what it needs. Then go and do that.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: I did not speak first. I could not. It spoke my name and asked what I had killed that year, and why — and I answered plainly, because lying to it is like lying to daylight. It told me that two of my answers had been wrong. It was right about both, and it was kind about neither.

monsters.name: Avoral (Guardinal)
monsters.senses: darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, true seeing

lore.summary: Half a man's shape and half a great bird's: feathered, hollow-boned, taller than most men and lighter than the lad who holds your horse. Each wing carries a small hand at its bend, so nothing is lost when the wings are folded. Avorals are the scouts and couriers of the good planes, and they see farther than anything alive — a rider's eye-colour at bowshot, a moving cart at a morning's ride.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — taller than a man, and light as a bundle of kindling for all that.
Durability: Hardy for something built of air and hollow bone, but it is made for the sky, not the anvil.
Defenses: Honest steel slides off it; silver bites, and so does a blade with evil worked into it. Lightning cannot touch it, nor the petrifying gaze; cold and shrieking noise trouble it little. Spells slip past it more often than they land.
Speed: Quick afoot, and in the air a stooping hawk — fast, and able to turn upon a coin.
Might: Talons that open a man's coat and the man beneath. Grounded, it beats with the wings themselves, and those blows break bones. It calls down lightning, throws darts of pure force, and can root a man where he stands with a word.
Mind: Sharp, curious and fond of talk. It bargains fairly, keeps its half exactly, and never forgets a face.
Disposition: Good-hearted but no crusader; it is a scout before it is a warrior. It will watch you a long while before it greets you.
Bane: Its enemies carry silver, or steel with a wicked grain — either will do, and that is the loosest guard of any celestial I have met. Beyond metal: it is frail for its reach, it can be brought out of the sky, and the terror it sheds comes only once between dawns. Spend that and it must fight on feathers and bone like anything else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It takes the air at once and stays there, because grounded it gives up half its worth. It blurs its outline, opens with lightning or a rain of force-darts, then stoops to rake with the talons and is gone again before the answering swing arrives — it will not hover for you. Against a crowd it looses its terror once, and once only, and reaps whoever runs. Cornered on the ground it fights with the wings themselves, heavier blows than the claws, and it can step out of a closing ring through a door of its own making. It never stops looking at everything at once.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not try to creep up on one. It watched you leave the treeline this morning.
• In the air it uses talons; grounded it clubs you with the wings, and those hit harder. Bringing one down is not the mercy you think.
• Silver, or a wicked blade. Honest steel is a broom handle to it — and if you are fighting one at all, you have already erred twice.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: One shadowed me across two valleys before it came down. It had already counted the arrows in my quiver and read my errand off the way I walked, and it said so, pleasantly. We traded — my road for its news of what waited along it. It kept its half to the letter. They always do.

sections.body:
Guardinal Traits: Guardinals are the celestials of the neutral good planes, and the avoral's own line confirms the family traits: darkvision out to 60 feet and low-light vision; immunity to electricity and petrification; resistance to cold 10 and sonic 10; a +4 racial bonus on saves against poison (Fort +10, rising to +14 against poison); damage reduction 10/evil or silver; and spell resistance 25. Every guardinal can speak with animals and lay on hands. An avoral's natural weapons, as well as any weapon it wields, are treated as good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Avorals speak Celestial, Infernal, and Draconic, but can speak with almost any creature.

Combat: On the ground an avoral lashes out with its wings, each of which carries a small hand at the midpoint that can do nearly anything a human hand can. It prefers to meet foes in the air, where it uses its talons and the full measure of its speed and agility; it cannot make wing attacks while flying. An avoral's bones are strong but hollow, so even the largest weighs no more than 120 pounds.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—aid, blur (self only), command (DC 14), detect magic, dimension door, dispel magic, gust of wind (DC 15), hold person (DC 16), light, magic circle against evil (self only), magic missile, see invisibility; 3/day—lightning bolt (DC 16). Caster level 8th. The save DCs are Charisma-based. Its Empower Spell-Like Ability feat applies to magic missile.

Fear Aura (Su): Once per day an avoral can create an aura of fear in a 20-foot radius. It is otherwise identical with fear cast by an 8th-level caster (Will DC 17 partial). The save DC is Charisma-based.

Lay on Hands (Su): Each day it can heal, by touch, a total amount of damage equal to its own full undamaged vigour. It will spend that on a wounded mortal without being asked twice.

Speak with Animals (Su): This ability works like speak with animals (caster level 8th) but is a free action and does not require sound.

True Seeing (Su): Identical with true seeing (caster level 14th), except that it has personal range and the avoral must concentrate for 1 full round before it takes effect. Thereafter it remains in effect for as long as the avoral keeps concentrating. Nothing you wear, carry, or pretend will survive that stare.

Skills: An avoral's sharp eyes give it a +8 racial bonus on Spot checks. Its visual acuity is virtually unmatched: it can pick out detail on objects up to 10 miles away, and is said to name the color of a creature's eyes at 200 paces.

lore.summary: Lion-headed and lion-maned, walking upright and running on all fours when the running matters. Leonals are the strongest of the guardinals and the least subtle of them: where the avoral watches, the leonal arrives. They keep prides on the good planes and come into the world in answer to great cruelty — and they come at a dead run.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall man's height, and every finger of it muscle under a tawny hide.
Durability: Very hard to put down, and harder to keep down: it mends its own hurts and its pride-mates' with a laying on of hands.
Defenses: Only a blade that is silvered and of wicked make troubles it — both together, not one or the other, which is a thing almost nobody carries. Lightning and the petrifying gaze do nothing; cold and clamour do little. Spells fail against it more often than not, and a ward of grace stands about it, shielding it and any who keep close.
Speed: It outruns a horse, over broken ground, and it is still fresh when you are not.
Might: Claws, and a bite that takes hold and does not let go — and while it holds you the hind legs work. It charges from out of nothing and lands a whole flurry at the end of the charge. Then there is the roar: a holy blast of sound that flings the wicked back, and can strike the worst of them dead where they stand.
Mind: Clever enough, and plain-dealing to a fault. It says what it means, and it speaks with beasts as easily as with men.
Disposition: Warm, hot-tempered, and utterly straight. Cruelty done in front of it is a decision made for it.
Bane: Its enemies must bring silver and wickedness in the same blade, and almost none manage it. The real seam is elsewhere: it will not stoop to a trick, it announces itself, and it cannot fly. Get above it and it has no answer but to wait for you to come down.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It roars first — always first — a cone of holy sound that scatters the wicked, deafens the rest, and kills outright any evil thing too slight to stand it. Then it is on you in one bound, claws working, and if the bite takes hold you are pinned and the hind legs open you up. Its pride fights as a pride: they watch one another's flanks, drive quarry onto waiting claws, and pull a wounded one out of the press to be healed and sent straight back in. It will drop a burst of fire or a wall of unseen force across a gap when it must, but it would always rather close.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It roars before it moves. That is your only warning and your only moment — use both.
• It cannot fly and it will not bluff. Those two facts are worth more to you than any weapon in your pack.
• Talk to it about the beasts. It speaks with them, and it will listen longer to what a hound has told it than to anything you say.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: A pride of them stopped me on a road of white grass and asked, courteously enough, what the blood on my coat had belonged to. I told them. One went to look. They came back, gave me meat and a place at their fire, and pointed me at something a good deal worse than the thing I had killed.

Otherwise it functions as a magic circle against evil effect and a lesser globe of invulnerability, both with a radius of 20 feet, at a caster level equal to the leonal's own level. (The defensive benefits of the circle are not included in the leonal's statistics block.)

Speak with Animals (Su): This ability works like speak with animals (caster level 8th) but is a free action and does not require sound.

Skills: Leonals have a +4 racial bonus on Balance, Hide, and Move Silently checks. A thing that runs 60 feet a round, jumps at +35, and hides at +22 is on you before the word of warning is finished.

lore.summary: Elf-like at a glance and nothing like an elf at all: broad-shouldered, wild-eyed, hair the colour of the weather that day. A bralani is a piece of the wind that has decided to carry a scimitar. It arrives and departs as a whirl of dust or snow, laughs easily, fights the same way, and holds nothing at all against you by morning.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — the build of a stocky elf, on the days it troubles to keep a build at all.
Durability: Hardy, but unarmoured. It stays whole by not being where the blow lands.
Defenses: Cold iron bites it, and so does a blade of wicked make; either will serve, which is a low door for a celestial. Lightning cannot touch it, nor the petrifying gaze, and cold and fire are half-spent on it. It blurs its edges and throws false copies of itself into the air — but of all its kin, spells find it the easiest.
Speed: Quick on its feet; in the wind-shape it flies perfectly, turning as the air turns.
Might: A scimitar and a great bow, both blessed against wickedness, and it is stronger in the arm than its frame suggests. In the wind-shape it looses a scouring blast down a line, and at any time it calls lightning, gusts, and a wall of wind that swallows arrows.
Mind: Bright, changeable, chaotic to the bone. Good-hearted, and not one whit more governable for it.
Disposition: It means well and will not be told how. Quick to laughter, quick to a fight, and it forgets the fight far faster than you will.
Bane: Its enemies carry cold iron, or steel with evil worked into it; either alone is enough. Better still, it must choose: as a wind it flies and scours but cannot lift a blade, and in its own shape it fights and conjures but cannot leave the ground. Catch it in the wrong shape and it must spend a moment changing.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at distance — lightning, or arrows off a blessed bow — with its outline blurred and false copies of itself drifting about it, so half your shots go into nothing. It throws up a wall of wind to eat your archery, then takes the whirlwind shape to close, scouring a line through your rank as it comes. Where it wants a body it drops back into its own shape and cuts with the scimitar, fast and unpredictable, and it will patch its own wounds once or twice mid-fight. It fights as weather fights: from every side, and never twice from the same one.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Its wall of wind eats arrows. Do not build your plan around the bow.
• Wind-shape cannot swing a sword; its own shape cannot fly. Watch which it is wearing and you know what is coming.
• Cold iron in the pack, always. Of all the celestials this is the one a plain warband might actually anger.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: I have shared fire with three, and all three were gone before dawn without a word of farewell — which is not rudeness in them, only weather. Speak plainly, offer drink, ask no promises. They keep every promise they give; they simply give very few, and never the one you asked for.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable power

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Eladrin Traits: Eladrins are the celestials of the chaotic good planes, and the bralani's own line confirms the family traits: darkvision out to 60 feet and low-light vision; immunity to electricity and petrification; resistance to cold 10 and fire 10; damage reduction 10/cold iron or evil; spell resistance 17; and tongues, always active. A bralani's natural weapons, as well as any weapon it wields, are treated as both chaotic-aligned and good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Bralanis speak Celestial, Infernal, and Draconic, but can talk with nearly anything.

Combat: Bralanis prefer the scimitar and the bow, the weapons of the desert nomads they most closely resemble — and theirs are holy. In addition to their humanoid shape they can take the form of a whirlwind or a zephyr of dust, snow, or sand.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—blur, charm person (DC 13), gust of wind (DC 14), mirror image, wind wall; 2/day—lightning bolt (DC 15), cure serious wounds (DC 15). Caster level 6th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Whirlwind Blast (Su): When in whirlwind form, a bralani can attack with a scouring blast of wind, dealing 3d6 points of damage in a 20-foot line (Reflex DC 16 half). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Alternate Form (Su): A bralani can shift between its humanoid and whirlwind forms as a standard action. In humanoid form it cannot fly or use its whirlwind blast, but it can use its spell-like abilities and its weapons. In whirlwind form it can fly, make slam attacks and whirlwind blast attacks, and use spell-like abilities. A bralani remains in one form until it chooses to assume a new one; a change in form cannot be dispelled, nor does the bralani revert to any particular form when killed. A true seeing spell, however, reveals both forms at once.

Tongues (Su): Bralanis can speak with any creature that has a language, as though using a tongues spell (caster level 14th). This ability is always active, so there is never an excuse for a misunderstanding.

lore.summary: The knights of the eladrin: tall, fair, bright as fresh plate, carrying a great blessed sword that burns white in the hand. A ghaele hunts wickedness through the world the way I hunt beasts, and it is better at it than I am. It can also put its body off altogether and travel as a drifting globe of shifting colours — which is the shape I would fear most.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall man's height in its own shape; in the other, a globe of moving colour about the span of a man's arms.
Durability: Sturdy, and its own shape wears a hide that turns blows like mail. In globe-shape there is no flesh there to cut at all.
Defenses: Nothing marks it but a blade that is cold iron and of wicked make at once — both in the one weapon, and I have never seen such a thing outside a fiend's hand. Lightning and the petrifying gaze fail on it, cold and fire are half-spent, spells mostly slide away, and a ward of grace shields it and everyone close beside it.
Speed: Swift on foot, and in globe-shape it flies effortlessly and turns without cost.
Might: A great blessed sword swung with more strength than its frame admits, and it disarms and trips as readily as it cuts. It prays as a bishop prays, with everything that follows from it. Its plain look kills the lesser sort of wicked thing outright and puts terror into everything else. In globe-shape it cannot swing or pray, but it lances out rays of light that no armour, hide or ward turns aside.
Mind: Learned, courteous and entirely certain. It will argue with you at length, and it will not be moved.
Disposition: A knight before it is anything else. It is looking for evil, not for you — but it will look at you, and you will feel it.
Bane: Its enemies need a blade that is cold iron and evil-forged together, and almost nothing carries one. Its seams are of another kind: it is proud, it prefers a straight fight to a clever one, and it will take up a challenge it ought to refuse. And its killing look is a thing you can simply decline to meet.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It prefers the front and the open blade. It fixes the wicked with its gaze — the slighter sort fall dead on the spot, and everything else that meets its eyes runs — then wades in with the greatsword, disarming and tripping as much as cutting, because it would rather end a fight than a life. It holds the dangerous ones motionless, throws a wall of force across a doorway, or spends one of its few great strokes: chained lightning, or a spray of murderous colour. If it wants distance it becomes the globe, lifts out of reach, and lances you with light that armour does not answer. It heals as readily as it strikes.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Look at its chin, never its eyes. That gaze does the work of a whole company.
• In globe-shape its light goes through armour, hide and ward alike. There is no guard against it but not being there.
• It fights fair when it need not. That is the only advantage you will ever hold over one, and taking it ought to shame you.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: One judged me on a white bridge in the eladrins' own country — my whole life read in the time it takes to draw breath — and told me which of my killings had been needful and which merely convenient. Then it stood aside. Address it as you would a queen, answer straight, and keep your eyes off its eyes while you do.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire adversary

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Eladrin Traits: Eladrins are the celestials of the chaotic good planes, and the ghaele's own line confirms the family traits: darkvision out to 60 feet and low-light vision; immunity to electricity and petrification; resistance to cold 10 and fire 10; damage reduction 10/evil and cold iron — a ghaele needs both, where a bralani needs either — and spell resistance 28. It also carries a protective aura and the always-active tongues ability. A ghaele's natural weapons, as well as any weapon it wields, are treated as both chaotic-aligned and good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. A ghaele stands about 6 feet tall and weighs about 170 pounds; its other shape is an incorporeal globe of eldritch colors 5 feet across.

Combat: Ghaeles who enter combat prefer direct confrontation and damaging attacks to subtler methods. They usually fight in humanoid form, wielding incandescent +4 holy greatswords; if a ghaele wants mobility, it assumes globe form and blasts the enemy with light rays.

Gaze (Su): In humanoid form the ghaele's gaze slays evil creatures of 5 levels or fewer, range 60 feet, Will DC 18 negates. Even on a successful save such a creature is affected as though by a fear spell for 2d10 rounds. Nonevil creatures, and evil creatures above 5 levels, must succeed on a DC 18 Will save or suffer the fear effect. The save DCs are Charisma-based. Meet its eyes only if your conscience is clear.

Light Ray (Ex): A ghaele in globe form can project light rays with a range of 300 feet, two per round at +11 ranged touch for 2d12 each. This attack overcomes damage reduction of any type.

Alternate Form (Su): A ghaele can shift between its humanoid and globe forms as a standard action. In humanoid form it cannot fly or use its light rays, but it can use its gaze attack and spell-like abilities, make physical attacks, and cast spells. In globe form it can fly, use its light rays, and use spell-like abilities, but it cannot cast spells or use its gaze attack; the globe form is incorporeal, and the ghaele has no Strength score while in it. A ghaele remains in one form until it chooses to assume a new one; a change in form cannot be dispelled, nor does the ghaele revert to any particular form when killed. A true seeing spell or ability, however, reveals both forms at once.

Protective Aura (Su): Against attacks made or effects created by evil creatures, this ability grants a +4 deflection bonus to AC and a +4 resistance bonus on saving throws to anyone within 20 feet of the ghaele. Otherwise it functions as a magic circle against evil effect and a lesser globe of invulnerability, both with a radius of 20 feet, at a caster level equal to the ghaele's own level. (The defensive benefits of the circle are not included in the ghaele's statistics block.)

Tongues (Su): Ghaeles can speak with any creature that has a language, as though using a tongues spell (caster level 14th). This ability is always active. Ghaeles speak Celestial, Infernal, and Draconic besides.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—aid, charm monster (DC 17), color spray (DC 14), comprehend languages, continual flame, cure light wounds (DC 14), dancing lights, detect evil, detect thoughts (DC 15), disguise self, dispel magic, hold monster (DC 18), greater invisibility (self only), major image (DC 16), see invisibility, greater teleport (self plus 50 pounds of objects only); 1/day—chain lightning (DC 19), prismatic spray (DC 20), wall of force. Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spells: Ghaeles in humanoid form cast divine spells as 14th-level clerics, with access to two of the following domains: Air, Animal, Chaos, Good, or Plant (plus any others from its deity). The save DCs are Wisdom-based. Typical cleric spells prepared (6/7/7/6/5/4/4/3; save DC 13 + spell level), domains Air and Animal: 0—cure minor wounds, detect magic, guidance, light, resistance, virtue; 1st—bless, calm animals*, command, divine favor, obscuring mist, sanctuary, shield of faith; 2nd—aid, align weapon, bear's endurance, hold animal*, lesser restoration, remove paralysis, zone of truth; 3rd—daylight, gaseous form*, prayer, remove curse, searing light, water breathing; 4th—death ward, dismissal, divine power, restoration, summon nature's ally IV (animal)*; 5th—control winds*, flame strike, raise dead, true seeing; 6th—banishment, blade barrier, chain lightning*, heal; 7th—animal shapes*, holy word, summon monster VII. (*Domain spell.)

lore.summary: A serpent clad in feathers of green and gold, wings the span of a cart, and behind its eyes a mind older and kinder than mine. Couatls keep the warm forests and the old temples buried in them, guarding oaths sworn before any kingdom stood. They speak straight into your thoughts without moving that jewelled head, and they know a lie for what it is.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a coiled serpent longer than a war-horse, with a wingspan broader still.
Durability: Sturdier than any serpent has a right to be, though not a thing built to soak punishment.
Defenses: Scaled, quick and warded by its own charms; hard pressed, it steps sideways into the ethereal and is simply not there.
Speed: Slow and awkward on the ground; in the air a swift and steady flier that can hang motionless above your reach.
Might: A bite whose venom drains the strength clean out of your limbs, and coils that take hold and squeeze.
Mind: Keen and deeply learned, wiser than most sages, and it reads your intent before you have shaped the words.
Disposition: Lawful and good to the marrow — patient, courteous, and utterly unbending once it has given its word.
Bane: It carries no iron hide and no ward against honest steel — that is what its enemies bring, and it is enough. But its real seam is its own law: it keeps a bargain to the letter even when the letter runs against it, and it will not strike first at anyone who has offered no harm.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It sifts your thoughts before it shows itself, then works from above and at distance — searing light, mists, silences, wards laid on itself — hovering out of a swordsman's reach. Only when the odds are settled does it close, bite, and wind its coils about you until you stop moving. Cornered, it goes ethereal and leaves. Where several keep a wood, they settle their plan before a single one is seen.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Speak first. It is already listening, and it already knows why you came.
• Its venom empties the strength from your arms. If you are fighting one, you have chosen wrong.
• Ask leave to pass through its wood. Twice that has cost me nothing but courtesy.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Always talk. One spoke into my head before I ever saw it and asked, politely, why I had come armed into its wood. I told the truth and was let by. Do not lie to a couatl — it hears the shape of a lie — and do not swear it anything you cannot keep.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Native)
Initiative: +7
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 60 ft. (good)
Armor Class: 21 (-1 size, +3 Dex, +9 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 18

Full Attack: Bite +12 melee (1d3+6 plus poison)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A couatl uses its detect thoughts ability on any creature that arouses its suspicions. Since it is highly intelligent, a couatl usually casts spells from a distance before closing. If more than one couatl is involved, they discuss their strategy before a battle. A couatl is about 12 feet long, with a wingspan of about 15 feet, and weighs about 1,800 pounds. Couatls speak Celestial, Common, and Draconic.

Constrict (Ex): A couatl deals 2d8+6 points of damage with a successful grapple check.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a couatl must hit a creature of up to two size categories larger with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 16, initial damage 2d4 Str, secondary damage 4d4 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Psionics (Sp): At will—detect chaos, detect evil, detect good, detect law, detect thoughts (DC 15), invisibility, plane shift (DC 20). Effective caster level 9th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spells: A couatl casts spells as a 9th-level sorcerer. It can choose its spells known from the sorcerer list, the cleric list, and from the lists for the Air, Good, and Law domains. The cleric spells and domain spells are considered arcane spells for a couatl, meaning that the creature does not need a divine focus to cast them.

Typical Spells Known: (6/7/7/7/4; save DC 13 + spell level) 0—cure minor wounds, daze, disrupt undead, light, obscuring mist, ray of frost, read magic, resistance; 1st—endure elements, mage armor, protection from chaos, true strike, wind wall; 2nd—cure moderate wounds, eagle's splendor, scorching ray, silence; 3rd—gaseous form, magic circle against evil, summon monster III; 4th—charm monster, freedom of movement.

Change Shape (Su): A couatl can assume the form of any Small or Medium humanoid.

Ethereal Jaunt (Su): This ability works like the ethereal jaunt spell (caster level 16th).

Telepathy (Su): A couatl can communicate telepathically with any creature within 90 feet that has an Intelligence score. The creature can respond to the couatl if it wishes—no common language is needed.

lore.summary: A woman to the waist and a great serpent below, wings striped like a jay's, and a voice that stops a camp mid-argument. Lillends keep the wild places and the making of art — a song, a carving, a painted cave wall. They wander the wilder planes and slip into ours wherever beauty is being made, or unmade. A few of them wear a man's torso instead.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a slender torso above coils longer than a wagon.
Durability: Tougher than that graceful build suggests, and she does not tire.
Defenses: Venom cannot touch her and flame troubles her little; beyond that she trusts to speed, to glamour and to song.
Speed: Slow crawling, but a strong and untiring flier.
Might: A short sword in a practised hand, a lashing tail that hooks you off your feet, and coils that close and do not open.
Mind: Clever, well read in old lore and in music, warm company until you cross her.
Disposition: Chaotic and good — generous, unpredictable, and implacable towards anyone who harms an artist or a made thing.
Bane: She wears no armour of magic. Plain steel finds her, which is what her enemies bring, and only poison and fire are wasted on her. Her seam is her cause: harm no maker, no made thing and no wild grove, and she has no quarrel with you at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She opens with glamour rather than the blade — darkness, a false landscape laid over honest ground, a burst of sound, a sleep or a charm — sorting the guilty from the rest before anyone bleeds. Then she closes: the tail hooks you, the coils crush, and the short sword works the whole time. Where several hunt together they agree the plan first, and once she has named you guilty she does not tire of the chase.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never burn a book, a grove or a shrine where one of these might hear of it.
• Fire and venom are wasted on her. Bring steel — or better, bring an apology.
• If she is singing at you, listen. The song is usually the warning.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Praise the work, not the maker, and mean it. I shared a fire with one who sang until dawn and then set me straight on the road to the thing I was actually hunting. Cross her over a burned library or a felled grove and no words will serve — she has already judged you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril if wronged

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Chaotic, Extraplanar, Good)
Initiative: +3

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Lillends are generally peaceful unless they intend vengeance against someone they believe guilty of harming, or even threatening, a favored art form, artwork, or artist. Then they become implacable foes. They use their spells and spell-like abilities to confuse and weaken opponents before entering combat. A covey of lillends usually discusses strategy before a battle. A typical lillend's coils are 20 feet long and the creature weighs about 3,800 pounds; a few lillends have male torsos. Lillends speak Celestial, Infernal, Abyssal, and Common.

Aligned Strikes (Ex): A lillend's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned and good-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Constrict (Ex): A lillend deals 2d6+5 points of damage with a successful grapple check. Constricting uses the entire lower portion of its body, so it cannot take any move actions when constricting, though it can still attack with its sword.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a lillend must hit with its tail slap attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Spells: A lillend casts arcane spells as a 6th-level bard.

Typical Bard Spells Known: (3/4/3; save DC 14 + spell level) 0—dancing lights, daze, detect magic, lullaby, mage hand, read magic; 1st—charm person, cure light wounds, identify, sleep; 2nd—hold person, invisibility, sound burst.

Spell-Like Abilities: 3/day—darkness, hallucinatory terrain (DC 18), knock, light; 1/day—charm person (DC 15), speak with animals, speak with plants. Caster level 10th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Bardic Music: A lillend also has the bardic music ability as a 6th-level bard.

Skills: Lillends have a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks.

lore.summary: Half again the height of a tall man, blue-skinned and cloud-haired, and prouder than any lord I have supped with. The djinn come from the plane of air, where they raise palaces out of cloud. They walk our skies for trade, for curiosity, and for the old blood-grudge they carry against the efreet, which they will happily explain at length.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — head and shoulders above the biggest man you know, and lighter than he is.
Durability: Solidly made, though it would far rather not be struck at all.
Defenses: Acid slides off it entirely. It goes unseen when it pleases, thins to vapour, or becomes a whirlwind nothing can lay hands on.
Speed: Ponderous afoot; in the air, faultless — it flies as easily as you breathe.
Might: Two hammering fists, and a whirlwind shape that plucks armoured men off the ground, spins them blind and drops them.
Mind: Sharp, widely travelled and finely skilled at some craft; it argues well and is flattered easily.
Disposition: Chaotic and good at heart — generous, boastful, quick to take offence and quicker to forgive a courteous man.
Bane: No ward against honest steel; only acid is wasted on it. Never meet one in open air, where the wind favours it and never you. Its seam is pride: it will accept a challenge it ought to refuse, and it bargains rather than dies.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It disdains fists and reaches first for illusion and vanishing — an image to pull your eye one way, a disappearance to change its ground — then hammers in from the angle you were not watching. Overmatched, it becomes a whirlwind and harries whoever follows, snatching men up and flinging them down, or takes the wind and is gone. Trapped outright, it will offer treasure and favours for its freedom, and mean them.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Wishes come only from the noble ones, and only to whoever has bound them. Ask a common djinni and you have called him a servant.
• Bring wine and manners. It can make better wine than yours, but it will note that you brought some.
• Never take one under open sky. Fight it in a cellar or not at all.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The best conversation I have had with anything not human. Greet it by its rank, keep your own word to the letter, and it will keep its. Never speak kindly of the efreet in its hearing. And do not ask a common djinni for wishes — it has none to give, and the asking insults it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable spirit

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Air, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +8
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 60 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 16 (-1 size, +4 Dex, +3 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+15
Attack: Slam +10 melee (1d8+4)
Full Attack: 2 slams +10 melee (1d8+4)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Air mastery, spell-like abilities, whirlwind
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to acid, plane shift, telepathy 100 ft.
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +9, Will +7
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 19, Con 14, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 15
Skills: Appraise +12, Concentration +12, Craft (any one) +12, Diplomacy +4, Escape Artist +14, Knowledge (any one) +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +14, Sense Motive +12, Spellcraft +12, Spot +12, Use Rope +4 (+6 with bindings)
Feats: Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative (B)
Environment: Elemental Plane of Air
Organization: Solitary, company (2-4), or band (6-15)
Challenge Rating: 5 (noble 8)
Alignment: Always chaotic good
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 8-10 levels (Large); 11-21 levels (Huge); level adjustment +6

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Djinn disdain physical combat, preferring to use their magical powers and aerial abilities against foes. A djinni overmatched in combat usually takes flight and becomes a whirlwind to harass those who follow. A djinni is about 10½ feet tall and weighs about 1,000 pounds. Djinn speak Auran, Celestial, Common, and Ignan.

Air Mastery (Ex): Airborne creatures take a -1 penalty on attack and damage rolls against a djinni.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—invisibility (self only); 1/day—create food and water, create wine (as create water, but wine instead), major creation (created vegetable matter is permanent), persistent image (DC 17), wind walk. Once per day, a djinni can assume gaseous form (as the spell) for up to 1 hour. Caster level 20th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Whirlwind (Su): A djinni can transform itself into a whirlwind once every 10 minutes and remain in that form for up to 7 rounds. In this form it can move through the air or along a surface at its fly speed. The whirlwind is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 30 feet wide at the top and up to 50 feet tall; the djinni controls the exact height, but it must be at least 10 feet. Its movement while in whirlwind form does not provoke attacks of opportunity, even if the djinni enters the space another creature occupies. Another creature might be caught in the whirlwind if it touches or enters the whirlwind, or if the djinni moves into or through the creature's space. Creatures one or more size categories smaller than the djinni might take damage when caught in the whirlwind and be lifted into the air. An affected creature must succeed on a DC 20 Reflex save when it comes into contact with the whirlwind or take 3d6 points of damage. It must also succeed on a second DC 20 Reflex save or be picked up bodily and held suspended in the powerful winds, automatically taking 1d8 points of damage each round. A creature with a fly speed is allowed a DC 20 Reflex save each round to escape the whirlwind; it still takes damage but can leave if the save is successful. The save DC is Strength-based and includes a +3 racial adjustment.

Whirlwind, continued (Su): Creatures trapped in the whirlwind cannot move except to go where the djinni carries them or to escape it. They can otherwise act normally, but must make a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level) to cast a spell, and they take a -4 penalty to Dexterity and a -2 penalty on attack rolls. The djinni can have only as many trapped inside the whirlwind at one time as will fit inside its volume, and it can eject any carried creatures whenever it wishes, depositing them wherever the whirlwind happens to be. If the whirlwind's base touches the ground it creates a swirling cloud of debris centered on the djinni, with a diameter equal to half the whirlwind's height; the cloud obscures all vision, including darkvision, beyond 5 feet. Creatures 5 feet away have concealment, while those farther away have total concealment, and those caught in the cloud must succeed on a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level) to cast a spell. A djinni in whirlwind form cannot make melee attacks and does not threaten the area around it.

Plane Shift (Sp): A genie can enter any of the elemental planes, the Astral Plane, or the Material Plane. This ability transports the genie and up to eight other creatures, provided they all link hands with the genie. It is otherwise similar to the spell of the same name (caster level 13th).

Telepathy: A genie can communicate telepathically with any creature within 100 feet that has a language, whether or not the two share a tongue in common.

Noble Djinn: Some djinn (1 percent of the total population) are noble. A noble djinni can grant three wishes to any being (nongenies only) who captures it. Noble djinn perform no other services and, upon granting the third wish, are free of their servitude. Noble djinn are as strong as efreet, standing at ten outsider levels rather than seven, and are Challenge Rating 8. Ordinary djinn grant no wishes at all.

lore.summary: A giant out of the plane of fire, red as forge-iron and too hot to stand beside, horned, and smiling in a way that means nothing good. Efreet keep cities of brass and fill them with slaves. They come to our world for tribute, for amusement, and for the particular pleasure of granting a mortal exactly what he asked for.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a head taller than a djinni and half again as heavy.
Durability: Hard to put down; the brass cities breed them thick and durable.
Defenses: Fire does nothing to it whatever. It goes unseen, thins to vapour, or takes another shape entirely and walks among your men wearing a face you trust.
Speed: Slow-footed, but it flies without any effort at all.
Might: Two blows from red-hot fists that scorch where they land, a standing wall of flame at a word, lances of fire at distance, and the power to swell a man clumsy or shrink him to nothing.
Mind: Cunning, a superb liar, and a lawyer to the bone.
Disposition: Lawful and thoroughly evil — cruel, vain, and scrupulously exact about the wording of any bargain.
Bane: Cold. It cannot abide it — frost and winter magic hurt it worse than anything else in your pack, and honest steel serves besides. Its other seam is its own law: it must keep the letter of what it swore. Make the letter airtight or do not swear at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights by misleading, and enjoys that more than the killing — an unseen approach, a false image where it is not, a wall of fire cut between you and your friends. Then it closes and burns you with its hands, or takes hold and holds you against that furnace of a body while you cook. It will swell one man past his own balance and shrink another to a doll's size, laughing throughout, and it fights on when a djinni would have bargained.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Three wishes. Three ruins. There is no wording it cannot turn, so do not try to out-word it.
• Bring cold in any form you can carry. It is the one thing that truly frightens it.
• It can wear another face. If a friend suddenly wants you to swear to something, test him first.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk if you must, but write nothing and swear nothing. I watched one offer three wishes to a caravan-master. Each was granted, each to the letter, and each ruined him — the third took his sons. If the offer seems generous you have already missed the hook. Refuse, and walk.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Extraplanar, Fire)
Initiative: +7
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 40 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 18 (-1 size, +3 Dex, +6 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +10/+20
Attack: Slam +15 melee (1d8+6 plus 1d6 fire)
Full Attack: 2 slams +15 melee (1d8+6 plus 1d6 fire)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Change size, heat, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Change shape, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to fire, plane shift, telepathy 100 ft., vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +9, Ref +10, Will +9
Abilities: Str 23, Dex 17, Con 14, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 15
Skills: Bluff +15, Concentration +15, Craft (any one) +14, Diplomacy +6, Disguise +2 (+4 acting), Intimidate +17, Listen +15, Move Silently +16, Sense Motive +15, Spellcraft +14, Spot +15
Feats: Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative (B), Quicken Spell-Like Ability (scorching ray)
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire
Organization: Solitary, company (2-4), or band (6-15)
Challenge Rating: 8
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: Standard coins; double goods; standard items
Advancement: 11-15 levels (Large); 16-30 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Efreet love to mislead, befuddle, and confuse their foes. They do so for enjoyment as well as a battle tactic. An efreeti stands about 12 feet tall and weighs about 2,000 pounds. Efreet speak Auran, Common, Ignan, and Infernal.

Change Size (Sp): Twice per day, an efreeti can magically change a creature's size. This works just like an enlarge person or reduce person spell (the efreeti chooses when using the ability), except that the ability can work on the efreeti. A DC 13 Fortitude save negates the effect. The save DC is Charisma-based. This is the equivalent of a 2nd-level spell.

Heat (Ex): An efreeti's red-hot body deals 1d6 points of extra fire damage whenever it hits in melee, or in each round it maintains a hold when grappling.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—detect magic, produce flame, pyrotechnics (DC 14), scorching ray (1 ray only); 3/day—invisibility, wall of fire (DC 16); 1/day—grant up to three wishes (to nongenies only), gaseous form, permanent image (DC 18). Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Change Shape (Su): An efreeti can assume the form of any Small, Medium, or Large humanoid or giant.

Plane Shift (Sp): A genie can enter any of the elemental planes, the Astral Plane, or the Material Plane. This ability transports the genie and up to eight other creatures, provided they all link hands with the genie. It is otherwise similar to the spell of the same name (caster level 13th).

Telepathy: A genie can communicate telepathically with any creature within 100 feet that has a language, whether or not the two share a tongue in common.

Vulnerability to Cold: An efreeti takes half again as much (+50 percent) damage as normal from cold, regardless of whether a saving throw is allowed or whether the save is a success or failure.

lore.summary: The least of the genies and much the most companionable. A janni is made of all four elements at once, and so must live in our world rather than any pure one. The jann keep the deep deserts — tented camps, fine horses, better swords — and will trade with anyone who comes politely. They also remember a slight for generations.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a tall, well-made desert-dweller; at any distance you would take one for a man.
Durability: Hardy, mail-clad and bred to hard living, but no tougher than a good soldier.
Defenses: Flame troubles it little. It can vanish from sight, or step half out of the world entirely, and it wears honest mail besides.
Speed: Quick afoot and nimble in the air, though the mail on its back weighs those wings badly.
Might: A scimitar in a trained hand, a longbow at distance, and the trick of swelling a man clumsy or shrinking him mid-fight.
Mind: Bright, worldly and proud; a shrewd trader who prices everything in sight, yourself included.
Disposition: Neutral and even-handed — warm to the courteous, murderous to anyone who insults or robs it.
Bane: Nothing about it turns a blade, and it wears down like a man does. It cannot endure the pure elemental planes for long — it must come home or die there. Its true seam is trade: it would nearly always rather deal than fight.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights like a good soldier, because it is one — the bow first at distance, then the scimitar, and it does not break and run. Meeting something it cannot beat straight, it goes unseen, takes to the air, circles wide and comes back at your flank. It is rarely alone; count the tents before you count the swords, because the rest of the company will already be moving.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Water and salt first, business afterward. In that order or not at all.
• Buy something. Anything. It costs far less than the alternative.
• Never one alone. Where there is one janni there is a company, and it has already seen you.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The easiest talk in the desert. Come openly, offer water and salt, buy something you do not need, and you have a guide, an ally and a bed for the night. Insult one and you have insulted a family that will still remember it when your grandsons ride through.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Native)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 15 ft. (perfect) in chainmail; base land speed 30 ft., base fly speed 20 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 18 (+2 Dex, +1 natural, +5 chainmail), touch 12, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+9
Attack: Scimitar +9 melee (1d6+4/18-20) or longbow +8 ranged (1d8/×3)
Full Attack: Scimitar +9/+4 melee (1d6+4/18-20) or longbow +8/+3 ranged (1d8/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Change size, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., elemental endurance, plane shift, resistance to fire 10, telepathy 100 ft.
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +7
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 13
Skills: Appraise +11, Concentration +10, Craft (any two) +11, Diplomacy +3, Escape Artist +6, Listen +11, Move Silently +6, Ride +11, Sense Motive +11, Spot +11, Use Rope +2 (+4 with bindings)
Feats: Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative (B), Mobility
Environment: Warm deserts
Organization: Solitary, company (2-4), or band (6-15)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 7-9 levels (Medium); 10-18 levels (Large); level adjustment +5

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Jann are physically strong and courageous, and do not take kindly to insult or injury. If they meet a foe they cannot defeat in a standup fight, they use flight and invisibility to regroup and maneuver to a more advantageous position. The jann are the weakest of the genies; formed out of all four elements, they must spend most of their time on the Material Plane. Jann speak Common, one elemental language (Aquan, Auran, Ignan, or Terran) and one alignment language (Abyssal, Celestial, or Infernal).

Change Size (Sp): Twice per day, a janni can magically change a creature's size. This works just like an enlarge person or reduce person spell (the janni chooses when using the ability), except that the ability can work on the janni. A DC 13 Fortitude save negates the effect. The save DC is Charisma-based. This is the equivalent of a 2nd-level spell.

Spell-Like Abilities: 3/day—invisibility (self only), speak with animals. Caster level 12th. Once per day a janni can create food and water (caster level 7th) and can use ethereal jaunt (caster level 12th) for 1 hour. The save DCs are Charisma-based. A janni grants no wishes.

Elemental Endurance (Ex): Jann can survive on the Elemental Planes of Air, Earth, Fire, or Water for up to 48 hours. Failure to return to the Material Plane before that time expires causes a janni to take 1 point of damage per additional hour spent on the elemental plane, until it dies or returns to the Material Plane.

Plane Shift (Sp): A genie can enter any of the elemental planes, the Astral Plane, or the Material Plane. This ability transports the genie and up to eight other creatures, provided they all link hands with the genie. It is otherwise similar to the spell of the same name (caster level 13th).

Telepathy: A genie can communicate telepathically with any creature within 100 feet that has a language, whether or not the two share a tongue in common.

Jann as Characters: Janni characters gain +6 Strength, +4 Dexterity, +2 Constitution, +4 Intelligence, +4 Wisdom, +2 Charisma; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet and fly 20 feet (perfect); darkvision 60 feet; +1 natural armor; six racial outsider levels granting a +6 base attack bonus and base saves of Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +5, three feats (Improved Initiative among them) and skill points equal to 9 × (8 + Int modifier). Class skills are Appraise, Concentration, Craft (any), Escape Artist, Listen, Move Silently, Ride, Sense Motive, and Spot. Favored class rogue; level adjustment +5.

lore.summary: Fire-folk of the burning plane: a smith's torso above, a long coiling serpent below, and every span of it hot enough to cook a man inside his mail. They are craftsmen without equal and cruel in the bargain. I have met them at lava vents, at cracked planar gates, and in the deep halls of masters who bought their work.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium above the waist and a long serpent behind it, so its reach is longer than its shoulders promise.
Durability: Forge-tough. It absorbs a beating the way an anvil does and goes on working.
Defenses: Honest steel slides off its scaled hide with barely a mark; carry an enchanted arm or carry nothing.
Speed: Slow. It shuffles and coils where you can stride, and it knows it, so it fights where you cannot leave.
Might: A spear driven with a smith's arm, a tail that sweeps you off your feet, and skin that scalds through glove and grip alike.
Mind: Sharp as a learned man, patient, and a blacksmith better than any mortal who ever held tongs.
Disposition: Wicked, though of no single stripe — some will trade with you, some will simply gut you and use your buckles for scrap.
Bane: Cold. Flame does nothing to it whatever, but frost and ice bite it doubly deep; and it is slow, so a fighting retreat is always open to you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at spear's length and keeps you there, the metal of the shaft glowing with its own heat. Should you close, the tail comes round, knocks your legs away and takes hold, and then it simply crushes and burns you while the spear keeps working. Its smaller kin, the flamebrothers, swarm instead of duelling; the great nobles fight with fire itself — sheets of flame, walls of it, and elementals called up out of the air.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Frost on your blade, or stay home. Its own fire will not scare it and yours will not either.
• Never grapple. Never let it grapple you. Everything it owns is hot, chains and buckles included.
• It wants metalwork and it wants it badly. I have bought a night's safe passage with a broken sword.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: They talk, and the older ones talk in the trade tongue as well as their own hissing speech. I have bargained with one over a hoard of nails and come away whole. But they are evil to the bone and they honour a bargain only while it profits them. Keep your back to the cold air.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar, Fire)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (+1 Dex, +7 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +9/+11
Attack: Spear +11 melee (1d8+3/×3 plus 1d6 fire)
Full Attack: Spear +11/+6 melee (1d8+3/×3 plus 1d6 fire) and tail slap +9 melee (2d6+1 plus 1d6 fire)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft. (10 ft. with tail)
Special Attacks: Constrict 2d6+1 plus 1d6 fire, heat, improved grab
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/magic, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to fire, vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +8
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 13
Skills: Bluff +11, Craft (blacksmithing) +19, Diplomacy +3, Disguise +1 (+3 acting), Hide +11, Intimidate +3, Listen +8, Move Silently +11, Search +12, Spot +8
Feats: Alertness, Multiattack, Power Attack
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire
Organization: Solitary, pair, or cluster (3-5)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Usually evil (any)
Treasure: Standard (nonflammables only)
Advancement: 8-14 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: If a salamander has damage reduction, its natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Salamanders speak Ignan; some average salamanders and all nobles also speak Common.

Constrict (Ex): A salamander deals automatic tail slap damage (including fire damage) with a successful grapple check. A noble salamander can constrict multiple creatures simultaneously, provided they are all at least two sizes smaller than it.

Heat (Ex): A salamander generates so much heat that its mere touch deals additional fire damage. Salamanders' metallic weapons also conduct this heat.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a salamander must hit a creature of up to one size larger than itself with its tail slap attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Spell-Like Abilities: (Noble salamanders only) 3/day—burning hands (DC 13), fireball (DC 15), flaming sphere (DC 14), wall of fire (DC 16); 1/day—dispel magic, summon monster VII (Huge fire elemental). Caster level 15th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Skills: Salamanders have a +4 racial bonus on Craft (blacksmithing) checks.

Feats: Salamanders have the Multiattack feat even though they do not have the requisite three natural weapons.

Other Kinds of Salamander: The stat block above is the average salamander (CR 6). Two other castes appear in the SRD. The flamebrother is the smallest: Small, AC 19 (touch 12, flat-footed 18), base attack/grapple +4/+1, spear +6 melee (1d6+1/×3 plus 1d6 fire) and tail slap +4 melee (1d4 plus 1d6 fire), 5 ft./5 ft., constrict 1d4 plus 1d6 fire, no damage reduction, Fort +6 Ref +5 Will +6, Str 12 Dex 13 Con 14 Int 14 Wis 15 Cha 13, feats Alertness and Multiattack, CR 3, advancement 4-6 levels (Small), level adjustment +4. The noble salamander is the greatest: Large, AC 18 (touch 10, flat-footed 17), base attack/grapple +15/+25, +3 longspear +23/+18/+13 melee (1d8+9/×3 plus 1d8 fire) and tail slap +21 melee (2d8+3 plus 1d8 fire), 10 ft./10 ft. (20 ft. with tail or longspear), constrict 2d8+3 plus 1d8 fire plus the spell-like abilities listed above, damage reduction 15/magic, Fort +12 Ref +10 Will +11, Str 22 Dex 13 Con 16 Int 16 Wis 15 Cha 15, feats Alertness, Cleave, Great Cleave, Multiattack, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Craft [blacksmithing]), organization solitary, pair, or noble party (9-14), CR 10, treasure double standard (nonflammables only) and a +3 longspear, advancement 16-21 levels (Large); 22-45 levels (Huge). All three castes are usually evil (any) and native to the Elemental Plane of Fire.

lore.summary: Dwarf-built folk of the burning plane, short and broad and heavy, in kilts of brass and bronze and copper, with beard and hair burning like a banked forge. They mine, they cut gems, they hammer metal, and they are the surest craftsmen a traveller will meet out there. Met at fire-gates, in deep vents, and wherever the rock runs hot.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A dwarf's build — no taller than your shoulder and half again your weight.
Durability: Stubborn. Not hard to kill, but he will not fall while there is a fight left in him.
Defenses: Scale mail, a heavy shield, thick hide beneath, and a stubbornness in the blood that turns aside a fair share of spells outright.
Speed: A workman's pace. Armoured and short-legged, he neither chases nor flees quickly.
Might: A well-forged hammer or a broad-headed spear, and failing both, hands that seize and scald whatever they hold.
Mind: Orderly and quick-witted. He appraises everything he sees, values it correctly, and will out-bargain you every time.
Disposition: Lawful and unsentimental — unfriendly, taciturn, neither kind nor cruel. He starts no quarrel except over gems, which he loves past all reason; threatened, he fights to the death, though he is glad enough to take you alive.
Bane: Cold. Fire means nothing to him; frost cuts him to the quick, and his own armour will not save him from it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He advances in order, shield up, and hammers you down at close quarters, or plants the spear and lets you come onto it. Disarmed he simply grabs hold, and his grip alone blisters. They fight shoulder to shoulder in teams and squads with a sergeant calling the line, and they do not break — but they will take prisoners rather than kill, if prisoners are worth more.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not touch him. Do not let him touch you. His weapons carry his heat straight down the haft.
• He wants gems and he wants them honestly. Offer stones before steel and you will likely never fight one.
• Ice, frost, a winter charm — anything cold. He has no answer to it at all.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: He speaks the trade tongue and speaks it plainly, and he keeps a bargain to the letter — which is exactly the trouble, since the letter will be his. I traded a pouch of river garnets for a guide across the ash flats and got precisely what I asked for and nothing more. Ask carefully.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar, Fire)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 20 ft. in scale mail (4 squares); base speed 30 ft.
Armor Class: 23 (+1 Dex, +6 natural, +4 scale mail, +2 heavy shield), touch 11, flat-footed 22
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+3
Attack: Warhammer +3 melee (1d8+1/×3 plus 1 fire) or shortspear +3 ranged (1d6+1 plus 1 fire)
Full Attack: Warhammer +3 melee (1d8+1/×3 plus 1 fire) or shortspear +3 ranged (1d6+1 plus 1 fire)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Heat
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to fire, spell resistance 13, vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +4
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 13, Con 13, Int 12, Wis 12, Cha 9
Skills: Appraise +6, Climb +0, Craft (any two) +6, Hide +0, Jump -6, Listen +6, Search +6, Spot +6
Feats: Power Attack
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire
Organization: Solitary, pair, team (3-4), squad (11-20 plus 2 3rd-level sergeants and 1 leader of 3rd-6th level), or clan (30-100 plus 50% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults, 5 5th-level lieutenants, and 3 7th-level captains)
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Always lawful neutral
Treasure: Standard coins; double goods (nonflammables only); standard items (nonflammables only)
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Azers use broad-headed spears or well-crafted hammers in combat. When unarmed, they attempt to grapple foes. Although unfriendly and taciturn, azers rarely provoke a fight except to relieve a foe of gems, which they love. If threatened, they fight to the last, but they see the value of taking prisoners themselves.

Heat (Ex): An azer's body is intensely hot, so its unarmed attacks deal extra fire damage. Its metallic weapons also conduct this heat.

Description: Azers are dwarflike beings native to the Elemental Plane of Fire. They wear kilts of brass, bronze, or copper, and speak Ignan and Common.

Azers as Characters: Azer characters have +2 Strength, +2 Dexterity, +2 Constitution, +2 Intelligence, +2 Wisdom, -2 Charisma; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision 60 ft.; +6 natural armor. Two racial outsider levels give a base attack bonus of +2 and base saving throws of Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +3, skill points equal to 5 × (8 + Int modifier) with Appraise, Climb, Craft, Hide, Jump, Listen, Search and Spot as class skills, and one feat. They keep heat, immunity to fire, spell resistance equal to 13 + class levels, and vulnerability to cold. Automatic languages Common and Ignan; bonus languages Abyssal, Aquan, Auran, Celestial, Infernal, Terran. Favored class fighter. Level adjustment +4.

lore.summary: A flightless bird taller than a mounted man, its heavy body carried on four stilt legs, with a beak that takes an arm off at the elbow. They come from the ordered planes where wars are fought forever, and they speak the flat, courteous tongue of devils. I have met them stalking old battlefields in loose flocks, unhurried, picking their ground.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — the body of a great bird set high on four thin legs, taller at the head than a rider.
Durability: Solid enough, but no monster of endurance; it dies like a big animal once you can reach it.
Defenses: Thick plated hide, and a resistance in its blood that spoils a good many spells before they touch it. No ward against plain steel, mind — ordinary arms hurt it perfectly well.
Speed: Very fast. It outpaces a horse over broken ground and dances in and out of your reach at will.
Might: Two of the four legs lash out like flails while the beak takes whatever they leave standing.
Mind: As clever as an ordinary man and a fine reader of intent. It speaks the devils' tongue and no other.
Disposition: Lawful and thoroughly cruel. It hunts for the pleasure of hunting and keeps a strict code while doing it.
Bane: That black cloud comes only a handful of times before it is spent — outlast it. And fight it in a corridor or a copse, never open ground, so it cannot strike and skip away.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It closes at a run, rakes with two legs and snaps with the beak, then springs back out of reach before you can answer, and does it again, and again, until you are ragged. When pressed it lets out a choking black cloud that scalds the lungs of everything near — and the poor souls who breathe it wander mad for hours afterward, striking friends, walking into fires. That cloud has killed more of my company than the beak ever did.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The cloud is the whole fight. Hold your breath, back out of it, and do not let a maddened friend near your blade.
• No enchanted steel needed. Plain iron does fine, if you can pin it in a corridor.
• It answers courtesy in Infernal. If nobody in your band has that tongue, you have no parley and no warning.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It talks — flat, formal, and only in the devils' speech. I bought a night's passage from a flock leader once with the location of a rival's roost, and it kept the letter of that deal exactly. It also watched me sleep. Bring the tongue, bring something to trade, and never turn your back.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar, Lawful)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares)
Armor Class: 20 (-1 size, +1 Dex, +10 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+14
Attack: Claw +9 melee (2d6+4)
Full Attack: 2 claws +9 melee (2d6+4) and bite +4 melee (4d6+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Black cloud
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 19
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +7
Abilities: Str 19, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 16
Skills: Balance +10, Climb +13, Diplomacy +5, Hide +6, Jump +21, Listen +11, Move Silently +10, Sense Motive +11, Spot +11
Feats: Dodge, Mobility, Spring Attack
Environment: A lawful-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary or flock (5-8)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: Double standard
Advancement: 7-12 levels (Large); 13-18 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Description: Achaierais are massive, 15-foot-tall flightless birds that inhabit lawful planes of battle and are only occasionally encountered elsewhere. They speak Infernal and weigh about 750 pounds.

Combat: In close combat, an achaierai lashes out with two of its four legs and snaps with its powerful beak. It makes frequent use of its Spring Attack feat to strike quickly and then retreat out of range before an enemy can counterattack. An achaierai's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned and lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Black Cloud (Ex): Up to three times per day an achaierai can release a choking, toxic black cloud. Those other than achaierai within 10 feet instantly take 2d6 points of damage. They must also succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be affected for 3 hours as though by an insanity spell (caster level 16th). The save DC is Constitution-based.

lore.summary: Godlike giants of the wild free planes, taller than a cottage, armoured in warded half-plate and carrying a hammer sized for something larger than themselves. They are learned past any sage, proud past any king, and their moods turn like weather off the sea. Most stand for good; all are wild; and some — the book must be honest — are wicked.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — head and shoulders above a barn door, and heavier than a team of draught horses.
Durability: Very nearly beyond killing. I watched one take a battle's worth of wounds and finish the sentence it had begun.
Defenses: Enchanted half-plate over a hide that shrugs off any blow not sworn to law, and a resistance to magic so deep that most spells simply come apart in the air before it.
Speed: Long-legged and quick for its bulk; only the armour slows it, and it can step sideways out of the world when it chooses.
Might: That oversized hammer, swung one-handed if it likes — it breaks shields, blades, gates and walls indifferently, and it throws javelins the way a siege engine throws bolts.
Mind: Brilliant. It knows the crafts and the histories, speaks many tongues, orates beautifully, and reads a liar at a glance.
Disposition: Proud, capricious, generous and lethal by turns, and never bound by any law but its own. Judge the one before you and never the kind: most are good, but the wicked ones wear the same face.
Bane: Pride and appetite. Nothing you carry will pierce it save arms sworn to law, and its wards devour spells — but it loves a melee too well, and will close and trade blows when it ought to stand off and burn you. It can be flattered, argued with, and shamed.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It charges, and its first care is your best weapon — it will shatter that before it touches you. Then the hammer works, and all the while a whip of lightning leaps from it to whoever stands back from the fight, thrown as easily as a man breathes. Trouble it with sorcery and it folds the offender into a maze of nowhere, or calls a swarm of falling stars down on the spot, or unmakes every charm in your company at a stroke. Losing, it opens a door in the air and is simply gone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Your finest sword is the first thing it breaks. Carry a second you do not love.
• Address it properly and at length. Vanity is the widest gate it has.
• It walks among men wearing a man's shape. The one who mocked my accent in that tavern was one, and I have been careful of my manners since.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Always speak first. They keep the courtesies, they are curious about mortals, and one gave me a whole night of talk and a plain answer to a question I had chased for years. But they are wild-hearted and easily slighted, and a few are plainly evil — so praise honestly, promise nothing loosely, and never presume friendship.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Legendary — A legendary power

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Outsider (Chaotic, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 40 ft. in half-plate armor (8 squares); base speed 60 ft.
Armor Class: 38 (-2 size, +19 natural, +11 +4 half-plate armor), touch 8, flat-footed 38
Base Attack/Grapple: +20/+44
Attack: Gargantuan +3 adamantine warhammer +37 melee (4d6+27/×3) or +3 javelin +22 ranged (2d6+19) or slam +34 melee (1d8+16)
Full Attack: Gargantuan +3 adamantine warhammer +37/+32/+27/+22 melee (4d6+27/×3) or +3 javelin +22 ranged (2d6+19) or 2 slams +34 melee (1d8+16)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./15 ft.
Special Attacks: Oversized weapon, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Change shape, damage reduction 15/lawful, darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 32
Saves: Fort +26, Ref +13, Will +21
Abilities: Str 43, Dex 12, Con 39, Int 21, Wis 28, Cha 24
Skills: Balance +7, Bluff +19, Climb +22, Concentration +37, Craft (any one) +28, Diplomacy +11, Disguise +7 (+9 acting), Heal +20, Intimidate +32, Jump +38, Knowledge (any one) +28, Listen +32, Perform (oratory) +30, Sense Motive +32, Search +28, Spellcraft +17, Spot +32, Survival +9 (+11 following tracks), Swim +16
Feats: Awesome Blow, Blind-Fight, Cleave, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Sunder, Power Attack, Quicken Spell-Like Ability (chain lightning)
Environment: A chaotic good-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary or pair
Challenge Rating: 21
Alignment: Always chaotic (any)
Treasure: Double standard plus +4 half-plate armor and Gargantuan +3 adamantine warhammer
Advancement: 21-30 levels (Huge); 31-60 levels (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Description: A titan is about 25 feet tall and weighs about 14,000 pounds. Titans speak Abyssal, Common, Celestial, Draconic, and Giant.

Combat: A titan's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Oversized Weapon (Ex): A titan wields a great, two-handed warhammer (big enough for Gargantuan creatures) without penalty.
