Spell-Like Abilities: At will—chain lightning (DC 23), charm monster (DC 21), cure critical wounds (DC 21), fire storm (DC 24), greater dispel magic, hold monster (DC 22), invisibility, invisibility purge, levitate, persistent image (DC 22); 3/day—etherealness, word of chaos (DC 22), summon nature's ally IX; 1/day—gate, maze, meteor swarm (DC 26). Caster level 20th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities (Good or Neutral Titans): In addition, titans of good or neutral alignment can use the following additional spell-like abilities: at will—daylight, holy smite (DC 21), remove curse (DC 21); 1/day—greater restoration. Caster level 20th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities (Evil Titans): Titans of evil alignment can use the following additional spell-like abilities: at will—bestow curse (DC 21), deeper darkness, unholy blight (DC 21); 1/day—crushing hand (DC 26). Caster level 20th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Change Shape (Su): A titan can assume the form of any Small or Medium humanoid. The titan retains its oversized weapon special attack regardless of form.

Tactics Round-By-Round: Titans enjoy combat and usually close with their foes. If that proves ineffective, they swiftly back off and pelt the foe with spell-like abilities and magical effects. Because of a titan's Quicken Spell-Like Ability feat, it can use chain lightning as a free action, and frequently attacks in melee while lashing out with this ability at the same time. Prior to combat: invisibility purge or invisibility. Round 1: charge and attempt to sunder the weapon of the most dangerous foe, hurling chain lightning at opponents standing away from the fight. Round 2: full attack against the disarmed opponent, and hurl chain lightning at other opponents. Round 3: back away from the first opponent and use maze or meteor swarm on any spellcaster causing trouble. Round 4: sunder the weapon of the next most effective combatant, or use greater dispel magic on all nearby opponents. Round 5: full attack against any nearby opponent, or use fire storm. Use another quickened chain lightning if foes seem really dangerous. A titan usually reserves its gate and etherealness abilities to escape a fight that is not going well.

lore.summary: A black hound out of the plane of shadow — low, heavy, smooth-coated, with a mouth built for hamstrings. It cannot speak, though it understands common speech well enough to know when you are afraid. They run in packs at the heel of evil masters and hunt in the hours no lamp can reach.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A big dog, no higher than your knee at the shoulder, and as heavy as a grown man.
Durability: Hardy for a hound — hard-run, hard-winded, and slow to go down.
Defenses: No armour, no ward, no charmed hide. It has no need of any: in anything short of true daylight it is simply not there to be struck.
Speed: Very fast. Faster than you, faster than most horses, and faster still in the dark it loves.
Might: One good bite that takes your legs from under you, and then it works on your throat while you are down.
Mind: Beast-witted and nothing more — yet cunning enough to step out of a bright light, or to steal away the very charm that made it.
Disposition: Wholly evil, wholly silent until it bays, and it hunts in packs for a master who set it on you.
Bane: True daylight. Real sun, or the charm that counters night, strips its concealment and leaves you fighting an ordinary dog. Nothing lesser works — lanterns, torches, even a conjured light, it hides in all of them equally.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: The pack bays first, and that howl empties the courage out of everything within earshot save the fiends they serve — men run, horses bolt, and the hounds take the runners from behind. Then they come out of the shadows on your flanks, bite, drag you off your feet and hold you there for the next one. Balked by real daylight they do not blunder on: they slip out of the light, or bay from beyond it until the light is alone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Carry a true daylight charm on your person, not in the baggage. They have learned to steal the baggage.
• The howl breaks your horses before it breaks you. Hobble and blindfold them at dusk, or lose them.
• Stand back to back in the light. Step out of it and you are dead before you finish the step.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing here to talk to. It understands your words and takes no meaning from them beyond your fear, it cannot answer, and it is evil through and through. In every case worth the name, the thing to bargain with is the master holding the leash. Strike the hound first, then negotiate.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares)
Armor Class: 14 (+1 Dex, +3 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+7
Attack: Bite +7 melee (1d6+4)
Full Attack: Bite +7 melee (1d6+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Bay, trip
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., shadow blend, scent
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 4, Wis 12, Cha 13
Skills: Hide +8, Listen +8, Move Silently +8, Spot +8, Survival +8*
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative, Track(B)
Environment: Plane of Shadow
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pack (5-12)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 5-6 levels (Medium); 7-12 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Description: This creature has the body of a large dog, with a smooth black coat and a mouth full of sharp teeth. A shadow mastiff is slightly more than 2 feet high at the shoulder and weighs about 200 pounds. Shadow mastiffs cannot speak, but they understand Common.

Combat: Shadow mastiffs prefer fighting in shadows or dark conditions, which gives them a great advantage. If a magical light source negates the shadows around them, shadow mastiffs are cunning enough to either move out of the light or back off and break up the opposition with their baying. They have been known to seize and carry off items enspelled with daylight spells.

Bay (Su): When a shadow mastiff howls or barks, all creatures except evil outsiders within a 300-foot spread must succeed on a DC 13 Will save or become panicked for 2d4 rounds. This is a sonic mind-affecting fear effect. Whether or not the save is successful, an affected creature is immune to the same mastiff's bay for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Trip (Ex): A shadow mastiff that hits with its bite attack can attempt to trip the opponent as a free action (+3 check modifier) without making a touch attack or provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react to trip the shadow mastiff.

Shadow Blend (Su): In any condition of illumination other than full daylight, a shadow mastiff can disappear into the shadows, giving it total concealment. Artificial illumination, even a light or continual flame spell, does not negate this ability. A daylight spell, however, will.

Skills: A shadow mastiff has a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent.

lore.summary: Small winged imps of the elemental planes, and there are ten kinds of them — air and dust, earth and salt, fire, magma and steam, ice, water and ooze — each wearing its element for flesh. They slip through the cracks between worlds to loiter in furnaces, cisterns and cellars, chattering, boasting, and breathing their element into your face.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — chest-high at most, winged, and lighter than a cat unless it happens to be made of stone, salt or mud.
Durability: Slight things, easily broken — but each mends itself steadily so long as it stands in its own element, and a fire-kin beside a torch or an ice-kin on frost knits as fast as you can open it.
Defenses: Common steel slides off; blessed or enchanted arms bite properly. The fire, magma and steam kinds laugh at flame and the ice-kin at frost, but the rest carry no such gift.
Speed: All of them fly — the airy sorts with perfect ease, the earthen and oozing ones heavily — and all are quick through a gap no dog could follow.
Might: Little in the claw. The danger is the breath: a cone of grit, cinders, ice shards, salt, steam or caustic slime, and the one small conjuring each kind carries.
Mind: Dull-witted but glib. Every one of them speaks the common tongue alongside the speech of its home element, and every one talks far more than it thinks.
Disposition: Neutral by nature, not devils — vain, mocking, forever taking each other's measure. The ice-kin are aloof, the salt-kin sarcastic, the water-kin tiresome jesters, the magma-kin slow and brutish, and the steam-kin bullies who charge in where all the rest hang back.
Bane: Deny it its element and it stops mending. Fire, magma and steam kin flinch from cold and the ice-kin from flame; and a blessed blade cuts every one of them the same.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at a distance with its breath — grit, cinders, salt, ice, steam or caustic slime — then flits about clawing and jeering while it spends its trick of the hour: a blur of vapour, a hurled bolt of acid, a buckle heated on your chest, a cloud of glittering dust. Once in a day each may call for a cousin of its own kind, and mostly the call goes unanswered. Cornered, most would rather flee; only the steam-kin, in their arrogance, come at you first.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold water in a skin, kept where you can reach it. A fire-kin loses all its swagger doused.
• Take away its element and it stops knitting itself. Drag the earthen one onto boards; carry the ice-kin into the sun.
• Plain steel slides off. Bring something blessed — or bring a bribe, which is cheaper.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have bargained with mephits far oftener than I have killed them. They speak the common tongue and dearly love the sound of it. Flatter one and it will sell you every secret of the cellar it haunts; turn your back on one and it will sell you to whatever else lives down there.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor nuisance

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Outsider (Extraplanar, Fire) — fire mephit as the reference
Initiative: +5
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 50 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 16 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +4 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/-1
Attack: Claw +4 melee (1d3 plus 1d4 fire)
Full Attack: 2 claws +4 melee (1d3 plus 1d4 fire)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Breath weapon, spell-like abilities, summon mephit
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to fire, fast healing 2, vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +4, Will +3
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 13, Con 10, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 15
Skills: Bluff +8, Diplomacy +4, Disguise +2 (+4 acting), Escape Artist +7, Hide +11, Listen +6, Move Silently +7, Spot +6, Use Rope +1 (+3 with bindings)
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire (other kinds hail from the Planes of Air, Earth and Water)
Organization: Solitary (1), gang (2-4 mephits of mixed types), or mob (5-12 mephits of mixed types)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 4-6 levels (Small); 7-9 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: All mephits fight by biting and clawing or by using a breath weapon, the nature and effects of which vary from creature to creature. A mephit's natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Breath Weapon (Su): A mephit can use its breath weapon once every 1d4 rounds as a standard action. The shape, damage and save vary by kind. Fire mephit: 15-foot cone, damage 1d8 fire, Reflex DC 12 half. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +1 racial adjustment.

Spell-Like Abilities: All mephits have one or more spell-like abilities (save DC 12 + spell level). Fire mephit: 1/hour—scorching ray (DC 14, caster level 3rd); 1/day—heat metal (DC 14, caster level 6th). The save DC is Charisma-based.

Summon Mephit (Sp): Once per day, a mephit can attempt to summon another mephit of the same variety, much as though casting a summon monster spell, but with only a 25% chance of success. Roll d%: on a failure, no creature answers the summons that day. A mephit that has just been summoned cannot use its own summon ability for 1 hour. This ability is the equivalent of a 2nd-level spell.

Fast Healing (Ex): Mephits recover 2 points of damage each round, provided they are still alive and certain other conditions are met — each kind heals only in its own element. A fire mephit heals only if it is touching a flame at least as large as a torch.

The Kinds of Mephit: Air (Elemental Plane of Air; fly 60 ft. perfect, AC 17, Init +7): 15-ft. cone of dust and grit 1d8, Reflex DC 12 half; blur 1/hour, gust of wind 1/day (DC 14); heals in moving air. Dust (Plane of Air; fly 50 ft. perfect, AC 17): 10-ft. cone of irritating particles 1d4, Reflex DC 12 half, failure means itching skin and burning eyes for -4 AC and -2 on attacks for 3 rounds; blur 1/hour, wind wall 1/day (DC 15); heals in an arid, dusty place. Earth (Plane of Earth; AC 16, Str 17, fly 40 ft. average): 15-ft. cone of rock shards 1d8, Reflex DC 13 half; soften earth and stone 1/day; change size 1/hour (as enlarge person on itself); heals underground or buried to the waist in earth. Fire (Plane of Fire — the reference column above): 15-ft. cone 1d8 fire, Reflex DC 12 half; scorching ray 1/hour, heat metal 1/day; immune to fire, vulnerable to cold; heals touching a flame. Ice (Plane of Air; AC 18, immune cold, vulnerable fire): 10-ft. cone of ice shards 1d4 cold, Reflex DC 12 half, with the same -4 AC / -2 attack penalty for 3 rounds unless immune to cold; magic missile 1/hour, chill metal 1/day (DC 14); heals touching ice or at 32 degrees F or below. Magma (Plane of Fire; immune fire, vulnerable cold): 10-ft. cone of magma 1d4 fire, Reflex DC 12 half, with the same 3-round penalty unless immune to fire; pyrotechnics 1/day (DC 14, using itself as the fire source unharmed); change shape 1/hour into a pool of lava 3 feet across and 6 inches deep, damage reduction improving to 20/magic, unable to attack but able to seep through cracks at speed 10 ft. and ignite flammables by touch; heals touching magma, lava or a torch-sized flame. Ooze (Plane of Water; swim 30 ft., Str 14, AC 16): 10-ft. cone of caustic liquid 1d4 acid, Reflex DC 13 half, same 3-round penalty unless immune to acid; acid arrow 1/hour, stinking cloud 1/day (DC 15); heals in a wet or muddy place. Salt (Plane of Earth; Str 17, AC 16): 10-ft. cone of salt crystals 1d4, Reflex DC 13 half, same 3-round penalty; glitterdust 1/hour (DC 14), and 1/day it draws the moisture from a 20-foot radius around itself for 2d8 damage (Fortitude DC 14 half), plant and aquatic creatures taking a -2 penalty on the save; heals in an arid place; sarcastic and loathes moisture. Steam (Plane of Fire; immune fire, vulnerable cold): 10-ft. cone of steam 1d4 fire, Reflex DC 12 half, same 3-round penalty unless immune to fire; blur 1/hour, and 1/day a rainstorm of boiling water over a 20-foot square for 2d6 fire damage (Reflex DC 14 half); heals touching boiling water or in a hot, humid place; bossy, ego-driven, and unlike other mephits it rushes eagerly into a fight. Water (Plane of Water; swim 30 ft., Str 14): 15-ft. cone of caustic liquid 1d8 acid, Reflex DC 13 half; acid arrow 1/hour, stinking cloud 1/day (DC 15); heals in rain or submerged to the waist; jaunty and relentlessly funny at everyone else's expense. Every kind is Challenge Rating 3, Small, usually neutral, with damage reduction 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 2, and the summon mephit ability.

Skills: Ooze and water mephits have a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. Such a mephit can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered, and can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: Ant and centaur wedded under one brown-red carapace, the formians raise hive-cities on the ordered planes and spill out of them by law and by conquest. Every one of them thinks with the queen: what a scout sees, the whole city knows before the scout has finished seeing it. They do not raid. They annex, and they keep what they annex.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: The labourers are small; warriors and drivers stand as tall as a man; the helmed marshals are bigger than a warhorse; and the queen is a mountain of chitin that never stirs.
Durability: Warriors and everything above them are well plated in carapace, and the marshals and the queen close their own wounds even as they take them.
Defenses: Poison cannot touch them, nor cold, nor any stone-glance. Lightning, flame and shattering sound they largely shrug aside. Spells slide off a warrior, slide off a marshal more surely, and glance from the queen almost entirely.
Speed: Swift on the ground and tireless — a warrior runs down a man, a marshal runs down a horse. The queen cannot move at all, and must be carried if she must be moved.
Might: Claw, mandible and a sting that leaves the limb weak and useless — the marshal's sting wrecks the hand's quickness instead, and it wets its javelins from that same sting. The drivers take a mind rather than a body, and set the stolen body on you.
Mind: Ordered past all reason. Labourers are simple, warriors are clever soldiers, drivers are cunning, marshals are genuine individuals with wants of their own — and the queen is wiser than most kings.
Disposition: Lawful and unfeeling, neither cruel nor kind. They seek to subdue everything they meet, and the least threat to hive or queen brings all of them at once, to the death.
Bane: Chaos maddens the marshals: put a truly chaotic thing in front of one and it will abandon good tactics to destroy that first. Bait it so, and you choose the ground instead of it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Warriors come in ranks and strike with claw, bite and sting all together, moving as one creature — no flanking them, no surprising them, no picking off a straggler. The drivers hang back and throw a stolen slave at you before they will lift a claw. A marshal commands from the front, wards its own against chaos, calls down a word of law that flattens a line of men, and steps away the moment it is pressed. The queen never fights; she looses spells from her chamber and sends everything that walks.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Kill one and you have insulted the whole city. Decide that before you draw, not after.
• The sting withers the arm. Carry the strong cordial, not the pretty one.
• Ask for the one in the bronze helm. Anything below it cannot answer you even if it wishes to.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Speech is possible, but only upward. Labourers and warriors have no voice at all — they answer the queen's thinking, not yours. Find a marshal in its bronze helm: it speaks the common tongue, it keeps a bargain to the letter, and it will trade fairly. It will also enter you in its census.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe, met in numbers

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Lawful, Extraplanar) — formian warrior as the reference
Initiative: +3
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (+3 Dex, +5 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+7
Attack: Sting +7 melee (2d4+3 plus poison)
Full Attack: Sting +7 melee (2d4+3 plus poison) and 2 claws +5 melee (1d6+1) and bite +5 melee (1d4+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison
Special Qualities: Hive mind, immunity to poison, petrification, and cold, resistance to electricity 10, fire 10, and sonic 10, spell resistance 18
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +5
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 16, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 11
Skills: Climb +10, Hide +10, Jump +14, Listen +8, Move Silently +10 (+3 following tracks), Tumble +12
Feats: Dodge, Multiattack
Environment: A lawful-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary, team (2-4), or troop (6-11)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always lawful neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 5-8 levels (Medium); 9-12 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Formians are generally aggressive, seeking to subdue all they encounter. If they perceive even the slightest threat to their hive-city or to their queen, they attack immediately and fight to the death. Any formian also attacks immediately if ordered to do so by a superior. A formian's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Hive Mind (Ex): All formians within 50 miles of their queen are in constant communication. If one is aware of a particular danger, they all are. If one in a group is not flat-footed, none of them are. No formian in a group is considered flanked unless all of them are.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 14, initial and secondary damage 1d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based. (Taskmaster DC 15, 1d6 Str; myrmarch DC 20, 2d6 Dex.)

Warrior: Warriors communicate through the hive mind to convey battle plans and make reports to their commanders. They cannot speak otherwise. A warrior is about 5 feet long and about 4 1/2 feet high at the front, and weighs about 180 pounds. Warriors are wicked combatants, using claws, bite, and a poisonous sting all at once, attacking through the hive mind with coordinated and extremely efficient tactics.

The Five Castes: Worker — Small, Challenge Rating 1/2, AC 17, Init +2, bite +3 melee (1d4+1), Str 13 Int 6, no special attacks; cannot speak but conveys simple concepts by body movement and talks freely through the hive mind; hands fit only for labour; about 3 feet long and 60 pounds; advances 2-3 levels (Medium). Warrior — Medium, Challenge Rating 3, the reference column above. Taskmaster — Medium, Challenge Rating 7, AC 19, Init +7, sting +10 melee (2d4+4 plus poison) and 2 claws +8 melee (1d6+2), Str 18 Wis 16 Cha 19, spell resistance 21, telepathy 100 ft., dominate monster and a dominated creature; it communicates only telepathically and feeds on the mental energies of those it dominates; advances 7-9 levels (Medium), 10-12 levels (Large). Myrmarch — Large, Challenge Rating 10, AC 28, Init +8, sting +15 melee (2d4+4 plus poison) and bite +13 melee (2d6+2) or javelin +15/+10 ranged (1d6+4) coated in its own venom, Str 19 Int 16, fast healing 2, spell resistance 25, spell-like abilities; the elite of formian society, true individuals with goals and creative thought, each wearing a bronze helm of office, speaking Formian and Common, and singleminded in destroying any chaotic creature; its claws are like hands and serve no combat purpose; advances 13-18 levels (Large), 19-24 levels (Huge). Queen — Large, Challenge Rating 17, speed 0 ft., AC 23, no attacks, Str and Dex nil, Con 20 Int 20 Wis 20 Cha 21, Fort +19 Will +19 (no Reflex save), fast healing 2, spell resistance 30, telepathy; she cannot move and does not fight, but casts arcane spells as a 17th-level sorcerer and wields a broad list of lawful spell-like abilities; a hive holds 1 queen plus 100-400 workers, 11-40 warriors, 4-7 taskmasters each with a dominated creature, and 5-8 myrmarchs; advances 21-30 levels (Huge), 31-40 levels (Gargantuan).

Cure Serious Wounds (Sp): Eight workers together can heal a creature's wounds as though using the cure serious wounds spell (caster level 7th). This is a full-round action for all eight workers.

Make Whole (Sp): Three workers together can repair an object as though using the make whole spell (caster level 7th). This is a full-round action for all three workers.

Dominate Monster (Su): A taskmaster can use a dominate monster ability as the spell from a 10th-level caster (Will DC 17 negates), although the subject may be of any kind and may be up to Large size. Creatures that successfully save cannot be affected by the same taskmaster's dominate monster ability for 24 hours. A single taskmaster can dominate up to four subjects at a time. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Dominated Creature (Ex): A taskmaster is never encountered alone. One dominated nonformian creature always accompanies it (choose or determine randomly any creature of Challenge Rating 4).

Spell-Like Abilities (Myrmarch): At will—charm monster (DC 17), clairaudience/clairvoyance, detect chaos, detect thoughts (DC 15), magic circle against chaos, greater teleport; 1/day—dictum (DC 20), order's wrath (DC 17). Caster level 12th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities (Queen): At will—calm emotions (DC 17), charm monster (DC 19), clairaudience/clairvoyance, detect chaos, detect thoughts, dictum (DC 22), divination, hold monster (DC 20), magic circle against chaos, order's wrath (DC 19), shield of law (DC 23), true seeing. Caster level 17th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spells (Queen): The queen casts arcane spells as a 17th-level sorcerer. Typical spells known (6/8/7/7/7/7/6/6/4, base save DC 15 + spell level): 0—acid splash, arcane mark, daze, detect magic, light, mage hand, read magic, resistance, touch of fatigue; 1st—comprehend languages, identify, mage armor, magic missile, shield; 2nd—hypnotic pattern, invisibility, protection from arrows, resist energy, scorching ray; 3rd—dispel magic, heroism, nondetection, slow; 4th—confusion, detect scrying, black tentacles, scrying; 5th—cone of cold, dismissal, teleport, wall of force; 6th—analyze dweomer, geas/quest, repulsion; 7th—summon monster VII, vision, waves of exhaustion; 8th—prismatic wall, temporal stasis.

Telepathy (Su): The queen can communicate telepathically with any intelligent creature within 50 miles whose presence she is aware of. A taskmaster has telepathy out to 100 feet.

lore.summary: A blue-green shell the length of a boat's plank, pierced with vents at either end, and out of them come seven stalks — four with paddles, two with claws, and one that carries the head. Tojanidas belong to the plane of water and reach us by deep pools, springs and sea-caves, where they hunt, hoard whatever bright rubbish drifts by, and talk without end about food.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized when grown. The young are smaller than a shield, the elders longer than a tall man and heavier than a pony.
Durability: Far harder to put down than its bulk suggests, and the elders are as tough as anything that swims.
Defenses: The shell turns blows like good plate. Acid and cold cannot touch it at all; lightning and fire trouble it little. It looks out of every vent at once, so there is no such thing as coming at its back.
Speed: A crawl on land — slower than a man walking — and appallingly swift in water, where it can run flat out in a straight line without tiring.
Might: A crushing bite and two clawed stalks. What it catches it holds, and hauls away alone into deep water while you are still looking for it.
Mind: As clever as an ordinary man, and talkative in the tongue of water — though the only subject it truly warms to is dinner.
Disposition: Neutral, curious, neither friend nor enemy until it decides you are meat. It keeps whatever glittering leavings the current brings it.
Bane: Ashore it can barely move. Its ink is a screen and a blinding jet, not a weapon; get it onto stone and it is a crawling thing with a good shell and nothing else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes out of dark water, bites, and holds — seizing one of you and swimming off with the catch while the rest of the party stands blinking in a spreading cloud of ink. Out of the water it squirts that ink in a stream straight into the eyes instead. It fights blinded about as well as most men fight sighted, and it does not let go of what it has taken.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It takes one of you and swims. Rope yourselves together before anybody goes in.
• Fight it on stone if you can lure it there. On land it crawls.
• Acid and frost are wasted, and so is circling behind it — it has no behind.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I shared a meal with one in a sea-cave, in the tongue of water. It asked what I had eaten, what my horse had eaten, and what I supposed a drowned man tasted like. Amiable company, all of it — right up until the tide turned and it began to consider its last question practically.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar, Water) — adult tojanida as the reference
Initiative: +1
Speed: 10 ft. (2 squares), swim 90 ft.
Armor Class: 23 (+1 Dex, +12 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 22
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+10
Attack: Bite +10 melee (2d8+3)
Full Attack: Bite +10 melee (2d8+3) and 2 claws +5 melee (1d6+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, ink cloud
Special Qualities: All-around vision, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to acid and cold, resistance to electricity 10 and fire 10
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +6
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 13, Con 15, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 9
Skills: Diplomacy +1, Escape Artist +11, Hide +11, Knowledge (the planes) +6, Listen +11, Search +14, Sense Motive +11, Spot +15, Survival +1 (+3 on other planes and following tracks), Swim +11, Use Rope +1 (+3 with bindings)
Feats: Blind-Fight, Dodge, Power Attack
Environment: Elemental Plane of Water
Organization: Solitary or clutch (2-4)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 8-14 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Appearance: A tojanida's shell is blue-green in colour. Inside the shell is a fleshy body from which extend seven stalks. Four of these stalks have paddles for locomotion, two are tipped with claws, and one bears the creature's head. Eight vents in the shell, four at each end, allow the tojanida to thrust its stalks out in whatever configuration it finds convenient. Tojanidas speak Aquan and can be loquacious, but usually only on the subject of food.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a tojanida must hit with a bite or claw attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. Underwater, a tojanida can tow a grabbed victim of its own size or smaller at its swim speed (but it cannot run). A favourite tactic is to grab a single opponent, then withdraw, hauling the opponent away from its allies.

Ink Cloud (Ex): A tojanida can emit a spherical cloud of jet-black ink with a radius of 30 feet once per minute as a free action. The effect is otherwise similar to fog cloud cast by an individual of a level equal to the tojanida's own. Out of water, the ink emerges in a stream up to 30 feet long, which a tojanida can squirt into an opponent's eyes. The affected creature must succeed on a Reflex save or be blinded for 1 round. The save DC is 13 against a juvenile, 15 against an adult, and 21 against an elder. The save DCs are Constitution based.

All-Around Vision (Ex): The multiple apertures in a tojanida's shell allow it to look in any direction, bestowing a +4 racial bonus on Spot and Search checks. Opponents gain no flanking bonuses when attacking a tojanida.

The Three Ages: Juvenile — up to 25 years old, Small, Challenge Rating 3, shell about 3 feet long and about 60 pounds; AC 22 (touch 12), attack bite +6 melee (2d6+2) and 2 claws +1 melee (1d4+1), Str 14 Con 15, saves Fort +5 Ref +4 Will +4, feats Blind-Fight and Dodge, ink cloud save DC 13; advances 4-6 levels (Small). Adult — aged 26 to 80, Medium, Challenge Rating 5, shell about 6 feet long and about 220 pounds; the reference column above, ink cloud save DC 15. Elder — up to 150 years old, Large, Challenge Rating 9, shell about 9 feet long and about 500 pounds; AC 24 (touch 10), reach 10 ft./5 ft., attack bite +20 melee (4d6+6) and 2 claws +15 melee (1d8+3), base attack/grapple +15/+25, Str 22 Con 19, saves Fort +13 Ref +10 Will +10, feats Alertness, Blind-Fight, Cleave, Dodge, Improved Sunder and Power Attack, ink cloud save DC 21; advances 16-24 levels (Large), 25-45 levels (Huge). All three share speed 10 ft. and swim 90 ft., all-around vision, immunity to acid and cold, resistance to electricity 10 and fire 10, and are always neutral.

Skills: A tojanida has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: A serpent-thing out of the plane of raw life, longer than a man is tall and no heavier than a child, with one clawed limb and a lashing tail. Wherever a ravid drifts, the dead things about it wake — chairs, spears, ladders, the armour on its stand — and shamble after it in a ragged honour guard. It wanders our world without aim, and the guard wanders with it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized — a long drifting serpent-shape with almost no weight to it.
Durability: Not a hardy thing in itself. The guard around it is what does the enduring.
Defenses: Its hide is armour such as no living creature ought to wear: blade and arrow find scarcely anywhere to land on it. Fire does not touch it at all.
Speed: A slow crawl on the ground, and flight of perfect ease in the air — it can stop or resume that flight with a thought, and falls helpless if the flight is taken from it.
Might: Tail and claw carry the touch of raw life. On living flesh that touch is no worse than a startling tingle; on anything dead that walks it is ruin. The real blow is always the furniture.
Mind: Dim, aimless, without speech. It does not scheme, cannot be reasoned with, and is not clever enough to use well the things it wakes.
Disposition: Neutral, and wholly harmless until struck. It fights only in its own defence — and then the whole room fights for it.
Bane: Its own lash barely troubles a living man, so the danger is entirely the woken objects. Choose bare ground and it has nothing to raise; and never waste flame on it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only when attacked, and badly. It hovers back and lashes with tail and claw while, moment by moment, one more dead thing within a stone's throw stands up and comes at you — the table, the door, the mail on the stand. It gives them no orders worth the name. It simply keeps waking more of them for as long as you keep at it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it in an empty cellar. In a furnished room, the room is the enemy.
• Fire is wasted on it. So is the torch you were about to throw.
• Its lash cannot really hurt a living man. Wear it, and kill the serpent rather than the chairs.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing in it to talk to. I tried — three tongues and then hand-signs — while a coat-rack beat upon my shield. It has no speech and hardly a thought behind the eyes. Mark this, though: it will not start the fight. The kindest parley with a ravid is to back out and shut the door.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Extraplanar)
Initiative: +4
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 60 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 25 (+15 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 25
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+4
Attack: Tail slap +4 melee (1d6+1 plus positive energy) or tail touch +4 melee touch (positive energy)
Full Attack: Tail slap +4 melee (1d6+1 plus positive energy) and claw +2 melee (1d4 plus positive energy); or tail touch +4 melee touch (positive energy) and claw touch +2 melee touch (positive energy)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Positive energy lash, animate objects
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., flight, immunity to fire
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +3, Will +4
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 10, Con 13, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 14
Skills: Escape Artist +6, Hide +6, Listen +7, Move Silently +6, Spot +7, Survival +7, Use Rope +0 (+2 with bindings)
Feats: Improved Initiative, Multiattack
Environment: Positive Energy Plane
Organization: Solitary (1 plus at least 1 animated object)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 4 levels (Medium); 5-9 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Description: Ravids are creatures from the Positive Energy Plane. These bizarre entities imbue creatures with energy by their touch and animate lifeless objects around them. Ravids that make their way to the Material Plane wander about aimlessly, followed by the objects to which they have given life. A ravid is about 7 feet long and weighs about 75 pounds.

Combat: Ravids fight only in self-defence. A ravid itself is not very powerful but is always accompanied by at least one animated object that defends it.

Positive Energy Lash (Su): A ravid can make a touch attack or hit with a claw or tail slap attack to infuse a target with positive energy. The energy produces an unpleasant tingle in living creatures, and against undead foes (even incorporeal ones) it deals 2d10 points of damage.

Animate Objects (Su): Once per round, a random object within 20 feet of a ravid animates as though by the spell animate objects (caster level 20th). These objects defend the ravid to the best of their ability, but the ravid isn't intelligent enough to employ elaborate tactics with them.

Flight (Su): A ravid can cease or resume flight as a free action. A ravid that loses this ability falls and can perform only a single action (either a move action or an attack action) each round.

Feats: A ravid has the Multiattack feat even though it does not have the requisite three natural weapons.

lore.summary: A severed head that will not lie still: a little larger than a man's own, with leathery bat-wings where the ears were, tentacles writhing from chin and scalp, and a mouth of long fangs. Vargouilles come from the evil planes and roost in clusters and mobs in caves and ruined vaults, hanging in the roof-dark until something warm walks beneath them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — no bigger than a head, on wings far broader than the head that carries them.
Durability: Frail. One good blow finishes it. They simply never come at you one at a time.
Defenses: None worth the name — no hide, no ward, no resistance to anything you are likely to be carrying.
Speed: Flies well and quietly, and hides in the dark far better than a thing with a face has any right to.
Might: A jagged bite whose venom keeps the wound from closing by salve or by prayer; a shriek that roots a man where he stands; and, for anyone so rooted, the kiss.
Mind: Dim, but not dumb. They speak the tongue of the lower planes, they roost and hunt together, and they know exactly what the kiss is for.
Disposition: Wholly evil and wholly patient. They do not want your purse, and they do not especially want you dead. They want another of themselves.
Bane: The shriek takes only those who both hear it and clearly see the creature. Look away, or fight them in pitch dark, and each is merely a biting head. A cry that fails against a man is spent on him by that same one for a day and a night.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They drop from the roof-dark together, shrieking. Whoever the cry takes stands paralysed with terror; while the rest of the party is busy, the others make for the frozen ones and kiss them. Any that cannot freeze a man bites instead, and that bite will not be closed by ordinary healing. They shriek again on new faces, since a cry already broken against a man is no use to that vargouille again.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Look away, or put out the lights. It cannot freeze what cannot see it.
• The bite will not close by salve or prayer. Carry something that draws venom out.
• If one of yours is kissed: get him into the sun, which halts it, then find a cure for sickness before a day is out. Do not wait for his hair to fall.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: No. I tried it once, in the tongue of the lower planes, and it answered me — they do speak — with the word for 'soon'. There is nothing it wants of you but your head on its own wings. Strike first, and strike the ones hanging quiet in the roof before the ones already screaming.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor horror, met in flocks

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Outsider (Evil, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +1
Speed: Fly 30 ft. (good) (6 squares)
Armor Class: 12 (+1 size, +1 Dex), touch 11, flat-footed 11
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/-3
Attack: Bite +3 melee (1d4 plus poison)
Full Attack: Bite +3 melee (1d4 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Shriek, kiss, poison
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +3
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 13, Con 12, Int 5, Wis 12, Cha 8
Skills: Hide +11, Intimidate +3, Listen +5, Move Silently +7, Spot +5
Feats: Stealthy, Weapon Finesse (bonus)
Environment: An evil-aligned plane
Organization: Cluster (2-5) or mob (6-11)
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 2-3 levels (Small)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Description: A vargouille is slightly larger than a human head, about 18 inches high, with a wingspan of 4 feet. It weighs about 10 pounds. Vargouilles speak Infernal.

Combat: Vargouilles attack by biting with their jagged teeth. Their special attacks make them even more dangerous. A vargouille's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as evil-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Shriek (Su): Instead of biting, a vargouille can open its distended mouth and let out a terrible shriek. Those within 60 feet (except other vargouilles) who hear the shriek and can clearly see the creature must succeed on a DC 12 Fortitude save or be paralyzed with fear for 2d4 rounds or until the monster attacks them, goes out of range, or leaves their sight. A paralyzed creature is susceptible to the vargouille's kiss. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same vargouille's shriek for 24 hours. The shriek is a mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +1 racial bonus.

Kiss (Su): A vargouille can kiss a paralyzed target with a successful melee touch attack. An affected opponent must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or begin a terrible transformation that turns the creature into a vargouille within 24 hours (and often much sooner; roll 1d6 separately for each phase of the transformation). First, over a period of 1d6 hours, all the victim's hair falls out. Within another 1d6 hours thereafter, the ears grow into leathery wings, tentacles sprout on the chin and scalp, and the teeth become long, pointed fangs. During the next 1d6 hours, the victim takes Intelligence drain and Charisma drain equal to 1 point per hour (to a minimum of 3). The transformation is complete 1d6 hours later, when the head breaks free of the body (which promptly dies) and becomes a vargouille. This transformation is interrupted by sunlight, and even a daylight spell can delay death, but to reverse the transformation requires remove disease. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +4 racial bonus.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 12 or be unable to recover the damage of the vargouille's bite either naturally or by magic. A neutralize poison or heal spell removes the effect, while delay poison allows magical healing. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +1 racial bonus.

lore.summary: A serpent of the open sky, born where there is no ground at all. Wings and a long whipping tail carry it in any direction it pleases — backward as readily as forward, and at full speed either way. It hunts and scavenges the winds of the elemental air, and where the world wears thin at high passes and torn gates, it comes through and claims that air as its own.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — longer than a tall man from beak to tail-tip, and most of that is tail.
Durability: Lean and light-boned; it does not mean to be struck, and has little to spare when it is.
Defenses: Acid, lightning and poison do nothing to it whatever, and it shrugs off a good part of cold and flame. Its hide is tougher than so slight a thing has any right to.
Speed: Flies faster than a horse gallops and turns on nothing at all — up, back, sideways, without losing a stride.
Might: A lash of lightning loosed from the tail, again and again, and a beak that shears when it deigns to close.
Mind: As sharp as an ordinary man, though it cares for little beyond its territory and its next meal.
Disposition: Fiercely territorial and forever hungry. It goes for near enough anything it meets, to eat it or to drive it off.
Bane: It is frail and it must have a clear line to loose that lightning. Break the line, or ground it — a net, a good bow, anything that spoils its dance settles the matter fast. Cold and flame still bite it; only in part, but they bite.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at a distance, lightning cracking from the tail-tip once and again while it keeps well out of reach, sweeping past on the wing and never once hanging still to be answered. Only when a rival will not yield, or a meal is nearly finished, does it come in to bite — and even then it strikes and is gone before you have turned to face it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The lightning comes off the tail, not the head. Watch the wrong end and you will watch the rest from the ground.
• Nothing you own will turn that ray. Do not try. Break the line of sight instead — rock, cloud, anything solid.
• It cannot be poisoned and it drinks acid. Bring cold, bring flame, or bring a net.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have spoken the air-tongue to one from behind a rock, and it heard me out — they are no fools, only seldom talkative. Its answer was that the sky was its own. Offer meat, then leave its air. Argue, and you are arguing with lightning.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Air, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +5
Speed: Fly 60 ft. (perfect) (12 squares)
Armor Class: 21 (+5 Dex, +6 natural), touch 15, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+9
Attack: Electricity ray +12 ranged touch (2d8) or bite +12 melee (1d8+3)
Full Attack: Electricity ray +12 ranged touch (2d8) or bite +12 melee (1d8+3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Electricity ray
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to acid, electricity, and poison, resistance to cold 10 and fire 10
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +10, Will +6
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 21, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 13
Skills: Diplomacy +3, Escape Artist +15, Knowledge (the planes) +10, Listen +11, Move Silently +15, Search +10, Sense Motive +11, Spot +11, Survival +11 (+13 following tracks, +13 on the Plane of Air), Use Rope +5 (+7 with bindings)
Feats: Dodge, Flyby Attack, Weapon Finesse
Environment: Elemental Plane of Air
Organization: Solitary or clutch (2-4)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 8-14 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Electricity Ray (Su): An arrowhawk can fire this ray once per round, with a range of 50 feet. An adult arrowhawk's ray is a ranged touch attack at +12 that deals 2d8 points of electricity damage; a juvenile's deals 2d6 and an elder's 2d8 at +19.

Combat: Arrowhawks are extremely territorial and always hungry. They attack almost any other creature they meet, seeking a meal or trying to drive away a rival. The primary mode of attack is an electricity ray, fired from the tail. The creature also bites, but it prefers to stay out of reach.

Perfect Flight (Ex): By twisting its body and varying the cadence of its wingbeats, an arrowhawk can fly at top speed in any direction — 60 feet with perfect maneuverability. It has no land speed at all.

Immunities and Resistances (Ex): Arrowhawks are immune to acid, electricity, and poison, and have resistance to cold 10 and fire 10. They see in the dark to 60 feet.

Juvenile, Adult, and Elder Arrowhawks: The block above is the adult (11 to 40 years old), about 10 feet long from beak to tail with a 15-foot wingspan and a weight of about 100 pounds. A juvenile (1 to 10 years old) is Small, about 5 feet long with a 7-foot wingspan and 20 pounds: AC 20 (touch 16, flat-footed 15), Base Attack/Grapple +3/+0, electricity ray +9 ranged touch (2d6) or bite +9 melee (1d6+1), Fort +4, Ref +8, Will +4, Str 12, Dex 21, Con 12, feats Dodge and Weapon Finesse, CR 3. An elder (41 to 75 years old) is Large, about 20 feet long with a 30-foot wingspan and 800 pounds: AC 22 (touch 14, flat-footed 17), Base Attack/Grapple +15/+25, electricity ray +19 ranged touch (2d8) or bite +21 melee (2d6+9), space/reach 10 ft./5 ft., Fort +12, Ref +14, Will +10, Str 22, Dex 21, Con 16, feats Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Flyby Attack, Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (bite), CR 8.

Language: Arrowhawks speak Auran, but they are not usually talkative creatures.

lore.summary: Nothing in Limbo holds a shape, and this is the part of Limbo that hunts. It has claws, or pincers, or fangs, or wet coiling arms — never twice the same, never the same for as long as you can bear to watch. It weighs about what a man weighs and can be anything that weight will make. Where raw chaos leaks into the world, it follows the leak through.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — near enough the bulk of a man, and the bulk is the only thing about it that keeps still.
Durability: Hardier than it looks, and never in one shape long enough for a killing blow to find anything worth killing.
Defenses: No thrust ever finds a vital part, because it keeps none. Magic slides off it as often as not, and no spell will fix its form — turn it to stone and it is stone for a heartbeat, then it is not.
Speed: Slow. Shambling. It has never in its existence needed to hurry.
Might: Its blows are feeble things that scarcely mark good mail. The horror is entirely in what they leave behind.
Mind: As clever as an ordinary man, and wholly mute — it has never had a tongue and would not know the use of one.
Disposition: It comes on and keeps coming. There is nothing in it to bargain with, frighten, or appeal to.
Bane: Reach, and nothing else. It is slow, its blows are feeble, and a spear, a bow or a barred door beats it outright — which matters more than anything else in this book, because what its touch does has no undoing on the field. The flesh unmakes itself: bone goes soft, hands will not close on sword or scroll, feet spread like tallow, and the pain is such that a man swings at whoever stands nearest and does not know the face. Every moment spent so scrapes another sliver of sense away, and when the last sliver goes he stands up as one of them. Sheer will can claw the shape back for a breath, and again when it slips, and again — I watched a good sergeant do it four times and lose the fifth. Stone-skinning and shape-changing charms only pin the form and cure nothing; it takes a true restoring, or a healing that mends the whole man, to lift it, and a second restoring for the wits it ate.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It shambles in and strikes with whatever it has grown that hour — claws, pincers, a coil of something wet — twice and never a third time, because its own churning will not let it manage the coordination. It does not flank, feint, or flee. It simply closes, touches, and waits for the touch to do the work, and it climbs a sheer wall to reach you as easily as it crosses a floor.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Long weapons. Spear, polearm, boar-spear — anything that keeps its limbs off you. Your good sword is too short to be brave with.
• If a companion is touched, take his blade first and his weight second. He will swing at you and mean it.
• Stone-skinning cures nothing. It only holds the poor wretch together while you ride for someone who can restore what was taken.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is no talking to it. It has the wit of a man and none of a man's mind, and no mouth to answer with in any case. I tried once, at a torn place in the high rocks, more from habit than hope. It came on through my words the way water comes through a sieve. Kill it at the length of a spear.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave horror

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Outsider (Chaotic, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 16 (+1 Dex, +5 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +8/+10
Attack: Claw +10 melee (1d3+2 plus corporeal instability)
Full Attack: 2 claws +10 melee (1d3+2 plus corporeal instability)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Corporeal instability
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to critical hits and transformation, spell resistance 15
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +7, Will +6
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 13, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 10, Cha 10
Skills: Climb +13, Escape Artist +12, Hide +12, Jump +9, Listen +11, Search +11, Spot +11, Survival +0 (+2 following tracks), Tumble +14, Use Rope +1 (+3 with bindings)
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative, Mobility
Environment: Plane of Limbo
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Always chaotic neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9-12 levels (Medium); 13-24 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: For all its fearsome appearances, whether it has claws, fangs, pincers, tentacles, or spines, a chaos beast does little physical harm. Regardless of form, the creature seems unable to manage more than two attacks per round. Its continual transmutations prevent the coordination needed to do more.

Corporeal Instability (Su): A blow from a chaos beast against a living creature can cause a terrible transformation. The creature must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or become a spongy, amorphous mass. Unless the victim manages to control the effect, its shape melts, flows, writhes, and boils. The save DC is Constitution-based. An affected creature is unable to hold or use any item. Clothing, armor, rings, and helmets become useless. Large items worn or carried — armor, backpacks, even shirts — hamper more than help, reducing the victim's Dexterity score by 4. Soft or misshapen feet and legs reduce speed to 10 feet or one-quarter normal, whichever is less. Searing pain courses along the nerves, so strong that the victim cannot act coherently. The victim cannot cast spells or use magic items, and it attacks blindly, unable to distinguish friend from foe (-4 penalty on attack rolls and a 50% miss chance, regardless of the attack roll). Each round the victim spends in an amorphous state causes 1 point of Wisdom drain from mental shock. If the victim's Wisdom score falls to 0, it becomes a chaos beast. A victim can regain its own shape by taking a standard action to attempt a DC 15 Charisma check (this check DC does not vary for a chaos beast of different power or ability scores). A success reestablishes the creature's normal form for 1 minute. On a failure, the victim can still repeat this check each round until successful. Corporeal instability is not a disease or a curse and so is hard to remove. A shapechange or stoneskin spell does not cure an afflicted creature but fixes its form for the duration of the spell. A restoration, heal, or greater restoration spell removes the affliction (a separate restoration is necessary to restore any drained points of Wisdom).

Immunity to Transformation (Ex): No mortal magic can permanently affect or fix a chaos beast's form. Effects such as polymorphing or petrification force the creature into a new shape, but at the start of its next turn it immediately returns to its mutable form as a free action.

Chaotic Attacks (Ex): A chaos beast's claw attacks, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as chaotic-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Immunity to Critical Hits (Ex): A chaos beast has no fixed anatomy and no vital organs to strike, so critical hits simply do not apply to it. It also has spell resistance 15 and sees in the dark to 60 feet.

Form and Speech: The horrific creatures known as chaos beasts have mutable, ever-changing forms. A chaos beast's dimensions vary, but it always weighs about 200 pounds. Chaos beasts do not speak.

monsters.name: Pseudodragon
monsters.senses: Blindsense 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision

lore.summary: A dragon the size of a cat, red-brown as autumn bracken, with a bee's sting on the end of a long tail. They keep to old temperate woods, sun themselves high in the branches, and go all but invisible against bark and leaf when they would rather not be found. Proud out of all proportion to their measure, and worth every ounce of that pride.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — a body no longer than your forearm, and a tail longer than the body.
Durability: Slight. A careless boot would do it real harm, and it knows this better than you do.
Defenses: It cannot be lulled to sleep or held fast, and spells turn aside from it far more often than anything so small has a right to expect. Its hide takes the colour of whatever it rests against, and in a wood it simply ceases to be there.
Speed: Poor on the ground, quick and neat on the wing — it flits between branches like a swift.
Might: Almost none. A bite you would take from a badger, and the sting; the sting is the whole of its argument.
Mind: As clever as an ordinary man and far better mannered. It hears you plainly and answers inside your own head.
Disposition: Good-hearted, playful, vain, and fond of warmth, company and a decent supper. It starts no quarrels and holds no grudges long.
Bane: It cannot really hurt you and it knows it, so it hides or flies rather than fights. Its venom only puts a man to sleep — the danger is not the sting but waking somewhere it chose to leave you. And if you have driven a pseudodragon to sting you at all, the fault is yours; ask what you did.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only when cornered or in defence of its clutch, and then from the air: a dart in, a flick of the tail, and away into the leaves where its hide takes the colour of the bark and you lose it entirely. The sting carries a sleep a man cannot shrug off. It does not stay to finish the sleeper — it goes and finds better company. Dark is no cover from it either; it hears and scents its way about well enough that hiding is wasted effort.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never call one a lizard, a hatchling, or anybody's pet. It is a dragon, small, and it will make you feel the difference.
• Roast fowl and a warm hearth buy more than coin does. They have no use for money and every use for supper.
• If one flies with you, heed its warnings without arguing. It hears and smells what you cannot, and mine was never once wrong.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Speak aloud and it answers inside your skull; the little ones follow the common tongue and the elf-tongue both. Bring roast fowl, address it as a dragon and never as a pet, and it will guide you a day's walk through wood no map has held. One flew with me a whole winter. I have not earned better since.

sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A pseudodragon can deliver a vicious bite, but its principal weapon is its sting-equipped tail.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 14, initial damage sleep for 1 minute, secondary damage sleep for 1d3 hours. The save DC is Constitution-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Blindsense (Ex): A pseudodragon can locate creatures within 60 feet by nonvisual means (mostly hearing and scent, but also by noticing vibration and other environmental clues). Opponents the pseudodragon can't actually see still have total concealment against the pseudodragon.

Telepathy (Su): Pseudodragons can communicate telepathically with creatures that speak Common or Sylvan, provided they are within 60 feet. A pseudodragon can also vocalize animal noises.

Skills: Pseudodragons have a chameleonlike ability that grants them a +4 racial bonus on Hide checks. *In forests or overgrown areas, this bonus improves to +8.

Immunities (Ex): A pseudodragon is immune to sleep and paralysis effects, has spell resistance 19, sees in the dark to 60 feet, and has low-light vision.

Size: A pseudodragon has a body about 1 foot long, with a 2-foot tail. It weighs about 7 pounds.

lore.summary: A dragon that took to the sea and wore a mountain out of it. The shell is deep green, the colour of the water it favours, veined with silver like light on a swell; head, legs and tail are lighter green flecked with gold. It is as long as a coasting vessel and heavier than any cargo it will ever sink. It holds a stretch of cold water as its own and expects to be paid for passage through it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a shell like a hill, and a head that takes a rowing-boat whole.
Durability: Enormous. The shell is a wall, and there is a great deal of turtle behind the wall.
Defenses: Natural armour that turns anything short of a siege engine. Fire means nothing to it — not lamp oil, not a wizard's flame, not its own scalding breath — and it cannot be lulled to sleep or held fast.
Speed: Ponderous ashore, a terror in the water; it can run a straight line beneath the waves faster than most ships can flee along the top of them.
Might: Jaws and claws that break planking and men alike, and it snatches a man up in its teeth and takes him down with it. Its breath is a cloud of scalding steam that works as well beneath the water as above it.
Mind: Clever, articulate and greedy. It bargains, it counts, and it hoards like any of its kin.
Disposition: Grasping and territorial rather than cruel. It takes what it believes it is owed, and it believes it is owed a great deal.
Bane: Everything it has is worth less out of the water. Draw it onto a shoal or a beach and half its advantage drains away with the tide. Flame is wasted on it, so bring cold and steel instead. And it is greedy above all — tribute has bought me passage where a fight would have bought me a drowning.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights from underneath. It comes up beneath the keel and rolls the vessel over, then takes the swimmers at leisure, snatching one in its jaws and carrying him down while the rest are still finding the surface. In open water it breathes: a cloud of scalding steam across the deck or through the depths, and men boil in their mail either way. It fights hard for its water and seldom runs, having nowhere else it would rather be.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Pay it. A hoard-gift costs less than a hull, and a hull costs less than the crew.
• Its steam works under the water as well as over it. Going over the rail is not the escape you think it is.
• It comes up from below. If the water beneath the keel goes still and dark, you are already late.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It has the sea-tongue, the dragon-tongue and plain Common, and would far rather be paid than fed. I have bought passage from one twice — coin the first time, a good anchor-chain the second — and both bargains held. But it counts what you give and remembers what you withheld. Come with tribute in hand and no steel in the other.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Dragon turtles are fierce fighters and generally attack any creature that threatens their territory or looks like a potential meal.

Breath Weapon (Su): Cloud of superheated steam 20 feet high, 25 feet wide, and 50 feet long, once every 1d4 rounds, damage 12d6 fire, Reflex DC 21 half; effective both on the surface and underwater. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Capsize (Ex): A submerged dragon turtle that surfaces under a boat or ship less than 20 feet long capsizes the vessel 95% of the time. It has a 50% chance to capsize a vessel from 20 to 60 feet long and a 20% chance to capsize one over 60 feet long.

Snatch (Feat): The dragon turtle can choose to start a grapple when it hits with a claw or bite attack, as though it had the improved grab special attack. If it gets a hold on a creature three or more sizes smaller (Small or less), it squeezes each round for automatic bite or claw damage. A snatched opponent held in the turtle's mouth is not allowed a Reflex save against its breath weapon. The turtle can drop a snatched creature as a free action, or use a standard action to fling it aside; a flung creature travels 1d6 x 10 feet and takes 1d6 points of damage per 10 feet traveled.

Immunities (Ex): A dragon turtle is immune to fire, sleep, and paralysis effects. It has darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, and the scent ability.

Skills: A dragon turtle has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line. *Dragon turtles have a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks when submerged.

Description and Speech: Its rough, deep green shell is much the same color as the deep water the monster favors, and the silver highlights that line the shell resemble light dancing on open water. The turtle's legs, tail, and head are a lighter green, flecked with golden highlights. An adult dragon turtle can measure from 20 to 30 feet from snout to tail, with a shell from 15 to 25 feet in diameter, and can weigh 8,000 to 32,000 pounds. Dragon turtles speak Aquan, Draconic, and Common.

lore.summary: An ogre the way a duke is a farmhand — the same frame and nothing else the same. Skin of light green or pale blue, black hair, curved horns, loose good clothing over light mail. It keeps to cold hills with a handful of its dull cousins to fetch and carry, and it is cultured, patient and cruel. It will have thought carefully about you some while before you ever see it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — head and shoulders above the tallest man, and heavy in proportion.
Durability: Stout, and worse than stout: cut it and the wound knits while you are drawing back. It will pick up a severed arm, press it to the stump, and keep it.
Defenses: Spells fail against it as often as they land. Its flesh mends itself of nearly every hurt — flame and acid are the only wounds it cannot simply shrug closed — and it can wear the shape of any manlike creature from a small one to a giant.
Speed: Quick afoot for its bulk, and it flies well and freely, stopping and starting in the air as it pleases.
Might: A greatsword swung with a giant's arm, and a longbow for the reach. But its true armoury is the magic it was born holding: darkness whenever it likes, vanishing whenever it likes, a charm to turn an enemy into a friend, a sleep, a great cone of killing cold, and a mist-form to leave in.
Mind: Sharp, learned and vain. It plans, it negotiates, and it keeps servants and grudges in about equal number.
Disposition: Lawful in the worst sense — it keeps its word to the letter and shapes the letter to ruin you. Cruel by preference rather than by temper.
Bane: Flame and acid, and truly nothing else; every other hurt it closes before you can strike twice, so bring both to the field or do not come. Beyond that, it will not die for a cause: beaten, it turns to mist and drifts away to try again another year. Whatever you mean to do to it, do it quickly.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens unseen — vanished outright, or behind a darkness of its own making — and softens the party with a charm or a sleep before a blade is drawn. Then the cold, a great cone of it laid across your whole line at once. It comes to the sword only when it must, and it is counting the odds the entire while; the moment they turn, it goes to mist and is gone, and you have made a patient enemy with a long memory and years to spend on it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Flame and acid. Everything else you do to it, it undoes before you have drawn back for the second stroke.
• Ward yourself against cold or stand well apart. One breath of that cone takes a whole rank together.
• It will offer you terms. It always offers terms. Read them like a lawyer and refuse them like a soldier.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks Common as well as any lord and the giant-tongue to its servants, and it will talk gladly — it enjoys talking. I dined with one and came away with my life, an escort short by two men, and a bargain I spent three years regretting. Talk if you must. Promise nothing, and count your people at the door.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

Challenge Rating: 8

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Ogre mages rely on their spell-like abilities, resorting to physical combat only when necessary. When faced with obviously superior forces, they prefer to retreat using gaseous form rather than fight a losing battle.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will - darkness, invisibility; 1/day - charm person (DC 14), cone of cold (DC 18), gaseous form, sleep (DC 14). Caster level 9th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Flight (Su): An ogre mage can cease or resume flight as a free action. While using gaseous form it can fly at its normal speed and has perfect maneuverability.

Change Shape (Su): An ogre mage can assume the form of any Small, Medium, or Large humanoid or giant.

Regeneration (Ex): An ogre mage has regeneration 5: damage dealt to it is normally subdual, healing away swiftly. Fire and acid deal normal damage to an ogre mage. An ogre mage that loses a limb or body part can reattach it by holding the severed member to the stump. Reattachment takes 1 minute. If the head or some other vital organ is severed, it must be reattached within 10 minutes or the creature dies. An ogre mage cannot regrow lost body parts.

Spell Resistance (Ex): An ogre mage has spell resistance 19, and sees in the dark to 60 feet as well as having low-light vision.

Description and Speech: The ogre mage is a more intelligent and dangerous variety of its mundane cousin. An ogre mage stands about 10 feet tall and weighs up to 700 pounds. Its skin varies in color from light green to light blue, and its hair is black or very dark brown. Ogre mages favor loose, comfortable clothing and lightweight armor. Ogre mages speak Giant and Common.

lore.summary: A corpse that would not lie still and cannot stop eating. The ghoul haunts graveyards, crypts and old battlefields, crouching behind stones and bursting out of shallow earth to seize the living. It keeps the tongue it spoke in life and will use it, though hunger has long since eaten the sense out of every word.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Of a man's height and build, shrunken and stooped by the grave.
Durability: No tougher than the corpse it was made from; a good honest blow tells on it.
Defenses: Little but its own hardened hide — yet fear, charm, sleep, poison and sickness all slide off it, and it feels no pain and never tires.
Speed: Quick as a man afoot, and quicker than most at climbing a wall or vaulting a grave fence.
Might: Weak-armed by the measure of living men, but bite and both claws come at once, and every one of them carries the stillness.
Mind: It kept the wits and the tongue it had in life and lost the whole use of them to hunger.
Disposition: Ravenous without cease and evil without exception. It cannot be reasoned with, bargained with, or fed enough.
Bane: Its stiffening touch has no hold on elves whatever. Put one of the fair folk in the front rank and the pack's chief weapon is simply gone.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights from ambush — behind a tombstone, under a cairn slab, up out of loose grave-soil — and comes in low and fast for the legs. Bite and both claws land in the same breath, and each carries a cold that locks a man rigid where he stands. Once one of your company is stiff and staring, the rest of the pack will abandon the fight to gorge on him, which is the only mercy in it. They hunt in gangs and in true packs, and they do not break and run.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Put the elf in front. Their stiffening does nothing at all to the fair folk, and that alone has saved my whole company twice.
• The bite carries a fever that kills slow and buries badly. Burn the wound and find a priest before midnight.
• Never stand and fight over open grave-soil. They come up out of it behind you.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I tried. It answered me in good Common, in the accent of the village down the hill, and did not stop walking towards me while it spoke. There is a mind in there, and the hunger has eaten every part of it that could be reasoned with. Speak if you must; strike while you do.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser horror

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead
Initiative: +2
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 14 (+2 Dex, +2 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+2
Attack: Bite +2 melee (1d6+1 plus paralysis)
Full Attack: Bite +2 melee (1d6+1 plus paralysis) and 2 claws +0 melee (1d3 plus paralysis)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Ghoul fever, paralysis
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., undead traits, +2 turn resistance
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +2, Will +5
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 15, Con —, Int 13, Wis 14, Cha 12
Skills: Balance +6, Climb +5, Hide +6, Jump +5, Move Silently +6, Spot +7
Feats: Multiattack
Environment: Any (Lacedon: any aquatic)
Organization: Solitary, gang (2-4), or pack (7-12)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always chaotic evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 3 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Ghouls try to attack with surprise whenever possible. They strike from behind tombstones and burst from shallow graves.

Ghoul Fever (Su): Disease — bite, Fortitude DC 12, incubation period 1 day, damage 1d3 Con and 1d3 Dex. The save DC is Charisma-based. An afflicted humanoid who dies of ghoul fever rises as a ghoul at the next midnight. A humanoid who becomes a ghoul in this way retains none of the abilities it possessed in life. It is not under the control of any other ghouls, but it hungers for the flesh of the living and behaves like a normal ghoul in all respects. A humanoid of 4 levels or more rises as a ghast, not a ghoul.

Paralysis (Ex): Those hit by a ghoul's bite or claw attack must succeed on a DC 12 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 1d4+1 rounds. Elves have immunity to this paralysis. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Turn Resistance +2 (Ex): A ghoul is unusually hard for a cleric or paladin to affect. When a turn, rebuke, command or bolster attempt is resolved against it, it is treated as being two steps more powerful than it actually is.

Undead Traits: No Constitution score. Immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects). Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease and death effects. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. Negative energy heals it; a mindless one cannot mend its own wounds, though it can be mended by another. Not at risk of death from massive damage — it is simply destroyed when enough damage is dealt to it. Not affected by raise dead or reincarnate, though resurrection and true resurrection can restore it. Darkvision 60 ft. Undead do not breathe, eat or sleep.

Lacedon: These cousins of the ghoul have the aquatic subtype. They lurk near hidden reefs or other places where ships are likely to meet their end. They have a base land speed of 30 feet and a swim speed of 30 feet, and are found only in aquatic environments.

lore.summary: A ghast is what rises when the corpse the fever took was a stout one to begin with. It stands taller than a ghoul, thinks a good deal straighter, and walks at the head of a ghoul pack the way a sergeant walks before a rabble. You will smell it well before you see it: a reek of death and corruption that turns the stomach and buckles the knees.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man's height, but heavier through the shoulder and arm than any ghoul it leads.
Durability: Harder to put down than its lesser kin — thicker hide, and it soaks a stroke that would fell a common ghoul.
Defenses: Tough hide and the whole indifference of the dead: no poison, no sleep, no fear, no charm, no weariness reaches it.
Speed: As swift afoot as a running man, and a better climber and leaper than most of your company.
Might: Strong and quick both, striking with bite and both claws together, and every blow can lock a man rigid.
Mind: As clever as a ghoul and far more cunning with it. It lays ambushes and sends its lessers in first.
Disposition: Wholly and always evil, and greedy besides — alone among its kind it keeps what it strips off the dead.
Bane: Its reek is a poison of a sort. Whatever shrugs off venom never smells it at all, and a draught against poison lifts it clean from a man already sickened. Hold your breath through the first wave and that same ghast can never turn your stomach again.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens with the reek and lets the sickness do half its work, then sends the ghouls forward while it takes your flank. Bite and claws come together, and its grip on a man is far stronger than a common ghoul's. Mark this well: it does not spare the fair folk. Elves stiffen under a ghast's touch as readily as anyone else, and the trick that saves you from a ghoul pack will get you killed here.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The elf trick fails here. A ghast's touch takes the fair folk the same as it takes you — I near lost Aeleth learning that.
• Draughts against venom answer the reek, and anything that laughs at poison never smells the thing at all.
• Where the ghouls are thick, look for the one standing back out of the press. Kill that one and the rest forget their order.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. This one can plan, which makes it worse and not better. I called terms to a ghast across a barrow ditch once; it heard me out, agreed to every word, and had its ghouls behind me before I had finished speaking. It talks only to arrange where you will be standing.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor terror

sections.body:
