sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Ghast: Although these creatures look just like their lesser kin, they are far more deadly and cunning. Ghasts speak the languages they spoke in life (usually Common), and lead packs of ordinary ghouls.

Ghoul Fever (Su): Disease — bite, Fortitude DC 15, incubation period 1 day, damage 1d3 Con and 1d3 Dex. The save DC is Charisma-based. An afflicted humanoid who dies of ghoul fever rises as a ghoul at the next midnight, retaining none of the abilities it possessed in life; a humanoid of 4 levels or more rises as a ghast instead.

Paralysis (Ex): Those hit by a ghast's bite or claw attack must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 1d4+1 rounds. Even elves can be affected by this paralysis. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Stench (Ex): The stink of death and corruption surrounding these creatures is overwhelming. Living creatures within 10 feet must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be sickened for 1d6+4 minutes. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same ghast's stench for 24 hours. A delay poison or neutralize poison spell removes the effect from a sickened creature. Creatures with immunity to poison are unaffected, and creatures resistant to poison receive their normal bonus on their saving throws. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Turn Resistance +2 (Ex): A ghast is unusually hard for a cleric or paladin to affect. When a turn, rebuke, command or bolster attempt is resolved against it, it is treated as being two steps more powerful than it actually is.

Undead Traits: No Constitution score. Immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects). Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease and death effects. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. Negative energy heals it; a mindless one cannot mend its own wounds, though it can be mended by another. Not at risk of death from massive damage — it is simply destroyed when enough damage is dealt to it. Not affected by raise dead or reincarnate, though resurrection and true resurrection can restore it. Darkvision 60 ft. Undead do not breathe, eat or sleep.

lore.summary: A wight is a barrow's owner still keeping what he was buried with. Cold, orderly and quiet past belief, it waits in the dark of the mound or under the turf of an old field until someone opens the way. Its face is its living face gone wrong — a twisted reflection of the man. It speaks plainly, and it takes the life out of you a piece at a time.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: The height and the weight of the man it used to be.
Durability: Sturdier than a ghoul, and it neither tires nor flinches nor gives ground.
Defenses: Hardened flesh and the dead's whole armoury of nothings: no poison, no sleep, no charm, no fear, no sickness, no weariness.
Speed: It walks at a man's pace — but it walks in perfect silence, which is far worse.
Might: It fights with its fists and nothing else. There is no great force in the blow; the harm is in what the blow takes with it.
Mind: As sharp as an ordinary man and no sharper. It speaks Common, it plans, and it keeps to its orders.
Disposition: Lawful in the coldest sense of the word and always evil — it holds ground, keeps rank, and commands whatever it has killed.
Bane: It has no reach and no trick at all beyond its hands, and nothing about it turns a blade — a plain honest weapon bites a wight as well as any costly one. Hold it at spear's length and it can do nothing whatever.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hammers with its fists and never troubles with more, and every blow that lands takes the life out of you a piece at a time. Worse, what it takes it keeps: the thing is stronger at the end of a fight than it was at the beginning. They come in pairs, gangs and packs and they never break. And what a wight kills stands up again shortly after and fights on its side, enslaved to the wight that made it and freed only by that wight's destruction — freed, mind, not laid to rest.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Spear, polearm, anything long. It has no reach and no trick but its hands.
• The man you lost may be up and swinging at you before the fight is done. Kill the master and the rest are at least their own again.
• No blessing needed on the steel. A plain edge cuts a wight as well as a costly one — save your good blade for something that needs it.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, though it will answer you in plain Common and sound very nearly like a man doing it. I stood in a barrow mouth and traded words with one for a full turn of the glass. It was patient and it was courteous, and all the while it was only waiting on my torch to gutter.

sections.body: Minor — A patient menace

sections.body:

Full Attack: Slam +3 melee (1d4+1 plus energy drain)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A wight's appearance is a weird and twisted reflection of the form it had in life; it stands about the height and build of a human. Wights speak Common. They attack by hammering with their fists.

Create Spawn (Su): Any humanoid slain by a wight becomes a wight in 1d4 rounds. Spawn are under the command of the wight that created them and remain enslaved until its death. They do not possess any of the abilities they had in life.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a wight's slam attack gain one negative level. The DC is 14 for the Fortitude save to remove a negative level. The save DC is Charisma-based. For each negative level so bestowed, the wight is bolstered by the stolen vitality.

Skills: Wights have a +8 racial bonus on Move Silently checks.

Undead Traits: No Constitution score. Immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects). Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease and death effects. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. Negative energy heals it; a mindless one cannot mend its own wounds, though it can be mended by another. Not at risk of death from massive damage — it is simply destroyed when enough damage is dealt to it. Not affected by raise dead or reincarnate, though resurrection and true resurrection can restore it. Darkvision 60 ft. Undead do not breathe, eat or sleep.

lore.summary: A wraith is a shape of evil and darkness with nothing whatever inside the outline. Some wear the grim silhouette of the armour and arms they carried in life; that is only the memory of a shape and turns no blade. They drift through wall and door alike, hunt in gangs and in packs, and hollow out the living with the touch of a hand that is not there.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: About as tall as a man, and weightless — there is nothing there to weigh.
Durability: Steel passes clean through it. Only enchanted arms or magic itself can lay hold of a thing with no substance.
Defenses: It has no body to wound. Wall, door and armour are all one to it, and no poison, sleep, charm, fear or sickness finds any purchase.
Speed: It flies, and flies well — swifter than a running man, and through the stone if it cares to.
Might: No strength in the ordinary way at all. The whole harm is in the touch, which drains the vigour out of a living body until there is none left to lose.
Mind: Sharp, and worse, articulate. It speaks Common and the tongue of devils, and it is a practised talker.
Disposition: Always evil and coldly ordered. It hunts in gangs and packs, and everything it kills is bound to serve it.
Bane: Wraiths are utterly powerless in natural sunlight (not merely a daylight spell) and flee from it. Nothing else you carry will serve you half so well as waiting on the dawn.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes through the wall behind you, never the door in front. The touch of it drains the vigour out of a living body, and what it takes it keeps, so the longer the fight runs the stronger the thing gets. Anyone who falls to it does not stay fallen: the body lies there whole and empty while the spirit is torn out of it and rises as another wraith, enslaved to the one that made it until that one is destroyed. They press the attack in gangs and packs and will not stop for anything short of destruction or the sunrise.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Your horse knows first. When the beasts panic and will not go a step nearer, something without a body is close.
• A plain blade is a stick to it. Carry enchanted steel, or bring someone who can throw a light of their own.
• Wait on the sun if you possibly can. Real sunlight, mind, not a conjured glow — the difference between the two is your life.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, and this is the one I most want you to heed. A wraith talks well — a practised negotiator in Common and in the devils' tongue both — and it will discuss terms with you all evening while its gang drifts through the wall at your back. I heard one out once. I do not intend to again.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable haunt

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead (Incorporeal)
Initiative: +7
Speed: Fly 60 ft. (good) (12 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+3 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 15, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/—
Attack: Incorporeal touch +5 melee (1d4 plus 1d6 Constitution drain)
Full Attack: Incorporeal touch +5 melee (1d4 plus 1d6 Constitution drain)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Constitution drain, create spawn
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., daylight powerlessness, incorporeal traits, +2 turn resistance, undead traits, unnatural aura
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +4, Will +6
Abilities: Str —, Dex 16, Con —, Int 14, Wis 14, Cha 15
Skills: Diplomacy +6, Hide +11, Intimidate +10, Listen +12, Search +10, Sense Motive +8, Spot +12, Survival +2 (+4 following tracks)
Feats: Alertness (B), Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative (B)
Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary, gang (2-5), or pack (6-11)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 6-10 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Wraiths are incorporeal creatures born of evil and darkness. In some cases the grim silhouette of a wraith might appear armored or outfitted with weapons; this appearance does not affect its AC or combat abilities, but only reflects the shape it had in life. A wraith is about as tall as a human, and being incorporeal it is weightless. Wraiths speak Common and Infernal.

Constitution Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a wraith's incorporeal touch attack must succeed on a DC 14 Fortitude save or take 1d6 points of Constitution drain. The save DC is Charisma-based. On each such successful attack, the wraith is bolstered by the stolen vitality.

Create Spawn (Su): Any humanoid slain by a wraith becomes a wraith in 1d4 rounds. Its body remains intact and inanimate, but its spirit is torn free from its corpse and transformed. Spawn are under the command of the wraith that created them and remain enslaved until its death. They do not possess any of the abilities they had in life.

Unnatural Aura (Su): Animals, whether wild or domesticated, can sense the unnatural presence of a wraith at a distance of 30 feet. They will not willingly approach nearer than that and panic if forced to do so; they remain panicked as long as they are within that range.

Daylight Powerlessness (Ex): Wraiths are utterly powerless in natural sunlight (not merely a daylight spell) and flee from it.

Incorporeal Traits: Can be harmed only by other incorporeal creatures, by +1 or better magic weapons, or by magic (spells, spell-like abilities and supernatural abilities), and even then has a 50% chance to ignore any damage from a corporeal source — except for force effects such as magic missile, or attacks made with ghost touch weapons. It can pass through solid objects at will, and its own attacks pass through armor. It always moves silently and cannot be heard with Listen checks if it does not wish to be. It has no natural armor bonus but gains a deflection bonus equal to its Charisma bonus (always at least +1). It cannot fall or take falling damage, cannot make trip or grapple attacks nor be tripped or grappled, and cannot manipulate physical objects.

Turn Resistance +2 (Ex): A wraith is unusually hard for a cleric or paladin to affect. When a turn, rebuke, command or bolster attempt is resolved against it, it is treated as being two steps more powerful than it actually is.

Undead Traits: No Constitution score. Immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects). Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease and death effects. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. Negative energy heals it; a mindless one cannot mend its own wounds, though it can be mended by another. Not at risk of death from massive damage — it is simply destroyed when enough damage is dealt to it. Not affected by raise dead or reincarnate, though resurrection and true resurrection can restore it. Darkvision 60 ft. Undead do not breathe, eat or sleep.

Dread Wraith: The oldest and most malevolent wraiths lurk in the depths of forgotten temples and other forsaken places. They can sense the approach of living creatures, and hunger for them. Despite its size, the dread wraith possesses unearthly quickness, and makes use of its Spring Attack feat and natural reach to strike with deadly effect and melt back into the shadows — or the walls. A dread wraith is Large Undead (Incorporeal), Init +13, fly 60 ft. (good), AC 25 (-1 size, +9 Dex, +7 deflection), touch 25, flat-footed 16; base attack +8; incorporeal touch +16 melee (2d6 plus 1d8 Constitution drain, Fortitude DC 25); Space/Reach 10 ft./10 ft.; Fort +5, Ref +14, Will +14; Str —, Dex 28, Con —, Int 17, Wis 18, Cha 24; CR 11; always lawful evil; solitary; advancement 17-32 levels (Large). It has lifesense 60 ft. in place of turn resistance.

Lifesense (Su): A dread wraith notices and locates living creatures within 60 feet, just as if it possessed the blindsight ability. It also senses the strength of their life force automatically, as if it had cast deathwatch.

lore.summary: A corpse dried, wrapped and bound up by the rites of desert gods best forgotten, then set to keep a door for ever. A mummy is slow, dull and immensely strong, and it does not care in the least how long you take. You will meet them standing watch in tombs — alone, in wardens' squads, or in whole guardian details drawn up across a hall.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man's height, and surprisingly light — the flesh is all dried out of it.
Durability: Enormously hard to put down. It has stood a very long while already and can stand a good deal more.
Defenses: Dried flesh and wrapping blunt every weapon alike — plain steel and enchanted steel fare exactly the same, which is to say poorly — and no poison, sleep, fear, charm or sickness touches it at all.
Speed: Slow. Slower than a walking man, and it never once hurries.
Might: Terrible strength. One slam of that arm breaks bone through mail, and the blow leaves the rot behind in the wound.
Mind: Dull-witted and incurious. It can speak Common and almost never troubles itself to.
Disposition: Usually evil and always bound. It guards, and it will not negotiate over what it guards.
Bane: Fire. It is dry as tinder and burns as tinder does, and flame hurts it worse than anything else you can bring against it. A common mummy has no guard against burning whatever — only the great mummy lords are ever warded from flame, and that by the rings they wear rather than by anything in their nature.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It is a fight of one slow arm. The mummy shuffles in and slams, with appalling force behind it, but the real work is the rot it leaves in the wound — a curse rather than a sickness, which eats away flesh and spirit together and will not stop of its own accord until the victim shrivels to sand and blows away on the first wind. Worse still, healing prayers balk on a man so cursed; the curse must be broken before any mending will take. And you must survive the sight of it first, for the mere look of a mummy can freeze a man rigid with terror where he stands.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fire, always fire. Oil, torches, anything that catches — the thing goes up like old straw.
• The rot is a curse, not a sickness. Prayers of healing will not bite until the curse is lifted. Bring someone who can lift it or do not go in.
• Look away as you come through the door. The first sight of one can root you where you stand — and it only ever gets that one chance at you.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, though it is not malice exactly. There is a dull thing in there that can speak Common and has not bothered in centuries. I asked one politely to let me past a door in the Aszar barrows. It answered nothing at all and hit me so hard my ribs sang for a month. It has a charge, and you are on the wrong side of it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable guardian

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 20 (+10 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 20
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+11
Attack: Slam +11 melee (1d6+10 plus mummy rot)
Full Attack: Slam +11 melee (1d6+10 plus mummy rot)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Despair, mummy rot
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/—, darkvision 60 ft., undead traits, vulnerability to fire
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +2, Will +8
Abilities: Str 24, Dex 10, Con —, Int 6, Wis 14, Cha 15
Skills: Hide +7, Listen +8, Move Silently +7, Spot +8
Feats: Alertness, Great Fortitude, Toughness
Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary, warden squad (2-4), or guardian detail (6-10)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Usually lawful evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 9-16 levels (Medium); 17-24 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Mummies are preserved corpses animated through the auspices of dark desert gods best forgotten. Most are 5 to 6 feet tall and weigh about 120 pounds. Mummies can speak Common, but seldom bother to do so.

Despair (Su): At the mere sight of a mummy, the viewer must succeed on a DC 16 Will save or be paralyzed with fear for 1d4 rounds. Whether or not the save is successful, that creature cannot be affected again by the same mummy's despair ability for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Mummy Rot (Su): Supernatural disease — slam, Fortitude DC 16, incubation period 1 minute, damage 1d6 Con and 1d6 Cha. The save DC is Charisma-based. Unlike normal diseases, mummy rot continues until the victim reaches Constitution 0 (and dies) or is cured as described below. Mummy rot is a powerful curse, not a natural disease. A character attempting to cast any conjuration (healing) spell on a creature afflicted with mummy rot must succeed on a DC 20 caster level check, or the spell has no effect on the afflicted character. To eliminate mummy rot, the curse must first be broken with break enchantment or remove curse (requiring a DC 20 caster level check for either spell), after which a caster level check is no longer necessary to cast healing spells on the victim, and the mummy rot can be magically cured as any normal disease. An afflicted creature who dies of mummy rot shrivels away into sand and dust that blow away into nothing at the first wind.

Damage Reduction 5/— and Vulnerability to Fire: A mummy's dried, resin-soaked wrappings and hardened flesh turn aside the first of any blow — damage reduction 5/—, which nothing overcomes. Against fire it has no such protection: it takes half again as much damage (+50%) from fire, regardless of whether a saving throw is allowed or whether the save is a success or a failure. The base mummy has no resistance to fire; only a mummy lord bearing a ring of minor energy resistance (fire) does.

Undead Traits: No Constitution score. Immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects). Immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease and death effects. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. Negative energy heals it; a mindless one cannot mend its own wounds, though it can be mended by another. Not at risk of death from massive damage — it is simply destroyed when enough damage is dealt to it. Not affected by raise dead or reincarnate, though resurrection and true resurrection can restore it. Darkvision 60 ft. Undead do not breathe, eat or sleep.

Mummy Lord: Unusually powerful or evil individuals preserved as mummies sometimes rise as greater mummies after death. A mummy lord resembles its lesser fellows but often wears or carries equipment it used in life, and is frequently a potent divine spellcaster — the sample is a 10th-level cleric of the Death and Protection domains, CR 15, AC 30, slam +20 melee (1d6+12/19-20 plus mummy rot), despair and mummy rot both at DC 17, with rebuke undead and resistance to fire 10 from its gear. Most are sworn to defend for eternity the resting place of those whom they served in life; others are the product of a terrible curse or rite meant to punish treason, infidelity, or crimes of an even more abhorrent nature, and are usually imprisoned in a tomb never meant to be opened again.

lore.summary: A spectre is a murdered man's hatred left standing where his body fell. It wears the face it had in life, so plainly that those who knew him name him at once, and often the wound that ended him is still there to see. Weightless, it walks through stone, and it holds the ground of its death against everything that breathes.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized and weightless, wearing the face it had in life, often with the killing wound still on it.
Durability: There is nothing in it to tire, bleed or break; it is not flesh and does not pretend to be.
Defenses: Incorporeal. Honest steel and good arrows pass clean through and find nothing to bite; only enchanted arms and magic touch it at all. It sees in the dark far better than you do.
Speed: Quick afoot and far quicker on the wing, flying without effort or error, and no wall, floor or ceiling delays it.
Might: Its touch is a numbing cold that takes the life out of you a piece at a time, and every piece it takes it keeps to mend itself.
Mind: As clever as the man it was. It remembers its own name, its own murder, and everyone who had a hand in it.
Disposition: Always evil, and cold and orderly about it. Beasts feel it coming before you do; a horse will bolt sooner than carry you within reach.
Bane: Natural sunlight. Spectres are powerless in natural sunlight, not merely a conjured daylight, and they flee from it. One caught in the sun cannot attack at all, and can manage only a single move, or a single act, and no more.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes through the wall at your back or up out of the floor, lays that cold hand on whatever it finds, and sinks into the stone again before you have even faced about. It will cross a room inside the masonry and come out behind your rearmost man. It does not stand and trade. And what it kills gets up shortly after and serves it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it at dawn. Break the shutters, break the roof if you must; the sun does the work and takes no fee.
• Burn your dead where they fall, and before dusk. What it kills stands up wearing your friend's face.
• Plain steel is a stick against smoke. Enchanted arms, or a priest, or stay home.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It has a living man's wits and a living man's memory, so I have tried it, twice, in two barrows. Both times it answered me. Both times the answer was its hand on my chest. It hates breath itself, and there is no arguing a thing out of its own hatred. Speak from behind sunlight, or not at all.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Initiative: +7
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), fly 80 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 15 (+3 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 15, flat-footed 13

Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., incorporeal traits, +2 turn resistance, sunlight powerlessness, undead traits, unnatural aura
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +7

Skills: Hide +13, Intimidate +12, Knowledge (religion) +12, Listen +14, Search +12, Spot +14, Survival +2 (+4 following tracks)
Feats: Alertness, Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative

Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Always lawful evil
Treasure: None

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: In close combat a spectre attacks with its numbing, life-draining touch. It makes full use of its incorporeal nature, moving through walls, ceilings, and floors as it attacks.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures struck by a spectre’s incorporeal touch attack gain two negative levels. The DC is 15 for the Fortitude save to remove a negative level; the save DC is Charisma-based. The spectre is briefly strengthened by each negative level it bestows.

Create Spawn (Su): Any humanoid slain by a spectre becomes a spectre in 1d4 rounds. Spawn are under the command of the spectre that created them and remain enslaved until its death. They do not possess any of the abilities they had in life.

Unnatural Aura (Su): Animals, whether wild or domesticated, can sense the unnatural presence of a spectre at a distance of 30 feet. They do not willingly approach nearer than that and panic if forced to do so; they remain panicked as long as they are within that range.

Sunlight Powerlessness (Ex): Spectres are powerless in natural sunlight (not merely a daylight spell) and flee from it. A spectre caught in sunlight cannot attack and can take only a single move action or standard action in a round.

Incorporeal Traits: A spectre can be harmed only by other incorporeal creatures, magic weapons, spells, spell-like effects, or supernatural effects, and it has a 50% chance to ignore any damage from a corporeal source (except force effects, or attacks made with ghost touch weapons). It can pass through solid objects at will and its own attacks pass through armor. It always moves silently and cannot be heard with Listen checks if it doesn’t wish to be.

Undead Traits: Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects, and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, energy drain, fatigue, exhaustion, or damage to its physical ability scores. Darkvision 60 ft. Cannot be raised; resurrection works only if it is willing.

lore.summary: A shadow is not a cast shadow but a hungry absence in the shape of a man, as tall as a man and weighing nothing. It gathers in cellars, crypts and unlit stairs and waits for something warm to pass. It cannot speak and has nothing to say. It reaches out, and the strength goes out of your arms, and that is the whole of its conversation.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-tall and man-shaped and weightless, a hole in the light rather than a thing standing in it.
Durability: Slight, as these things go, and there is nothing in it to break; but it does not tire and it does not bleed.
Defenses: Incorporeal, so steel goes through it and comes out clean. Enchanted arms and magic are all it fears. It sees in the dark, and in gloom it is very hard to pick out; in a brightly lit place it stands out starkly and cannot hide at all.
Speed: It flies rather than walks, quick and well handled, and passes through walls without slowing.
Might: Its touch withers the strength out of a living body. Empty a man of his strength and he is dead of it, and shortly gets up as another shadow under the one that killed him.
Mind: Dim. Wit enough to lurk and to pick the straggler, and none at all for anything more. It cannot speak intelligibly.
Disposition: Chaotic and wholly malign. It waits in the dark for living prey to happen by and takes whoever happens.
Bane: Light. In a bright room it cannot hide and half the fight is already won. Note also that there is a greater kind, no cleverer but far stronger in the touch, which strikes and withdraws before you can bring a weapon to bear.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lets you walk past, then comes out of the wall behind you. It reaches for living flesh and nothing else, withering you touch by touch, and it prefers the straggler, the lame and the wounded to the man holding the lantern. Where there is one there are often many, and they come at once from every wall of a room. The greater sort will not stand and fight at all; it touches and is gone, and comes back at you from another quarter.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Carry more light than you think you need. In a bright room it cannot hide, and half the fight is over.
• Watch your arms. When the sword starts to feel heavy you are already losing. Get into the light.
• Whoever it empties gets up as another. Do not leave your fallen behind you in the dark.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing here to talk to. I hailed one in a Marrowvale cellar for my rule's sake, the dead being a wrongness to put right and not quarry, and I would know if it could be reasoned out of itself. It made a noise like cloth tearing and came for my arm. Save your breath for the greater dead.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Shadows lurk in dark places, waiting for living prey to happen by. A shadow can be difficult to see in dark or gloomy areas but stands out starkly in brightly illuminated places. A shadow is 5 to 6 feet tall and weightless, and cannot speak intelligibly.

Strength Damage (Su): The touch of a shadow deals 1d6 points of Strength damage to a living foe. A creature reduced to Strength 0 by a shadow dies. This is a negative energy effect.

Create Spawn (Su): Any humanoid reduced to Strength 0 by a shadow becomes a shadow under the control of its killer within 1d4 rounds.

It can pass through solid objects at will and its own attacks pass through armor. It always moves silently.

Undead Traits: Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects, and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, energy drain, fatigue, exhaustion, or damage to its physical ability scores. Darkvision 60 ft.

Greater Shadow: A larger, older shadow, no more intelligent than an average one but far more fearsome for its increased damage and its hit-and-run tactics. Medium Undead (Incorporeal); Init +2; fly 40 ft. (good); AC 14 (+2 Dex, +2 deflection), touch 14, flat-footed 12; Base Attack/Grapple +4/—; incorporeal touch +6 melee (1d8 Str); Space/Reach 5 ft./5 ft.; SA create spawn, Strength damage; SQ darkvision 60 ft., incorporeal traits, +2 turn resistance, undead traits; Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +7; Str —, Dex 15, Con —, Int 6, Wis 12, Cha 14; Hide +14*, Listen +9, Search +6, Spot +9; Alertness, Dodge, Mobility, Spring Attack; Organization solitary; CR 8; always chaotic evil; no further advancement.

lore.summary: A ghost is what remains when a creature of wit and will cannot lie quiet: a spectral form much as it was in life, held to the world by some matter left unsettled. It keeps to the far side of the veil and steps partway through to be seen. Not all are wicked. Many are only wretched, and some are simply waiting to be asked.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Whatever it was in life. Most are man-sized, but beasts, giants and worse leave ghosts too, so do not assume.
Durability: It cannot be finished by force. Beat the spirit down and it gathers itself again within a few days and returns to its old haunts.
Defenses: It dwells beyond the veil where nothing you carry can reach it. Stepping through, it is visible but incorporeal: enchanted arms, magic and other spirits can wound it, and even those often pass through with nothing to show. It moves in perfect silence, walks through solid stone, and its blows ignore armour entirely.
Speed: It drifts rather than walks, unerring in the air, and walls do not exist for it.
Might: They differ, each to its own grief. A gaze that rots the living where they stand. A cold touch, or one that drains away a man's strength, wits or nerve and mends the spirit with what it takes. A moan that sets veterans running. An aspect so foul that merely seeing it wastes the body. Unseen hands that hurl furniture and men. And worst, the power to step inside a living body and wear it.
Mind: Whatever it was in life, and it keeps what it knew: the ghost of a swordsman still fences, the ghost of a wizard still casts.
Disposition: Any temper at all, good or wicked, though most are simply unquiet. It clings to its old ground and to a few things it treasured in life; take one of those away and it will follow you to the world's end to have it back.
Bane: Force settles nothing. Find why it cannot rest, the grave unmade, the word unsaid, the debt unpaid, and set that right, and it goes of its own accord. That is the only sure end there is.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only when talk fails or when its business is threatened. It stays beyond the veil where you cannot touch it, steps through to strike, and steps back out of reach. It leads with terror, the moan, the gaze, the sight of itself, and then closes with a cold hand, or takes hold of the weakest of your company and sets him upon his friends. Cut it down and you have bought a few days, no more than that.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Ask what it wants. It will usually tell you, and telling is cheaper than steel.
• Never pocket the trinket it kept. Take a ghost's treasure and you have made an enemy that cannot be killed and will not be outrun.
• Put it down and it comes back in a few days, angrier. Settle its business or leave it be.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The one kind of dead I will always hail. A ghost keeps its own mind and every word it ever knew, and most want a thing done rather than a thing killed. I sat out a whole night with a drowned bargeman who wanted only his daughter told where the boat went down. Ask its name first; it is usually still proud of it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead (Augmented Humanoid, Incorporeal) — sample ghost, a 5th-level human fighter
Initiative: +5
Speed: Fly 30 ft. (perfect) (6 squares)
Armor Class: 21 (+1 Dex, +8 full plate, +2 heavy shield), touch 11, flat-footed 20 in ethereal encounters; or 12 (+1 Dex, +1 deflection), touch 12, flat-footed 11 when manifested
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+8
Attack: Incorporeal touch +6 melee (1d6), or +8 melee (1d6+3) against ethereal foes; or masterwork bastard sword +10 melee (1d10+3/19–20); or masterwork shortbow +7 ranged (1d6/×3)
Full Attack: Incorporeal touch +6 melee (1d6), or +8 melee (1d6+3) against ethereal foes; or masterwork bastard sword +10 melee (1d10+3/19–20); or masterwork shortbow +7 ranged (1d6/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Corrupting touch, malevolence, manifestation
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., incorporeal traits, rejuvenation, +4 turn resistance, undead traits
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +2, Will +2
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 13, Con —, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 12
Skills: Climb +1, Hide -1, Listen +11, Ride +9, Search +8, Spot +11
Feats: Blind-Fight, Cleave, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (bastard sword), Improved Initiative, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (bastard sword)
Environment: Any, often as the base creature (temperate plains for this sample)
Organization: Solitary, gang (2–4), or mob (7–12)
Challenge Rating: 7 (same as the base creature +2)
Alignment: Any (the template imposes none; the sample ghost is any)
Treasure: None
Advancement: By character class (level adjustment +5)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
The Template: “Ghost” is an acquired template that can be added to any aberration, animal, dragon, giant, humanoid, magical beast, monstrous humanoid, or plant with a Charisma score of at least 6. The creature’s type changes to undead and it gains the incorporeal subtype; size is unchanged, and base attack bonus, saves, and skill points are not recalculated. It has no Constitution score and its Charisma rises by +4, it gains a +8 racial bonus on Hide, Listen, Search, and Spot checks, and it flies at 30 feet (or faster, if the base creature flew faster) with perfect maneuverability. Natural armor applies only to ethereal encounters; when manifested the ghost instead gains a deflection bonus equal to its Charisma modifier or +1, whichever is higher. Every ghost gains manifestation plus one to three of the special attacks below. Save DCs are 10 + half the ghost’s levels + its Charisma modifier unless otherwise noted.

Manifestation (Su): Every ghost has this ability. A ghost dwells on the Ethereal Plane and, as an ethereal creature, cannot affect or be affected by anything in the material world. When it manifests it partly enters the Material Plane, becoming visible but incorporeal there. A manifested ghost can be harmed only by other incorporeal creatures, magic weapons, or spells, with a 50% chance to ignore any damage from a corporeal source. It can pass through solid objects at will, its own attacks pass through armor, and it always moves silently. It can strike with its touch attack or with a ghost touch weapon. A manifested ghost remains partially on the Ethereal Plane, where it is not incorporeal, and can be attacked by opponents on either plane; its incorporeality protects it from foes on the Material Plane but not from foes on the Ethereal Plane. A spellcasting ghost’s spells cannot reach the Material Plane while it is unmanifested; when manifested they work normally except for touch spells, which do not work on nonethereal targets. A ghost has two home planes, the Material and the Ethereal, and is not extraplanar on either.

Rejuvenation (Su): It is difficult to destroy a ghost by simple combat: the “destroyed” spirit usually restores itself in 2d4 days, and even the most powerful spells are only temporary solutions. A ghost that would otherwise be destroyed returns to its old haunts with a successful level check (1d20 + the ghost’s levels) against DC 16. As a rule, the only sure way to be rid of a ghost is to determine the reason for its existence and set right whatever prevents it from resting in peace. The exact means varies with each spirit and may require a good deal of research.

Corrupting Gaze (Su): A ghost can blast living beings with a glance, at a range of up to 30 feet. Creatures that meet the ghost’s gaze must succeed on a Fortitude save or take 2d10 points of damage and 1d4 points of Charisma damage.

Corrupting Touch (Su): A ghost that hits a living target with its incorporeal touch attack deals 1d6 points of damage. Against ethereal opponents it adds its Strength modifier to attack and damage rolls; against nonethereal opponents it adds its Dexterity modifier to attack rolls only.

Draining Touch (Su): A ghost that hits a living target with its incorporeal touch attack drains 1d4 points from any one ability score it selects. Each such successful attack also repairs 5 points of the damage the ghost has taken. Against ethereal opponents it adds its Strength modifier to attack rolls only; against nonethereal opponents it adds its Dexterity modifier to attack rolls only.

Frightful Moan (Su): A ghost can emit a frightful moan as a standard action. All living creatures within a 30-foot spread must succeed on a Will save or become panicked for 2d4 rounds. This is a sonic necromantic mind-affecting fear effect. A creature that successfully saves against the moan cannot be affected by the same ghost’s moan for 24 hours.

Horrific Appearance (Su): Any living creature within 60 feet that views a ghost must succeed on a Fortitude save or immediately take 1d4 points of Strength damage, 1d4 points of Dexterity damage, and 1d4 points of Constitution damage. A creature that successfully saves against this effect cannot be affected by the same ghost’s horrific appearance for 24 hours.

Malevolence (Su): Once per round, an ethereal ghost can merge its body with a creature on the Material Plane. This ability is similar to a magic jar spell (caster level 10th, or equal to the ghost’s level if higher), except that it does not require a receptacle. The ghost must be manifested and must try to move into the target’s space; doing so does not provoke attacks of opportunity. The target can resist with a successful Will save (DC 15 + the ghost’s Charisma modifier — DC 16 for the sample ghost). A creature that successfully saves is immune to that same ghost’s malevolence for 24 hours and the ghost cannot enter its space. If the save fails, the ghost vanishes into the target’s body.

Telekinesis (Su): A ghost can use telekinesis as a standard action (caster level 12th, or equal to the ghost’s level if higher). After using this power it must wait 1d4 rounds before using it again.

Turn Resistance (Ex): A ghost has +4 turn resistance.

Ghostly Equipment: When a ghost forms, all its equipment and carried items usually become ethereal along with it, and it retains 2d4 items it particularly valued in life (provided they are not in another creature’s possession). The equipment works normally on the Ethereal Plane but passes harmlessly through material objects and creatures. A weapon of +1 or better enhancement can harm material creatures when the ghost manifests, but any such attack has a 50% chance to fail unless the weapon is a ghost touch weapon. The original material items remain behind, as the ghost’s remains do; if another creature seizes the original, the ethereal copy fades away, and the loss invariably angers the ghost, which stops at nothing to return the item to its resting place.

lore.summary: A lich is a spellcaster who refused to die and found a way to make the refusal stick. What walks afterward is gaunt and skeletal, withered skin drawn tight over plain bone, the eyes long since rotted away with points of crimson light burning on in the empty sockets. It speaks the common tongue and every other it learned in life, and it has had centuries to think.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: As the man it was, and it was a man: gaunt, skeletal, dry skin over bone, crimson light where the eyes decayed away.
Durability: Its dead body is tough past reason. Blade and arrow slide off it. A heavy enchanted mace or hammer is what tells.
Defenses: Cold does not touch it, nor lightning. No magic will change its shape against its will, and nothing that works upon the mind works upon it at all. Add whatever wards its own craft has laid, and it has had a long while to lay them.
Speed: No faster than the man it was, and never in any hurry. It has craft enough to go where it likes without walking.
Might: Chief among its arms is its craft: it casts everything it could cast in life, and it has gone on studying since. Its bare touch carries the cold of the grave, and any living thing it lays a hand on may be stopped stiff for good, a stillness no dispelling breaks, and the stopped look dead to anyone who does not check closely. It goes shrouded in a dread that sends lesser folk running at a glance.
Mind: Brilliant, and sharper than it was alive. It thinks in centuries, plans, waits, and keeps servants. Vampires, often, and their get.
Disposition: Evil without exception, though not always cruel for sport. It wants knowledge, power and time, and it will trade courteously for all three while arranging your death at leisure.
Bane: The vessel it keeps its life in. Cut the body down and it is back in a matter of days, whole, unless you have found that vessel and broken it. Find it first. Until you have, you are not fighting the thing, you are amusing it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens at a distance with its craft and never willingly closes, having spent lifetimes assembling exactly the arts for exactly this. Should you reach it, it lays a hand on you and you stop where you stand, dead to the eye and alive inside, and it leaves you for later. It fights from a prepared place among its own wards and its own servants, and it withdraws without the least shame, because time costs it nothing and costs you everything.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Find the vessel before you find the lich. Everything else is theatre.
• Bring a blessed mace, not your good sword. Edges slide off it.
• Take nothing it offers and drink nothing it pours. I did. I am still paying.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It will talk. That is the trap. I took wine with one in a drowned library and had the finest conversation of my life, courteous, learned, generous with what it knew. I left with the answers I came for and a mark on me I did not know I had taken. Promise it nothing, take nothing, and go while it is still being polite.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Initiative: +3

Full Attack: Touch +5 melee (1d8+5 negative energy plus paralysis) or quarterstaff +5 melee (1d6) or dagger +5 melee (1d4/19–20) or masterwork light crossbow +9 ranged (1d8/19–20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.

Advancement: By character class (level adjustment +4)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
The Template: “Lich” is an acquired template that can be added to any humanoid creature able to create the required phylactery. The creature’s type changes to undead; size is unchanged, and base attack bonus, saves, and skill points are not recalculated. A lich gains a +5 natural armor bonus (or keeps the base creature’s, if better), Int +2, Wis +2 and Cha +2, and loses its Constitution score. Its natural weapons count as magic weapons for overcoming damage reduction. Liches speak Common plus any other languages they knew in life.

Phylactery: An integral part of becoming a lich is creating a magic phylactery in which the character stores its life force. As a rule, the only way to be rid of a lich for certain is to destroy its phylactery; unless the phylactery is located and destroyed, a lich reappears 1d10 days after its apparent death. Each lich must make its own, which requires the Craft Wondrous Item feat, the ability to cast spells and a caster level of 11th or higher; it costs 120,000 gp and 4,800 XP and has a caster level equal to its creator’s at the time of creation. The most common form is a sealed metal box containing strips of parchment inscribed with magical phrases — a Tiny object with hardness 20 and a break DC of 40 that can absorb 40 points of damage before it is destroyed. Rings, amulets and similar items also serve.

Fear Aura (Su): Liches are shrouded in a dreadful aura of death and evil. Creatures of fewer than 5 levels within a 60-foot radius that look at the lich must succeed on a Will save (DC 16 for the sample lich) or be affected as though by a fear spell from a sorcerer of the lich’s level. A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same lich’s aura for 24 hours.

Paralyzing Touch (Su): Any living creature a lich hits with its touch attack must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC 16 for the sample lich) or be permanently paralyzed. Remove paralysis or any spell that can remove a curse can free the victim; the effect cannot be dispelled. Anyone paralyzed by a lich seems dead, though a DC 20 Spot check or a DC 15 Heal check reveals that the victim is still alive.

Damage (Su): A lich without natural weapons has a touch attack that uses negative energy to deal 1d8+5 points of damage to living creatures; a Will save (DC 10 + half the lich’s levels + its Charisma modifier — DC 16 for the sample lich) halves the damage. A lich with natural weapons may use its touch attack or its natural weaponry; if the latter, it deals 1d8+5 points of extra damage on one natural weapon attack.

Damage Reduction (Su): A lich’s undead body is tough, giving the creature damage reduction 15/bludgeoning and magic. Its natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Immunities (Ex): Liches have immunity to cold, electricity, polymorph (though they can use polymorph effects on themselves), and mind-affecting attacks, in addition to the usual undead immunities.

Turn Resistance (Ex): A lich has +4 turn resistance.

Spells: A lich can cast any spells it could cast while alive. The sample lich casts as an 11th-level wizard (4/5/5/5/4/2/1; save DC 14 + spell level), with prepared: 0 — acid splash, detect magic, ray of frost*, touch of fatigue; 1st — expeditious retreat, magic missile (3), ray of enfeeblement; 2nd — mirror image, protection from arrows, scorching ray*, spectral hand, web; 3rd — dispel magic, fireball*, haste, lightning bolt*, vampiric touch; 4th — enervation, fear, ice storm*, shout*; 5th — cone of cold*, teleport; 6th — disintegrate. *Because of Spell Focus (evocation) the save DC for these spells is 15 + spell level.

Possessions: Bracers of armor +4, cloak of resistance +1, potion of gaseous form, ring of protection +1, scroll of summon monster IV (8th level), wand of magic missile (50 charges, 9th level).

Undead Traits: Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects, and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, energy drain, fatigue, exhaustion, or damage to its physical ability scores. Darkvision 60 ft. Cannot be raised; resurrection works only if it is willing.

lore.summary: A mohrg is what a murderer becomes when he dies with all his killing unrepented. The corpse walks, stripped to bone and gristle with its innards hanging plain to see, and behind its teeth lies a long grey tongue coiled like a whip. Man-sized, light, and nothing whatever like the shambling dead it keeps about it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized and light, a stripped corpse with its innards on show.
Durability: Hard going, and it feels nothing you do to it; but it is bone and gristle still and can be hewn apart like anything else that stands on legs.
Defenses: Its own tough hide and knotted sinew are all the armour it has, and that is armour enough to be tiresome. Beyond the cold indifference of all the dead it has no ward worth the name. It sees in the dark.
Speed: Here is the danger. It moves nothing like the shamblers it commands: quick as a live man and far quieter, and it climbs and swims well besides. It will be on you before you are anywhere near ready for it.
Might: Very strong. It slams with its fists, and once it has hold of you it does not let go. The tongue is the true weapon, and a touch of it leaves you stopped stiff and standing while it kills you at leisure.
Mind: Ordinary wits, no more than a man's and no less. Cunning enough to lie in wait, to choose its moment, and to send its dead in ahead of it.
Disposition: Chaotic and wholly murderous. It was a butcher of men in life and is nothing else now. It keeps a mob of its own dead about it wherever it goes.
Bane: It is flesh and bone. Plain good steel bites it, which is rare enough among the greater dead, and nothing shrugs off fire. So cut, and keep clear of the tongue's reach.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes fast and quiet, often before anyone knows it is there, and it strikes as a shambler strikes, a heavy fist and then hands on you. But the fist only holds you still for the tongue, and once the tongue lands you are a statue for as long as it needs you to be. It sets its dead upon your line to occupy you and works along your flank itself. Whoever it kills gets up a day or so later as another shambling corpse, its own creature and under its command.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The tongue, not the fists. The fists are only there to hold you still for it.
• Plain steel bites this one. That is a mercy among the greater dead. Spend it, and spend it fast.
• Never take one alone. Stopped stiff and alone is the same as dead.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing left in it but the murders. It has a man's wits, so I hailed one on the Gallows Road, as is my rule with anything that can answer me. It answered by taking my guide's arms off at the shoulder. Do not extend the courtesy. It costs somebody their life every single time.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.body:

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Mohrgs are the animated corpses of mass murderers or similar villains who died without atoning for their crimes; most are 5 to 6 feet tall and weigh about 120 pounds. Like zombies, mohrgs attack by slamming enemies with their fists. They often catch opponents flat-footed, for they move much faster than zombies.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a mohrg must hit a creature of its size or smaller with its slam attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Paralyzing Touch (Su): A mohrg lashes out with its tongue in combat. An opponent the tongue touches must succeed on a DC 17 Fortitude save or become paralyzed for 1d4 minutes. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Create Spawn (Su): Creatures killed by a mohrg rise after 1d4 days as zombies under the mohrg’s control. They do not possess any of the abilities they had in life.

Undead Traits: Immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects, and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. Not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, energy drain, fatigue, exhaustion, or damage to its physical ability scores. Darkvision 60 ft. Cannot be raised; resurrection works only if it is willing.

lore.summary: The spectral leavings of one driven to take their own life by a madness that afflicted them in life. It craves only revenge, and pursues without rest or reason those who tormented it and pushed it over the brink. It keeps no lair and guards no hoard; it drifts wherever the memory of its tormentors leads, and it cannot say so.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized, though there is nothing there to measure — a smear of grieving air in the shape of a person.
Durability: Nothing solid to break. Steel and stone pass clean through and it drifts on unmarked.
Defenses: Bodiless. Only enchanted arms and magic touch it at all; a plain sword is a stick to it.
Speed: Drifts at a walking pace, but with perfect and effortless command of every direction — up, back, through a wall.
Might: It cannot bruise you. Its touch instead peels the sense out of a man and leaves a wandering fool behind.
Mind: Wits enough to hate, none to speak with. It cannot shape intelligible words, only a ceaseless muttering and whining.
Disposition: Vengeful past all reason, and blind to the difference between its old tormentors and the stranger in the doorway.
Bane: It cannot wound the body at all. Stop your ears against the babble, keep your thoughts out of its head, and it can do nothing but flail.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It is unable to cause physical harm, though it does not appear to know that — it keeps flailing away and inflicts no wound. The danger is elsewhere. The constant muttering hangs a hypnotic stupor on every sane creature within hearing, and while they stand slack-jawed it reaches through mail and skin alike to drain the wit out of them. Anyone who pries at it with thought-reading or compulsion makes direct contact with a tortured mind and loses their own reason for the trouble.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Wax in the ears before you go down. The muttering, not the touch, is what takes the man beside you.
• Do not read its mind and do not try to charm it. Whatever you send into that head comes back and takes a piece of yours.
• It flails and flails and cannot mark you. Let it. Save the enchanted steel for the swing that matters.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never — not from cruelty, but because there is nobody left in there to answer. I tried once, in a flooded cellar under Harrowgate. It could not shape a single word, only whine, and the whining nearly had me. Lay it to rest, then find its grave and put right whatever drove it there.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor menace

sections.body:

Full Attack: Incorporeal touch +3 melee (1d4 Wisdom drain)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: An allip is unable to cause physical harm, although it doesn’t appear to know that. It keeps flailing away at enemies, yet it inflicts no wounds. An allip cannot speak intelligibly.

Babble (Su): An allip constantly mutters and whines to itself, creating a hypnotic effect. All sane creatures within 60 feet of the allip must succeed on a DC 16 Will save or be affected as though by a hypnotism spell for 2d4 rounds. This is a sonic mind-affecting compulsion effect. Creatures that successfully save cannot be affected by the same allip’s babble for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Madness (Su): Anyone targeting an allip with a thought detection, mind control, or telepathic ability makes direct contact with its tortured mind and takes 1d4 points of Wisdom damage.

Wisdom Drain (Su): An allip causes 1d4 points of Wisdom drain each time it hits with its incorporeal touch attack. On each such successful attack, the allip itself is briefly strengthened by what it has taken.

Incorporeal Traits: An incorporeal creature has no physical body. It can be harmed only by other incorporeal creatures, by magic weapons, by spells, spell-like effects and supernatural effects, and it takes only half damage from a corporeal source (with a 50% chance to ignore damage from a corporeal magic weapon entirely). It can pass through solid objects at will and its own attacks pass through armor, ignoring natural armor, ordinary armor and shields; it has a deflection bonus equal to its Charisma bonus instead. It moves silently and cannot be heard with Listen checks unless it chooses to be.

Turn Resistance (Ex): An allip is harder to turn or rebuke than an ordinary undead creature. Anyone attempting to turn, rebuke, command or bolster it treats the allip as though it were two levels more powerful than it actually is.

Undead Traits: Undead are immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. They are not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and are immune to damage to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution and to fatigue and exhaustion effects. They have no Constitution score, cannot be raised or resurrected, and are destroyed rather than merely beaten down. They are not at risk from massive damage, they cannot heal on their own unless they have fast healing or regeneration, and negative energy heals them while positive energy harms them. Darkvision 60 ft.

lore.summary: Once a mortal man or woman, destroyed not by blade nor plague but by the touch of absolute evil, and remade in its image: grey, hairless, slack-skinned, with black holes where the eyes were. It keeps fleeting scraps of the life it lost and the tongue it spoke. It belongs to the chaotic evil planes, and is met in our world only where such places have bled through.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized and man-shaped, which is the whole horror of it — you will know the shape before you know the thing.
Durability: Far tougher than its wasted frame suggests, and it never tires and never yields.
Defenses: A thick, corpse-grey hide that ordinary steel struggles to bite; cold iron cuts it as nothing else will. Lightning does not touch it at all, and both acid and flame are half-wasted on it.
Speed: Slow. A shambling, deliberate walk — you can outpace it at an easy jog and it will still be coming.
Might: A heavy slam with weight behind it, and that is the least dangerous thing about it.
Mind: Dull and dim. It retains fleeting memories of its past life and can speak Common, or whatever tongue it spoke living, though it seldom troubles to.
Disposition: Malice without appetite. It does not feed and it does not hoard; it kills in order to make more of itself.
Bane: Bodaks loathe sunlight, for its merest touch burns their impure flesh — each moment in the direct rays of the sun eats away at it. Fight one at noon in the open and the sky does half your work; cold iron does the rest.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It shambles toward you and meets your eyes, and that is the whole of its art: a stare that simply stops the heart. Any humanoid killed by that gaze stands up grey-skinned the following day, a bodak itself. Failing the stare it slams with a heavy fist. It keeps to the dark and the deep, hunts alone or in small silent gangs, and it does not withdraw once it has seen you.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never meet its eye. Fight it staring at its knees, and drill everyone in your company to do the same before you go in.
• Cold iron bites it. Plain steel skates off that hide, lightning does nothing at all, and fire and acid barely trouble it.
• Whoever it stares dead will rise as one of them by the next day. Burn your fallen before you sleep.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. It has words — I heard one repeat a woman's name over and over, in a voice like wet rope dragged over stone — but there is no bargain in it, and to hold its gaze while it talks is to die where you stand. If you must hear it out, hear it with your eyes on its feet.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Full Attack: Slam +6 melee (1d8+1)

Saves: Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +7

Challenge Rating: 8

Treasure: None

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Origin: Bodaks are the undead remnants of humanoids who have been destroyed by the touch of absolute evil. A bodak retains fleeting memories of its past life and can speak Common (or some other humanoid language).

Death Gaze (Su): Death, range 30 feet, Fortitude DC 15 negates. Humanoids who die from this attack are transformed into bodaks 24 hours later. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Vulnerability to Sunlight (Ex): Bodaks loathe sunlight, for its merest touch burns their impure flesh. Each round of exposure to the direct rays of the sun deals 1 point of damage to the creature.

Damage Reduction 10/Cold Iron: A bodak ignores the first 10 points of damage from each attack unless that attack is made with a cold iron weapon.

Undead Traits: Undead are immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. They are not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and are immune to damage to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution and to fatigue and exhaustion effects. They have no Constitution score, cannot be raised or resurrected, and are destroyed rather than merely beaten down. They are not at risk from massive damage, they cannot heal on their own unless they have fast healing or regeneration, and negative energy heals them while positive energy harms them. Darkvision 60 ft.

lore.summary: A gaunt, towering husk — a walking cage of bone that stalks the Ethereal and the Astral, preying on natives and travellers alike with sadistic glee. Behind its ribs floats a small shrivelled figure wearing the features of its last victim: a soul it swallowed whole and now burns for fuel. It does not hunt your life. It hunts what is left when the life is done.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Half again a tall man's height, and lean with it — dry bone and stretched hide, all reach and no bulk.
Durability: Enormously hardy, plated over in bone that turns aside most honest blows.
Defenses: Bone armour and a strong native resistance to spellcraft. Worse, much of what does get through is swallowed by the prisoner in its chest instead of touching the devourer at all — banishments, terrors, compulsions, charms and soul-traps all go into the wrong creature.
Speed: Walks at a man's pace and climbs like a spider, and it needs no more — it steps between the planes to find you.
Might: Immense strength. Its bony claws flay a man alive, and every furrow they open takes some of the life beneath along with the flesh.
Mind: Sharply clever, patient and watchful. It speaks Common and uses it well.
Disposition: Deliberate and cruel. It wants your essence, not your corpse; the killing is only the door it must open first.
Bane: The prisoner in its ribs is its powder magazine. Free that soul, or make it spend the last of it, and you are left facing claws and nothing else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens with stolen sorcery — confusion sown among your ranks, a withering ray, a ghostly hand sent gliding across the room to drain a man where he stands — and only then closes to rake with its claws, each stroke sapping the life beneath the skin. Against the one it truly wants it forgoes killing blows entirely and reaches out to take the essence instead. A soul so taken cannot be called back by any raising; only a great wish, or the destruction of the devourer itself, will loose it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The thing caged in its ribs is why it can throw sorcery at all. Empty it and you are fighting a big angry skeleton.
• Charms, fears, banishments and soul-traps land on the prisoner, not the monster. Do not spend your best that way.
• Every claw that lands takes life you will not get back by resting. Fight it at reach, and bring someone who can restore what it steals.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, though it will talk, and it is the cleverest dead thing I have faced. It speaks only to learn which of you is worth keeping. In the grey between worlds one offered me the soul behind its ribs if I would hand over my companion. Do not bargain for what it holds — break the thing and the soul goes free anyway.

sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Devourers lurk on the Ethereal Plane and the Astral Plane, stalking both natives and travelers with equal sadistic glee. A devourer is about 9 feet tall and weighs 500 pounds, and it speaks Common. Even if it had no special abilities, a devourer would be a terrible opponent, for its bony claws can flay enemies alive.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a devourer’s claw attack or spectral hand ability gain one negative level. The DC is 19 for the Fortitude save to remove a negative level. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Trap Essence (Su): The devourer is named for its ability to consume an enemy’s life essence. To do so, it must forgo its normal melee attacks and make a trap essence attack. This requires a normal attack roll but deals no damage. The save DC is Charisma-based. A slain creature’s essence is trapped within the devourer’s ribs, and the tiny figure takes on that victim’s features. The trapped essence cannot be raised or resurrected, but a limited wish, miracle, or wish spell frees it, as does destroying the devourer. A devourer can hold only one essence at a time. The trapped essence provides a devourer with enough power to use five spell-like abilities for each level of the trapped creature. As this energy is expended, the twisted soul fades away until it evaporates completely. The trapped essence gains one negative level for every five times the devourer uses one of its spell-like abilities. When the essence’s number of negative levels equals the creature’s total levels, the essence is destroyed. If an essence is freed, the restored creature must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save for each negative level or lose that level permanently.

Spell-Like Abilities: At the start of any encounter, the trapped essence within a devourer is assumed to have 3d4+3 levels (enough fuel for thirty to seventy-five uses). Once per round, a devourer can use one of the following abilities: confusion (DC 17), control undead (DC 20), ghoul touch (DC 15), lesser planar ally, ray of enfeeblement, spectral hand, suggestion (DC 16), true seeing. Caster level 18th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spell Deflection (Su): The trapped essence provides a measure of magical protection. If any of the following spells are cast at the devourer and overcome its spell resistance, they affect the imprisoned essence instead: banishment, chaos hammer, confusion, crushing despair, detect thoughts, dispel evil, dominate person, fear, geas/quest, holy word, hypnotism, imprisonment, magic jar, maze, suggestion, trap the soul, or any form of charm or compulsion. In many cases, this deflection effectively neutralizes the spell. Some of these effects might eliminate the trapped essence, depriving the devourer of its spell-like abilities until it can consume another victim.

Spell Resistance 21: A spell or spell-like ability directed at a devourer fails unless its caster succeeds on a caster level check against DC 21.

Undead Traits: Undead are immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. They are not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and are immune to damage to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution and to fatigue and exhaustion effects. They have no Constitution score, cannot be raised or resurrected, and are destroyed rather than merely beaten down. They are not at risk from massive damage, they cannot heal on their own unless they have fast healing or regeneration, and negative energy heals them while positive energy harms them. Darkvision 60 ft.

lore.summary: The middle of the three nightshades: a black giant in the shape of a man, composed of equal parts darkness and absolute evil, come up out of the Plane of Shadow to unmake whatever lives. Its kin are the nightwing, a batlike horror that hunts on the wing and eats the enchantment out of your arms, and the nightcrawler, a lightless worm that swims the earth and swallows men whole.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a man's shape grown to the height of a cottage, blacker than a starless sky, and heavy as a siege engine.
Durability: Appalling. Expect to spend everything you have brought and find it still standing over you.
Defenses: Silvered arms and enchanted arms both, or you are hitting a wall. Cold cannot touch it, spellcraft slides off it more often than it lands, and the ground about it is steeped in an unhallowed emanation that strengthens it and every dead thing standing near it.
Speed: Strides faster than a man runs, and can heave itself through the air, though clumsily and not far.
Might: Ruinous. Slams that break bone through good plate, and hands that will pick a weapon out of your grip and crush it to scrap, enchantment and all.
Mind: Brilliant and cold. It reads and understands every form of speech, answers inside your skull rather than aloud, and fights like a general rather than a beast.
Disposition: It hunts to extinguish. It waits in dark places where it can take the unwary, and calls shadows and wraiths up out of the ground to do the herding.
Bane: Natural daylight. Not a conjured light — the sun's own — which blunts every stroke, ward and save it makes. Bring silver, bring the dawn, and never let it take the weapon out of your hand.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits in the dark and it moves first. Expect it already hastened, already able to see what you have hidden, before you know it is in the room. Then a wave of unholy blight across your line, a snare laid on your best sword-arm, and a killing word aimed at whoever is chanting. It uses its stare to lock a man rigid with terror, wrenches weapons from hands and grinds them between its palms, and closes to slam whoever it has cut off from the others. Once in a night it can call up shadows, greater shadows or dread wraiths to finish what it began.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver and enchantment both, or you may as well be beating a cliff. Half-measures do nothing here.
• It crushes weapons out of your hands. Carry a spare, and keep the one that matters away from its reach.
• Fight it under open sky at midday or do not fight it. Conjured light will not serve — it must be the sun itself.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, though it will speak — courteously, and directly into your mind, for it uses no voice. That is the trap. It understands every tongue you own and answers in your own thoughts, and every word is aimed at parting you from the man beside you. I have talked to hags, dragons and devils. This one I ran from, and I am not ashamed of it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.body:

Special Qualities: Aversion to daylight, damage reduction 15/silver and magic, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to cold, spell resistance 29, telepathy 100 ft., undead traits
Saves: Fort +11, Ref +11, Will +19

Feats: Cleave, Combat Expertise, Combat Reflexes, Great Fortitude, Improved Disarm, Improved Initiative, Power Attack, Quicken Spell-Like Ability (unholy blight)
Environment: Plane of Shadow
