Challenge Rating: 16
Alignment: Always chaotic evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 22–31 levels (Huge); 32–42 levels (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Nightwalkers are human-shaped horrors that haunt the darkness. A nightwalker is about 20 feet tall and weighs about 12,000 pounds. Nightwalkers lurk in dark areas where they can almost always surprise the unwary. A nightwalker’s natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Aversion to Daylight (Ex): If exposed to natural daylight (not merely a daylight spell), nightshades take a –4 penalty on all attack rolls, saving throws, and skill checks.

Crush Item (Su): A nightwalker can destroy any weapon or item of Large size or smaller (even magic ones, but not artifacts) by picking it up and crushing it between its hands. The nightwalker must make a successful disarm attempt to grab an item held by an opponent. The item is entitled to a DC 34 Fortitude save to resist destruction. The save DC is Strength-based.

Desecrating Aura (Su): All nightshades give off a 20-foot-radius emanation of utter desecration, imbuing their surroundings with negative energy. This ability works much like a desecrate spell, except that the nightshade’s evil is so great that it is treated as the shrine of an evil power. All undead within 20 feet of the nightshade (including the creature itself) gain a +2 profane bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws, and are made hardier in proportion to their power. (The nightshade’s attack and save entries given here already include these profane bonuses.) Charisma checks made to turn undead within this area take a –6 penalty. A nightshade’s desecrating aura cannot be dispelled except by a dispel evil spell or similar effect. If the effect is dispelled, the nightshade can resume it as a free action on its next turn. Its desecrating aura is suppressed if a nightshade enters a consecrated or hallowed area, but the nightshade’s presence also suppresses the consecrated or hallowed effect for as long as it remains in the area.

Evil Gaze (Su): Fear, 30 feet. A creature that meets the nightwalker’s gaze must succeed on a DC 24 Will save or be paralyzed with fear for 1d8 rounds. Whether or not the save is successful, that creature cannot be affected again by the same nightshade’s gaze for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—contagion (DC 18), deeper darkness, detect magic, greater dispel magic, haste, see invisibility, and unholy blight (DC 18); 3/day—confusion (DC 18), hold monster (DC 19), invisibility; 1/day—cone of cold (DC 19), finger of death (DC 21), plane shift (DC 21). Caster level 21st. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Summon Undead (Su): A nightwalker can summon undead creatures once per night: 7–12 shadows, 2–5 greater shadows, or 1–2 dread wraiths. The undead arrive in 1d10 rounds and serve for 1 hour or until released.

Skills: *When hiding in a dark area, a nightwalker gains a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks.

Tactics Round-by-Round: The nightwalker is an exceedingly intelligent foe that makes the best use of all its abilities. It favors using its spell-like abilities to divide and disable its enemies, then closing to melee with opponents it has isolated from their allies. Prior to combat it keeps see invisibility active and uses haste and invisibility to prepare. Round 1: move within 30 feet to use its gaze and strike with confusion or hold monster, coupled with a quickened unholy blight. Round 2: hit a spellcaster with finger of death and another quickened unholy blight. Round 3: close and attempt to disarm an enemy fighter. Round 4: crush the disarmed weapon (or use the gaze if the disarm failed). Round 5: full attack against the unarmed foe or a nearby spellcaster.

Other Nightshades: Nightwing and Nightcrawler: The nightwalker is the middle of the three known nightshades, and all three share aversion to daylight, the desecrating aura, damage reduction 15/silver and magic, immunity to cold, telepathy 100 ft. and the power to summon undead. The nightwing (CR 14, Huge) is a batlike flyer with a 40-foot wingspan that hunts on the wing, all but invisible save for the stars it blots out; it flies 60 ft. (good), bites for 2d6+17 with a 19–20 critical, has spell resistance 27, and its magic drain lets a touch attack force a magic weapon, shield or suit of armor to make a DC 22 Fortitude save or lose 1 point of enhancement bonus — an item stripped of its entire bonus becomes merely masterwork and loses its special abilities, reversible only by dispel evil cast on it within a number of days equal to the caster’s level and on a DC 29 caster level check. It summons 5–12 shadows, 2–4 greater shadows, or 1 dread wraith. The nightcrawler (CR 18, Gargantuan) is the greatest of the three: about 7 feet thick and 100 feet long from maw to sting, weighing some 55,000 pounds. It burrows 60 ft. through earth and erupts beneath its prey, has spell resistance 31, bites with improved grab and swallows opponents of Huge size or smaller whole (2d8+12 bludgeoning plus 12 acid per round in its gizzard, cut free with 35 points of damage against AC 21), drains a negative level each round from anything inside it (DC 26 Fortitude to remove), and stings with a poison dealing 2d6 Strength initial and secondary damage (DC 22 Fortitude). It summons 9–16 shadows, 3–6 greater shadows, or 2–4 dread wraiths.

Spell Resistance 29: A spell or spell-like ability directed at a nightwalker fails unless its caster succeeds on a caster level check against DC 29.

Undead Traits: Undead are immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. They are not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and are immune to damage to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution and to fatigue and exhaustion effects. They have no Constitution score, cannot be raised or resurrected, and are destroyed rather than merely beaten down. They are not at risk from massive damage, they cannot heal on their own unless they have fast healing or regeneration, and negative energy heals them while positive energy harms them. Darkvision 60 ft.

lore.summary: Not a vampire — a vampire's leavings. A mortal slain by one and raised up as its property, bound like its maker to a coffin and to the soil of its own grave. It looks much as it did in life, with the softness gone out of the face and something predatory left in its place. It hunts where it is sent, and it remains enslaved until its master is destroyed.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized — whatever height and build it carried in life, it carries still.
Durability: It knits shut as fast as you open it, and when it finally drops it does not die: it turns to vapour and runs for its coffin to mend.
Defenses: Silver, or you are doing half the work you think you are. Cold and lightning barely trouble it.
Speed: Quick as a fit man and quicker of hand. It walks up sheer walls like a spider and becomes mist whenever it likes.
Might: Inhumanly strong — it hammers men down and dashes them against rock and wall — and every blow leaves a chill in the bone that no night's rest will lift. Let it pin you and it drinks.
Mind: It thinks, remembers and speaks; it kept its trade, its name and its manners. But its master's will lies over its own, and its master's will wins.
Disposition: Predatory and obedient. Evil now whatever it was before, and it hunts on orders rather than appetite alone.
Bane: Every weakness of its master and none of his strength. Direct sunlight ruins it, running water dissolves it, garlic and a mirror and a firmly presented holy symbol hold it at bay, it cannot enter a home uninvited, and a wooden stake through the heart ends it where it lies.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes in hard and physical — inhuman strength, hammering blows, men flung into walls — and threads its master's tricks through the brawl: mist and wall-crawling to reach whoever is least ready, a stare that takes a man's will and turns him on his own fellows, and a grapple that finishes with fangs in a throat and the strength draining out of the body. Cut it down and it will not lie still. It goes to vapour and flees for its coffin, and if it gets there it will be up again.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The spawn is not the quarry — its master is. Destroy him and the leash breaks; the spawn does not die of it, but it stops being someone's weapon.
• Do not let it fog and run. Find the coffin and burn it out before you ever knock, or block the road home and hold it there.
• Never hold its eye and never let it get its arms about you. The first makes you its weapon, the second makes you its supper.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary. There is a person in there, or the leavings of one, and it will talk — I had a spawn give me its name, its trade and where its master slept, all in the same flat voice. It told the truth about the first two. Remember who is listening through its ears, and that it cannot refuse him.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead
Initiative: +6
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+2 Dex, +3 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+5
Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d6+4 plus energy drain)
Full Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d6+4 plus energy drain)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Blood drain, domination, energy drain
Special Qualities: +2 turn resistance, damage reduction 5/silver, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 2, gaseous form, resistance to cold 10 and electricity 10, spider climb, undead traits
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 14, Con —, Int 13, Wis 13, Cha 14
Skills: Bluff +6, Climb +8, Craft or Profession (any one) +4, Diplomacy +4, Hide +10, Jump +8, Listen +11, Move Silently +10, Search +8, Sense Motive +11, Spot +11
Feats: Alertness(B), Improved Initiative(B), Lightning Reflexes(B), Skill Focus (selected Craft or Profession skill), Toughness
Environment: Any
Organization: Solitary or pack (2–5)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Always evil (any)
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: —

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Vampire spawn are undead creatures that come into being when vampires slay mortals. Like their creators, spawn remain bound to their coffins and to the soil of their graves. They appear much as they did in life, although their features are often hardened, with a predatory look, and they speak Common. Vampire spawn use their inhuman strength when engaging mortals, hammering their foes with powerful blows and dashing them against rocks or walls. They also use their gaseous form and flight abilities to strike where opponents are most vulnerable.

Blood Drain (Ex): A vampire spawn can suck blood from a living victim with its fangs by making a successful grapple check. If it pins the foe, it drains blood, dealing 1d4 points of Constitution drain each round. On each such successful drain attack, the spawn is briefly strengthened by the blood it has taken.

Domination (Su): A vampire spawn can crush an opponent’s will just by looking into his or her eyes. This is similar to a gaze attack, except that the spawn must take a standard action, and those merely looking at it are not affected. Anyone the spawn targets must succeed on a DC 14 Will save or fall instantly under its influence as though by a dominate person spell from a 5th-level caster. The ability has a range of 30 feet. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a vampire spawn’s slam attack gain one negative level. The DC is 14 for the Fortitude save to remove a negative level. The save DC is Charisma-based. For each such negative level bestowed, the vampire spawn is briefly strengthened.

Fast Healing (Ex): A vampire spawn recovers 2 points of damage each round so long as it has not been beaten down. If reduced to the point of collapse in combat, it automatically assumes gaseous form and attempts to escape. It must reach its coffin home within 2 hours or be utterly destroyed. (It can travel up to nine miles in 2 hours.) Once at rest in its coffin, it is helpless. It recovers slightly after 1 hour, then is no longer helpless and resumes healing at the rate of 2 points of damage per round.

Gaseous Form (Su): As a standard action, a vampire spawn can assume gaseous form at will as the spell (caster level 6th), but it can remain gaseous indefinitely and has a fly speed of 20 feet with perfect maneuverability.

Spider Climb (Ex): A vampire spawn can climb sheer surfaces as though with a spider climb spell.

Skills: Vampire spawn have a +4 racial bonus on Bluff, Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Sense Motive, and Spot checks.

Turn Resistance (Ex): A vampire spawn is harder to turn or rebuke than an ordinary undead creature. Anyone attempting to turn, rebuke, command or bolster it treats the spawn as though it were two levels more powerful than it actually is.

Vampire Spawn Weaknesses: Vampire spawn are vulnerable to all attacks and effects that repel or slay vampires. They cannot tolerate the strong odor of garlic and will not enter an area laced with it; they recoil likewise from a mirror or a strongly presented holy symbol. These things do not harm the spawn — they merely keep it at bay: a recoiling vampire must stay at least 5 feet away from the creature holding the mirror or holy symbol and cannot touch or make melee attacks against that creature for the rest of the encounter, and holding one at bay takes a standard action. They cannot cross running water, although they can be carried over it while resting in their coffins or aboard a ship, and they are utterly unable to enter a home or other building unless invited in by someone with the authority to do so (public places, being open to all, they may enter freely). Beating a vampire down in combat incapacitates it but does not always destroy it (see fast healing). Certain attacks, however, can slay one outright: exposing it to direct sunlight disorients it, so that it can take only a single move action or attack action and is destroyed utterly in the next round if it cannot escape; immersion in running water robs it of one-third of its remaining vitality each round until it is destroyed at the end of the third round; and driving a wooden stake through its heart instantly slays it, though it returns to unlife if the stake is removed unless the body is destroyed. A popular tactic is to cut off the creature’s head and fill its mouth with holy wafers.

Undead Traits: Undead are immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless it also works on objects or is harmless. They are not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain or energy drain, and are immune to damage to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution and to fatigue and exhaustion effects. They have no Constitution score, cannot be raised or resurrected, and are destroyed rather than merely beaten down. They are not at risk from massive damage, they cannot heal on their own unless they have fast healing or regeneration, and negative energy heals them while positive energy harms them. Darkvision 60 ft.

lore.summary: Bark for skin, a canopy of leaves for hair that turns colour with the season, and a face much like an elf-maid's. A dryad is one great oak given a woman's shape, and she may never wander far from it. Shy, curious, and rarely seen unless she wishes it. Met in old temperate forest, alone or in a small grove of sisters.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no taller than an elf-maid, and slighter of frame.
Durability: Frail as a woman, and she knows it; she never means to be struck at all.
Defenses: Honest steel slides off her wooden flesh; and she can stand as plain timber while you search the clearing for her.
Speed: She walks as you do, but she steps from trunk to trunk across the whole wood as though the trees were doorways.
Might: Slight. A dagger, and a very fine longbow she looses from cover.
Mind: Clever and resolute, and she has the trade tongue, the elf tongue and the tongue of the wood.
Disposition: Shy and curious, kindly to those who pass gently; her charm is her first answer to a threat, never her blade.
Bane: Cold iron cuts her where good steel will not — bring a cold-forged blade or bring nothing. And her oak is her life: she cannot stray far from it, and sickens and dies within a day if she is kept away.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She would rather not. Threatened, she reaches into the mind of whichever of you is most dangerous and turns him about to face his fellows, or drops the rest of you into a deep sleep, or binds your legs in grasping briars while she withdraws. Lay an edge on her oak, though, and she fights in earnest — arrows from cover, a step through the trees to come at your back, and no mercy asked or given.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Leave the axe at the camp. She counts axes before she counts men.
• If you find yourself agreeing to a small favour for a stranger, that is her charm at work. Go along with it; it is rarely cruel.
• Her oak is her heart. Threaten the tree and you have made an enemy of the whole wood.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Always talk. Show her empty hands, sit down on the leaf mould, praise her wood and mean it. I have had directions, clean water and a night's safe sleep from a dryad who had watched me all afternoon from inside her own trunk. Say nothing of axes. Better, carry none.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Fey
Initiative: +4
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (+4 Dex, +3 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+2
Attack: Dagger +6 melee (1d4/19-20) or masterwork longbow +7 ranged (1d8/×3)
Full Attack: Dagger +6 melee (1d4/19-20) or masterwork longbow +7 ranged (1d8/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/cold iron, tree dependent, wild empathy
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +8, Will +6
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 19, Con 11, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 18
Skills: Escape Artist +11, Handle Animal +11, Hide +11, Knowledge (nature) +11, Listen +9, Move Silently +11, Ride +6, Spot +9, Survival +9, Use Rope +4 (+6 with bindings)
Feats: Great Fortitude, Weapon Finesse
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Solitary or grove (4-7)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually chaotic good
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: At will—entangle (DC 13), speak with plants, tree shape; 3/day—charm person (DC 13), deep slumber (DC 15), tree stride; 1/day—suggestion (DC 15). Caster level 6th. The save DCs are Wisdom-based.

Tree Dependent (Su): Each dryad is mystically bound to a single, enormous oak tree and must never stray more than 300 yards from it. Any who do become ill and die within 4d6 hours. A dryad's oak does not radiate magic.

Wild Empathy (Ex): This power works like the druid's wild empathy class feature, except that the dryad has a +6 racial bonus on the check.

Combat: Shy, intelligent, and resolute, dryads are as elusive as they are alluring—they avoid physical combat and are rarely seen unless they wish to be. If threatened, or in need of an ally, a dryad uses charm person or suggestion, attempting to gain control of the attacker(s) who could help the most against the rest. Any attack on her tree, however, provokes the dryad into a frenzied defense.

lore.summary: Look away. Read this with your eyes on the page and not on her. A nymph is the living spirit of some perfect place — a fall of water, a hidden pool, a glade no map records — and she is beautiful past a mortal's bearing. Those who look full upon her are struck blind, and stay blind. She is kind. She does not always mean to be.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — the height and weight of an elf-woman.
Durability: Slight, and no tougher in the flesh than she appears.
Defenses: A grace beyond nature turns blows aside and shrugs off what ought to fell her, and blades that are not cold iron scarcely trouble her at all.
Speed: She walks as a woman walks and swims like an otter — and when she has finished with you she steps through a door in the air and is elsewhere.
Might: A dagger she barely knows how to hold. All her strength is the druid's craft: lightning called down out of a clear sky, metal made scalding, iron rusted from your grip, briars at the ankle — and healing hands for those she favours.
Mind: Keen, watchful, long of memory and long of humour. She has the wood-tongue and the trade tongue both.
Disposition: Good-hearted and generous to the gentle; she loathes cruelty and ugliness, and her wrath comes without warning.
Bane: Cold iron, and cold iron alone, bites through her guard — ordinary steel is wasted on her. Past that, the whole defence is your own eyelids: keep your gaze on the ground and she can neither blind you nor strike you senseless with a look.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She does not want the fight, and says so. Wrathful, she lets her beauty do the first work — every man who looks up is blinded where he stands — and a second look from her leaves one of you standing stunned and open. Then the druid's art in earnest: briars, storm overhead, armour rusting off the body, a blade gone too hot to hold. When it turns against her she steps through the air and is simply gone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Eyes down. On the ground. Not on her. I have led a blinded man out of a glade and I do not care to do it twice.
• That blindness is not for a season. It is for the rest of your days, barring a miracle you cannot afford.
• Any cruelty done in front of her is a death sentence. Keep your rough men outside the glade.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The finest conversation in this book, if you can keep your eyes on her feet. Speak first, apologise for the intrusion, offer nothing but courtesy and go when told. I once traded songs with one for a whole summer evening and came away with a wound closed and a warning that later saved my life. Look at the ground.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Fey
Initiative: +3
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), swim 20 ft.
Armor Class: 17 (+3 Dex, +4 deflection), touch 17, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+3
Attack: Dagger +6 melee (1d4/19-20)
Full Attack: Dagger +6 melee (1d4/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Blinding beauty, spells, spell-like abilities, stunning glance
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/cold iron, low-light vision, unearthly grace, wild empathy
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +12, Will +12
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 17, Con 12, Int 16, Wis 17, Cha 19
Skills: Concentration +10, Diplomacy +6, Escape Artist +12, Handle Animal +13, Heal +12, Hide +12, Listen +12, Move Silently +12, Ride +5, Sense Motive +12, Spot +12, Swim +8, Use Rope +3 (+5 with bindings)
Feats: Combat Casting, Dodge, Weapon Finesse
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Usually chaotic good
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 7th-12th level (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Blinding Beauty (Su): This ability affects all humanoids within 30 feet of a nymph. Those who look directly at a nymph must succeed on a DC 17 Fortitude save or be blinded permanently as though by the blindness spell. A nymph can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Stunning Glance (Su): As a standard action, a wrathful nymph can stun a creature within 30 feet with a look. The target creature must succeed on a DC 17 Fortitude save or be stunned for 2d4 rounds. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day—dimension door. Caster level 7th.

Spells: A nymph casts divine spells as a 7th-level druid.

Typical Druid Spells Prepared: (6/5/4/3/1, save DC 13 + spell level) 0—cure minor wounds, detect magic, flare, guidance, light, resistance; 1st—calm animals, cure light wounds, entangle, longstrider, speak with animals; 2nd—barkskin, heat metal, lesser restoration, tree shape; 3rd—call lightning, cure moderate wounds, protection from energy; 4th—rusting grasp.

Unearthly Grace (Su): A nymph adds her Charisma modifier as a bonus on all her saving throws, and as a deflection bonus to her Armor Class. (The statistics block already reflects these bonuses.)

Wild Empathy (Ex): This power works like the druid's wild empathy class feature, except that a nymph has a +6 racial bonus on the check.

Skills: A nymph has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. She can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. She can use the run action while swimming, provided she swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: Goat below the belt and man above, chestnut-haired, with horns and hooves of jet. A satyr is wine, music, theft and mischief, and one in any band carries a set of pan pipes that can charm a clearing, drop it asleep, or send it running in terror. Met in old temperate wood — alone, in pairs, or in a whole rowdy troop.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — about the height of a half-elf, and heavier in the leg.
Durability: Hardier than the rest of the wood-folk, and quick enough to be elsewhere when the blow lands.
Defenses: A thick hide and a dodging step; common steel does poorly against him.
Speed: Faster afoot than any man in armour, and he knows every deer-path in the wood by heart.
Might: Little. A head butt with those black horns, a dagger held low, and a shortbow he looses from the brush.
Mind: Clever, quick-tongued and a practised liar. He has the wood-tongue and usually the trade tongue as well.
Disposition: Neither good nor wicked — pleasure-seeking, prankish, and now and then cruel about it. His ears and eyes are terribly keen; you will not creep up on him in the wild.
Bane: Cold iron cuts him where ordinary steel will not. And the pipes are the whole of his danger: take them and he is only a thief with a bow — in any other hands they are carved reeds and nothing more.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: The piper plays first, and chooses his tune: it charms, or lays the clearing into sleep, or sets grown men running blind with terror. Then arrows out of the brush while you stand witless. Come to grips and he butts with the horns and stabs low with the dagger, giving ground the whole while and leading you where his fellows are waiting.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Wine buys more than steel here. Bring a full skin and ask for directions.
• Shake off his piping once and that same set of pipes cannot touch you again for a day and a night. Press him hard in that window.
• Count your purse, your rings and your companions before you leave the clearing.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Talk, and bring drink. A satyr will trade almost anything for good wine and a song he has not heard, and he knows the wood better than the wood knows itself. Do not gamble with him. I lost a good cloak, one boot and most of an evening to one who was still laughing when I woke.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser danger

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Fey
Initiative: +1
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+1 Dex, +4 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+2
Attack: Head butt +2 melee (1d6) or shortbow +3 ranged (1d6/×3)
Full Attack: Head butt +2 melee (1d6) and dagger –3 melee (1d4/19-20); or shortbow +3 ranged (1d6/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Pipes
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/cold iron, low-light vision
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +5
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 13, Con 12, Int 12, Wis 13, Cha 13
Skills: Bluff +9, Diplomacy +3, Disguise +1 (+3 acting), Hide +13, Intimidate +3, Knowledge (nature) +9, Listen +15, Move Silently +13, Perform (wind instruments) +9, Spot +15, Survival +1 (+3 aboveground)
Feats: Alertness(B), Dodge, Mobility
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Solitary, pair, band (3-5), or troop (6-11)
Challenge Rating: 2 (without pipes) or 4 (with pipes)
Alignment: Usually chaotic neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 6th-10th level (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Pipes (Su): Satyrs can play a variety of magical tunes on their pan pipes. Usually, only one satyr in a group carries pipes. When it plays, all creatures within a 60-foot spread (except satyrs) must succeed on a DC 13 Will save or be affected by charm person, sleep, or fear (caster level 10th; the satyr chooses the tune and its effect). In the hands of other beings, these pipes have no special powers. A creature that successfully saves against any of the pipe's effects cannot be affected by the same set of pipes for 24 hours. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Skills: Satyrs have a +4 racial bonus on Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Perform, and Spot checks.

Combat: The keen senses of a satyr make it almost impossible to surprise one in the wild. Conversely, with their own natural grace and agility, satyrs can sneak up on travelers who are not carefully watching the surrounding wilderness. Once engaged in battle, an unarmed satyr attacks with a powerful head butt. A satyr expecting trouble is likely to be armed with a bow and a dagger and typically looses arrows from hiding, weakening an enemy before closing.

lore.summary: You may hear them. You will not see them. A pixie stands no higher than a child's waist, wears bright cloth and shoes with curled and pointed toes, and is unseen from birth — unseen even in the act of shooting you. Carefree until crossed, ferocious about intruders, and merciless towards anything wicked that enters their wood.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — waist-high to a child, and winged.
Durability: You could break one in your hands. If you could ever find one.
Defenses: Unseen always, even as it looses; spells slide off it as often as not; and nothing short of cold iron does it any real harm.
Speed: Quick on the wing and quicker through branches — it flies rings about a running man.
Might: Almost none in the arm. It is all in the arrows and the small arts: grasping briars, your thoughts read off your face, your own magic snuffed out, a whole false glade raised around you, a muddling of the wits, and now and then a borrowed shape. A rare one can set a man dancing until he drops.
Mind: Bright, curious, and well-spoken in the wood-tongue and the trade tongue alike.
Disposition: Carefree until crossed. They guard their wood and they have judged you before you are three paces inside it.
Bane: Cold iron, and only cold iron, gets through — everything else is wasted effort. Beneath that it is a frail thing; the whole trouble is landing anything on it at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Ambush, always, and never a fair one. Arrows come out of empty air: one sort drops a man asleep however hardy he is, another wipes his memory clean away — he wakes still knowing his sword-work and his letters and nothing whatever of his own name. They tangle your feet, strip your wards, read your intent, and raise up an illusion of a glade that is not there to walk you in circles until you give up and leave. Only the cruel are killed outright.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Throw flour, ash or fine dust on the wind. You still will not see it — but you will see where it is not.
• The memory arrow is the one to fear. Write your name and your errand inside your helm before you enter that wood.
• They kill wicked men and merely rob good ones. Be the second sort.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Speak to the empty air. They are listening; they are always listening. Be plain, be courteous, say why you have come and offer to go again. I have been guided out of a warded wood by a voice I never once laid eyes on. Draw steel and the arrows start.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Fey
Initiative: +4
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 60 ft. (good)
Armor Class: 16 (+1 size, +4 Dex, +1 natural), touch 15, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +0/–6
Attack: Short sword +5 melee (1d4–2/19-20) or longbow +5 ranged (1d6–2/×3)
Full Attack: Short sword +5 melee (1d4–2/19-20) or longbow +5 ranged (1d6–2/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities, special arrows
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 10/cold iron, greater invisibility, low-light vision, spell resistance 15
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +6, Will +4
Abilities: Str 7, Dex 18, Con 11, Int 16, Wis 15, Cha 16
Skills: Bluff +7, Concentration +4, Escape Artist +8, Hide +8, Listen +10, Move Silently +8, Ride +8, Search +9, Sense Motive +6, Spot +10
Feats: Alertness, Dodge(B), Weapon Finesse(B)
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Gang (2-4), band (6-11), or tribe (20-80)
Challenge Rating: 4 (5 with irresistible dance)
Alignment: Always neutral good
Treasure: No coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 2nd-3rd level (Small)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Greater Invisibility (Su): A pixie remains invisible even when it attacks. This ability is constant — a natural invisibility the pixie need not cast — but the pixie can suppress or resume it as a free action.

Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day—lesser confusion (DC 14), dancing lights, detect chaos, detect good, detect evil, detect law, detect thoughts (DC 15), dispel magic, entangle (DC 14), permanent image (DC 19; visual and auditory elements only). Caster level 8th. The save DCs are Charisma-based. One pixie in ten can use irresistible dance (caster level 8th) once per day.

Special Arrows (Ex): Pixies sometimes employ arrows that deal no damage but can erase memory or put a creature to sleep.

Memory Loss: An opponent struck by this arrow must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or lose all memory. The save DC is Charisma-based and includes a +2 racial bonus. The subject retains skills, languages, and class abilities but forgets everything else until he or she receives a heal spell or memory restoration with limited wish, wish, or miracle.

Sleep: Any opponent struck by this arrow, regardless of how powerful or experienced, must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or be affected as though by a sleep spell. The save DC is Charisma-based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Skills: Pixies have a +2 racial bonus on Listen, Search, and Spot checks.

Combat: The normally carefree pixies ferociously attack evil creatures and unwanted intruders. They take full advantage of their invisibility and other abilities to harass and drive away opponents.

lore.summary: No taller than a wine bottle, blue of skin and green of hair, with the brown hairy hind legs of a cricket and a fiddle the size of a spoon. Grigs are the smallest and by far the boldest of the sprite-folk: they leap absurd distances, they run from nothing at all, and they are found in noisy bands throughout old temperate forest.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — no taller than a wine bottle, and lighter than the bottle when empty.
Durability: The frailest thing in this book. A carelessly placed boot would do it.
Defenses: Hard to see and harder to hold; spells mostly fail against it outright; and honest steel barely marks it.
Speed: It leaps astonishing distances, flies well enough though clumsily, and crosses leaf mould without a whisper.
Might: None worth the word — a sword like a pin and a little bow. The danger is the fiddle and the small tricks: grasping briars, a voice thrown across the clearing, a borrowed face, and a burst of smoke or blinding sparks.
Mind: Plain by fey standards but far from stupid, and merry with it. It has the wood-tongue, and sometimes the trade tongue.
Disposition: Mischievous, good-hearted, and fiercely brave for something so small. It fights well above its size because it has never learned better.
Bane: Cold iron cuts it as nothing else will. And the fiddle holds you only while the bow keeps moving — silence the fiddler and the whole band is a handful of pins.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: One in each band carries the fiddle, and the moment trouble starts he strikes up: everyone within hearing who is not sprite-kin dances helplessly for as long as he keeps playing. The rest shoot from the leaves, throw their voices to draw you the wrong way, go unseen, or set off a burst of light and smoke and leap clean out of your reach.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Go for the fiddler. Nothing else in the band matters.
• Wax in the ears before you go looking. It has spared me a great deal of undignified dancing.
• They are good, they are brave, and they are the size of a spoon. Do not kill them. You will feel like the monster, and you will be right.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The easiest talk in the wood and the least useful. A grig wants a song, a joke, or a bright button, and will tell you everything it knows in exchange — most of which is wrong. I have been fiddled into dancing twice, both times for laughing at the wrong moment. They meant no harm either time.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A small nuisance

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Tiny Fey
Initiative: +4
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 40 ft. (poor)
Armor Class: 18 (+2 size, +4 Dex, +2 natural), touch 16, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +0/–11
Attack: Short sword +6 melee (1d3–3/19-20) or longbow +6 ranged (1d4–3/×3)
Full Attack: Short sword +6 melee (1d3–3/19-20) or longbow +6 ranged (1d4–3/×3)
Space/Reach: 2½ ft./0 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities, fiddle
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/cold iron, low-light vision, spell resistance 17
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +6, Will +3
Abilities: Str 5, Dex 18, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 14

Feats: Dodge(B), Stealthy, Weapon Finesse(B)
Environment: Temperate forests

Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always neutral good
Treasure: No coins; 50% goods; 50% items

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: 3/day—disguise self, entangle (DC 13), invisibility (self only), pyrotechnics (DC 14), ventriloquism (DC 13). Caster level 9th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Fiddle (Su): One grig in each band carries a tiny, grig-sized fiddle. When the fiddler plays, any nonsprite within 30 feet of the instrument must succeed on a DC 12 Will save or be affected as though by irresistible dance for as long as the playing continues. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Skills: Grigs have a +8 racial bonus on Jump checks. *They also have a +5 racial bonus on Move Silently checks in a forest setting.

Combat: Grigs are fierce by sprite standards, attacking opponents fearlessly with bow and dagger.

lore.summary: Six legs, a lean blue-black cat the length of a fallen man, and two barbed tentacles rising from its shoulders — and never quite where the eye insists it is. It bends the light about itself, so the shape you cut at stands a pace from the flesh that kills you. Temperate hills and deep wood. It kills for the pleasure of it, fed or starving alike.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a gaunt panther, longer than a man is tall, carried on six legs.
Durability: Tough as any great cat and no tougher; it is the missing, not the mending, that keeps it alive.
Defenses: The light bends about it. Half your honest blows meet empty air, and arrows fare worse still.
Speed: Very quick, and given to dashing past the front rank on all six legs.
Might: Two barbed tentacles that punch through good steel, backed by claw and tooth.
Mind: Dull for a speaking thing, but a cunning hunter — it lures, it ambushes, and it knows a spellcaster on sight.
Disposition: Lawful and wholly evil; it plays with what it catches, then drags the carcass to a bone-strewn lair.
Bane: Its displacement is an illusion of light, not a working to be unravelled — true sight strips it bare, and so does any sense that does not use the eyes. Pen it in a narrow place and it cannot dance. Faced with certain ruin it flees rather than dies.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It marks the robed and the wand-carrying first, whipping barbed tentacles at them from beyond sword's reach while it faces the armoured head-on. It slips past the front rank to maul whoever looks weakest, worries the wounded for sport, and when the odds turn it simply leaves. A pride hunts in concert, driving prey onto one another's claws from ambush.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Half your swings find the ghost. Swing oftener, not better.
• The bow is worse than useless here. Close, or go.
• Fight it in a corridor. In open hill country it circles you and eats your wizard.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It speaks a little of the common tongue. I have heard one do it — a purring, half-swallowed greeting out of a thornbrake, in a child's voice. That is not conversation. That is bait, and it is answered with a spear.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +2
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 16 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +5 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+14
Attack: Tentacle +9 melee (1d6+4)
Full Attack: 2 tentacles +9 melee (1d6+4) and bite +4 melee (1d8+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft. (10 ft. with tentacles)
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., displacement, low-light vision, resistance to ranged attacks
Saves: Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +3
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 5, Wis 12, Cha 8
Skills: Hide +10, Listen +5, Move Silently +7, Spot +5
Feats: Alertness, Dodge, Stealthy
Environment: Temperate hills
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pride (6–10)
Challenge Rating: 4 (12 for a pack lord)
Alignment: Usually lawful evil
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 7–9 levels (Large); 10–18 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Displacement (Su): A light-bending glamer continually surrounds a displacer beast, making it difficult to surmise the creature's true location. Any melee or ranged attack directed at it has a 50% miss chance unless the attacker can locate the beast by some means other than sight. A true seeing effect allows the user to see the beast's position, but see invisibility has no effect.

Resistance to Ranged Attacks (Su): A displacer beast gains a +2 resistance bonus on saves against any ranged spell or ranged magical attack that specifically targets it (except for ranged touch attacks).

Combat: Displacer beasts rake opponents with their two barbed tentacles and bite any foe that closes. They hunt in prides and prefer ambush, striking from cover and relying on the glamer to make the first exchange of blows a waste of the hunter's effort.

Skills: A displacer beast has a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks, thanks to its displacement ability.

Displacer Beast Pack Lord: A rare mutant strain grows to Huge size — up to 20 feet long and around two tons — with the same displacement and ranged-attack resistance, a heavier natural armor and a sharper mind. A pack lord is a Challenge Rating 12 opponent and commonly leads an ordinary pride.

Source: The displacer beast is not Open Game Content and does not appear in the SRD. This block is reconstructed from Monster Manual 3.5 (pages 66–67) as mirrored by the Forgotten Realms Wiki, realmshelps.net and dndtools.one; two independent mirrors agree on every line above.

lore.summary: Lion behind, eagle before, with broad golden wings and no mane on either sex. Griffons keep the temperate hill country in prides, nesting on crags where nothing walks. They cannot speak — but they understand the common tongue well enough to know when they are being spoken of, which is more than can be said for most beasts a hunter meets.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — nose to tail the length of a cart, with a wingspan several times broader.
Durability: Solidly built under the feathers; a hard beast to put down, though nothing of it is proof against steel.
Defenses: No armour but bone, feather and height. Its safety is the sky.
Speed: Ground-swift, air-swifter; it outflies any horse that ever ran.
Might: The beak is the killing thing and it shears. Claws follow, and the hind talons rake once it has landed on you.
Mind: Dull-witted, yet not an animal: it takes in the common tongue without speaking a word of it, and it remembers a face.
Disposition: Neutral, proud and territorial — it hunts to feed and guards nest and pride to the last.
Bane: It fights from above; take the sky from it. Under a low roof, in dense wood, or tangled in a stout net it is only a large and furious cat. Its will is stubborn, though — it will not be frightened off, so it must be beaten or befriended.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It takes the high air and stoops, diving or springing from a crag to strike with everything at once — beak first, foreclaws next, the hind talons raking as it settles its weight on you. A pride comes in relays, one stooping while another climbs for its turn. It will not break off while the nest lies behind it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It can be flown. Make it friendly first, then six patient weeks and a saddle cut for its shape — no horse tack will sit on that back.
• It will carry you and fight at the same time, but you will not fight well from its back until you have learned its rhythm.
• Eggs and chicks fetch a small fortune, and that is why the crags are littered with egg-thieves. The pride comes home.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It has no voice, but it takes in the common tongue, and I have made my business understood by saying it aloud and slowly at the foot of a crag. That is manners, not parley. Say your piece, then leave. Words do not stop a stoop.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +2
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 80 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 17 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +6 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+15
Attack: Bite +11 melee (2d6+4)
Full Attack: Bite +11 melee (2d6+4) and 2 claws +8 melee (1d4+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Pounce, rake 1d6+2
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent
Saves: Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +5
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 5, Wis 13, Cha 8
Skills: Jump +8, Listen +6, Spot +10
Feats: Iron Will, Multiattack, Weapon Focus (bite)
Environment: Temperate hills
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pride (6–10)
Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 8–10 levels (Large); 11–21 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Griffons prefer to pounce on their prey, either diving to the attack or leaping from above. A griffon cannot speak, but it understands Common.

Pounce (Ex): If a griffon dives upon or charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): Attack bonus +8 melee, damage 1d6+2.

Skills: Griffons have a +4 racial bonus on Jump and Spot checks.

Training a Griffon: Although intelligent, a griffon requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. To be trained, a griffon must have a friendly attitude toward the trainer (this can be achieved through a successful Diplomacy check). Training a friendly griffon requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a griffon requires an exotic saddle. A griffon can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Griffon eggs are worth 3,500 gp apiece on the open market, while young are worth 7,000 gp each. Professional trainers charge 1,500 gp to rear or train a griffon.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a griffon is up to 300 pounds; a medium load, 301–600 pounds; and a heavy load, 601–900 pounds.

lore.summary: Horse behind, giant eagle before, and hungrier than either. Hippogriffs are voracious omnivores of the temperate hills and will take a man as readily as a hare. They nest in flights along high ledges and go up in a shrieking cloud at any shadow that crosses the rock — then come down again, feet first.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer and heavier than a warhorse, with a wingspan that shades a wagon.
Durability: Ordinary flesh beneath the feathers. It dies much as a horse dies.
Defenses: None worth the name, but it is nimble aloft and turns tighter than a thing that size has any right to.
Speed: Very fast afoot and faster still in the air — among the swiftest fliers in hill country.
Might: Clawed forelegs first, carrying the whole weight of the dive; the beak is an afterthought, and a foul one to receive.
Mind: An animal, plainly — no speech, no understanding of any tongue, only appetite and a keen nose.
Disposition: Neutral and aggressive; it hunts whatever it meets, and it will die on its nest rather than give up the eggs.
Bane: It is only a beast: no working, no armour, no cunning. Break the dive and it must land and fight on foot, where it is much the poorer. Met away from its ledge it can be driven off — never while hatchlings lie behind it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It climbs, turns over, and comes down clawed feet first with the weight of the dive behind them; grounded, it slashes with claws and beak. Mated pairs and whole flights work together, stooping again and again to drive intruders off or kill them, and not one of them will break away while the nest is threatened.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Trainable, and cheaper to come by than a griffon. Six weeks of patient work and a saddle cut for its shape.
• The chicks fetch a good price and the flight knows it. They fight to the death over a ledge — take eggs only if you mean to kill every bird on the rock.
• Never stand in the open watching one climb. It is coming back down at you, and the feet arrive before the head.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: A horse's body, an eagle's head, and no more mind than either. I have tried; it took the offering and came back for the hand. There is no talking to a hippogriff — but there is feeding one, and feeding is where every ridden hippogriff began.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Initiative: +2
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares), fly 100 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 15 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +4 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+11
Attack: Claw +6 melee (1d4+4)
Full Attack: 2 claws +6 melee (1d4+4) and bite +1 melee (1d8+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +5, Will +2
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 8
