sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Hippogriffs dive at their prey and strike with their clawed forelegs. When they cannot dive, they slash with claws and beak. Mated pairs and flights of these creatures attack in concert, diving repeatedly to drive away or kill intruders. Hippogriffs fight to the death to defend their nests and their hatchlings, which are prized as aerial mounts and fetch a handsome price in many civilized areas.

Skills: Hippogriffs have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks.

Training a Hippogriff: A hippogriff requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. Training a hippogriff requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a hippogriff requires an exotic saddle. A hippogriff can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Hippogriff eggs are worth 2,000 gp apiece on the open market, while young are worth 3,000 gp each. Professional trainers charge 1,000 gp to rear or train a hippogriff.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a hippogriff is up to 300 pounds; a medium load, 301–600 pounds; and a heavy load, 601–900 pounds.

lore.summary: A grey-brown reptile the length of a barge, low in the fen water, pale-bellied, amber-eyed, with a thicket of long necks rising from one heavy body. The lesser sort carries five heads; the greater carry more, up to a dozen. They do not speak. They keep to temperate marshes, and they swim far better than they walk.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a body like an overturned boat, with necks that reach clear across a ford.
Durability: Vast, and worse than vast: every wound closes while you watch. You will not bleed it out.
Defenses: No hide worth the name and no magic at all. Its defence is simply that it does not stay hurt.
Speed: Ponderous ashore, quick and tireless in water. It will not chase you far up a bank.
Might: Every head bites, and all of them bite at once whether it stands or charges. Step in among those necks and each one that can turn will take a piece of you.
Mind: A beast, and a dull one — no speech, no plan, only many mouths and a fen it knows well.
Disposition: Neutral and territorial; it hunts nothing beyond its own water, and nothing that enters that water leaves whole.
Bane: Fire and acid, and nothing else. A severed neck sprouts twins unless the stump is seared in the very same breath — flame on the blade, or a torch ready in the off hand. Take every head and sear every stump, or it will not die at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It stands in the shallows and lets you come, biting with every head at once, and it bites again the instant you step past a neck — the necks watch every angle and punish every opening. Wounds close as fast as you open them. Take a head and, unless the stump is burnt in the same stroke, two rise in its place and the fight worsens. It grows more mouths as the battle goes on, and dies only when the last stump is closed with fire or acid.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Carry fire in your off hand before you ever draw. A blade alone lengthens the fight; it does not win it.
• Reddish means it breathes flame and laughs at your torch — sear those stumps with cold instead. Purplish means frost, and fire will serve.
• Fight it up the bank and never with your back to the fen. In its own water it is quick and you are not.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing behind those amber eyes but appetite, and no tongue in any of the mouths. I tried once from a punt, in three languages, while a five-necked thing watched me the way a cat watches a jar. It was measuring the distance. Leave the fen.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Magical Beast (five-headed hydra; a pyrohydra is Huge Magical Beast [Fire], a cryohydra Huge Magical Beast [Cold])
Initiative: +1
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), swim 20 ft.
Armor Class: 15 (–2 size, +1 Dex, +6 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+16
Attack: 5 bites +6 melee (1d10+3)
Full Attack: 5 bites +6 melee (1d10+3)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: — (a pyrohydra or cryohydra breathes fire or frost from every head)
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 15, low-light vision, scent
Saves: Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +3
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 12, Con 20, Int 2, Wis 10, Cha 9
Skills: Listen +6, Spot +6, Swim +11
Feats: Combat Reflexes (B), Iron Will, Toughness
Environment: Temperate marshes (pyrohydra: warm marshes; cryohydra: cold marshes)
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 4 (normal); 6 (pyro- or cryohydra)
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: — (a hydra grows by gaining heads, not by advancing)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Hydras can attack with all their heads at no penalty, even if they move or charge during the round. A hydra is grey-brown to dark brown with a light yellow or tan underbelly, amber-eyed and yellow-toothed, about 20 feet long and some 4,000 pounds in weight. Hydras do not speak.

Severing a Head (Ex): A hydra can be killed either by severing all its heads or by slaying its body. To sever a head, an opponent must make a successful sunder attempt with a slashing weapon, declaring where the attack is aimed before the attack roll is made. Making a sunder attempt provokes an attack of opportunity unless the foe has the Improved Sunder feat. Because a hydra's heads writhe and whip about in combat, an opponent can strike at them from any position in which he could strike at the hydra itself, and can ready an action to attempt to sunder a head when the creature bites at him. A head is severed once it has taken enough damage — each head can absorb only a fraction of what the whole creature can — and losing a head also tears at the body, though a natural reflex seals the neck shut to prevent further blood loss. A hydra can no longer attack with a severed head but takes no other penalties. Targeted magical effects cannot sever a hydra's heads (and thus must be directed at the body) unless they deal slashing damage and could be used to make sunder attempts. Any attack that is not, or cannot be, an attempt to sunder a head affects the body instead.

Regrowing Heads (Ex): Each time a head is severed, two new heads spring from the stump in 1d4 rounds. A hydra can never have more than twice its original number of heads at any one time, and any extra heads it gains beyond its original number wither and die within a day. To prevent a severed head from growing back into two heads, at least 5 points of fire or acid damage must be dealt to the stump (a touch attack to hit) before the new heads appear — a stump seared with fire or acid does not regrow. A flaming weapon or similar effect sears the stump in the same blow in which the head is severed, and fire or acid from an area effect may burn several stumps at once. A hydra does not die from losing its heads until every head has been cut off and every stump seared.

Fast Healing (Ex): Each round, a hydra heals damage equal to 10 plus the number of its original heads: fast healing 15 for a five-headed hydra, rising by one for each further head to fast healing 22 for a twelve-headed one. Its body can be slain like any other creature's, but the healing makes that a slow and costly way to kill it.

Feats: A hydra's Combat Reflexes feat allows it to use all its heads for attacks of opportunity.

Skills: Hydras have a +2 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks, thanks to their multiple heads. A hydra has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Larger Hydras (6 to 12 Heads): All hydras are Huge, move 20 ft. and swim 20 ft., have Initiative +1, a space of 15 ft. with 10 ft. reach, are solitary, and carry the same treasure. Everything else scales with the number of heads. Armor Class climbs from 15 (touch 9) with five heads through 17 with seven and 20 with ten to 22 (touch 9) with twelve, as natural armor rises one point per head. Base attack and grapple run from +5/+16 up to +12/+26. Each hydra bites once per head: five bites +6 melee (1d10+3) at five heads, seven bites +10 (1d10+4), nine bites +13 (1d10+5), eleven bites +16 (1d10+6), and twelve bites +17 melee (2d8+6). Strength rises from 17 to 19 at seven heads, 21 at nine, and 23 at eleven; Dex 12, Con 20, Int 2, Wis 10 and Cha 9 never change. Saves go from Fort +9, Ref +5, Will +3 to Fort +13, Ref +9, Will +6. Fast healing equals 10 plus the original head count, so 15 through 22. Feats add Weapon Focus (bite) at six heads, Blind-Fight at nine, and Improved Natural Attack (bite) at twelve, on top of Combat Reflexes (B), Iron Will and Toughness. Challenge Rating runs 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 for five through twelve heads, and is two higher for a pyrohydra or cryohydra of the same size.

Pyrohydra: Huge Magical Beast (Fire). These reddish hydras can breathe jets of fire 10 feet high, 10 feet wide and 20 feet long. All heads breathe once every 1d4 rounds. Each jet deals 3d6 points of fire damage per head, and a successful Reflex save halves the damage; the save DC is 10 + one-half the hydra's original number of heads + the hydra's Constitution modifier. Fire attacks cannot prevent a pyrohydra's stump from growing new heads, since a pyrohydra has immunity to fire, but 5 points of cold damage does. A pyrohydra's Challenge Rating is two higher than an ordinary hydra with the same number of heads, and it haunts warm marshes.

Cryohydra: Huge Magical Beast (Cold). These purplish hydras can breathe jets of frost 10 feet high, 10 feet wide and 20 feet long. All heads breathe once every 1d4 rounds. Each jet deals 3d6 points of cold damage per head, and a successful Reflex save halves the damage; the save DC is 10 + one-half the hydra's original number of heads + the hydra's Constitution modifier. Cold attacks cannot prevent a cryohydra's stump from growing new heads, since a cryohydra has immunity to cold, but 5 points of fire damage does. A cryohydra's Challenge Rating is two higher than an ordinary hydra with the same number of heads, and it haunts cold marshes.

lore.summary: From the waist up a comely woman or man; below, a lion's body on four swift paws. Lamias keep to the temperate deserts and the dead towns baking in them, and they lie for a living — a voice out of an empty doorway, a face that is not there, a friend calling your name from a ruin. What they want is your will. They keep the purse as well.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — lion-bodied and long, heavier than it looks and light on its feet.
Durability: Well-muscled and thick-hided for a talking thing, though it dies cleanly enough once you can catch it.
Defenses: No ward but deceit — mirrored doubles, borrowed faces, a voice thrown across a room. It hides better than a thing that size should.
Speed: It cannot fly. It runs down a horse, and it fights by bounding in, striking, and bounding out again before you can answer.
Might: A dagger in one human hand and lion's claws below — but the true blow is a bare touch that takes the wits out of a man and leaves the body unmarked.
Mind: Clever, articulate and a practised liar. It reads a party at a glance and works on the weakest first.
Disposition: Chaotic and cruel, and playful with its cruelty; it beguiles before it kills, and prefers a victim who walked in willingly.
Bane: It has no stomach for a fair fight — corner it and it is only a lion with a knife. Its draining touch feeds it nothing, so it must land many; keep your wits whole and the beguilements that follow find nothing to grip. Illusion is its entire armoury. See through it and the lamia stands naked.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It never opens honestly. It dresses the ground first with false images and a thrown voice, splits itself into mirrored copies, then springs from cover to lay a hand on you and is back out of reach before your swing lands. It aims to hollow out your judgment early, because a wit-sick victim cannot shake off the beguiling and the whispered suggestion that follow — and once one of your company is turned, it stands back and lets your own friend do the work.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never trust its first face. Nor its second.
• It cannot fly and it will not stand and trade. Block the doorway before you begin.
• The touch does not wound, it empties. Count your own clear thoughts, and pull back the moment you cannot.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It will talk, and talk well, and every word is placed. I traded stories with one at a dry well in the eastern waste: true about the road, lying about the water, and it touched my wrist twice while I admired my own cleverness. Learn what you can. Give it nothing.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +2
Speed: 60 ft. (12 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +7 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +9/+17
Attack: Touch +12 melee (1d4 Wisdom drain) or dagger +12 melee (1d6+4/19–20) or claw +12 melee (1d4+4)
Full Attack: Touch +12 melee (1d4 Wisdom drain); or dagger +12/+7 melee (1d6+4/19–20) and 2 claws +7 melee (1d4+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities, Wisdom drain
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +8, Will +7
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 12, Int 13, Wis 15, Cha 12
Skills: Bluff +14, Concentration +10, Diplomacy +3, Disguise +1 (+3 acting), Hide +11, Intimidate +3, Spot +11
Feats: Dodge, Iron Will, Mobility, Spring Attack
Environment: Temperate deserts
Organization: Solitary, pair, or gang (3–4)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 10–13 levels (Large); 14–27 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Though a lamia is powerful and dangerous in close combat, it has no stomach for a fair fight. It uses its illusion abilities to lure heroes into perilous situations, and then uses its Spring Attack feat to bound out of the shadows and drain Wisdom from its opponents. When it has sapped the will of its victim, it uses its enchantment abilities to beguile and ensnare the unfortunate soul. A lamia forced into physical combat attacks with a dagger in one of its human hands and a pair of lion-like claws. A typical lamia is about 8 feet long and weighs about 700 pounds.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—disguise self, ventriloquism; 3/day—charm monster (DC 15), major image (DC 14), mirror image, suggestion (DC 14); 1/day—deep slumber (DC 14). Caster level 9th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Wisdom Drain (Su): A lamia drains 1d4 points of Wisdom each time it hits with its melee touch attack. (Unlike with other kinds of ability drain attacks, a lamia does not heal any damage when it uses its Wisdom drain.) Lamias try to use this power early in an encounter to make foes more susceptible to charm monster and suggestion.

Skills: Lamias have a +4 racial bonus on Bluff and Hide checks.

lore.summary: A winged horse of the temperate wood, white as fresh drift and shyer than a deer. Pegasi belong to no man; they graze the high meadows in small herds, wheel above the treeline at dusk, and are over the ridge before you have finished admiring them. They know a good heart from a wicked one at a glance, and they always look.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a war-horse in the body, with a wingspan broader than a barn door.
Durability: Sturdy as any fine horse and no more; it lives by flight, not by enduring blows.
Defenses: Hide and speed, nothing else. No ward, no armour, no charm to turn a shaft.
Speed: Runs faster than any mortal horse and flies faster still, tireless over open country.
Might: Two hammering forehooves and a bite it rarely bothers with; it kicks to make room, then goes.
Mind: As clever as a man. It cannot shape our words, but it understands the common tongue perfectly well.
Disposition: Wild, shy and good-hearted; unimpressed by rank, by gold, and most of all by you.
Bane: Skittish and lightly built — a bow or a net takes one easily. Which is why every scoundrel in the realm hunts them, and why I never will.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights only when cornered or when the herd is threatened, and then it fights upward — beating clear of reach, turning, and striking on the pass with both forehooves before it climbs away again. It senses the wicked and the good about it without effort, and it will not suffer the wicked near its meadow. Given any choice at all, it chooses to be elsewhere.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not walk up with a rope in your hand. It sees the rope long before it sees you.
• It weighs the heart of every man who comes near. If it shies from your companion, believe it.
• Grain, salt and patience. Weeks of patience, and a proper saddle after. There is no shorter road.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Speak aloud, and mean it. It cannot answer, but it hears every word and reads the heart behind them — I have never met a creature quicker to judge. I stood still, spoke plainly, and offered nothing. The grey mare came to me on the third morning. She has never once let me name her.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +2
Speed: 60 ft. (12 squares), fly 120 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 14 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +3 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+12
Attack: Hoof +7 melee (1d6+4)
Full Attack: 2 hooves +7 melee (1d6+4) and bite +2 melee (1d3+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent, spell-like abilities
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +4
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 13
Skills: Diplomacy +3, Listen +8, Sense Motive +9, Spot +8
Feats: Flyby Attack, Iron Will
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Solitary, pair, or herd (6–10)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually chaotic good
Treasure: None
Advancement: 5–8 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: At will—detect good and detect evil within a 60-foot radius. Caster level 5th.

Scent (Ex): A pegasus can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell, noticing creatures within 30 feet by scent alone (twice that upwind, half that downwind), and further still if the scent is strong.

Skills: Pegasi have a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Training a Pegasus: Although intelligent, a pegasus requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. To be trained, a pegasus must have a friendly attitude toward the trainer (this can be achieved through a successful Diplomacy check). Training a friendly pegasus requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a pegasus requires an exotic saddle. A pegasus can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Pegasus eggs are worth 2,000 gp each on the open market, while young are worth 3,000 gp per head. Pegasi mature at the same rate as horses. Professional trainers charge 1,000 gp to rear or train a pegasus, which serves a good or neutral master with absolute faithfulness for life.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a pegasus is up to 300 pounds; a medium load, 301–600 pounds; and a heavy load, 601–900 pounds.

lore.summary: A hunting spider the size of a pony that does not live entirely in this world. It steps sideways into the grey country between the planes, walks there unseen while you argue about the noise, and steps back beside your throat. Warm hill country is its ground. You will find the drained husks of its meals long before you find the spider.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a body longer than a man is tall, on legs that fold shut like a trap.
Durability: Tough enough for its bulk, though it never stays long enough to be worn down.
Defenses: Its shield is the other place. It is simply not there when your blow arrives.
Speed: Quick afoot, quicker up a wall; it goes over sheer stone without slowing at all.
Might: One bite, carrying a venom that wastes the vigour of the body, then wastes it again a while later.
Mind: Dull-witted and speechless. Cunning only in the hunt, the way a wolf is cunning.
Disposition: Neutral and simply hungry. Aggressive by habit, and it does not negotiate.
Bane: It must enter our world to bite. Watch the empty air, hold your swing for the instant it appears, and it is only a spider. Pin it here by any art you have and it dies like anything else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not stalk you where you can see it. It waits in the grey, picks whichever of you is looking the wrong way, slips through for a single bite while that man is still flat-footed, and is gone again before the blood has run. It repeats this at its leisure until the venom has hollowed you out, and only then does it stay to feed.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight in a ring, backs together. It always takes the one looking elsewhere.
• Hold your swing. The moment it shows itself is the only moment it can be struck.
• Carry something for wasting venom, or carry your friend home over your shoulder.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing there to talk to. It cannot speak, it barely thinks, and it wants nothing beyond meat. I tried once out of pure stubbornness, at a cave mouth in the warm hills, and it answered by taking the man standing beside me. Strike the instant it shows.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable ambusher

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +7
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), climb 20 ft.
Armor Class: 15 (–1 size, +3 Dex, +3 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+12
Attack: Bite +7 melee (1d6+4 plus poison)
Full Attack: Bite +7 melee (1d6+4 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., ethereal jaunt, low-light vision
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +7, Will +2
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 17, Con 16, Int 7, Wis 13, Cha 10
Skills: Climb +11, Move Silently +11, Spot +4
Feats: Ability Focus (poison), Improved Initiative
Environment: Warm hills
Organization: Solitary or cluster (2–5)
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 6–8 levels (Large); 9–15 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Phase spiders dwell and hunt on the Material Plane. Once a spider locates prey, however, it shifts to the Ethereal Plane to attack, attempting to catch its victim flat-footed. The spider shifts in, bites its victim, and retreats quickly back to the Ethereal Plane.

Ethereal Jaunt (Su): A phase spider can shift from the Ethereal Plane to the Material Plane as a free action, and shift back again as a move action (or during a move action). The ability is otherwise identical with ethereal jaunt (caster level 15th).

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 17, initial and secondary damage 1d8 Con. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Skills: A phase spider has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened.

lore.summary: The great worm of the deep earth, longer than a village street and thicker through than a cart. It swims the rock as an eel swims weed, eating whatever the stone gives it, and leaves behind the smooth round tunnels that half the underworld walks upon. It feels your footfalls through the floor long before you hear a sound of it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Gargantuan — a coiling body wider than a doorway and longer than any hall you will fight it in.
Durability: Immense. It carries wounds the way a mountain carries rain.
Defenses: Hide like layered leather laid over stone; blows land readily, but few land deep.
Speed: Slow overland, slow in water, slow through rock — yet it never stops, and there is nowhere it cannot follow.
Might: A maw that takes a man whole, and a tail-sting whose venom robs the limbs of their strength twice over.
Mind: Almost none. It is an appetite with a body wrapped around it.
Disposition: Neutral and wholly indifferent. It does not hate you; it cannot tell you from a vein of ore.
Bane: Slow, witless, and it finds you by the tremor of your tread — get up off the stone and it must hunt you blind. And should it take you whole, a light blade will still open the gizzard from within.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It gathers into a great ring and works the middle of it, biting and stinging everything within reach at once. What the jaws catch they hold; what they hold gets swallowed, and the gizzard crushes and burns with acid at the same time. The sting comes from behind while you are watching the mouth. That is the whole of its cleverness, and it is quite enough.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Round tunnel, smooth walls, no tool marks — turn back. That is a road, and something drives on it.
• Keep a light knife loose at your belt. If you go down the throat, that knife is the entire plan.
• Fight it in a passage too narrow to coil in, or do not fight it at all.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: You may as well parley with a landslide. No tongue, no name, and nothing behind the eyes worth addressing. I have shouted at one; it ate the shouting and the man who did it. If the tunnel is round and smooth, you are already standing in its road.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Gargantuan Magical Beast
Initiative: –2
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), burrow 20 ft., swim 10 ft.
Armor Class: 19 (–4 size, –2 Dex, +15 natural), touch 4, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +16/+40
Attack: Bite +25 melee (2d8+12)
Full Attack: Bite +25 melee (2d8+12) and sting +20 melee (2d6+6 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 20 ft./15 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, swallow whole, poison
Special Qualities: Tremorsense 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +17, Ref +8, Will +4
Abilities: Str 35, Dex 6, Con 25, Int 1, Wis 8, Cha 8
Skills: Listen +18, Swim +20
Feats: Awesome Blow, Cleave, Improved Bull Rush, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (bite), Weapon Focus (sting)
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 12
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: No coins, 50% goods (stone only), no items
Advancement: 16–32 levels (Gargantuan); 33–48 levels (Colossal)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: In battle, a purple worm forms into a coil 20 feet in diameter, biting and stinging anything within reach.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a purple worm must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can attempt to swallow the foe the following round.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 25, initial damage 1d6 Str, secondary damage 2d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Swallow Whole (Ex): A purple worm can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of a smaller size than itself by making a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d8+12 points of crushing damage plus 8 points of acid damage per round from the worm’s gizzard. A swallowed creature can cut its way out with a light slashing or piercing weapon by dealing enough damage to the gizzard (AC 17). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A Gargantuan worm’s interior can hold 2 Large, 8 Medium, 32 Small, 128 Tiny, or 512 Diminutive or smaller opponents.

Tremorsense (Ex): A purple worm automatically senses the location of anything within 60 feet that is in contact with the ground.

Skills: A purple worm has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

monsters.name: Remorhaz
monsters.senses: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 60 ft.

lore.summary: A worm of the frozen wastes, pale blue-white and plated along the back, and those plates flush red as a forge when the thing wakes in anger. It lies beneath the crust and listens for boots overhead, then comes up through the snow in one motion. Where a sleeping one has lain, the ice above melts to a long clear scar — that scar is all the warning you get.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — longer than a wagon and its team, and heavier than the whole of them together.
Durability: Heavily built and hard to put down. It does not flinch and it does not withdraw.
Defenses: A thick plated hide, and beneath it a furnace — the true armour is that touching the beast burns you.
Speed: Middling overland, but it moves under snow and ice as easily as a fish moves under a frozen pond.
Might: One enormous bite that seizes and swallows, and a gut hot enough to cook whatever it has taken.
Mind: Beast-witted and speechless, with no interest whatever in acquiring speech.
Disposition: Usually neutral, permanently hungry, and it hunts by ambush from underneath.
Bane: For all its furnace, the lore grants it no ward against flame — nor against cold, for all that it lives in the ice. Both bite it as they bite anything. Keep off the open ice and it loses you; and a swallowed man with a light blade can still cut his way out of the gut.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hides beneath the crust until it hears you above, then erupts underfoot and takes the nearest man in its jaws. What it grips it swallows, and the swallowed are cooked while they are crushed. All the while its back glows white-hot: fists, claws and bare teeth that strike it are seared for the trouble, and any weapon laid against that heat may soften and fail outright.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not punch it, do not wrestle it, do not lay a bare hand on it. Not once.
• Bring your second-best blade. The heat of its back eats steel that touches it.
• It has no ward against fire or frost, whatever the taverns tell you. Burn it freely.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing to say, and nothing there to hear it. It cannot speak; it is a hungry furnace on a great many legs. I watched a shaman of the ice-folk sing to one for the length of a prayer. The song ended when the snow opened. Strike first, and strike with a weapon you can bear to lose.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Magical Beast
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), burrow 20 ft.
Armor Class: 20 (–2 size, +1 Dex, +11 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 19
Base Attack/Grapple: +7/+23
Attack: Bite +13 melee (2d8+12)
Full Attack: Bite +13 melee (2d8+12)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, swallow whole
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., heat, low-light vision, tremorsense 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +10, Ref +6, Will +3
Abilities: Str 26, Dex 13, Con 21, Int 5, Wis 12, Cha 10
Skills: Listen +8, Spot +8
Feats: Awesome Blow, Improved Bull Rush, Power Attack
Environment: Cold desert
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 8–14 levels (Huge); 15–21 levels (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Remorhazes hide under the snow and ice until they hear movement above them, then attack from below and surprise prey.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a remorhaz must hit an opponent at least one size category smaller than itself with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can attempt to swallow the opponent the following round.

Swallow Whole (Ex): When a remorhaz begins its turn with a grappled opponent in its mouth, it can swallow that opponent with a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d8+12 points of bludgeoning damage plus 8d6 points of fire damage per round from the remorhaz’s gizzard. A swallowed creature can cut its way out with a light slashing or piercing weapon by dealing enough damage to the gizzard (AC 15). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A Huge remorhaz’s interior can hold 2 Large, 4 Medium, 8 Small, 32 Tiny, 128 Diminutive, or 512 Fine or smaller opponents.

Heat (Ex): An enraged remorhaz generates heat so intense that anything touching its body takes 8d6 points of fire damage. Creatures striking a remorhaz with natural attacks or unarmed attacks are subject to this damage, but creatures striking with melee weapons do not take damage from the remorhaz’s heat. This heat can melt or char weapons; any weapon that strikes a remorhaz is allowed a DC 18 Fortitude save to avoid destruction. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Tremorsense (Ex): A remorhaz automatically senses the location of anything within 60 feet that is in contact with the ground — which is how it finds prey walking on the ice above it.

Skills: Remorhazes have a +4 racial bonus on Listen checks.

lore.summary: The white guardian of one forest and no other — horned, silent-footed, the stallions bearded, the eyes deep sea-blue or violet or fiery gold. It walks its wood unheard, mends what it finds broken there, and within its own borders it can step from place to place in an instant. Past the treeline it will not go, and neither can you follow it in.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a tall horse, and the horn adds a lance to the length of it.
Durability: Strong and hale, and it can close its own hurts with a touch of the horn.
Defenses: A ward against wickedness rides upon it always and cannot be put out. Poison will not take, and neither charm nor compulsion finds the least purchase.
Speed: Swift as the finest courser and silent with it, and it treads its own wood without a sound.
Might: It charges, and the horn goes through a man like a lance — for it is a lance, and an enchanted one. Hooves after, if anything worth trampling remains.
Mind: Sharp, well-spoken and older in judgment than it looks. It has the Sylvan tongue and ours both.
Disposition: Chaotic and good, fiercely territorial about its forest, and it strikes only in its own defence or the wood's.
Bane: It is bound to its forest — beyond the boundary its power to step away is gone entirely, and it cannot come back in from outside. And the horn's enchantment dies with the beast that wore it, whatever the alchemists promise the fools who buy them.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not begin fights and it does not skirmish. When the wood is threatened it charges from cover at full stride, impaling with the horn as a knight impales with a lance, and follows through with the hooves. Between passes it steps across its own forest in a blink to reach the wounded, close their hurts and draw the venom out of them. You do not outlast a unicorn on its own ground.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Sheathe the blade before you enter the clearing. It counts that, and it remembers.
• If a wounded friend can be got into its wood, get them there. It heals, and it draws out poison.
• The horn is worthless once the beast is dead. Anyone selling you one is selling you a stick.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Speak first, and speak true. It has our tongue and the Sylvan one, and it will hear you out — but it reads the heart, and it has no patience for a clever answer. I told one honestly what I hunted and why. It walked with me to the edge of its wood and no further, carrying a wounded girl of my party the whole way. It never let me touch it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +3
Speed: 60 ft. (12 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (–1 size, +3 Dex, +6 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+13
Attack: Horn +11 melee (1d8+8)
Full Attack: Horn +11 melee (1d8+8) and 2 hooves +3 melee (1d4+2)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., magic circle against evil, spell-like abilities, immunity to poison, charm, and compulsion, low-light vision, scent, wild empathy
Saves: Fort +9, Ref +7, Will +6
Abilities: Str 20, Dex 17, Con 21, Int 10, Wis 21, Cha 24
Skills: Jump +21, Listen +11, Move Silently +9, Spot +11, Survival +8*
Feats: Alertness, Skill Focus (Survival)
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Solitary, pair, or grace (3–6)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Unicorns normally attack only when defending themselves or their forests. They either charge, impaling foes with their horns like lances, or strike with their hooves.

Horn: The horn is a +3 magic weapon, though its power fades if removed from the unicorn. It is also the unicorn’s instrument of healing: the cure and neutralize poison abilities are delivered by a touch of the horn.

Magic Circle against Evil (Su): This ability continuously duplicates the effect of the spell. A unicorn cannot suppress this ability.

Spell-Like Abilities: Unicorns can use detect evil at will as a free action. Once per day a unicorn can use greater teleport to move anywhere within its home. It cannot teleport beyond the forest boundaries nor back from outside. A unicorn can use cure light wounds three times per day and cure moderate wounds once per day (caster level 5th) by touching a wounded creature with its horn. Once per day it can use neutralize poison (DC 21, caster level 8th) with a touch of its horn. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Immunities (Ex): A unicorn is immune to poison, charm effects, and compulsion effects.

Wild Empathy (Ex): This power works like the druid’s wild empathy class feature, except that a unicorn has a +6 racial bonus on the check.

Skills: Unicorns have a +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks. *Unicorns have a +3 competence bonus on Survival checks within the boundaries of their forest.

Celestial Charger: The celestial charger is a greater unicorn — a celestial unicorn of eight racial levels with seven levels of cleric (CR 13, Large Magical Beast [Extraplanar], AC 24, damage reduction 10/magic, spell resistance 20, resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and electricity 10, turn undead 13/day, cleric spells with the Animal and Good domains). Its natural weapons count as magic weapons for overcoming damage reduction, and once per day it can smite evil for 15 points of extra damage against an evil foe. The save DC for its neutralize poison ability (DC 20) is adjusted for its greater power and altered Charisma score.

lore.summary: Bigger than any barn, brown or gold from beak to tail-root, the roc keeps the high warm crags and hunts the valleys beneath them. It takes a plough-ox from the furrow and a horse from under its rider, then beats back up the mountain with the meal still kicking. It is no thinker. It is appetite, with wings wider than a ship is long.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Gargantuan — longer beak to tail than a war-galley's mast is tall, and broader still across the wings.
Durability: Enormously tough. A thing built on that scale soaks up punishment that would fell a bull outright.
Defenses: No armour but dense plumage over hard-packed muscle. It trusts to height, not to hide.
Speed: Ponderous and clumsy afoot, but a strong and steady flier that carries off a horse without labouring.
Might: Talons like grapnel hooks and a shearing beak. It does not merely strike — it grips, and takes you with it.
Mind: Beast-dull, no wiser than a hawk. It knows hunger, its mate, and its nest, and nothing beyond them.
Disposition: Neutral and without malice, but it will stoop on anything horse-sized or larger that looks edible. A mated pair guarding a nest fights to the death and will not be driven off.
Bane: It has to come down to feed, and on the ground it is slow, clumsy and easily flanked. Take away the sky and you have taken away the roc.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hunts from above and out of the sun, dropping in one long stoop to close its talons and climb again with you dangling. Expect to be snatched rather than savaged — the killing is done later, on the ledge, by the young. Where it cannot lift a thing it works with both feet and the beak between them. A pair hunts in concert, one striking while the other circles for the next pass.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Nothing smaller than a horse interests it. Send the mule up the trail ahead of you and walk in its shadow.
• Cut yourself free before it gains height, or the mountain does its killing for it.
• Never go near the nest. A hunting roc may lose interest. A parent never does.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None to be had. There is nothing behind that eye to bargain with — less wit than a hound, and no speech in any tongue. I have shouted at one from a ledge. It shifted its grip on the goat and went on climbing. Save your breath for cover.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A roc attacks from the air, swooping earthward to snatch prey in its powerful talons and carry it off for itself and its young to devour. A solitary roc is typically hunting and will attack any Medium or larger creature that appears edible. A mated pair of rocs attack in concert, fighting to the death to defend their nests or hatchlings.

Snatch (Feat): A roc has the Snatch feat: being Gargantuan, it can snatch Medium or smaller opponents. When it hits with a talon or bite attack it can start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity, and thereafter deals automatic talon or bite damage each round it maintains the hold. It can instead fling a snatched foe aside as a free action, tossing it 1d6×10 feet for 1d6 points of damage per 10 feet thrown.

Skills: Rocs have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks.

lore.summary: The male of the sphinxes: a lion's body, a bearded king's face, and feathered wings that fold like a shut book. He keeps a warm desert alone, guarding some spring or ruin he has appointed himself to, prays as a priest of the kindly powers, and will trade courtesy for courtesy. He is proud, he is honest, and his voice can throw down a wall.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — lion-bodied and deep-chested, heavier through the shoulder than any warhorse.
Durability: Very hard to kill, and the deepest-built of all his kin.
Defenses: Hide like tanned oak laid over slabbed muscle, and prayers to ward and mend himself in the middle of a fight.
Speed: Faster across sand than a galloping horse. He flies strongly but turns like a barge.
Might: Two claws that open armour, and a leaping rake with the hind feet when he lands on you. Above all of it, the roar.
Mind: Clever, deeply learned in one chosen subject, and honourable with it. He has the sphinx tongue, the common one, and the speech of dragons.
Disposition: Chaotic and good-natured, though savage when he must be. He can tell a wanderer who strayed from a thief who came on purpose, and he judges accordingly.
Bane: His honour — give him a decent reason to let you pass and he will take it. Failing that, outlast the roars. They are few, and when the last is spent he is only a lion with a good heart and no war-craft, trusting claw over cunning.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He opens with the roar and lets it do the work. The first sets men running blind; a second in the same fight locks limbs and takes the hearing out of everyone near; a third shakes the strength from them, throws down the smaller ones, and cracks stone and crystal outright — arches, pillars, the flask on your belt. Then he charges, wings beating him forward, and comes down clawing and raking. His prayers go to shielding and mending himself; he has none that blast.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Speak before you draw. He would honestly rather you had a good reason for being there.
• Stone shatters when he opens his throat. Do not fight him under an arch or in a hall you want standing.
• He mends himself faster than a poor swordsman can cut. Come with weight of arms, or do not come.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The best conversation I have ever had with a thing that could eat me. I answered his question about the ruin I was standing in, truthfully, and got water and a warning about the pass for it. Be honest. He is chaotic, not stupid, and he hears a lie in your breathing.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: In battle, an androsphinx rips apart enemies with its razor-sharp claws. It relies on its natural weapons in a fight, employing its spells for defense or healing. Most sphinxes fight on the ground, using their wings to help them pounce much as lions do. If outnumbered by earthbound creatures, a sphinx takes wing and attacks on the fly.

Pounce (Ex): If a sphinx charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): A sphinx that pounces onto a creature can make two rake attacks with its hind legs. Attack bonus +18 melee, damage 2d4+3.

Roar (Su): Three times per day an androsphinx can loose a mighty roar. The first time it does this, all creatures within 500 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Will save or be affected as though by a fear spell for 2d6 rounds. If the sphinx roars a second time during the same encounter, all creatures within 250 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 1d4 rounds, and all those within 90 feet are deafened for 2d6 rounds (no save). If it roars a third time during the same encounter, all those within 250 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or take 2d4 points of Strength damage for 2d4 rounds. In addition, any Medium or smaller creature within 90 feet must succeed on a DC 19 Fortitude save or be thrown to the ground and take 2d8 points of damage. The force of this roar is so great that it deals 50 points of damage to any stone or crystalline object within 90 feet. Magic items and held or carried items can avoid damage with a DC 19 Reflex save. Other androsphinxes are immune to these effects. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Spells: An androsphinx casts divine spells as a 6th-level cleric from the cleric spell list and from the Good, Healing, and Protection domains.

Typical Cleric Spells Prepared: (5/5/5/4; save DC 13 + spell level) 0—cure minor wounds, detect magic, guidance, light, resistance; 1st—divine favor, protection from evil*, shield of faith, remove fear, summon monster I; 2nd—bull's strength, remove paralysis, resist energy, shield other*, summon monster II; 3rd—cure serious wounds*, daylight, invisibility purge, searing light. *Domain spell. Domains: Good and Healing.

lore.summary: The female of the sphinxes: a woman's face, a lioness's body, wings of soft feather. She hoards knowing as a dragon hoards gold — where a thing lies buried, whose curse is on it, what the old name of a road was. She would far rather talk than fight, and she charges for the talking. Her toll of me was this: I am owed by every man, paid by every man, and no man is the richer for the paying.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — lioness-built, lower and lighter through the chest than her mate.
Durability: The frailest of the sphinxes. She has the least stomach of the family for being hit.
Defenses: Good thick hide and quick reflexes, but her true defence is never being where the blow falls.
Speed: Swift over sand and off the ground in a heartbeat, though her flying is laboured and wide-turning.
Might: Two flaying claws and a pouncing rake. Enough to open a man, but never her first choice.
Mind: The keenest wit of the family. She sees what is invisible, reads any script, listens and looks through walls at a distance, undoes curses, strips away enchantment, and can call up the whole legend of a thing merely named to her.
Disposition: Neutral and territorial, but she tells deliberate trespass from honest wandering. Courtesy and payment carry a long way; she avoids a fight where she can.
Bane: Her curiosity and her want of endurance. Interest her and she will not strike at all; corner her and she breaks off sooner than any of her kin.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She avoids it if she can, and if she cannot, she has had days to prepare the ground. Watch for the graven sigils she scribes about a threshold or a floor — sleep, pain, fear, madness, persuasion, death — which work on whoever looks at them and fade after a while untended. In the open she strips your protections away first, then charges and lands on you clawing. She is the likeliest of the four to quit a fight she is losing.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Answer the riddle. The answer was death. She let me by, and seemed disappointed in me.
• Never read the writing on a sphinx's threshold. Watch your own boots and walk through.
• Bring her something she does not already know. Knowledge buys more from her than coin ever will.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Open, and worth the trouble. She trades an answer for an answer and hers are true — I had the whole history of a barrow out of one for a riddle and a bad silver ring. Be polite, be brief, and do not lie. She reads a face better than any court sharp I have met.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: In close combat, gynosphinxes use their powerful claws to flay the flesh from their enemies. Despite their deadly nature, they prefer to avoid combat whenever possible. Most sphinxes fight on the ground, using their wings to help them pounce much as lions do. If outnumbered by earthbound creatures, a sphinx takes wing and attacks on the fly.

Pounce (Ex): If a sphinx charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): A sphinx that pounces onto a creature can make two rake attacks with its hind legs. Attack bonus +11 melee, damage 1d6+2.

Spell-Like Abilities: 3/day—clairaudience/clairvoyance, detect magic, read magic, see invisibility; 1/day—comprehend languages, locate object, dispel magic, remove curse (DC 18), legend lore. Caster level 14th. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Symbols: Once per week a gynosphinx can create a symbol of death, a symbol of fear, a symbol of insanity, a symbol of pain, a symbol of persuasion, a symbol of sleep, and a symbol of stunning as the spells (caster level 18th), except that all save DCs are 22 and each symbol remains a maximum of one week once scribed. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

lore.summary: The ram-headed brother: heavy horns, heavier shoulders, and a plain blunt head set between them. He holds a stretch of desert road or a dead temple and expects paying for the crossing. He is not wicked and not clever. Where his brother would argue and his sister would riddle, he names a price, waits, and butts down whoever will not meet it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — the thickest-built of the winged kin, all neck and shoulder.
Durability: Solid and stubborn. He takes a great deal of breaking.
Defenses: Heavy hide and a skull made for hitting things with. No magic at all, neither his own nor borrowed.
Speed: Plodding on the ground beside his brother, and a heavy, poor flier who would rather keep his feet.
Might: A goring charge with those horns that will fold a shield in on its bearer, and claws to follow it.
Mind: Middling — no worse than a caravan guard's, and no better. He has the sphinx tongue, the common one, and the speech of dragons, and uses them to haggle.
Disposition: Neutral and acquisitive. Territorial, and wanting a toll rather than a corpse; give him one and the business usually ends there.
Bane: Dull eyes and a duller plan. His sight is poor, he fights the same way every time, and he cannot be taught a new trick in the middle of one.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He charges, and that is very nearly the whole of it. Wings beating him along, head down, horns first, and where the charge lands he comes down on his man and rakes with the hind feet as all his family do. He does not feint, does not withdraw, and does not think to take the air until matters on the ground have gone badly for him.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• He wants a toll, not a corpse. Carry something you can bear to hand over.
• He sees badly and hears keenly. Move to his flank quietly rather than trusting cover.
• Set a spear and let him come. He will come the very same way the second time.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, but he does talk. The trouble is that the talk is a toll, he pitches it high, and he remembers what else you were carrying. I paid one a saddle and kept the horse. Pay, pass, and do not come back down that road with anything he saw.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Criosphinxes attack with their claws, as do their kin, but they can also butt with their horns. They don't cast spells and employ only the most simple battle tactics. Most sphinxes fight on the ground, using their wings to help them pounce much as lions do. If outnumbered by earthbound creatures, a sphinx takes wing and attacks on the fly.

Pounce (Ex): If a sphinx charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): A sphinx that pounces onto a creature can make two rake attacks with its hind legs. Attack bonus +15 melee, damage 1d6+3.

lore.summary: The hawk-headed one, and the worst of the family. Chaotic and cruel, a stooping hunter that keeps no hoard and offers no bargain worth the name. He nests in warm desert crags, sometimes in flocks, and takes whatever walks below. Of all his kin he flies fastest and thinks least — a killer's temper poured into the shape of a sphinx.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — lean and high-shouldered, built long for the dive.
Durability: Sturdy enough, but the lightest-boned and least enduring of the four.
Defenses: The thinnest hide of the family. He trusts to speed and height instead of armour.
Speed: The swiftest wing among the sphinxes, though he still turns badly. Unremarkable on foot.
Might: A tearing beak that does the real work, claws behind it, and the family's rake when he comes down on you.
Mind: Dim and cruel. He has the sphinx tongues and little worth saying in any of them.
Disposition: Chaotic and evil. He hunts because he enjoys it, hoards nothing, and grants no passage. A flock is far worse than a lone bird.
Bane: Stupidity and thin skin. He will dive straight into an obvious trap, and once he is on the ground among you he is the easiest sphinx in the desert to kill.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He circles high, picks the straggler, and comes down out of the sun beak-first to land on his man and rake him open. He is cunning enough not to stand and trade — he climbs and stoops again, and again, wearing a party down. Where there is a flock they take you apart one at a time, coming from different quarters so that no shield faces the right way.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Watch the sky at your back, never the road ahead.
• He keeps nothing worth taking. There is no profit in this one — go round him if the country allows.
• Ground him and he is a bad-tempered lion with a beak. Nets, caves, low ceilings.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: He has the words and no use for them. I tried once from under an overhang and got a mouthful of abuse in the sphinx tongue before he tried the overhang itself. Talk only to buy the moment you need to reach hard cover, and expect nothing else of it.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Hieracosphinxes can make short work of even the most dangerous opponents with their claws. They are not particularly intelligent, but are cunning enough to dive at their enemies from above with their flying ability. Most sphinxes fight on the ground, using their wings to help them pounce much as lions do. If outnumbered by earthbound creatures, a sphinx takes wing and attacks on the fly.

Pounce (Ex): If a sphinx charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): A sphinx that pounces onto a creature can make two rake attacks with its hind legs. Attack bonus +13 melee, damage 1d6+2.

Skills: Hieracosphinxes have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks.

lore.summary: White as the drift it hunts from, and clever enough to reckon what you are worth. The winter wolf runs the cold forests in packs, circling, biting, breaking a man's legs out from under him; and when its patience thins it opens its jaws and breathes a killing frost. Frost giants keep them as hounds and call them cousins.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer than a pony and heavier, shoulder-high to a tall man.
Durability: Tough as any great beast of the north; it will take a deal of killing, but it is meat and it bleeds.
Defenses: A deep winter pelt over hide the colour of old snow. Cold cannot touch it at all — frost, ice, the bitterest wind, all slide off unfelt.
Speed: Very swift over open snow, and it does not tire the way you do.
Might: Jaws that crush and freeze in the one bite, a trip that takes your feet from under you, and a fanned breath of killing cold.
Mind: Cunning. It has the tongue of giants and enough of ours to bargain, boast and lie in either.
Disposition: Wicked, proud, and greedy. It hunts for the pleasure as much as the meat, and serves frost giants gladly for a share of the spoil.
Bane: Fire. It suffers from flame worse than any beast I have met, and it knows it — a burning brand will move a winter wolf where a bared blade will not.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: A pack rings you and works you like a mill: each wolf darts in, bites, trips, and gives ground while the next takes its turn, until the quarry is blown and stumbling. Then they close and pin. If they are in haste they skip the circling and go straight for the pin. The cold breath comes out over a spread of ground when the biting is going badly, or when a foe stands where two or three can be caught at once.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Torches out before you enter the tree line. Fire is the whole argument.
• It will offer you terms while the rest of the pack comes round behind. Keep your back to rock.
• Where you find them you will find giants, or the sign of giants. Count the tracks before you commit.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It talks, and that is the danger. I have bought passage from a pack twice with salt beef and flattery, and been stalked for a day after both times. Speak to the biggest and speak of payment; never of mercy. And never let the talking stop you counting the ones you cannot see.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Breath Weapon (Su): 15-foot cone, once every 1d4 rounds, damage 4d6 cold, Reflex DC 16 half. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Freezing Bite (Su): A winter wolf deals an extra 1d6 points of cold damage every time it bites an opponent, as if its bite were a frost weapon.

Trip (Ex): A winter wolf that hits with a bite attack can attempt to trip the opponent (+8 check modifier) as a free action without making a touch attack or provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react to trip the winter wolf.

Skills: Winter wolves have a +1 racial bonus on Listen, Move Silently, and Spot checks, and a +2 racial bonus on Hide checks. *Their natural coloration grants them a +7 racial bonus on Hide checks in areas of snow and ice. *A winter wolf has a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent.

Tactics: Winter wolves typically hunt in packs. Their size, cunning, and formidable breath weapon allow them to hunt and kill creatures much larger than themselves. A pack usually circles an opponent, each wolf attacking in turn to exhaust it. If they are in a hurry, winter wolves try to pin their foes.

lore.summary: Bigger than a wolf, blacker of heart, and it thinks. Worgs run the temperate grass in packs and take a wicked joy in the long chase, biting and giving ground until the quarry founders. Where goblins ride to war it is worgs that carry them — allies by their own choosing, and they will bite the goblin who forgets it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a grey or black wolf grown past any hound you have ever kennelled.
Durability: Hardy and well-muscled, but it is only flesh; a good spear settles the matter.
Defenses: Fur and tough hide, nothing more. No ward, no immunity, no charm on it. Steel bites it as steel should.
Speed: Swift and tireless, and better at the long pursuit than the short dash.
Might: One bite, but a strong one, and it will have your legs out from under you with the same snap.
Mind: Dull for a talking thing, yet a talking thing all the same — its own snarling speech, often goblin, now and then a little of ours.
Disposition: Cruel and vain. It hunts in company, carries goblins to war for its own reasons, and it remembers a slight for years.
Bane: Its pride. Insult the pack leader and it will come at you alone, which is exactly how you want it — and alone, a worg is a dog with opinions and no armour at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Pairs and packs work as one to bring down big game; a lone worg picks on what is smaller than itself. The method is exhaustion — bite and retreat, bite and retreat, the pack wheeling about a larger foe and each taking its turn until the thing can no longer stand. Then they move in for the kill. Grow impatient, or outnumber them badly, and they abandon the circling to pin you outright.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Kill the talker first. The pack has one, and it does the thinking for the rest.
• They understand you before you know they do. Do not plan aloud within earshot.
• Goblin riders fall off. Take the worg's legs and you have two foes on the ground and neither happy about it.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have talked a pack out of a fight with a haunch of venison and a promise to name their leader well in the next village. It held. But a worg bargains as a bandit bargains — it will take the meat, and then weigh whether your throat is worth the trouble besides.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser peril

sections.body:

Initiative: +2
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares)

Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+7

Full Attack: Bite +7 melee (1d6+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Trip
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent

Environment: Temperate plains
Organization: Solitary, pair, or pack (6–11)
Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Usually neutral evil
Treasure: 1/10 coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 5–6 levels (Medium); 7–12 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Trip (Ex): A worg that hits with a bite attack can attempt to trip the opponent (+3 check modifier) as a free action without making a touch attack or provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react to trip the worg.

Skills: A worg has a +1 racial bonus on Listen, Move Silently, and Spot checks, and a +2 racial bonus on Hide checks. *A worg has a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent.

Tactics: Mated pairs or packs work together to bring down large game, while lone worgs usually chase down creatures smaller than themselves. Both often use strike-and-withdraw tactics to exhaust their quarry. A pack usually circles a larger opponent: each worg attacks in turn, biting and retreating, until the creature is exhausted, at which point the pack moves in for the kill. If they get impatient or heavily outnumber the opponent, worgs attempt to pin it.

Language: More intelligent than their smaller cousins, worgs speak their own language. Some can also speak Common and Goblin.

monsters.name: Ankheg
monsters.senses: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 60 ft.

lore.summary: It waits a little under the furrow, feeling for footfalls, and comes up through the soil beneath a ploughman before he has heard a thing. The ankheg is all mandible and appetite — a great brown six-legged digger of the warm plains that bites, holds, and hauls what it has caught backward down its own tunnel to eat in the dark.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer than a farm cart and heavier than the horse that draws it.
Durability: Stout and well-fed. It takes honest work to put down.
Defenses: A hard shell of plated chitin over the whole of it — better armour than any man in the village owns.
Speed: Middling on the surface and slower beneath, yet it swims through good soil quickly enough to be on you before you turn.
Might: Mandibles that crush and drip a burning ichor, a grip it will not release, and now and again a spat line of that same burning stuff.
Mind: None worth the word. A beast, and a hungry one, with no speech and no bargain in it.
Disposition: Not malicious. Simply always hungry. It keeps no hoard, holds no grudge, and wants only the meat.
Bane: It reads you through the ground and little else. Stand still, or stand on bare rock, and it loses you entirely. Its spit is soon spent, too — weather that once and it has nothing left but jaws for hours after.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lies just beneath the field until its feelers catch an approaching tread, then bursts up under you like a charge from cover. The bite takes hold and does not let go; once it is hurt it backs down its own tunnel dragging the catch with it, which is the moment you lose people. The burning spit it keeps for desperation — when it is badly hurt, or when it has snapped at you and missed once too often.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Ride, or stand on stone. It hunts your tread and nothing else.
• The instant it takes hold, cut the hold. Let it back down the tunnel and you are digging out a corpse.
• A cluster shares the field but will not fight together. Draw them one at a time and it is three easy days' work.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing there to speak to. No tongue, no thought past the next mouthful. I have tried offering meat and it took the meat and then took the arm. Do not walk out to meet one; make it come to you, over ground of your choosing.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Magical Beast
Initiative: +0
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), burrow 20 ft.
Armor Class: 18 (–1 size, +9 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+12
Attack: Bite +7 melee (2d6+7 plus 1d4 acid)
Full Attack: Bite +7 melee (2d6+7 plus 1d4 acid)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, spit acid
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, tremorsense 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +6, Ref +3, Will +2
Abilities: Str 21, Dex 10, Con 17, Int 1, Wis 13, Cha 6
Skills: Climb +8, Listen +6, Spot +3
Feats: Alertness, Toughness
Environment: Warm plains
Organization: Solitary or cluster (2–4)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 4 levels (Large); 5–9 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, an ankheg must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If the ankheg is damaged after grabbing its prey, it retreats backward down its tunnel at its land speed (not its burrow speed), dragging the victim with it.

Spit Acid (Ex): 30-ft. line, once every 6 hours; damage 4d4 acid, Reflex DC 14 half. One such attack depletes the ankheg's acid supply for 6 hours; it cannot spit acid or deal acid damage during this time. The save DC is Constitution-based. An ankheg does not use this ability unless it is desperate or frustrated. It most often spits acid when badly wounded — cut down to less than half its full strength — or when it has failed to grab an opponent.

Acid Bite (Ex): An ankheg's mandibles drip a corrosive fluid: its bite deals an extra 1d4 points of acid damage on every hit, unless its acid supply has been spent by a spit acid attack within the last 6 hours.

Burrowing: An ankheg burrows with legs and mandibles. A burrowing ankheg usually does not make a usable tunnel, but can construct one; it burrows at half speed when it does so. It often digs a winding tunnel up to 40 feet below the surface in the rich soil of forests or farmlands. The tunnel is 5 feet tall and wide, and from 60 to 150 feet long ([1d10 + 5] × 10).

Tactics: An ankheg usually lies 5 to 10 feet below the surface until its antennae detect the approach of prey. It then burrows up to attack — treat this as a charge, even though the ankheg does not need to move 10 feet before attacking. Clusters of ankhegs share the same territory but do not cooperate.

lore.summary: A blue serpent as long as a barn, walking on a dozen short legs or folding them away to slither like a snake. The behir keeps to warm hills and broken rock, climbing where nothing so heavy has any right to climb. It bites, wraps, rakes what is caught in the coils, and swallows whatever will fit. Those grand curling horns are for preening its scales, not for war.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — longer than a village bridge, and heavy in proportion.
Durability: Very hard to kill. There is a great deal of serpent to work through before you reach anything that matters.
Defenses: Overlapping scales like blue slate, banded grey-brown. Lightning does nothing to it whatsoever, and you will not throw it off its feet — it has far too many.
Speed: Quick over the level and quicker up a sheer face than you will credit until you have watched it.
Might: A crushing bite, coils that stave in ribs, raking claws for whatever is held in them, a gullet that takes a man entire, and a bolt of lightning loosed straight down a line.
Mind: Slow-witted, but not witless. It has our tongue and uses it plainly, with little enough to say.
Disposition: Neither good nor wicked — territorial, vain about its scales, and hungry. Found alone or with its mate, never in numbers.
Bane: It saves the lightning for when it is beset, and it comes seldom. Crowd it, make it spend the bolt early, then spread out. And once it has swallowed a man it is distracted — a short blade worked from the inside is felt keenly. Never fight it on its own rocks.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens with the bite and takes hold, then decides between swallowing you and crushing you; the claws come out only for what is already in the coils. Beset by a crowd it rears and lays a bolt of lightning down the line of them. It will climb to a ledge and come down on the party from above, and it will take one man whole and carry on biting for the next while the first is still going down.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Whoever it swallows must keep a short blade on the belt, not the back. Say this aloud before you go in.
• Do not stand in a line. Never in a line. That is the whole of the lightning.
• Praise its scales. I am not joking — it is vain as a duchess, and vanity has bought me an hour of talk more than once.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks our tongue, slowly, and it can be reasoned with if the reasoning is short and there is food in it. I bought passage through a gorge with two goats and a long compliment about its horns. But it is hungry always, and a hungry thing changes its mind between one word and the next.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Magical Beast
Initiative: +1
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares), climb 15 ft.

Full Attack: Bite +15 melee (2d4+12)

Special Qualities: Can't be tripped, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to electricity, low-light vision, scent

Challenge Rating: 8
Alignment: Often neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 10–13 levels (Huge); 14–27 levels (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Breath Weapon (Su): 20-foot line, once every 10 rounds, damage 7d6 electricity, Reflex DC 19 half. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Constrict (Ex): A behir deals 2d8+8 points of damage with a successful grapple check. It can make six rake attacks against a grappled foe as well.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a behir must hit a creature of any size with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can attempt to constrict the opponent or swallow the opponent in the following round.

Rake (Ex): Six claws, attack bonus +15 melee, damage 1d4+4. A behir can employ its claws only against a foe caught in its coils.

Swallow Whole (Ex): A behir can try to swallow a grabbed Medium or smaller opponent by making a successful grapple check. A behir that swallows an opponent can use its Cleave feat to bite and grab another opponent. A swallowed creature takes 2d8+8 points of bludgeoning damage and 8 points of acid damage per round from the behir's gizzard. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by using a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal enough damage to the gizzard — 25 points against AC 15. Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A behir's gizzard can hold 2 Medium, 8 Small, 32 Tiny, or 128 Diminutive or smaller opponents.

Skills: Behirs have a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on Climb checks, even if rushed or threatened.

Tactics: A behir usually bites and grabs its prey first, then either swallows or constricts the opponent. It can employ its claws only against foes caught in its coils. If beset by a large number of foes, it uses its breath weapon. Behirs speak Common.

lore.summary: A yellow-brown hound the size of a wolf that is never quite where you are swinging. Blink dogs run the temperate plains in great packs, flickering half out of the world and back again a pace to your left. They are as decent a folk as any I have met on the road, and they speak among themselves in yaps and whines that carry more than most men manage aloud.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a lean, tall hound with nothing about it to frighten anyone.
Durability: Slight. One solid blow would end it, if a solid blow could ever find it.
Defenses: It is half elsewhere. Blade, arrow and spell alike pass through the space it has only just left.
Speed: Fleet afoot, and it steps out of the world and back as easily as breathing — a pack is all around you before you have finished turning.
Might: A dog's bite and no more. Their strength is numbers and standing where you are not looking.
Mind: As clever as an unlettered man, and about as hard to fool. Their barking speech will carry anything you could put in ours.
Disposition: Lawful and good-hearted, and rare among the things in this book for it. They keep their own country, walk travellers who mean no harm past the bad ground, and set on wicked things without being asked.
Bane: None worth the writing, and I am glad of it. Pen one where it cannot flicker and it is only a dog — but you will have made an enemy of a great many honest creatures to do it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: The pack winks about you in no order you can predict, appearing and vanishing until they have you ringed and half of them are behind your guard. Then they bite from the blind side, and are gone before the answer comes. They fight this way only against what they judge wicked; against travellers they bristle, bark, and give ground rather than open a fight.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never draw first. They judge you at once, and their judgement carries to the whole pack.
• Meat offered open-handed and set down on the grass. Thrown meat is a challenge, and they take it as one.
• If they fall in beside you on the road, something worse is ahead. Trust the dogs. I always have and I am still writing.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: One of the few friends in this book. They have no word of our speech, but they read a man's hands and face better than his own kin do. Kneel, show the empty palm, set food down and wait. I have been guided three nights across country by a pack that never let me touch one of them, and never asked a thing for it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — Small danger, and seldom an enemy

sections.body:

Initiative: +3
Speed: 40 ft. (8 squares)
Armor Class: 16 (+3 Dex, +3 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+4
Attack: Bite +4 melee (1d6)
Full Attack: Bite +4 melee (1d6)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Blink, darkvision 60 ft., dimension door, low-light vision, scent
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +7, Will +4
Abilities: Str 10, Dex 17, Con 10, Int 10, Wis 13, Cha 11

Challenge Rating: 2
