sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Blink (Su): A blink dog can use blink as the spell (caster level 8th), and can evoke or end the effect as a free action.

Dimension Door (Su): A blink dog can teleport, as dimension door (caster level 8th), once per round as a free action. The ability affects only the blink dog, which never appears within a solid object and can act immediately after teleporting.

Tactics: Blink dogs hunt in packs, teleporting in a seemingly random fashion until they surround their prey, allowing some of them to take advantage of flanking.

Language: Blink dogs have their own language, a mixture of barks, yaps, whines, and growls that can transmit complex information.

lore.summary: Hangs from the cave roof and waits, shell and skin the very colour of the limestone above you, tentacles held stiff so it reads as one more stalactite. It smothers your lamp with a pall of its own dark, drops upon your head, and draws the membrane tight until you stop breathing. Common on the deep roads, alone or in clutches.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — no longer than your arm from tentacle-tip to crown, and lighter than a full pack.
Durability: Slight. A solid blow ends it; the difficulty is landing one before it lands on you.
Defenses: A pebbled shell and a hide that shifts to match any stone. It is hidden, not armoured.
Speed: Shuffles poorly on the ground and flies worse — short, clumsy hops from roof to roof.
Might: Startling strength in the grip. The tentacles crush and smother where a jaw would only tear.
Mind: Beast-dumb. It knows ceiling, dark, and meat, and nothing else at all.
Disposition: Neutral and hungry. No malice in it — only an appetite and a good ceiling.
Bane: It sees by a shriek you cannot hear; a ward of utter silence blinds it outright. And it must have a roof to work from — draw it into the open and it is a flapping rag.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It kills the light first, then falls. The drop wraps your head, the membrane clamps, and the squeezing goes on until you smother — your fellows must haul it off you, for you will not. Miss its plunge and it labours back up to the roof to try the same fall again, and that climb is the moment to kill it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Walk the deep roads with a hand on your helm and your eyes up. They fall like fruit.
• When the lamp dies for no good reason, it has already chosen you. Step sideways at once.
• A ward of silence unmakes it. Failing that, keep a friend behind you to pull the thing off your face.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. There is nothing behind those tentacles to bargain with. I tried once in three tongues with the lamp held high and my sword grounded, and got a face full of wet membrane for the courtesy. Kill it on the ceiling before it kills you off it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Magical Beast
Initiative: +4
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), fly 30 ft. (poor)
Armor Class: 17 (+1 size, +6 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+0
Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d4+4)
Full Attack: Slam +5 melee (1d4+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Darkness, improved grab, constrict 1d4+4
Special Qualities: Blindsight 90 ft.
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +2, Will +0
Abilities: Str 16, Dex 10, Con 13, Int 2, Wis 10, Cha 10
Skills: Hide +10, Listen +5*, Spot +5*
Feats: Improved Initiative
Environment: Underground
Organization: Solitary, pair, clutch (3-9), or swarm (6-15)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 2-3 levels (Small)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Darkness (Su): Once per day a darkmantle can cause darkness as the darkness spell (caster level 5th). It most often uses this ability just before attacking.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a darkmantle must hit a Large or smaller creature with its slam attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it attaches to the opponent's head and can constrict.

Constrict (Ex): A darkmantle deals 1d4+4 points of damage with a successful grapple check.

Blindsight (Ex): A darkmantle can "see" by emitting high-frequency sounds, inaudible to most other creatures, that allow it to ascertain objects and creatures within 90 feet. A silence spell negates this ability and effectively blinds the darkmantle.

Skills: A darkmantle has a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks. These bonuses are lost if its blindsight is negated. The creature's variable coloration gives it a +4 racial bonus on Hide checks.

lore.summary: A lean, hunched reptile that runs its supper down on two legs and dissolves it where it stands. Grey-green and mottled to the warm forest floor, it carries a fluted horn upon its back through which it hurls acid — a wide gout across a rank of men, or a single scalding jet at arm's reach. It is nearly always hungry. Where one hunts, a pack may.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no taller than a man, but longer than one, all haunch and tail.
Durability: Tough for its bulk. It will take a fair few honest blows before it drops.
Defenses: Pebbled hide, and flesh wholly untroubled by acid — its own or anybody else's.
Speed: Very fast. It outruns a horse over broken ground and leaps like a hound.
Might: Raking hind feet, and the acid: a spraying gout that scours a whole rank, or a close jet that goes through mail and the man inside it.
Mind: Beast-dumb, but with a true hunter's instinct — it picks its mark before it ever charges.
Disposition: Neutral and endlessly hungry. Fed and idle it lies low and lets you pass; hungry, which is nearly always, it hunts.
Bane: The spray must gather again between gouts, and that pause is the entire fight. It wears no armour worth the name — press it hard in the gap and it dies like any beast.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It watches from cover, chooses one of you, then charges and opens with the acid. If the gout does not finish its mark it closes and kicks with those hind feet, worrying the same man and no other, until the spray has gathered once more — and then it burns him at arm's reach with a jet far worse than the gout was.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Count the beats between sprays. That gap is your only door; go through it.
• Its own burning cannot touch it, so acid flasks are wasted breath. Bring steel and fire.
• Never let it choose your mark for you. Spread wide, and never stand in a line before that horn.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. There is no mind there to speak with, only appetite. I threw a whole deer to one to buy my passage, and it ate the deer and then came on for me all the same. Do not bargain. Break the charge, take the nearest one down, and let the rest scatter.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Magical Beast
Initiative: +6
Speed: 60 ft. (12 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (+2 Dex, +5 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +8/+11
Attack: Claw +11 melee (1d8+4)
Full Attack: Claw +11 melee (1d8+4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Acid spray
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immunity to acid, low-light vision, scent
Saves: Fort +9, Ref +10, Will +3
Abilities: Str 17, Dex 15, Con 17, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 10
Skills: Hide +9, Jump +21, Listen +6, Spot +6
Feats: Alertness, Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes
Environment: Warm forests
Organization: Solitary or pack (3-6)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9-12 levels (Medium); 13-24 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Acid Spray (Ex): A digester can spray acid in a 20-foot cone, dealing 4d8 points of damage to everything in the area. Once a digester uses this ability, it can't use it again until 1d4 rounds later. The creature can also produce a concentrated stream of acid that deals 8d8 points of damage to a single target within 5 feet. In either case, a DC 17 Reflex save halves the damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Skills: A digester's coloration gives it a +4 racial bonus on Hide checks. It also has a +4 racial bonus on Jump checks.

lore.summary: Brass-scaled and lion-bodied, maned like an old male, with a dragon's head and wings far too small for the beast beneath them. It keeps the temperate deserts, hunts by scent and by hearing, and hoards what it strips from the dead. It speaks the dragon-tongue in a growling, contemptuous way — and its roar leaves a whole warband too weary to lift a shield.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a great lion cast in brass, longer than a warhorse and heavier.
Durability: Very tough. Deep-set, thickly scaled, and slow to give ground.
Defenses: Brass scales that turn a poor stroke, and wings enough to quit any patch of ground you have made dangerous for it.
Speed: Swift across the sand. It flies too — badly, and only for a short spell, but far enough to break your ring.
Might: It leaps and lands jaws and both claws in the one rush. And the roar, which drains the strength out of every ear within hearing and leaves those closest wrung out entirely.
Mind: Dull for a talking thing, but it does talk — the dragon-tongue, and it is proud of the fact.
Disposition: Neutral, and greedy in the dragon fashion. It guards what it has gathered and resents anything that walks near it.
Bane: It cannot stay aloft; the wings serve for a short while and no longer. Its roar spares only its own kind, so it will not roar long beside allies. Stop your ears before you crest the ridge.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It roars first, and half your company is wrung out before a blade is clear of the scabbard. Then it charges and delivers everything in a single leap — jaws and both claws together. When you press it, or try to close a ring about it, it lifts on those short wings, comes down on ground you do not hold, and roars again from there.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Wax in the ears before you come over the ridge. The roar takes the fight out of you before it does.
• Those wings tire fast. Wait it out on open ground rather than chasing it up a cliff face.
• It talks, and it hoards. Bring something bright to offer before you bring the sword.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, but genuine. It speaks Draconic and thinks slowly; flatter it, show it brass and coin, and it may name a toll rather than a fight. I paid one in candlesticks and crossed its ground unbled. Greedy, mind — not honourable. Never turn your back on the bargain.

sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Pounce (Ex): If a dragonne charges, it can make a full attack in the same round.

Roar (Su): A dragonne can loose a devastating roar every 1d4 rounds. All creatures except dragonnes within 120 feet must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or become fatigued. Those within 30 feet who fail their saves become exhausted. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Skills: Dragonnes have a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a dragonne is up to 348 pounds; a medium load, 349-699 pounds; and a heavy load, 700-1,050 pounds.

lore.summary: A white worm as long as a barge, coiled beneath the snow of the cold plains with nothing showing at all. It sings before it strikes — a trill that roots you where you stand — and then it rises. Its body burns with cold, its breath is a killing wind, and when at last it dies it turns to ice and bursts. It tunnels ice and frozen earth, never stone.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a serpent thicker through than a man is tall and longer than a mead-hall.
Durability: Immense. It soaks punishment that would fell a whole warband and comes on.
Defenses: Hide like plate, cold cannot touch it at all, and it lies so well buried in the snow you will not know it until it is upon you.
Speed: Slow above the snow and slower beneath it — but it need not hurry. It comes to you under the ground.
Might: A bite that freezes as it crushes; a breath of killing frost, though only once in a long while; and the trill, which holds a whole field still for its convenience.
Mind: Beast-dumb, and none the less deadly for it. It knows the ambush and nothing besides.
Disposition: Neutral, solitary, and always hunting. No hoard, no lair-craft, no interest in you but meat.
Bane: Fire. Nothing else troubles it, and fire troubles it worse than any beast I have hunted. Mark also: a man held by the song may be shaken back to himself, so shake him.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lies under the snow until you are near, sings you motionless, and then feeds at its leisure — and any man held by that song has no chance whatever to duck the frost of its breath. In the press its cold body burns the bare hand or claw that touches it. Kill it and it shatters: the corpse bursts in a ring of frost and flying ice.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fire, always fire. Nothing else in your pack will move it.
• When it sings, whoever keeps his wits must shake the others awake — hard, and at once.
• Kill it and then run. The bursting corpse has done for better hunters than the living worm ever did.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. It is an appetite with a song in it; nothing there hears words. I once shouted my name and my whole lineage at one across the ice, which bought me only a nearer view of the inside of its mouth. Strike from a distance, and burn it.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Trill (Su): A frost worm can emit a noise that forces its prey to stand motionless. This sonic mind-affecting compulsion affects all creatures other than frost worms within a 100-foot radius. Creatures must succeed on a DC 17 Will save or be stunned for as long as the worm trills and for 1d4 rounds thereafter, even if they are attacked. However, if attacked or violently shaken (a full-round action), a victim is allowed another saving throw. Once a creature has resisted or broken the effect, it cannot be affected again by that same frost worm's trill for 24 hours. The effect's caster level is 14th. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Cold (Ex): A frost worm's body generates intense cold, causing opponents to take an extra 1d8 points of cold damage every time the creature succeeds on a bite attack. Creatures attacking a frost worm unarmed or with natural weapons take this same cold damage each time one of their attacks hits.

Breath Weapon (Su): 30-foot cone, once per hour, damage 15d6 cold, Reflex DC 22 half. Opponents held motionless by the frost worm's trill get no saving throw. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Death Throes (Ex): When killed, a frost worm turns to ice and shatters in an explosion that deals 12d6 points of cold damage and 8d6 points of piercing damage to everything within 100 feet (Reflex DC 22 half). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Burrowing: A frost worm cannot burrow through stone, but can manage ice and frozen earth. When moving through such hard materials it leaves behind a usable tunnel about 5 feet in diameter.

Skills: *A frost worm, due to its coloration and its affinity for burying itself in the snow, has a +10 racial bonus on Hide checks in its native environment.

lore.summary: A white-furred ape with four arms, broad as a doorway, walking the warm forest on its legs and its lower hands. It lies up in the branches or under the leaf-litter with only its nose showing, and takes whatever passes beneath. It hunts alone or in companies, and whatever it can lift it carries off into the canopy before the rest of you have turned round.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — head and shoulders above a tall man, and half again as broad across the chest.
Durability: Solid, and slow to put down. It will take a great deal of hurting first.
Defenses: Thick fur and heavy muscle, and no more than that. It trusts to the first blow, not to soaking yours.
Speed: Fast on the ground and just as fast straight up a trunk. In the canopy it is quicker than you are anywhere.
Might: Four clawed hands and a bite — and worse, when a pair of those hands take hold together it fastens on and tears the flesh open in the one motion.
Mind: Beast-dumb, yet a patient ambusher with real craft in the waiting.
Disposition: Neutral and savage, jealous of its wood. It does not hate you; it eats you.
Bane: No armour, no magic, no trick beyond speed and surprise. Deny it the ambush and the fight turns honest. Keep it in the open, well clear of trunk and branch.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits above you, or beneath the leaves at your boot, until you are square under it, then falls on one man with everything at once. If he is light enough it simply gathers him up and goes back into the trees before a bow can be raised. If he is not, it stays and works on him alone — all four hands, and the tearing when a pair of them find purchase — and pays the rest of you no mind until he is finished.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Look up first, then look hard at the leaf-litter. Often only the nose shows.
• It will snatch the smallest of you and vanish upward. Put your lightest in the middle of the line.
• Fight it in the open, never beneath the canopy. On flat ground it is only a very strong animal.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. I have tried meat, I have tried fire, I have tried standing perfectly still — the last worked best, and only until it grew hungry again. There is no more talking to a girallon than to a landslide. Watch the branches, and loose before it drops.

Skills: A girallon has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened.

lore.summary: Deep water hides a mind as cold and patient as the trench it keeps. The kraken is a squid grown past all reason — two barbed tentacles longer than a mast, six shorter arms, and a beak where they all meet. It is no brute. It speaks, it schemes, and it will call the storm down on your ship long before it shows itself.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Gargantuan — a body the length of a war-galley, with arms longer still.
Durability: Immense. It can lose limbs and fight on, and grows them back in a matter of weeks.
Defenses: A slick rubbery hide that turns most blows, and a cloud of black ink to vanish behind. It wears no armour but its own bulk, and magic finds it as readily as it finds any beast.
Speed: Ponderous while it stalks, but it can jet backward faster than any ship under sail — always in a straight line.
Might: Terrible. The barbed tentacles reach far past your longest spear, crush what they catch and haul it to the arms; the arms pass it to the beak.
Mind: As clever as a learned man and rather better travelled — it knows the coasts, the currents, and the price of things.
Disposition: Cruel and covetous, and it hoards what it takes. It bargains gladly and drowns those who disappoint it.
Bane: Its limbs can be hewn like rope. Take both barbed tentacles, or three of the shorter arms, and it quits the field of its own accord. And it cannot follow you ashore — the water is the whole of its world.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes from below, unseen. The long barbed arms lash in first from far outside your reach, hook a man off the deck and haul him inboard to the shorter arms, and those pass him along to the beak. The foul weather that drove you onto its water was likely its doing; so was the whale that rammed your hull. When a fight turns against it, it fills the sea with ink and is simply gone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it from a boat and you are fighting on its table. Get to a cliff, a reef, anything with rock under your heel.
• Hew the long arms. It counts its own losses better than you do, and it leaves when the sum displeases it.
• The storm is not weather. The storm is the beast announcing itself. Make harbour.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It speaks Common and the tongue of the sea folk, and it will talk at length — always for gain. I bargained with one off the Sallow Reach for safe passage. It kept the letter of the bargain and drowned my pilot on a technicality. Bring tribute, keep a blade by the anchor cable, and never turn your back on the water.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Dire — A dire quarry

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Krakens strike their opponents with their barbed tentacles, then grab and crush with their arms or drag victims into their huge jaws. Six of the beast's tentacles are shorter arms about 30 feet long; the remaining two are nearly 60 feet long and covered with barbs. Its beaklike mouth is located where the tentacles meet the lower portion of its body. Krakens speak Common and Aquan.

Severing Limbs: An opponent can make sunder attempts against a kraken's tentacles or arms as if they were weapons. A tentacle can absorb 20 points of damage before it is severed, an arm 10. If a kraken is currently grappling a target with one tentacle or arm, it usually uses another limb to make its attack of opportunity against the sunder attempt. Severing a limb wounds the kraken itself for half the damage the limb could have absorbed. A kraken usually withdraws from combat if it loses both tentacles or three of its arms. A kraken regrows severed limbs in 1d10+10 days.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, the kraken must hit with an arm or tentacle attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Constrict (Ex): A kraken deals automatic arm or tentacle damage with a successful grapple check.

Jet (Ex): A kraken can jet backward once per round as a full-round action, at a speed of 280 feet. It must move in a straight line, but does not provoke attacks of opportunity while jetting.

Ink Cloud (Ex): A kraken can emit a cloud of jet-black ink in an 80-foot spread once per minute as a free action. The cloud provides total concealment, which the kraken normally uses to escape a fight that is going badly. Creatures within the cloud are considered to be in darkness.

Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day—control weather, control winds, dominate animal (DC 18), resist energy. Caster level 9th. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Skills: A kraken has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: A lean forest cat with a long narrow head, and skin about that head so loose the beast can drag it back to the bone. What comes out of the ferns at you is a running skull with a scream in it. They hunt the temperate woods in prides, and the one you see is never the one that means to bite you.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no bigger than a large hunting hound, and lighter than the fright suggests.
Durability: Slight. One solid blow finishes it.
Defenses: A thin hide and quick feet, and nothing else worth the name.
Speed: Swift, and a prodigious jumper. It crosses undergrowth without a sound.
Might: A bite and two raking paws — enough for a lone traveller on a road, little enough against a shield wall.
Mind: Dull, but not witless. It scouts, it drives game, it keeps to a plan, and it can be taught.
Disposition: A plain predator. It takes what it can panic and leaves what it cannot.
Bane: The scream is nearly the whole of it. Stand fast against one beast's shriek and that same beast cannot touch your nerve again for a day and a night — and its own kin are wholly deaf to the trick.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: A lone scout shows itself, peels its face back to the skull and screeches. The quarry breaks and runs, and runs straight into the rest of the pride lying in the brush. The scout gives chase and joins the kill. If the scream fails they will still spring the ambush, but a pride that has spent its terror rarely presses a fight it might lose.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It is a face, not a wound. Look once, look away, keep swinging.
• The one that screams is not the one that kills. Turn and face the brush behind you.
• Take a cub, raise it on liver, and let it do your shouting. Best kennel I ever kept.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nobody in there to answer. It has wit enough to hunt and no tongue at all, and a grown one only runs or bites. But a cub taken young heels as gladly as any hound, and a screaming cat at your shoulder is worth swords in a night ambush. Raise one; do not negotiate with one.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: The krenshar is a strange, catlike carnivore with extremely flexible skin on its head. A typical krenshar measures 4 or 5 feet in length with a long, narrow head, and weighs about 175 pounds. Krenshars use solitary scouts to drive prey into the waiting clutches of the pride. The scout appears from hiding, uses its scare ability, then chases the fleeing target to join the attack.

Scare (Ex or Su): As a standard action, a krenshar can pull the skin back from its head, revealing the musculature and bony structures of its skull. This alone is usually sufficient to scare away foes (treat as a Bluff check with a +3 bonus). Combining this scare ability with a loud screech produces an unsettling effect that works like a scare spell from a 3rd-level caster (Will DC 13 partial). A creature that successfully saves cannot be affected again by the same krenshar's scare ability for 24 hours. The shriek does not affect other krenshars. This is a supernatural, sonic mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Skills: Krenshars have a +4 racial bonus on Jump and Move Silently checks.

lore.summary: A great lion with an eagle's wings and the bearded face of a wise old man. The lammasu keeps the desert marches alone, and about it hangs a ring of quiet holiness that turns evil things back the way a hand turns a candle flame. It is a priest as much as a beast, and it will come down out of the sun for a stranger it has never met.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a lion built heavy, with wings enough to shade a wagon.
Durability: Stout, with a warhorse's frame beneath the pelt, but no more than that.
Defenses: Thick hide and a standing ward of blessing that keeps foul things from laying hands on it. Mark this well: honest steel and a plain arrow bite it as they would bite any beast. Only the golden half-dragon kind is armoured beyond that.
Speed: It walks at a lion's pace and flies steadily rather than swiftly.
Might: Razor claws, and a charging leap that lands raking with all four. Its real weight, though, is in its prayers.
Mind: Learned, patient, deep in the arcane, and slow to misjudge a man.
Disposition: Lawful and good to the marrow. It joins any fight where it sees a decent soul threatened, invited or not.
Bane: It fights fair, and that is the crack in it — feign surrender, or put the innocent between you, and it will check its blow. It also stands alone, always, and weight of numbers tells on anything that stands alone.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It sees a wrong being done and enters the fight uninvited. Blessings first — courage, strength, wards named against the evil it has already sniffed out — then a diving charge, claws raking as it comes down. Through the melee it mends its allies, strips enchantments off your side, and calls down a searing light that burns only the wicked. If matters sour it walks out of sight entirely, or steps through the air to better ground.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never approach with a blade drawn. It already sees the shape of everything you carry.
• It wards evil the way a wall wards wind. If your company includes something foul, leave that thing over the ridge.
• Ask for healing before you ask for anything else. It says yes, and the rest of the conversation goes easier.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Talk. Always talk. It has Common, the dragon tongue, and the speech of the higher planes, and it would far rather have your oath than your blood. I sat a whole night with one above the salt pans arguing scripture and left with my wounds closed and a road that is on no map. Come with clean hands and it will believe you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.body:

Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 60 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 20 (-1 size, +1 Dex, +10 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 19

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A typical lammasu is about 8 feet long and weighs about 500 pounds. Lammasus speak Common, Draconic, and Celestial. A lammasu attacks with spells or its razor-sharp claws. It almost always enters combat if it observes a good creature being threatened by evil.

Spells: A lammasu casts spells as a 7th-level cleric, and can choose spells from the cleric spell list, plus any two of the following domains: Good, Healing, Knowledge, or Law.

Typical Cleric Spells Prepared: (6/6/5/4/2; save DC 13 + spell level) 0—detect magic, guidance (2), light, read magic, resistance; 1st—bless (2), detect evil, divine favor, entropic shield, protection from evil*; 2nd—aid*, bear's endurance, bull's strength, lesser restoration, resist energy; 3rd—daylight, dispel magic, magic circle against evil*, remove curse; 4th—holy smite*, neutralize poison. *Domain spell. Domains: Good and Healing.

Magic Circle against Evil (Su): A lammasu radiates a continuous magic circle against evil that affects a 20-foot radius.

Spell-Like Abilities: 2/day—greater invisibility (self only); 1/day—dimension door. Caster level 7th.

Pounce (Ex): If a lammasu charges a foe, it can make a full attack, including two rake attacks.

Rake (Ex): Attack bonus +12 melee, damage 1d6+3.

Skills: Lammasus have a +2 racial bonus on Spot checks.

Golden Protector (Celestial Half-Dragon Lammasu): Child of a celestial lammasu and a gold dragon, the golden protector has migrated to the Material Plane to more actively combat evil. It is a Large Dragon (Extraplanar), CR 13, with AC 29 (touch 13, flat-footed 26), 2 claws +19 melee (1d6+9) and bite +13 melee (1d8+4), damage reduction 5/magic, immunity to fire, sleep, and paralysis, resistance to acid 10, cold 10, and electricity 10, and spell resistance 15. Its natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction. Breath Weapon (Su): 30-foot cone, 1/day, damage 6d8 fire, Reflex DC 21 half. Smite Evil (Su): once per day it can make a normal melee attack to deal an extra 10 points of damage against an evil opponent. Rake (Ex): attack bonus +19 melee, damage 1d6+4.

lore.summary: A blue-grey lizard about the size of a cat, marked blue-black along the spine, common in warm marshes and never truly alone. Touch one and it empties a numbing jolt into you. Corner several and they answer one another and loose the whole colony's charge at once. They climb, they swim, and they feel any jolt loosed a bowshot off.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — a marsh lizard you could carry under one arm, were you fool enough to try.
Durability: Frail. Almost anything kills one outright.
Defenses: Lightning cannot touch them at all — not their own, not a storm's, not a wand's. Past that, only a thin hide and very good hiding colours.
Speed: Quick over ground, quicker up a trunk, and perfectly at home in the water.
Might: Alone, a jolt that lays a man out senseless without leaving a mark on him. Together, a killing discharge that fills the reeds, and the more of them there are the worse it is.
Mind: A beast's mind and no more — yet the colony behaves as one animal.
Disposition: Skittish. A lone lizard shocks and bolts. It is the neighbours that kill you.
Bane: The great discharge wants company, so scatter or kill them singly and the danger leaves with the crowd. And they come to any jolt they feel — loose one wide and the colony will chase it instead of you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hides in the reeds, lets you come within arm's length, and empties itself into you. The bite comes only after you are down, or after the jolt has plainly done nothing. A solitary one bolts immediately afterward — but every lizard within reach felt that discharge and comes running, and once enough of them ring you the shock they raise together stops being merciful.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not wear the mail into the marsh, and do not stand in the water beside your friends.
• Spread out. Bunched men are one target for the big jolt.
• A wand of shocks fired wide into a bog pulls the whole colony after it. Best coin I ever spent.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing to say to them and nothing in them that could hear it. But they answer a loosed jolt like hounds to the horn. I have drawn a whole colony off a ford by throwing sparks into a bog downstream, and walked across dry. Treat them as weather, not as enemies.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A shocker lizard has a pale gray or blue underside, shading to a darker hue on its back, with blue-black markings along its back and tail. It is about 1 foot tall at the shoulder and weighs about 25 pounds. A shocker lizard relies on its electricity abilities in combat. A lizard tends to bite only after its shock has rendered an opponent unconscious or when the shock seems to have no effect at all. A solitary lizard flees once it delivers its shocks, but if other shocker lizards are nearby, they all home in on their comrade's discharges and attempt to administer their shocks to the foe.

Stunning Shock (Su): Once per round, a shocker lizard can deliver an electrical shock to a single opponent within 5 feet. This attack deals 2d8 points of nonlethal damage to living opponents (Reflex DC 12 half). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Lethal Shock (Su): Whenever two or more shocker lizards are within 20 feet of each other, they can work together to create a lethal shock. This effect has a radius of 20 feet, centered on any one contributing lizard. The shock deals 2d8 points of electricity damage for each lizard contributing to it, to a maximum of 12d8. A Reflex save (DC 10 + number of lizards contributing) reduces the damage by half.

Electricity Sense (Ex): Shocker lizards automatically detect any electrical discharges within 100 feet.

Skills: Shocker lizards have a +4 racial bonus on Hide checks due to their coloration, and a +2 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks. They use their Dexterity modifier instead of their Strength modifier for Climb and Jump checks. A shocker lizard has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened. It also has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard, can always take 10 on a Swim check even if distracted or endangered, and can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: I have never fought the tarrasque. No man I have shared a fire with has fought it and spoken of it after. There is one. It sleeps beneath the world, wakes seldom, and when it wakes it walks a straight line eating what stands in it — cattle, carts, walls, the folk behind the walls — then sleeps again. Every other page here I weighed in my own hands. This one I only assembled.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Colossal — a thing you measure against hills, not against beasts.
Durability: There is no honest word for it. What is told is that armies have opened its belly and watched the belly close while they worked.
Defenses: A carapace like a mirrored cliff, which turns aside every ray, beam and cone flung at it and now and then throws the thing back at the one who cast it. Beyond the shell, common steel scarcely marks it, spells slide off, and whatever wound is dealt closes about as fast as it opens.
Speed: It plods, and that is the one mercy in it — save that now and again it lowers its head and rushes, and then nothing on foot outruns it.
Might: Horns, claws, a sweeping tail, and jaws that take a man or a horse entire and swallow. What it bites, it bites through.
Mind: Dull as an ox and altogether without speech. It is not wicked. It is hunger wearing a hide.
Disposition: It does not hate, does not hunt for sport, does not hoard. It eats, walks, and sleeps. That is the whole of its nature, and it is enough to unmake a province.
Bane: Nothing you do to it kills it. It can be beaten down and it can be held down, but it rises again unless a wish or a miracle is spoken over it while it lies. That is the one true rule about the tarrasque, and every tale that forgets it ends the same way. Fire, venom, plague and the draining of life it does not feel at all; cold, acid and lightning it does.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes in a straight line and does not stop. Its dread runs ahead of it, and men's hands shake before the thing is even near. It gores, it rends, it sweeps with the tail, and what it catches in the jaws goes down whole to be crushed and burned in the gut — a man who cuts his way out from the inside leaves a hole that seals behind him. Rays and beams and blasts come off the shell, sometimes back into the caster's teeth. There is no craft in any of it. There does not need to be.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not stand in front of it. That is not cowardice; that is the entire surviving art.
• Leave the wands of ray and beam in the cart. The shell hands them back, and I have seen what that costs a wizard.
• Beat it down if you must, but have the wish or the miracle ready and spoken over it before anyone sits to rest. Without that you have only postponed the thing.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nobody to speak to. It has no tongue and less curiosity than a landslide. I set this stance down without any pride: every other page here I earned by trying words first. Here I would not try. Move the town, and be beyond the hills by morning.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: The tarrasque is 70 feet long and 50 feet tall, and it weighs about 130 tons. The tarrasque cannot speak. It attacks with its claws, teeth, horns, and tail. Its natural weapons are treated as epic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Augmented Critical (Ex): The tarrasque's bite threatens a critical hit on a natural attack roll of 18-20, dealing triple damage on a successful critical hit.

Frightful Presence (Su): The tarrasque can inspire terror by charging or attacking. Affected creatures must succeed on a DC 36 Will save or become shaken, remaining in that condition as long as they remain within 60 feet of the tarrasque. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, the tarrasque must hit a Huge or smaller opponent with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the foe the following round.

Rush (Ex): Once per minute, the normally slow-moving tarrasque can move at a speed of 150 feet.

Swallow Whole (Ex): The tarrasque can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of Huge or smaller size by making a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d8+8 points of crushing damage plus 2d8+6 points of acid damage per round from the tarrasque's digestive juices. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by dealing 50 points of damage to the gizzard wall (AC 25). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. The tarrasque's gullet can hold 2 Huge, 8 Large, 32 Medium, 128 Small, or 512 Tiny or smaller creatures.

Carapace (Ex): The tarrasque's armorlike carapace is exceptionally tough and highly reflective, deflecting all rays, lines, cones, and even magic missile spells. There is a 30% chance of reflecting any such effect back at the caster; otherwise, it is merely negated. Check for reflection before rolling to overcome the creature's spell resistance.

Regeneration 40 (Ex): No form of attack deals lasting damage to the tarrasque — every wound closes, and the beast is only ever beaten down, never truly killed. It regenerates even if it fails a saving throw against a disintegrate spell or a death effect. A spell or effect that would kill it instantly instead merely batters it toward unconsciousness, adding its full capacity to endure plus ten to the punishment it has taken. The tarrasque is immune to effects that produce incurable or bleeding wounds, such as mummy rot, a sword with the wounding special ability, or a clay golem's cursed wound ability. If it loses a limb or body part, the lost portion regrows in 1d6 minutes (the detached piece dies and decays normally); it can reattach a severed member instantly by holding it to the stump.

Killing It: The tarrasque can be slain only by battering it senseless — driving its accumulated nonlethal punishment past everything it can endure, plus ten more (868 points in all) — and then using a wish or miracle spell to keep it dead. Short of that, reducing it past the point of destruction only buys time: the wounds knit and the beast rises again.

Skills: The tarrasque has a +8 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

lore.summary: Rust-red above and dirty yellow beneath, the stirge is a wing and a hunger fastened to a needle. It roosts in warm marshes and drowned ruins, hanging still among the reeds until warm blood passes below, then drops in a whirring cloud. Alone it is a nuisance. A storm of them will empty a horse before the beast can bolt.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tiny — lighter than a loaf of bread, and mostly wing.
Durability: Frail past belief; a boot, a torch or a swatted glove ends one.
Defenses: None worth the name, save that it is small, quick, and cursed hard to see against reed and rust-coloured stone.
Speed: Wretched on the ground, but it flies swiftly and hangs on the air like a wasp.
Might: Feeble in itself. The harm is all in the proboscis, which drinks the vigour out of a man until his knees fold under him.
Mind: Animal, and barely that. It knows warmth, blood, and where to sink the needle.
Disposition: No malice in it, only appetite. It comes for anything with blood in it and departs the moment it has drunk its fill.
Bane: Fire, smoke and open water scatter a roost better than steel; and if you cannot kill it, outlast it — one that has fed lets go and blunders away of its own accord.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes in a whirring rush and picks the softest spot on a body — the throat, the inside of a wrist, the gap above a boot — then plunges its proboscis in and latches on with eight small pincers, clinging with a tenacity out of all proportion to its weight. After that it does nothing but drink, swelling and darkening, while its fellows fasten elsewhere. Sated, it detaches and lurches off to digest; if the victim fails first, it simply chooses another.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Gauntlets, gorget, and hose tucked into the boot. They hunt the gaps in your harness.
• A smoking brand swung slowly clears a roost where a sword only wearies the arm.
• Never hack at one fastened to a friend. Take hold of it, pin it against him, and prise — the alternative is your blade in his throat.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing there to speak with. I tried it once in the fen country, cooing at a roost as a man coos at a hound; they came off the reeds all together and I was three days getting my strength back. You would do better bargaining with a mosquito.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A stirge attacks by landing on a victim, finding a vulnerable spot, and plunging its proboscis into the flesh. This is a touch attack and can target only Small or larger creatures.

Attach (Ex): If a stirge hits with a touch attack, it uses its eight pincers to latch onto the opponent's body. An attached stirge is effectively grappling its prey. The stirge loses its Dexterity bonus to AC and has an AC of 12, but holds on with great tenacity. Stirges have a +12 racial bonus on grapple checks (already figured into the Base Attack/Grapple entry above). An attached stirge can be struck with a weapon or grappled itself. To remove an attached stirge through grappling, the opponent must achieve a pin against the stirge.

Blood Drain (Ex): A stirge drains blood, dealing 1d4 points of Constitution damage in any round when it begins its turn attached to a victim. Once it has dealt 4 points of Constitution damage, it detaches and flies off to digest the meal. If its victim dies before the stirge's appetite has been sated, the stirge detaches and seeks a new target.

lore.summary: Named for its favourite meat, the spider eater is a wasp grown to the bulk of a warhorse — glassy wings, plated hide, shearing mandibles, and a sting curled beneath the belly. It keeps to temperate forest and hunts alone, taking the great spiders in their own lairs, for no strand and no snare has ever held one yet.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — long as a farm wagon, with a wingspan twice that again.
Durability: Heavy and well armoured in chitin; it soaks up a great deal of punishment before it drops.
Defenses: A hard shell, and a stranger gift than that: nothing binds it. Web, net, grasping vine, the clinging spells that slow a man — it walks free of all of them as though they were not there.
Speed: Brisk on the ground and swift and nimble in the air; it hovers as easily as it charges.
Might: Mandibles that shear, and a sting whose venom is far worse than the wound — no pain at first, then a stillness that holds a man for weeks.
Mind: Beast-dull. It hunts, it breeds, and a patient hand can break it to the saddle; there are few finer mounts in the air.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor kind. It stings, withdraws, and waits for the poison to do the work for it.
Bane: It has no answer at all to a bow. Keep out of the sting's reach and never let it stand over a fallen comrade — the eggs go into the living.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Its way is patient and horrible. It stings once, then backs off and hovers beyond reach, circling while the venom works, and only closes with the mandibles when the victim has stiffened. Nothing tangles it — webs, nets, snares and clinging magic all slide off — so a spider's lair is no refuge and neither is your prepared ground. A female will drag paralysed prey of good size away to a quiet place and lay her eggs inside it; the young eat their way out.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Nets, webs, entangling tricks — all wasted breath. Do not buy that lesson twice.
• If it stings a man and he goes stiff, carry him out that same hour and find someone who can purge him. What follows the stillness is worse than the sting.
• Take it at distance or take a fast horse. Do not stand and trade blows beneath a hovering sting.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: A dull hunger with wings. I have never had a word from one, though I have had a season's good service out of one — they can be reared and ridden, and I flew a broken-in male over the Thornwood for a summer. Wild, it does not hear you at all.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A spider eater attacks with its venomous sting and powerful mandibles. Its usual tactic is to deliver a sting, then back off, hovering out of reach until the venom takes effect.

Implant (Ex): Female spider eaters lay their eggs inside paralyzed creatures of Large or larger size. The young emerge about six weeks later, literally devouring the host from inside.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 17, initial damage none, secondary damage paralysis for 1d8+5 weeks. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Freedom of Movement (Su): Spider eaters have a continuous freedom of movement ability as the spell (caster level 12th). When the spider eater serves as a mount, this effect does not extend to its rider.

Skills: Spider eaters have a +4 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

Training a Spider Eater: A spider eater requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. Training a spider eater requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a spider eater requires an exotic saddle. A spider eater can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Spider eater eggs are worth 2,000 gp apiece on the open market, while young are worth 3,000 gp each. Professional trainers charge 3,000 gp to rear or train a spider eater.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a spider eater is up to 306 pounds; a medium load, 307-612 pounds; and a heavy load, 613-920 pounds.

lore.summary: From the shoulders forward a lion — maned, fanged, and without a grain of fear; from there back a fish, scaled and finned, driving it through cold water faster than a boat can be rowed. Sea cats hold stretches of temperate coast the way lions hold grassland, and they take seals, swimmers and sailors alike, singly, in pairs, or in a whole pride.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer than a rowing boat, and heavier than any two men in mail.
Durability: Thick-hided and stubbornly hard to put down; it keeps coming long past the point a beast ought to quit.
Defenses: A tough scaled hide and nothing else — no craft, no venom, no magic. Meat and armour only.
Speed: In the water it is swift as a porpoise and tireless. Ashore it is a floundering thing that can scarcely drag itself up a shingle bank.
Might: Two raking claws and a lion's bite. When both paws take hold it hauls itself along the body and tears, and that tearing is what actually kills.
Mind: Animal, and brave beyond all sense; it will set upon creatures many times its size and it does not break.
Disposition: Territorial and immediate. It attacks on sight — for meat, or simply for the water it claims — and it fights to the death.
Bane: It cannot follow you ashore. Reach a rock, a deck, a beach, and it is finished with you; and it must surface to breathe at last, though it can hold that breath a long while.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It rises from below and takes you in the water, where every advantage is its own. Both paws hook in first, then it drags itself along the body and rends — the grip is the warning and the tearing is the wound that ends the fight. A pride works in concert, worrying at an enemy from all quarters until one of them can finish it, and not one of them will flee. Expect no retreat, no display, no mercy.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it from a boat or a rock. In the water you are only meat that talks.
• The moment both paws land, break the hold. What comes after the grip is what kills.
• Kill one of a pride and the rest do not scatter. They come on harder.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I have called down to prides from a gunwale and thrown them good fish. They take the fish and then they come for the arm. There is nothing behind those eyes but the coast they own, and they will die before they yield a yard of it. Get out of the water and let them have it.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Sea cats attack on sight, either for food or to defend their territory, and use both claws and teeth to grab and rend their prey. They display tremendous courage, always fighting to the death, even against creatures many times their size. Pairs and prides of sea cats attack in concert, trying to wear the opponent down until one beast can dispatch it.

Hold Breath (Ex): A sea cat can hold its breath for a number of rounds equal to 6 × its Constitution score before it risks drowning.

Rend (Ex): A sea cat that hits with both claw attacks latches onto the opponent's body and tears the flesh. This automatically deals an extra 2d6+6 points of damage.

Skills: A sea cat has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: Eyeless, long-jawed and yellow-green, the yrthak rides the winds over high stone country and hears the world entire through an organ on its lolling tongue. The crest on its skull throws a lance of pure sound that punches through a shield like a bolt, and a flick of that same lance against a cliff turns the rock itself into a killing spray. Mountain folk call it a dragon. It is not.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — long as a river barge, with wings half again as wide.
Durability: Heavy-boned and thickly scaled; it endures a great deal of hard work before it comes down.
Defenses: It is blind, so nothing you show it counts for anything — no gaze, no dazzling light, no illusion, no conjured phantom will touch it at all. But sound wounds it far worse than it wounds you.
Speed: Ponderous on the ground and a master of the air; it strafes, and is gone before the answer leaves the bow.
Might: A lance of sound at range, jaws and raking claws at close quarters, and strength enough to snatch an armed man off a ledge and let go of him over the drop.
Mind: Cunning enough to plan and to learn a valley's habits, though there is not a word of speech in it; it hunts alone or in a small clutch.
Disposition: Territorial and pitiless within its own country, and it fights from above where it need not be answered.
Bane: Deafen it and you have blinded it — clamour, ringing metal, horns, leave it groping. Better still, hurt it with sound outright; it suffers from that worse than any creature I know. And its hearing has an edge; step beyond that edge and you are simply gone.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It will not land if it can avoid landing. It circles high, throws its lance of sound down at whatever holds still, then swings away — the lance needs a moment to gather itself before it can be thrown again, and that pause between is your whole chance, so spend it moving. Shelter behind stone and it fires at the stone on purpose, shattering it into a spray of splinters that flays everyone crouched there. Stand apart from your fellows and it stoops instead, snatches you up, climbs, and opens its claws.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It hears you; it does not see you. Soft ground, wrapped buckles, shut mouth.
• Never take cover behind rock. It breaks the rock over you deliberately — that is the trick of the thing.
• Anything that shrieks, rings or thunders hurts it badly. Carry a horn. A deafened yrthak is a lost one.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is a mind in it — better than a hound's, poorer than a man's — but no tongue at all, and it has never once cared what I had to say. I stood in a scree gully and talked at one for the length of a prayer. It answered by shattering the boulder I sheltered behind.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A yrthak is blind. It senses sound and movement by means of a special organ on its long tongue, and emits powerfully focused beams of sound from the protrusion on its head. Despite their intelligence, yrthaks do not speak. A yrthak prefers to attack from the air, strafing the ground with sonic attacks or snatching up and dropping prey.

Sonic Lance (Su): Once every 2 rounds, a yrthak can focus sonic energy in a ray up to 60 feet long. This is a ranged touch attack that deals 6d6 points of damage to a single target.

Explosion (Su): A yrthak can fire its sonic lance at the ground, a large rock, a stone wall, or the like to create an explosion of shattered stone. This attack deals 2d6 points of piercing damage to all within 10 feet of the effect's center. This counts as a use of the sonic lance attack and thus is usable only once every 2 rounds, and never on the round following a sonic lance attack.

Blindsight (Ex): A yrthak can ascertain all foes within 120 feet. Beyond that range it is considered blinded. Yrthaks are invulnerable to gaze attacks, visual effects of spells such as illusions, and other attack forms that rely on sight. A yrthak whose sense of hearing is impaired is effectively blinded, treating all targets as having total concealment.

Immunities: Yrthaks have immunity to gaze attacks, visual effects, illusions, and other attack forms that rely on sight.

Vulnerability to Sonic: A yrthak takes half again as much damage (+50%) as normal from sonic effects, regardless of whether a saving throw is allowed or if the save is a success or failure.

Skills: Yrthaks have a +4 racial bonus on Listen checks.

lore.summary: A humpbacked spider with a body larger than a man's chest — the hump is all brain — bearing small clever hands beneath its fangs and the sorcery to match them. An aranea also wears a second face, one fixed human shape it never varies, worn so long and so well that a village never learns what has taken the room above its inn. Look for them in temperate woods and at the hearths on their edge.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — in its own shape a spider bulkier than a man's torso; in its borrowed shape, someone you would pass in the street without a glance.
Durability: No hardier than an ordinary man, and it is perfectly aware of the fact.
Defenses: Little armour and no appetite whatever for being struck. Its true guard is deceit: the borrowed shape is no mere glamour to be unravelled by a countercharm, and it does not slip even in death — only a sight that pierces every lie will strip it.
Speed: Very swift on its own legs and swifter still up a sheer wall than along the floor; slower, and far more careful, in the shape it wears among folk.
Might: Weak of arm. It fights with a thrown web, a venom that unstrings the muscles of a strong man, and a sorcerer's small unkindnesses — sleep, phantoms, and a shimmer of armour about itself.
Mind: Sharp as a well-schooled scholar and a great deal more patient. It has the common tongue and the sylvan one, and it keeps a bargain so long as the bargain still profits it.
Disposition: Secretive and acquisitive, rarely murderous by preference; it would far rather take you alive and sell you back to your own people.
Bane: Fire. It will not throw fire, it flinches from fire, and its webbing burns away in a breath. A bright lamp is nearly as good — hold it close and you may catch the fangs and spinnerets under a borrowed collar.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not want a fight and it fights accordingly. First a web flung out of the dark to pin whoever swings hardest; then a creeping sleep and a phantom or two to thin and scatter the rest; only then the bite, whose venom leaves a strong man unable to lift his own sword. It works from walls and ceilings, from behind, from above, and it breaks off the instant the odds sour. Survivors are frequently kept rather than killed — an aranea would sooner have a ransom than a corpse.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The handsome stranger at the crossroads inn is always the same handsome stranger. Ask the locals how many years they have known that face.
• Carry a brand, not just a lantern. Web burns, and the weaver hates the burning worse.
• It would rather ransom you than bury you. That is a lever — use it, but pay in something you can bear to lose.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: This one talks, and talks well. I have bargained twice with the same aranea and been dealt with squarely both times — coin for safe passage, and it kept the road honest. I have also woken to a web across the door of an inn I had thought safe. Talk by all means. Talk with your back to a wall and your eyes on the ceiling.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Magical Beast (Shapechanger)
Initiative: +6
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares), climb 25 ft.
Armor Class: 13 (+2 Dex, +1 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 11
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+3
Attack: Bite +5 melee (1d6 plus poison) or web +5 ranged
Full Attack: Bite +5 melee (1d6 plus poison) or web +5 ranged
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison, spells, web
Special Qualities: Change shape, darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +4
Abilities: Str 11, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 14, Wis 13, Cha 14
Skills: Climb +14, Concentration +8, Escape Artist +5, Jump +13, Listen +6, Spot +6
Feats: Improved Initiative, Iron Will (B), Weapon Finesse
Environment: Temperate forests

Challenge Rating: 4
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: Standard coins; double goods; standard items
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: An aranea avoids physical combat and uses its webs and spells when it can. In a battle, it tries to immobilize or distract the most aggressive opponents first. Araneas often subdue opponents for ransom. Araneas speak Common and Sylvan.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 13, initial damage 1d6 Str, secondary damage 2d6 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Spells: An aranea casts spells as a 3rd-level sorcerer. It prefers illusions and enchantments and avoids fire spells. Typical Sorcerer Spells Known (6/6; save DC 12 + spell level): 0—daze, detect magic, ghost sound, light, resistance; 1st—mage armor, silent image, sleep.

Web (Ex): In spider or hybrid form (see below), an aranea can throw a web up to six times per day. This is similar to an attack with a net but has a maximum range of 50 feet, with a range increment of 10 feet, and is effective against targets of up to Large size. The web anchors the target in place, allowing no movement. An entangled creature can escape with a DC 13 Escape Artist check or burst the web with a DC 17 Strength check. The check DCs are Constitution-based, and the Strength check DC includes a +4 racial bonus. The web has hardness 0, is torn apart by 6 points of damage, and takes double damage from fire.

Change Shape (Su): An aranea's natural form is that of a Medium monstrous spider. It can assume two other forms. The first is a unique Small or Medium humanoid; an aranea in its humanoid form always assumes the same appearance and traits, much as a lycanthrope would. In humanoid form, an aranea cannot use its bite attack, webs, or poison. The second form is a Medium spider-humanoid hybrid. In hybrid form, an aranea looks like a Medium humanoid at first glance, but a DC 18 Spot check reveals the creature's fangs and spinnerets. The aranea retains its bite attack, webs, and poison in this form, and can also wield weapons or wear armor. When in hybrid form, an aranea's speed is 30 feet (6 squares). An aranea remains in one form until it chooses to assume a new one. A change in form cannot be dispelled, nor does an aranea revert to its natural form when killed. A true seeing spell, however, reveals its natural form if it is in humanoid or hybrid form.

Skills: Araneas have a +2 racial bonus on Jump, Listen, and Spot checks. They have a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on Climb checks even if rushed or threatened.

lore.summary: Every wood has vines. This one keeps a larder. The assassin vine grows where the soil is rich because it makes the soil rich — it seizes what walks past, crushes it, and lets the carcass rot down among its own roots. Its late-summer fruit looks like wild grapes and makes a heady, bitter wine. I have drunk it. I have also dug men out from under it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a main stem long as a wagon, with lesser vines branching off it the whole length.
Durability: Woody and stubborn. It takes honest hacking, but nothing about it mends.
Defenses: Lightning does nothing to it whatever, and both frost and flame come off it half-blunted. Being a plant, it knows no fear, cannot be charmed, poisoned or put to sleep, and has no vitals to find — a cunning thrust is only a thrust.
Speed: It can creep, barely, and only to reach new hunting ground. Once settled it does not chase.
Might: A mill-press grip. It strikes further than the visible plant suggests, hauls you in, and crushes without hurry or pause.
Mind: None whatever. There is nothing in it to reason with, frighten, or trick.
Disposition: Patient past patience, and it looks like ordinary greenery until flesh comes within reach. Even a woodsman's eye can pass over one.
Bane: It cannot follow. Break the hold, get clear of the patch, and you are simply gone. Waste no lightning on it; an axe does the honest work.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It lies still as any hedge until you are close, and then the ground turns on you — grass, briar and creeper all writhe up and bind your legs at once. While you are fouled, the main vine slams, takes hold, drags you in and crushes. It keeps the surrounding growth thrashing as long as it pleases, as much to spoil a rescue as to hold the meal.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Read the ground before you read the vine. Greenery too thick and too green means you are already standing in the larder.
• Cut the growth off your legs first, not the vine. The vine will still be there; your legs may not be.
• Lightning is wasted on it — I watched a good wand achieve nothing at all. Steel, axes, and patience.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. There is nothing there to answer. The only bargain an assassin vine keeps is the one it strikes with the soil: your body for its fruit. Drink the wine if it is offered — I have, and it is good — but do not raise the cup to the vine.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

Special Qualities: Blindsight 30 ft., camouflage, immunity to electricity, low-light vision, plant traits, resistance to cold 10 and fire 10
Saves: Fort +7, Ref +1, Will +2

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: An assassin vine uses simple tactics: it lies still until prey comes within reach, then attacks. It uses its entangle ability both to catch prey and to deter counterattacks.

Constrict (Ex): An assassin vine deals 1d6+7 points of damage with a successful grapple check.

Entangle (Su): An assassin vine can animate plants within 30 feet of itself as a free action (Ref DC 13 partial). The effect lasts until the vine dies or decides to end it (also a free action). The save DC is Wisdom-based. The ability is otherwise similar to entangle (caster level 4th).

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, an assassin vine must hit with its slam attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can constrict.

Blindsight (Ex): Assassin vines have no visual organs but can ascertain all foes within 30 feet using sound, scent, and vibration.

Camouflage (Ex): Since an assassin vine looks like a normal plant when at rest, it takes a DC 20 Spot check to notice it before it attacks. Anyone with ranks in Survival or Knowledge (nature) can use one of those skills instead of Spot to notice the plant. Dwarves can use stonecunning to notice the subterranean version.

Plant Traits (Ex): An assassin vine is immune to all mind-affecting effects, to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, polymorph and stunning, and is not subject to critical hits. It cannot be raised or resurrected, and it has low-light vision.

lore.summary: A hillock that stands up. The tendriculos is a heaped mass of creeper, root and rotting leaf with a maw in the middle of it and a pair of long tendrils to feed that maw. It does not stalk so much as prowl — slow, shameless, swallowing whatever flesh it can reach. Deer will not graze where one has passed, nor for a full day after.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a mound of vegetation that rears up taller than a mounted man and weighs more than a cart of stone.
Durability: Enormous, and worse than enormous: it knits itself back together. Wounds close, lopped parts regrow within minutes, and a severed piece held against the mass rejoins on the instant.
Defenses: Plant through and through — no fear, no charm, no sleep, no venom, no binding of the limbs will touch it. It has no organs to pierce, so a clever thrust buys nothing, and what blade and arrow open, it mends.
Speed: Slow, but not rooted. It prowls, and it will follow you at a walk for as long as it likes.
Might: Frightful strength. It bites, seizes, lifts and swallows in the space of a breath, and the tendrils hand you to the mouth whether you are willing or not.
Mind: A dull animal spark, no more. It hunts by hunger, not by plan, and no word will reach it.
Disposition: Utterly fearless and wholly indiscriminate. It waits looking like a small rise in the ground, and every beast and green thing in the wood knows to shun the place it has been.
Bane: Its mending fails against crushing weight and against caustics. Bring hammers, mauls, and a flask of something that eats. If you are swallowed, a light blade will cut you out — though the hole seals behind you, so it saves no one else.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It squats like a hummock until you are within reach, then rears and bites. What the bite catches, it holds; what the tendrils catch, they carry up to the mouth. Then it swallows you whole and lets its juices work — the stuff burns while it stiffens a man's limbs to uselessness, and it does not stop biting for those still outside. It shows no fear and yields no ground.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Hammers and mauls. Sword-work feeds it — it closes the cut before you have drawn back.
• Carry a small blade on your body, not your belt. Inside the thing, a belt is out of reach and that knife is your only door.
• Where the deer will not graze and the birds will not nest, look hard at any hillock that was not there last season.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None. There is a spark in it, but it is the spark of a starving dog with no ears. I once tried backing off with soft words. It came after me at a walk for the length of a valley and would have kept on. Words are for things that can stop eating.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Huge Plant
Initiative: –1
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 16 (–2 size, –1 Dex, +9 natural), touch 7, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+23
Attack: Bite +13 melee (2d8+9)
Full Attack: Bite +13 melee (2d8+9) and 2 tendrils +8 melee (1d6+4)
Space/Reach: 15 ft./15 ft.
Special Attacks: Improved grab, paralysis, swallow whole
Special Qualities: Low-light vision, plant traits, regeneration 10
Saves: Fort +12, Ref +2, Will +4
Abilities: Str 28, Dex 9, Con 22, Int 3, Wis 8, Cha 3
Skills: Hide +9, Listen +1, Move Silently +1, Spot +1

Treasure: 1/10th coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: 10–16 levels (Huge); 17–27 levels (Gargantuan)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Prowling deep forests or waiting in vegetated areas (looking like nothing more than a small hillock), a tendriculos attacks savagely, showing no fear. It attempts to swallow as much flesh as it can, as quickly as it can.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a tendriculos must hit a creature at least one size smaller than itself with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the opponent in the following round. A tendriculos can also use its improved grab ability on a tendril attack. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold, picks up the opponent, and transfers it to the mouth as a free action, automatically dealing bite damage.

Swallow Whole/Paralysis (Ex): A tendriculos can try to swallow a grabbed opponent by making a successful grapple check. Once inside the plant's mass, the opponent must succeed on a DC 20 Fortitude save or be paralyzed for 3d6 rounds by the tendriculos's digestive juices, taking 2d6 points of acid damage per round. A new save is required each round inside the plant. The save DC is Constitution-based. A swallowed creature that avoids paralysis can climb out of the mass with a successful grapple check. This returns it to the plant's maw, where another successful grapple check is needed to get free. A swallowed creature can also cut its way out by using a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 points of damage to the tendriculos's interior (AC 14). Once the creature exits, the plant's regenerative capacity closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A Huge tendriculos's interior can hold 2 Large, 8 Medium, 32 Small, 128 Tiny, or 512 Diminutive or smaller opponents.

Regeneration 10 (Ex): Bludgeoning weapons and acid deal normal damage to a tendriculos. Every other kind of damage is turned aside as merely temporary harm, which the plant shrugs off at a rate of 10 points each round. A tendriculos that loses part of its body mass can regrow it in 1d6 minutes; holding the severed portion against the mass enables it to reattach instantly.

Plant Traits (Ex): A tendriculos is immune to all mind-affecting effects, to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, polymorph and stunning, and is not subject to critical hits. It cannot be raised or resurrected, and it has low-light vision.

lore.summary: The most feared thing in the deep tunnels is the one nobody has seen. The phantom fungus is a squat brown and green mass on stumpy legs, crowned with a knot of sensing nodules and split by a gaping maw of teeth — and while it lives it cannot be seen at all. It walks quietly, it hunts alone, and the first you know of it is the bite.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — squat and broad, about the bulk of a big hound.
Durability: Sturdier than a mushroom has any right to be, but nothing remarkable. Once you can find it, it dies like a plant.
Defenses: Its whole defence is that it is unseen — and this is no spell laid upon it but part of the thing itself, so no purging magic will strip it away. Beyond that, the plant's flat indifference to fear, charm, sleep and venom, and no vitals worth aiming for.
Speed: An unhurried walk, and quieter than yours.
Might: One heavy bite from a mouth of ranked teeth, and then another. No venom, no trickery — it does not need any.
Mind: Barely past instinct. It knows a lone traveller from a band, and prefers open ground when it must face a crowd. That is the whole of its cleverness.
Disposition: A patient hunter of stragglers. It roams the dark passages and takes whoever walks last.
Bane: It is unseen, not unfindable. Flour, ash, water, blood or a smoking fire will all put an outline on it, and a good ear will find it before your eyes do. Kill it and it shows itself soon enough — that corpse is the only look you will ever get.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes at a walk out of nothing at all, takes one solid bite, and keeps biting; being unseen does not fail it while it fights. Against a lone traveller it will attack almost anywhere. Against a band it hangs back until you are in open ground, where it can circle and be nowhere in particular.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Carry a sack of flour or fine ash and throw it wide, not at where you think the thing stands.
• Purging magic does nothing — the unseeing is part of it, not a charm laid on. Listen instead. It is quiet, but it is not silent.
• It takes the straggler. In its tunnels, nobody walks last alone.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: No. I have talked to worse and got further. There is an animal wit in it, but you cannot meet the eye of a thing with no eye and no shape to address. I stood very still once and spoke softly for a good while. It bit me in the middle of a sentence.
