Skills: A dire wolverine has a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on Climb checks, even if rushed or threatened.

lore.summary: Longer than the boat you are standing in and heavier than her whole season's catch, the dire shark of the cold seas eats whatever it judges edible — and it judges generously, taking on beasts larger than itself. It smells blood across a morning's sail and comes fast and straight. Sailors know it by the fin, and by the sudden silence of the gulls.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — longer than the hull beneath your feet.
Durability: Vast and thick-muscled. It carries wounds that would end a whale and keeps swimming.
Defenses: Hide like wet stone, rough enough to take the skin from your palm as it passes.
Speed: Swift and tireless in the water. It runs a straight course faster than any man can swim.
Might: One bite, and that bite is everything — jaws that close on a man and take him whole.
Mind: Simple as ballast. It has appetite where other beasts keep their thoughts.
Disposition: It attacks anything it reckons food, and it reckons almost everything food.
Bane: It is bound utterly to the water. Gain a hull, a rock, a floating spar, and it can do nothing but circle and sulk. And a swallowed man is not a finished man — keep a light blade, cut outward, and it will give you back.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It takes you in its jaws, holds fast, and swallows — and then you are in the dark, crushed and burning in its gut while it swims on untroubled. It circles a bleeding swimmer, comes up from below where the light is worst, and always chooses the one already wounded. Do not lose your knife, and do not go into the water to fetch a friend.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Keep a light blade where a swallowed man can still reach it. Cut outward, not about.
• Blood in the water calls it from further off than you would credit. Gut the catch ashore.
• It charges in a straight line. Turn the boat across its path and let it go by.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing behind that eye to speak with. I once shouted at one over a gunwale, which shamed me and delighted the crew for a fortnight. Talk instead to the sea: stay out of it, keep your blood and your offal aboard, and it will go and find something else to eat.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Dire sharks attack anything they perceive to be edible, even larger creatures. They bite with their powerful jaws, swallowing smaller creatures in one gulp.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a dire shark must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the foe in the following round.

Swallow Whole (Ex): A dire shark can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of up to one size smaller by making a successful grapple check. Once inside, the opponent takes 2d6+6 points of bludgeoning damage plus 1d8+4 points of acid damage per round from the shark's digestive juices. A swallowed creature can cut its way out using a light slashing or piercing weapon by dealing 25 points of damage to the shark's digestive tract (AC 13). Once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole; another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A Huge dire shark's gullet can hold 2 Large, 8 Medium or Small, 32 Tiny, 128 Diminutive, or 512 Fine or smaller opponents.

Keen Scent (Ex): A dire shark can notice creatures by scent in a 180-foot radius and can detect blood in the water at a range of up to 1 mile.

Skills: A dire shark has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

lore.summary: A bat with the wingspan of a barn door, roosting in quiet colonies through the hot desert country and the caves beneath it. It hunts by sound alone, stooping on prey from above with no warning and no shadow to give it away. Mild enough as beasts go — it wants meat, not murder — but a roused colony in a narrow passage is a very poor place to be standing.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — wings broader than a wagon is long, over a body no heavier than a big hound.
Durability: Light-boned and easily broken, which matters little until you have managed to touch it.
Defenses: Nothing but its own quickness, and it is very quick — the hardest flying thing I know to strike.
Speed: Slow and wretched crawling; on the wing, fast and beautifully handled.
Might: A single hard bite, delivered on the stoop, and nothing else in its whole repertoire.
Mind: Simple beast wit. Curious, easily startled, no malice anywhere in it.
Disposition: It hunts what it can carry and leaves alone what it cannot. A roused colony strikes out of fright, not appetite.
Bane: It sees with its ears. Bells, shouting, a waterfall, a cave full of echoes — all of it blinds the creature, and in true darkness it cannot make you out at all save by the noise you make. Ground it and it is helpless.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It swoops from above on prey that has not looked up: one pass, one hard bite, and gone before you have turned about. On the ground it is a different animal entirely — it crawls badly, it can be run down, and it knows it. Bring it out of the air by any means you have and the fight is more than half won.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fill the passage with noise and it is as good as blinded. A cord of bells is worth more than a shield.
• It hunts from above. Fight under an overhang, or with your back to the roof.
• Ground it and it is helpless. Nets, a thrown cloak — anything that fouls a wing.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Words are wasted on a thing that navigates by echoes; mine came back to me and nothing else. Yet I have sheltered in a roost with a whole colony through a sandstorm and taken no hurt of them. Move slowly, make no sudden noise, and they will let you pass. That is as near to talking as it gets.

sections.body: Minor — A lesser peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Dire bats swoop down upon unsuspecting prey from above.

Blindsense (Ex): A dire bat uses echolocation to pinpoint creatures within 40 feet. Opponents still have total concealment against the bat unless it can actually see them.

Skills: Dire bats have a +4 racial bonus on Spot and Listen checks. These bonuses are lost if its blindsense is negated.

lore.summary: You never see the thing itself, only the dust and leaves it drags in a circle. Air elementals belong to a plane of endless sky and come here chiefly because someone called them — a lit censer, a spoken word, a circle chalked on a floor. Met on tower tops, open moors and mastheads, and worst of all met while your own feet are off the ground.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Judge it by the column of dust: the least is no taller than a child, the greatest a howling pillar higher than a barn.
Durability: It weighs less than a full wineskin and yet it takes an unholy amount of killing; the larger sort simply do not feel a lesser blow at all.
Defenses: No flesh, no blood, no vitals. Venom, sleep-craft, palsy and stunning slide off it; there is no soft place to find, and nothing is gained by taking it from behind.
Speed: Swifter than a courier's horse and perfectly turned in the air — it hovers, reverses and darts without ever losing its footing on nothing.
Might: Buffeting slams that come from every side at once, and the whirlwind: it draws itself into a spinning column, snatches lighter folk off the ground and batters them aloft while it carries them where it likes.
Mind: Dull-witted but not mindless. It knows the tongue of the air and it understands an order; the eldest are cleverer than most men expect.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor kind. Mostly it wants its errand done and its road home; obliged or angered, it is single-minded.
Bane: Keep your boots on solid earth — anything fighting it aloft fights it at a disadvantage. And while it spins as a whirlwind it cannot strike with its arms, nor hold that shape long, nor take it up again for a good while after.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes fast and does not stay to trade blows: a rush across the field, a battering as it passes, and away before you have turned. Against a crowd or a deck of men it draws itself into a whirlwind, walks through your line without a soul being able to stop it, lifts the lightest of you into the air and grinds them there in a cloud of dust that blinds everything within it — then spits them out, wherever it happens to be standing, and comes back around for the rest.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it standing. The moment your feet leave the ground you have made its work easier.
• Count out its spinning. It cannot hold the whirlwind, and it cannot take it up again straight away — that gap is your whole fight.
• The one who lit the incense is the real quarry. Break the vessel, break the errand.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Words work, if you have the tongue of the air and something worth saying. Every one I have spoken to wanted the same thing: release. Offer to break the summoner's hold and it will hear you out — but it owes you nothing once it is free, and it does not linger to thank a man.

sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.body:

Organization: Solitary

Treasure: None
Advancement: 9–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Sizes (Small to Elder): The block above is the Large air elemental. The family runs: Small — AC 17 (touch 14), slam +5 melee (1d4), Str 10, CR 1. Medium — AC 18 (touch 15), slam +8 melee (1d6+1), Str 12, CR 3. Large — AC 20 (touch 16), 2 slams +12 melee (2d6+2), Str 14, CR 5. Huge — AC 21 (touch 17), 2 slams +19 melee (2d8+4), Str 18, CR 7. Greater — AC 26 (touch 18), 2 slams +23 melee (2d8+5), Str 20, CR 9. Elder — AC 27 (touch 19), 2 slams +27 melee (2d8+6), Str 22, CR 11. All fly 100 ft. (perfect). Damage reduction begins at Large (5/—) and rises to 10/— for greater and elder. Whirlwind save DC and damage by size: Small DC 11/1d4, Medium DC 13/1d6, Large DC 16/2d6, Huge DC 22/2d8, greater DC 25/2d8, elder DC 28/2d8. Heights run 4 ft. (Small) to 40 ft. (elder), and an air elemental weighs almost nothing — 1 to 12 pounds. Air elementals speak Auran, though they rarely choose to do so.

Air Mastery (Ex): Airborne creatures take a –1 penalty on attack and damage rolls against an air elemental.

Whirlwind (Su): The elemental can transform itself into a whirlwind once every 10 minutes and remain in that form for up to 1 round for every 2 levels it possesses. In this form it can move through the air or along a surface at its fly speed. The whirlwind is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 30 feet wide at the top, and up to 50 feet tall depending on the elemental's size; the elemental controls the exact height, but it must be at least 10 feet. Its movement while in whirlwind form does not provoke attacks of opportunity, even if it enters the space another creature occupies. Another creature might be caught in the whirlwind if it touches or enters the whirlwind, or if the elemental moves into or through the creature's space. Creatures one or more size categories smaller than the elemental may take damage when caught (Large: 2d6, DC 16) and may be lifted into the air. An affected creature must succeed on a Reflex save on contact or take the indicated damage, and must also succeed on a second Reflex save or be picked up bodily and held suspended in the powerful winds, automatically taking the indicated damage each round. A creature that can fly is allowed a Reflex save each round to escape; it still takes damage but can leave if the save succeeds. The save DC varies with the elemental's size and is Strength-based. Trapped creatures cannot move except to go where the elemental carries them or to escape. They can otherwise act normally, but must succeed on a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level) to cast a spell, and take a –4 penalty to Dexterity and a –2 penalty on attack rolls. The elemental can hold only as many creatures as will fit inside the whirlwind's volume, and can eject any carried creature whenever it wishes, depositing it wherever the whirlwind happens to be; a summoned elemental always ejects trapped creatures before returning to its home plane. If the whirlwind's base touches the ground it creates a swirling cloud of debris centred on the elemental, with a diameter equal to half the whirlwind's height, that obscures all vision including darkvision beyond 5 feet — creatures 5 feet away have concealment, those farther away total concealment — and those caught in the cloud must succeed on a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level) to cast a spell. An elemental in whirlwind form cannot make slam attacks and does not threaten the area around it.

Combat: Their rapid speed makes air elementals useful on vast battlefields or in extended aerial combat.

Elemental Traits: An elemental is a being composed of one of the four classical elements. Elementals have darkvision out to 60 feet and immunity to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning. They are not subject to critical hits or flanking. Unlike most other living creatures, an elemental does not have a dual nature — its soul and body form one unit, so when an elemental is slain no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate and resurrection, do not work on an elemental; it takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle or true resurrection, to restore it to life. Elementals are proficient with natural weapons only, unless generally humanoid in form, and are not proficient with armor unless described as wearing it. Elementals do not eat, sleep or breathe.

lore.summary: A walking piece of the world's foundation, made of whatever it was called out of — clay and cobbles in a village lane, ore and raw gemstone in a rich seam. It swims through stone as a fish swims water and leaves no hole behind it, so the first you know of it is the floor rising into a fist. Met wherever a summoner wanted a wall broken.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: From a squat thing the height of a child to a slab-shouldered giant taller than a house, and heavy past all reckoning.
Durability: The most stubborn body in the elemental kin. It is a boulder that has decided to walk, and the great ones shrug off ordinary weapons as a cliff shrugs rain.
Defenses: No vitals to hunt for, no back to stab, and no use in poison, sleep-craft, palsy or stunning. Stone does not swoon.
Speed: Ponderous on the surface and never in a hurry — but through rock it moves as easily as you walk a road, and it never stops coming.
Might: Slams that shatter a shield and the arm behind it, and a shove that puts a man on his back and keeps him there. The eldest strike hard enough to break a wall in a single pass.
Mind: Slow and literal. It speaks the deep tongue of stone, keeps to the letter of an order, and rarely bothers to answer a stranger.
Disposition: Patient, indifferent, relentless. It bears no malice and it does not tire, which is worse.
Bane: Get off the ground or get onto the water — it fights badly against anything it cannot touch through the earth, it cannot swim a step, and a body of water will send it walking the long way round. Craft that heaves the earth about will fling a buried one out of the rock and leave it reeling.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It rarely arrives from the direction you are watching. It glides up through the floor or out of a wall, opens with a shove to break your line and put men down, then works methodically along your flank with slams, taking blows without complaint and following you at a walking pace forever. It will pull a building down over you if that serves. It fights worst when you take to a boat or the air, and it knows it — so it will bring the roof down instead.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Watch the dust in a still room. It cannot glide without shifting a little grit.
• Take to a boat, a roof, or a rope. It has no answer to water and no answer to the air.
• Never fight one indoors. It does not need to hit you if it can drop the ceiling.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have bargained with one in a mine and found it honest and desperately slow. Speak plainly, speak short, promise one thing only. It will hold you to your word to the letter, and if you cheat it, it will come up through your bedroom floor a season later, patient as a mountain.

Medium — AC 18 (touch 9), slam +8 melee (1d8+7), Str 21, CR 3. Large — AC 18 (touch 8), 2 slams +12 melee (2d8+7), Str 25, CR 5. Huge — AC 18 (touch 7), 2 slams +19 melee (2d10+9), Str 29, CR 7. Greater — AC 20 (touch 7), 2 slams +23 melee (2d10+10), Str 31, CR 9. Elder — AC 22 (touch 7), 2 slams +27 melee (2d10+11/19–20), Str 33, CR 11. Speed is 20 ft. up to Large and 30 ft. for Huge and above. Damage reduction begins at Large (5/—) and rises to 10/— for greater and elder. Every size has earth glide and Dex 8. Heights run 4 ft. (Small) to 40 ft. (elder), weights 80 lb. to 60,000 lb. When summoned to the Material Plane an earth elemental consists of whatever dirt, stone, precious metal and gems it was conjured from. Earth elementals speak Terran but rarely choose to do so.

Earth Mastery (Ex): An earth elemental gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls if both it and its foe are touching the ground. If an opponent is airborne or waterborne, the elemental takes a –4 penalty on attack and damage rolls. (These modifiers are not included in the statistics block.)

Push (Ex): An earth elemental can start a bull rush maneuver without provoking an attack of opportunity. The combat modifiers given in Earth Mastery, above, also apply to the elemental's opposed Strength checks.

Earth Glide (Ex): An earth elemental can glide through stone, dirt, or almost any other sort of earth except metal as easily as a fish swims through water. Its burrowing leaves behind no tunnel or hole, nor does it create any ripple or other sign of its presence. A move earth spell cast on an area containing a burrowing earth elemental flings the elemental back 30 feet, stunning the creature for 1 round unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Fortitude save.

Combat: Though an earth elemental moves slowly, it is a relentless opponent. It can travel through solid ground or stone as easily as humans walk on the earth's surface. It cannot swim, however, and must either walk around a body of water or go through the ground under it. An earth elemental can move along the bottom of a body of water but prefers not to.

Elemental Traits: An elemental is a being composed of one of the four classical elements. Elementals have darkvision out to 60 feet and immunity to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning. They are not subject to critical hits or flanking. Unlike most other living creatures, an elemental does not have a dual nature — its soul and body form one unit, so when an elemental is slain no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate and resurrection, do not work on an elemental; it takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle or true resurrection, to restore it to life. Elementals are proficient with natural weapons only, unless generally humanoid in form, and are not proficient with armor unless described as wearing it. Elementals do not eat, sleep or breathe.

lore.summary: A flame that has learned to run. Fire elementals come from a plane that is nothing but burning, and they take open joy in reducing our world to ash — the only one of the four kin I would call gleeful. Called up in braziers by men who wanted a siege ended, and left behind in the ruin afterwards, which is how most folk meet one.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A candle-flame shape the height of a child at the least; the great ones stand taller than a barn and light a whole valley.
Durability: Weightless as smoke and dreadfully hard to put down; the larger it burns, the less a plain weapon means to it.
Defenses: Fire cannot harm it — not torch, not lamp oil, not another of its own kind. No vitals, no sleep, no venom, no palsy, and no reward for flanking.
Speed: The quickest thing in the elemental kin on its feet; it crosses a courtyard while you are drawing breath, and the eldest are quicker still.
Might: Its touch is both a blow and a brand: what it strikes catches light and keeps burning after it has moved on. Everything flammable it passes goes up in its wake.
Mind: Simple and savage. It speaks the tongue of flame if it troubles to speak at all, and mostly it does not trouble.
Disposition: Eager. It does not stalk or circle; it comes straight at you and takes pleasure in the burning.
Bane: Cold undoes it faster than any blade. Water is a wall: it cannot set foot in a pond, a moat or a flooded cellar, and must go round or leap over. And never strike it with fist or claw — the hand that touches it catches alight.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It charges. There is no cunning in it and no need for any — it closes at a sprint, lashes with burning limbs, and leaves men rolling on the ground beating out their own clothes while it turns to the next. Its favourite ground is a granary, a barn, a ship, anywhere the fire will do the killing for it. Bring it to a river or a cellar with a foot of water in it and it is suddenly a very stupid creature indeed.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Frost, ice, a winter charm — anything cold. It feels that more than steel.
• Fight with your back to water. It cannot follow you in, and a ditch is as good as a wall.
• Drop the burning man and roll him. He can smother it with one good effort, but only if someone makes him stop running.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I have had perhaps three words out of one, and two of them were laughter. They will hear an offer of dry timber and a free hand with it; they will not hear mercy. If it is between you and a village, do not talk. Talk works better with the fool who lit the brazier.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Initiative: +9
Speed: 50 ft. (10 squares)
Armor Class: 18 (–1 size, +5 Dex, +4 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+12
Attack: Slam +10 melee (2d6+2 plus 2d6 fire)
Full Attack: 2 slams +10 melee (2d6+2 plus 2d6 fire)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Burn
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/—, darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits, immunity to fire, vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +5, Ref +11, Will +2
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 21, Con 16, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 11
Skills: Listen +5, Spot +6
Feats: Dodge, Improved Initiative(B), Mobility, Spring Attack, Weapon Finesse(B)
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Sizes (Small to Elder): The block above is the Large fire elemental. The family runs: Small — AC 15 (touch 12), slam +3 melee (1d4 plus 1d4 fire), Str 10, CR 1. Medium — AC 16 (touch 13), slam +6 melee (1d6+1 plus 1d6 fire), Str 12, CR 3. Large — AC 18 (touch 14), 2 slams +10 melee (2d6+2 plus 2d6 fire), Str 14, CR 5. Huge — AC 19 (touch 15), 2 slams +17 melee (2d8+4 plus 2d8 fire), Str 18, CR 7. Greater — AC 24 (touch 16), 2 slams +22 melee (2d8+5 plus 2d8 fire), Str 20, CR 9. Elder — AC 25 (touch 17), 2 slams +26 melee (2d8+6 plus 2d8 fire), Str 22, CR 11. Speed is 50 ft. up to Large and 60 ft. for Huge and above. Damage reduction begins at Large (5/—) and rises to 10/— for greater and elder. Every size is immune to fire and vulnerable to cold. Burn save DC by size: Small 11, Medium 14, Large 17, Huge 22, greater 24, elder 26. Heights run 4 ft. (Small) to 40 ft. (elder) at 1 to 12 pounds. Fire elementals speak Ignan, though they rarely choose to do so.

Burn (Ex): A fire elemental's slam attack deals bludgeoning damage plus fire damage from the elemental's flaming body. Those hit by the slam attack must also succeed on a Reflex save or catch on fire; the flame burns for 1d4 rounds. The save DC varies with the elemental's size (DC 17 for a Large elemental) and is Constitution-based. A burning creature can take a move action to put out the flame. Creatures hitting a fire elemental with natural weapons or unarmed attacks take fire damage as though hit by the elemental's attack, and also catch on fire unless they succeed on a Reflex save.

Water Barrier: A fire elemental cannot enter water or any other nonflammable liquid. A body of water is an impassable barrier unless the fire elemental can step or jump over it.

Combat: A fire elemental is a fierce opponent that attacks its enemies directly and savagely. It takes joy in burning the creatures and objects of the Material Plane to ashes.

Elemental Traits: An elemental is a being composed of one of the four classical elements. Elementals have darkvision out to 60 feet and immunity to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning. They are not subject to critical hits or flanking. Unlike most other living creatures, an elemental does not have a dual nature — its soul and body form one unit, so when an elemental is slain no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate and resurrection, do not work on an elemental; it takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle or true resurrection, to restore it to life. Elementals are proficient with natural weapons only, unless generally humanoid in form, and are not proficient with armor unless described as wearing it. Elementals do not eat, sleep or breathe.

lore.summary: A wave that turns and looks at you. Water elementals are called out of the nearest pool, cistern or sea and stay tethered to it, so they haunt harbours, mill-races and ships' wakes. They fight by vanishing under the surface and swelling up behind a man's back, and they can roll a fishing boat over as easily as you would tip a cup.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A knee-high surge at the least; the great ones rear taller than a barn and come with the weight of a millpond behind them.
Durability: It has no shape to break. Blows go through it and close again, and the greater ones scarcely notice a common weapon.
Defenses: Nothing to pierce and nothing to poison; it does not sleep, does not stun, cannot be palsied, and has no back for a knife.
Speed: In water it outruns anything with fins. Ashore it lumbers, and the eldest lumber only a little faster.
Might: Slams with the whole weight of a wave, and the vortex: beneath the surface it becomes a whirlpool, drags swimmers down into the turning and holds them there in a blinding churn of silt.
Mind: Slow and old-feeling. It speaks the tongue of the deep water, understands what it is told, and answers about as often as the sea does.
Disposition: Sullen rather than cruel. It resents being called from its pool and takes that out on whoever is nearest the shore.
Bane: Bring it onto dry land — it fights poorly the moment either of you is standing on the ground, and it cannot stray far from the water it was drawn from. Stay on the bank and it will have to come to you, and it can raise no whirlpool with its head above the surface.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights from below. It sinks, moves, and rises behind the line; in open water it becomes a whirlpool, takes the swimmers, and holds them under in a cloud of stirred silt where no man can see his own hands. Against boats it does not bother with the crew at all — it overturns the small craft, stops the middling ones dead in the water and leaves the great ones wallowing. Its touch snuffs out lanterns and campfires, and it can quench even a conjured flame it lays a hand on.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never argue with one while wading. Get your boots on dry ground first.
• Find the pool it was called from. It cannot follow you past a certain distance from that water — walk inland and it must let you go.
• It will put out every light you own with a touch. Carry something that burns without a flame.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: I sat on a jetty and talked to one for the better part of an evening. It wanted the man who called it, and it wanted to be let back into the bay. Stay on dry stone while you speak — it is honest enough, but it is also very close to a great deal of water, and it does not always wait for you to finish.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Elemental (Water, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +2
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), swim 90 ft.
Armor Class: 20 (–1 size, +2 Dex, +9 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 18
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+15
Attack: Slam +10 melee (2d8+5)
Full Attack: 2 slams +10 melee (2d8+5)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Water mastery, drench, vortex
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/—, darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits
Saves: Fort +10, Ref +4, Will +2
Abilities: Str 20, Dex 14, Con 19, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 11
Skills: Listen +5, Spot +6
Feats: Cleave, Great Cleave, Power Attack
Environment: Elemental Plane of Water
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 5
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9–15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Sizes (Small to Elder): The block above is the Large water elemental. The family runs: Small — AC 17 (touch 11), slam +4 melee (1d6+3), Str 14, CR 1. Medium — AC 19 (touch 11), slam +6 melee (1d8+4), Str 16, CR 3. Large — AC 20 (touch 11), 2 slams +10 melee (2d8+5), Str 20, CR 5. Huge — AC 21 (touch 12), 2 slams +17 melee (2d10+7), Str 24, CR 7. Greater — AC 22 (touch 13), 2 slams +21 melee (2d10+8), Str 26, CR 9. Elder — AC 23 (touch 14), 2 slams +25 melee (2d10+9/19–20), Str 28, CR 11. Land speed is 20 ft. up to Large and 30 ft. above, with swim 90 ft. up to Large and swim 120 ft. above. Damage reduction begins at Large (5/—) and rises to 10/— for greater and elder. Vortex save DC and damage by size: Small DC 13/1d4, Medium DC 15/1d6, Large DC 19/2d6, Huge DC 25/2d8, greater DC 28/2d8, elder DC 31/2d8. Heights run 4 ft. (Small) to 40 ft. (elder), weights 34 lb. to 24,000 lb. Water elementals speak Aquan but rarely choose to do so.

Water Mastery (Ex): A water elemental gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls if both it and its opponent are touching water. If the opponent or the elemental is touching the ground, the elemental takes a –4 penalty on attack and damage rolls. (These modifiers are not included in the statistics block.) A water elemental can be a serious threat to a ship that crosses its path: it can easily overturn small craft (5 feet of length per level of the elemental) and stop larger vessels (10 feet of length per level). Even large ships (20 feet of length per level) can be slowed to half speed.

Drench (Ex): The elemental's touch puts out torches, campfires, exposed lanterns and other open flames of nonmagical origin if these are of Large size or smaller. The creature can dispel magical fire it touches as dispel magic (caster level equals the elemental's level).

Vortex (Su): The elemental can transform itself into a whirlpool once every 10 minutes, provided it is underwater, and remain in that form for up to 1 round for every 2 levels it possesses. In vortex form it can move through the water or along the bottom at its swim speed. The vortex is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 30 feet wide at the top, and 10 feet or more tall depending on the elemental's size; the elemental controls the exact height, but it must be at least 10 feet. Its movement while in vortex form does not provoke attacks of opportunity, even if it enters the space another creature occupies. Another creature might be caught in the vortex if it touches or enters it, or if the elemental moves into or through the creature's space. Creatures one or more size categories smaller than the elemental may take damage when caught (Large: 2d6, DC 19) and may be swept up by it. An affected creature must succeed on a Reflex save on contact or take the indicated damage, and must also succeed on a second Reflex save or be picked up bodily and held suspended in the powerful currents, automatically taking damage each round. An affected creature is allowed a Reflex save each round to escape; it still takes damage but can leave if the save succeeds. The save DC varies with the elemental's size and is Strength-based. Trapped creatures cannot move except to go where the elemental carries them or to escape. They can otherwise act normally, but must make a Concentration check (DC 10 + spell level) to cast a spell, and take a –4 penalty to Dexterity and a –2 penalty on attack rolls. The elemental can hold only as many creatures as will fit inside the vortex's volume, and can eject any carried creature whenever it wishes; a summoned elemental always ejects trapped creatures before returning to its home plane. If the vortex's base touches the bottom it creates a swirling cloud of debris centred on the elemental, with a diameter equal to half the vortex's height, that obscures all vision including darkvision beyond 5 feet — creatures 5 feet away have concealment, those farther away total concealment — and those caught in the cloud must make a Concentration check (DC 15 + spell level) to cast a spell. An elemental in vortex form cannot make slam attacks and does not threaten the area around it.

Range from Water: A water elemental can't venture more than 180 feet from the body of water from which it was conjured.

Skills: A water elemental has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Combat: A water elemental prefers to fight in a large body of water where it can disappear beneath the waves and suddenly swell up behind its opponents.

Elemental Traits: An elemental is a being composed of one of the four classical elements. Elementals have darkvision out to 60 feet and immunity to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning. They are not subject to critical hits or flanking. Unlike most other living creatures, an elemental does not have a dual nature — its soul and body form one unit, so when an elemental is slain no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate and resurrection, do not work on an elemental; it takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle or true resurrection, to restore it to life. Elementals are proficient with natural weapons only, unless generally humanoid in form, and are not proficient with armor unless described as wearing it. Elementals do not eat, sleep or breathe.

lore.summary: A squat little man of cooling lava, cracked all over with red, wrapped in a haze of heat that hurts to stand near. Magmins come from the burning plane in gangs and squads, love arson the way a magpie loves silver, and hoard whatever loot will not burn. Met in mines, forges and the smoking ruin of a barn they thought was funny.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — no higher than a child's shoulder, and heavier than a man twice its height.
Durability: A crust of stone over a furnace. Plain steel barely troubles it; you want an enchanted edge, or a great deal of patience.
Defenses: Fire means nothing to it. No vitals, no venom, no sleep, no palsy, no stunning, and no bonus for coming at its back. Worse: a metal weapon that strikes it may simply run off the haft as slag.
Speed: Brisk on its stubby legs and a fair climber — it will go up a mine gallery or a rafter to get above you.
Might: Its touch sets clothes alight and turns armour into an oven, and the burning goes on long after it lets go. Standing anywhere near it cooks you where you are.
Mind: The cleverest of the lesser elemental kin — a scheming, joking sort of wit. It speaks the tongue of flame and can hold a conversation, though it will lie in it for sport.
Disposition: Chaotic, mischievous, and delighted by fire. Not evil so much as utterly without care for what it burns down.
Bane: Cold. It cannot bear it. Beyond that: it is a coward — hurt it once and it runs, though only far enough to double back and set an ambush. Never bring your good blade; bring a stave, a spear you can lose, or something with reach.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: A gang of them scatters and comes in from the flanks, touching whatever will catch — thatch, satchels, a man's cloak — and letting the fire finish the work. Against anyone who laughs at flame they drop the burning touch and simply beat on him instead. They are not brave. Wound one and it flees, but it flees uphill to a rafter or a gallery, waits, and drops on you in the dark with its whole gang behind it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Leave the good sword in its scabbard. Metal that touches one comes away as slag.
• Anything cold, and quickly. It is braver than it looks only until it feels frost.
• Keep a spear's length from it. Standing close is a wound all on its own — no blow required.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Of all the elemental kin these are the ones who will actually talk to you — and lie, and giggle, and set your pack alight while you shake hands. Offer them something to burn that you do not want. I bought a night's peace once with a broken cart. They kept the bargain, in their fashion, and burned the cart twice.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Elemental (Fire, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (+1 size, +6 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/–1
Attack: Burning touch +4 melee touch (1d8 fire plus combustion) or slam +4 melee (1d3+3 plus combustion)
Full Attack: Burning touch +4 melee touch (1d8 fire plus combustion) or slam +4 melee (1d3+3 plus combustion)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Combustion, fiery aura
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/magic, darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits, immunity to fire, melt weapons, vulnerability to cold
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +0

Skills: Climb +4, Spot +3
Feats: Great Fortitude
Environment: Elemental Plane of Fire
Organization: Solitary, gang (2–4), or squad (6–10)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Always chaotic neutral
Treasure: Standard coins; standard goods (nonflammables only); standard items (nonflammables only)
Advancement: 3–4 levels (Small); 5–6 levels (Medium)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combustion (Ex): Anyone a magmin touches must succeed on a DC 12 Reflex save or take an extra 1d8 points of fire damage as clothes ignite or armor becomes searing hot. The damage continues for another 1d4+2 rounds after the magmin's last successful attack. Magmins can also ignite flammable materials with a touch. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Fiery Aura (Ex): Anyone within 20 feet of a magmin must succeed on a DC 12 Fortitude save or take 1d6 points of heat damage per round from the intense heat. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Melt Weapons (Ex): Any metal weapon that strikes a magmin must succeed on a DC 12 Fortitude save or melt away into slag. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Damage Reduction and Magic Weapons: A magmin has damage reduction 5/magic, so only magic weapons cut through it in full. Its own natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Immunity to Fire, Vulnerability to Cold (Ex): A magmin is immune to fire damage of every kind. It takes half again as much damage (+50%) from cold, regardless of whether a saving throw is allowed or whether the save is a success or failure.

Combat: Although small, magmins are dangerous opponents. Their touch is effective against those who lack protection or immunity from heat and flames, but if faced with opponents who have immunity to fire, magmins rely on their slam attack. In any case, magmins are not valiant fighters. They usually flee if injured, although often only far enough to set up a fiery ambush for their enemies. A typical magmin is 4 feet tall and weighs 400 pounds, and they speak Ignan.

Elemental Traits: An elemental is a being composed of one of the four classical elements. Elementals have darkvision out to 60 feet and immunity to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning. They are not subject to critical hits or flanking. Unlike most other living creatures, an elemental does not have a dual nature — its soul and body form one unit, so when an elemental is slain no soul is set loose. Spells that restore souls to their bodies, such as raise dead, reincarnate and resurrection, do not work on an elemental; it takes a different magical effect, such as limited wish, wish, miracle or true resurrection, to restore it to life. Elementals are proficient with natural weapons only, unless generally humanoid in form, and are not proficient with armor unless described as wearing it. Elementals do not eat, sleep or breathe.

lore.summary: Smoke given wings and malice. A belker comes off the Plane of Air, longer than a tall man yet lighter than the cloak on your back, and its winged shape is so demonic that half the priests who meet one report a fiend. Reclusive things, caring nothing for our doings — but wicked to the marrow, and met where hot vents breathe in the deep dark.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large in span, and nearly nothing in weight — you could carry one under an arm if it would let you.
Durability: Frail for its reach. It survives by being smoke, not by being tough.
Defenses: Elemental through and through: venom, sleep, palsy and stunning slide off it, it has no vitals to seek, and two of you flanking it gains nothing. Its true guard is the smoke shape, in which steel finds nothing to bite.
Speed: Poor afoot; in the air it is perfect, and faster still once it goes to vapour.
Might: Beating wings, a bite and raking claws when solid — but its proper weapon is to become smoke, roll over you, and be breathed in.
Mind: Dull for a thing that ambushes. Cunning enough to drop on you from a flue, too slow for any real scheme. It speaks the tongue of air and little else.
Disposition: Reclusive; it wants nothing from you and will often let you pass. But it is evil, and an evil thing that finds you alone in a still shaft will kill you for the pleasure of it.
Bane: It cannot hold the smoke shape all day. Endure the vapour and it must come solid again, and solid it is fragile — one good blow ends it. Fight in open wind, never in a closed shaft, and if it gets inside you, cough hard and keep coughing.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits high in the dark and comes down as smoke, spreading over one of you without giving you the chance to strike as it settles. Breathe and you have swallowed part of it; the smoke hardens into a claw inside your chest and tears at your organs until you hack it out. Those who keep their lungs clean it fights the plain way — two wings, bite and claws, going back to vapour whenever the fight turns against it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never take one in a closed shaft. Give yourself sky, a doorway, or at least a draught.
• When it goes to vapour, hold your breath and back off. Breathe it and you are the battlefield.
• It weighs less than your cloak. Catch it solid, hit it once properly, and it is finished.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None. I tried once in the vent-caves under the Ash Reach — I had the words of the air-tongue and it had my breath. It understood me well enough. It came anyway. It wants nothing you can offer and fears nothing you can keep back. Strike first, and strike it while it is solid.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Elemental (Air, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 50 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 22 (-1 size, +5 Dex, +8 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+11
Attack: Wing +9 melee (1d6+2)
Full Attack: 2 wings +9 melee (1d6+2) and bite +7 melee (1d4+1) and 2 claws +7 melee (1d3+1)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Smoke claws
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits, smoke form
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +10, Will +2
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 21, Con 13, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 11
Skills: Listen +7, Move Silently +9, Spot +7
Feats: Alertness, Multiattack, Weapon Finesse
Environment: Elemental Plane of Air
Organization: Solitary, pair, or clutch (3-4)
Challenge Rating: 6
Alignment: Usually neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: 8-10 levels (Large); 11-21 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: In most cases, a belker fights with its nasty claws and painful bite. It is about 7 feet long and weighs about 8 pounds, being composed almost entirely of smoke. Belkers speak Auran.

Smoke Claws (Ex): A belker in smoke form can engulf opponents by moving on top of them. It fills the air around one Medium or smaller opponent without provoking an attack of opportunity. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Fortitude save or inhale part of the creature. The save DC is Constitution-based. Smoke inside the victim solidifies into a claw and begins to rip at the surrounding organs, dealing 3d4 points of damage per round. An affected creature can attempt another Fortitude save each subsequent round to cough out the semivaporous menace.

Smoke Form (Su): Most of the time a belker is more or less solid, but at will it can assume smoke form. It can switch forms once per round as a free action and can spend up to 20 rounds per day in smoke form. A belker in smoke form can fly at a speed of 50 feet (perfect). The ability is otherwise similar to a gaseous form spell (caster level 7th).

Elemental Traits (Ex): An elemental has no discernible anatomy and no vital organs, so it is immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning, and it cannot be sneak attacked or struck in the vitals. It is not subject to flanking. It cannot be raised or resurrected — only a wish, miracle or true resurrection will restore one. It has darkvision 60 ft. and does not eat, breathe or sleep. Its body is its whole self: destroy it and nothing remains to bury.

Skills: Belkers have a +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks.

lore.summary: Nobody meets an invisible stalker by accident. Some wizard says a name, and a thing of roiling vapour out of the Plane of Air is sent to find one particular person, though that person flees a thousand leagues. It cannot lose a trail, does not tire, and obeys only the one who summoned it — while resenting the errand with all the wit it has.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large, though you will never see it so. Sight-magic gives a dim outline; only true seeing shows the roiling cloud of vapour it is.
Durability: Sturdy, and worse than sturdy: away from its own plane you cannot truly kill it. Beat it apart and it simply goes home.
Defenses: Unseen at all times, which is defence enough. Beyond that, the elemental grants: no venom, no sleep, no palsy, no stunning, no vitals to find, no gain from surrounding it.
Speed: Quick afoot and flies with perfect command. It will not be outrun and it will not be outlasted.
Might: It makes a weapon of the air itself, a sudden battering blast that hammers one chosen target and then another blast, and another.
Mind: As clever as a man, and sour with it. It speaks only the tongue of air but understands common speech well enough to know when it has been mocked.
Disposition: It holds no grudge of its own. It goes where it is sent, serves nobody but the summoner, and a long errand or a loosely worded one it will twist to the letter while gutting the intent.
Bane: Its master's wording, and its master's throat. Break the summoner and the hunt ends. Failing that it is unseen, not weightless — flour, fine ash, spilled meal or still water will show you where it stands.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It opens without warning on whoever it was sent for and ignores everyone else unless they get in the road. Blast after blast of hammering wind on the one target, from a new quarter each time, never closing to grapple, never staying where the last blow came from. It does not gloat, does not pause, and does not stop when the rest of your party runs.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Throw flour, ash or fine meal. You still cannot see it — but you can see where it is not.
• Ask it aloud what it was told to do. Word-play is its one joy; it may hand you the loophole itself.
• Off the Plane of Air you cannot kill it, only send it home. So kill the summoner instead.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk, and talk fast — it has wits and it loathes its work. Twice I bought my life by asking it, aloud, exactly what it had been told to do; the second time it answered at length and I found the crack in the wording. But it lies happily to keep the letter of its orders, and it strikes while you are still being courteous.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Elemental (Air, Extraplanar)
Initiative: +8
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), fly 30 ft. (perfect)
Armor Class: 17 (-1 size, +4 Dex, +4 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+14
Attack: Slam +10 melee (2d6+4)
Full Attack: 2 slams +10 melee (2d6+4)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits, natural invisibility, improved tracking
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +10, Will +4
Abilities: Str 18, Dex 19, Con 14, Int 14, Wis 15, Cha 11
Skills: Listen +13, Move Silently +15, Search +13, Spot +13, Survival +2 (+4 following tracks)
Feats: Combat Reflexes, Improved Initiative, Weapon Focus (slam)
Environment: Elemental Plane of Air
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 7
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9-12 levels (Large); 13-24 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: An invisible stalker attacks by using the air itself as a weapon. It creates a sudden, intense blast of wind that pounds a single target on the same plane as the creature. An invisible stalker can be destroyed only while it is on the Elemental Plane of Air; when performing a task elsewhere it automatically returns to its home plane the moment it takes damage enough to unmake it.

Summoning and Service: Invisible stalkers are native to the Elemental Plane of Air and sometimes serve wizards and sorcerers who summon them for specific tasks. A summoned stalker undertakes whatever its summoner commands, even if the task sends it hundreds or thousands of miles away, and it follows that command until the task is complete, obeying only the summoner. However, it resents protracted missions or complex tasks and seeks to pervert its instructions accordingly.

Natural Invisibility (Su): This ability is constant, allowing a stalker to remain invisible even when attacking. The ability is inherent and is not subject to the invisibility purge spell. Invisible stalkers have an amorphous form: a see invisibility spell shows only a dim outline of a cloud, while a true seeing spell reveals a roiling cloud of vapor.

Improved Tracking (Ex): An invisible stalker is a consummate tracker and makes Spot checks instead of the usual Survival checks to trace a creature's passage.

Elemental Traits (Ex): An elemental has no discernible anatomy and no vital organs, so it is immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning, and it cannot be sneak attacked or struck in the vitals. It is not subject to flanking. It cannot be raised or resurrected — only a wish, miracle or true resurrection will restore one. It has darkvision 60 ft. and does not eat, breathe or sleep. Its body is its whole self: destroy it and nothing remains to bury.

Languages: These creatures speak only Auran but can understand Common.

lore.summary: A worm of earth and fire, thick as a man's thigh and no longer than he is tall, hot enough to swim through solid rock. It leaves smooth round tunnels behind it, glazed and still warm, and that is generally how you learn one is near. It bores because boring is what it is for; it attacks because something woke it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A stubby blunt-nosed worm no longer than a tall man, and heavy as a small anvil.
Durability: Slag-hard hide, well armoured for its bulk, but there is not much of it to break.
Defenses: Fire cannot touch it, nor venom, sleep, palsy or stunning; it has no vitals to pierce and no flank to turn. Cold, though, hurts it far worse than it hurts most things.
Speed: Unhurried on open ground — but it swims through stone, and it feels your footfalls through the rock long before you feel its heat.
Might: Its whole body is the weapon: a searing slam that sets hair, cloth and oil alight. Even brushing against it scalds to the bone.
Mind: Dim. It bores, it eats stone, it lashes at whatever disturbs it. There is a scrap of animal shrewdness there and nothing more.
Disposition: Not malicious, merely short-tempered and made of fire. Disturbed, its first instinct is to attack; it does not stalk, hoard, or bargain.
Bane: Cold in any form — a frost-blade, a flask of rime, a mountain stream. And it announces itself: glazed round tunnels and warm rock mean one is boring nearby, so you need never be surprised by one.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It coils and launches itself like a loosed spring, bursting straight out of a wall at the nearest warm body without needing a run-up. Then it slams and slams again, and its heat catches you burning; a man on fire must stop everything to beat out the flames, and the worm knows to keep hitting while he does. Break off and it dives back into the rock and comes at you from another face.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold. Anything cold. That is the whole of the answer.
• Do not touch it, grapple it, or try to pin it. Merely being touched by the thing burns you.
• Glazed round tunnels and warm stone: one is at work nearby. Take another passage and save your frost.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: None to be had. Too little mind for words, too much heat for patience. I hailed one in the fire-tongue out of courtesy in the Kaldmere workings; it came out of the wall at my knees before I finished the sentence. Give it distance or give it frost — it understands only the second.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:

Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., elemental traits, immunity to fire, tremorsense 60 ft., vulnerability to cold

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A thoqqua is about 1 foot in diameter and 4 to 5 feet long, and weighs about 200 pounds. When one is disturbed, its first instinct is to attack. Its favored tactic is to spring directly at a foe, either by bursting out of the rock or by coiling up its body and launching itself like a spring. (Treat this as a charge, even though the thoqqua does not need to move 10 feet before attacking.)

Heat (Ex): Merely touching or being touched by a thoqqua automatically deals 2d6 fire damage.

Burn (Ex): When a thoqqua hits with its slam attack, the opponent must succeed on a DC 12 Reflex save or catch fire. The save DC is Constitution-based. The flame burns for 1d4 rounds if not extinguished sooner. A burning creature can use a full-round action to put out the flame.

Burrow (Ex): A thoqqua bores through earth and stone at a speed of 20 feet, its molten body melting a tunnel behind it, and it senses everything in contact with the ground within 60 feet by tremorsense.

Elemental Traits (Ex): An elemental has no discernible anatomy and no vital organs, so it is immune to poison, sleep effects, paralysis and stunning, and it cannot be sneak attacked or struck in the vitals. It is not subject to flanking. It cannot be raised or resurrected — only a wish, miracle or true resurrection will restore one. It has darkvision 60 ft. and does not eat, breathe or sleep. Its body is its whole self: destroy it and nothing remains to bury. A thoqqua is further immune to fire and vulnerable to cold, taking half again as much damage (+50%) from cold regardless of whether a save is allowed or the save succeeds.

lore.summary: Slim, comely water-folk of lakes and quiet pools: pale green scaled skin, dark green hair strung with shells and pearl, wraps woven of coloured weed. They keep to their own water and want nothing beyond it. Not cruel — but fey, and a nixie who wants a weir mended will simply take a passing traveller's will and set him to the work.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — child-height, slight, and lighter than she looks.
Durability: Slight. She is not built to be struck, and does not intend to be.
Defenses: Cold iron cuts her true; common steel bites shallow. Spells slide off her more often than they land. In her own water she is next to invisible among the reeds and shadows.
Speed: Ordinary on land, and she dislikes being there. In water she is swift, tireless, and can hold her line at a run.
Might: A short sword and a light crossbow, both made small. Her real weapon is her voice.
Mind: Bright, sociable, quick with a bargain and quicker with a flattery. She speaks the water-tongue and the fey-tongue, and often enough the common speech besides.
Disposition: Neither good nor wicked. She guards her lake, sings, crafts, keeps the company of water beasts, and takes labourers when labour is wanted — then walks them politely out of the valley when she is done.
Bane: Cold iron, and dry ground. Draw her out of the water and she loses her cover and her speed at a stroke. But guard your mind first: the charm is the whole fight, and everything after it is a formality.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She would very much rather not. Faced with steel she sings her charm at the biggest of you and turns him on his fellows, or simply walks him away out of the fight; the rest of the band looses little bolts from the reeds and slips under the surface between shots. Press them hard and they go to deep water, where you will not follow and they can wait longer than you can.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Cold iron on your belt, never in your hand. Showing it is an insult, and she counts insults.
• The charm holds a day and a night, no longer. If a friend wanders off glassy-eyed, follow at a distance and wait — she hands them back.
• Bring worked metal or good stone. They keep no coin at all, and they do love a well-made thing.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Wholly open, and worth every minute. I have taken supper on a nixie's raft and traded a copper mirror for safe passage the length of a flooded valley. Speak first, praise the water, offer worked metal or stone. Refuse nothing outright, never swim armed, and do not lie — she reads a liar at once.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat, if handled well

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Fey (Aquatic)
Initiative: +3
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), swim 30 ft.
Armor Class: 14 (+1 size, +3 Dex), touch 14, flat-footed 11
Base Attack/Grapple: +0/-6
Attack: Short sword +4 melee (1d4-2/19-20) or light crossbow +4 ranged (1d6/19-20)
Full Attack: Short sword +4 melee (1d4-2/19-20) or light crossbow +4 ranged (1d6/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Charm person
Special Qualities: Amphibious, damage reduction 5/cold iron, low-light vision, spell resistance 16, water breathing, wild empathy
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +5, Will +3
Abilities: Str 7, Dex 16, Con 11, Int 12, Wis 13, Cha 18
Skills: Bluff +8, Craft (any one) +5, Escape Artist +6, Handle Animal +8, Hide +7*, Listen +8, Perform (sing) +7, Search +3, Sense Motive +5, Spot +8, Swim +6
Feats: Alertness, Dodge(B), Weapon Finesse(B)
Environment: Temperate aquatic
Organization: Gang (2-4), band (6-11), or tribe (20-80)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: No coins; 50% goods (metal or stone only); 50% items (no scrolls)
Advancement: 2-3 levels (Small)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Nixies rely on their charm person ability to deter enemies, entering combat only to protect themselves and their territory. A nixie stands about 4 feet tall and weighs about 45 pounds; most are slim and comely, with lightly scaled, pale green skin and dark green hair. Nixies prefer not to leave their lakes. They speak Aquan and Sylvan, and some also speak Common. Level adjustment +3.

Charm Person (Sp): A nixie can use charm person three times per day as the spell (caster level 4th). Those affected must succeed on a DC 15 Will save or be charmed for 24 hours. Most charmed creatures are used to perform heavy labor, guard duty, and other onerous tasks for the nixie community. Shortly before the effect wears off, the nixie escorts the charmed creature away and orders it to keep walking. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Amphibious (Ex): Although nixies are aquatic, they can survive indefinitely on land.

Water Breathing (Sp): Once per day a nixie can use water breathing as the spell (caster level 12th). Nixies usually bestow this effect on those they have charmed.

Wild Empathy (Ex): This ability works like the druid's wild empathy class feature, except that a nixie has a +6 racial bonus on the check.

Damage Reduction and Spell Resistance: A nixie ignores the first 5 points of damage from any weapon that is not cold iron, and has spell resistance 16.

Skills: A nixie has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line. *Nixies have a +5 racial bonus on Hide checks when in the water.

lore.summary: Bones raised and set walking. It is not one creature but a thing done to a corpse, and it can be done to anything with a spine. Most are men in the rot of the armour they died in; I have also fought a wolf's frame, an owlbear's, and once the picked ribs of something winged that could no longer use the wings. Wherever a necromancer sets up, a graveyard grows short of tenants.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Whatever it was in life. The common sort is a man's height in rusted mail; but troll, ettin and cloud giant have all been walked on bare bone, and worse things than those.
Durability: As sturdy as the frame it was raised from. A farmhand's bones fall to one good stroke; a giant's take a very great deal of breaking.
Defenses: It is bare bone — blade and arrow pass through and find nothing worth cutting. Cold does not touch it at all, nor venom, nor disease, nor fear, nor sleep, nor any trick that works upon a living mind, for it has none to work upon.
Speed: As the base creature was in life, save that a winged one cannot fly on bone wings alone. Quick to act, always: the raising leaves them oddly fast off the mark.
Might: Whatever weapon it carried in life, or a raking claw from each hand. The hands of a big beast strike very hard, and a raised beast keeps every scrap of the strength it had.
Mind: None whatever. It draws no conclusion, takes no initiative, learns nothing, and must be given orders simple enough for a child to follow.
Disposition: It does exactly as it was told and attacks until it is broken apart. It will not flee, will not treat, will not be frightened or fooled, and will not stop at nightfall or at the boundary of its master's land.
Bane: Bludgeoning and holy word. A hammer, a mace, a stave or a good stone does what a sword will not, and any priest worth the name will scatter or unmake a whole rank at once. Above all, find the one who raised them — the bones are only the hand.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes straight on, in silence, and keeps coming. No feint, no circling, no retreat, no mercy and no self-preservation; a rank of them will walk into a fire if that is where the order points them. They are dangerous in number, in a corridor, or when the frame under the bone was something monstrous to begin with — and their master will always place them where they cannot be gone around.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bring a hammer, not your good sword. Bone laughs at an edge and blunts it besides.
• Any priest worth his salt will scatter a rank with a raised holy symbol. Bring one, or bring twice the muscle.
• Read the frame, not the skull. A raised owlbear or troll wears the same bare ribs as a ploughman and hits like a falling tree.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing in there to speak to. I have tried in six tongues out of sheer stubbornness and got the same reply each time — a scimitar, at the same speed, from the same empty face. Save your breath for the necromancer behind it. He, at least, can be reasoned with, bought, or hanged.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe, met singly

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead (Human Warrior Skeleton — reference block)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+1 Dex, +2 natural, +2 heavy steel shield), touch 11, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +0/+1
Attack: Scimitar +1 melee (1d6+1/18-20) or claw +1 melee (1d4+1)
Full Attack: Scimitar +1 melee (1d6+1/18-20) or 2 claws +1 melee (1d4+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Damage reduction 5/bludgeoning, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to cold, undead traits
Saves: Fort +0, Ref +1, Will +2
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 13, Con —, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 1
Skills: — (a skeleton has no skills)
Feats: Improved Initiative
Environment: Temperate plains (any, usually as the base creature)
Organization: Any
Challenge Rating: 1/3
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: — (as the base creature)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Creating a Skeleton: "Skeleton" is an acquired template that can be added to any corporeal creature (other than an undead) that has a skeletal system — the base creature. The creature's type changes to undead; it retains any subtype except alignment subtypes and subtypes that indicate kind, and does not gain the augmented subtype. It uses all the base creature's statistics and special abilities except as noted. Any levels gained from character classes are stripped away (to a minimum of one), and the remaining levels become far frailer, being rolled on d12s; a creature of more than twenty levels cannot be made into a skeleton by the animate dead spell. Skeletons are the animated bones of the dead, mindless automatons that obey the orders of their evil masters, seldom garbed in more than the rotting remnants of what they wore when slain. A skeleton does only what it is ordered to do, can draw no conclusions of its own and takes no initiative, so its instructions must always be simple. It attacks until destroyed.

Damage Reduction 5/Bludgeoning (Ex): A skeleton lacks flesh and internal organs, so piercing and slashing weapons find little to bite on: it ignores the first 5 points of damage from any attack that is not a bludgeoning one. Maces, hammers, staves and clubs are the right tools; swords and arrows are close to useless.

Immunity to Cold (Ex): Skeletons are not affected by cold.

Undead Traits (Ex): A skeleton has no Constitution score and no mind at all. It is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns and morale effects), and to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless that effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, energy drain, or damage to its Strength, Dexterity or Constitution, and it cannot be fatigued or exhausted. Negative energy heals it and positive energy sears it. It is never at risk from massive damage, and when battered down it is destroyed outright rather than falling unconscious. It has darkvision 60 ft., does not breathe, eat or sleep, and cannot be raised or resurrected — only a true resurrection or a resurrection cast on the original remains restores the base creature.

Improved Initiative: A skeleton loses every feat of the base creature and gains Improved Initiative, for a +4 bonus on initiative checks. Even the slowest creature in life becomes a quick starter in death.

Template Adjustments: Natural armor changes with size: +0 for Tiny or smaller, +1 Small, +2 Medium or Large, +3 Huge, +6 Gargantuan, +10 Colossal. Base attack bonus becomes half the creature's remaining levels. A skeleton keeps all the natural weapons, manufactured weapon attacks and weapon proficiencies of the base creature except those that cannot work without flesh, and a creature with hands gains one claw attack per hand, each striking at its full attack bonus. Claw damage by size: 1 for Diminutive or Fine, 1d2 Tiny, 1d3 Small, 1d4 Medium, 1d6 Large, 1d8 Huge, 2d6 Gargantuan, 2d8 Colossal (use the skeleton claw damage only if it is better than the base creature's). A skeleton retains none of the base creature's special attacks and loses most of its special qualities, keeping only extraordinary qualities that improve its melee or ranged attacks. Base saves become Fort +1/3 and Ref +1/3 per level and Will +1/2 per level plus 2. Dexterity increases by +2, Wisdom becomes 10 and Charisma becomes 1. Winged skeletons cannot use their wings to fly, though a base creature that flew magically still can.

Challenge Rating by Power: A skeleton's Challenge Rating rises with the power of the bones raised: half a level, CR 1/6; one level, CR 1/3; two to three levels, CR 1; four to five, CR 2; six to seven, CR 3; eight to nine, CR 4; ten to eleven, CR 5; twelve to fourteen, CR 6; fifteen to seventeen, CR 7; eighteen to twenty, CR 8. Treasure is always none and alignment always neutral evil, whatever the creature was in life.

Sample Skeletons: Wolf Skeleton: Medium Undead, CR 1; speed 50 ft.; bite +2 melee (1d6+1). Owlbear Skeleton: Large Undead, CR 2; 2 claws +6 melee (1d6+5) and bite +1 melee (1d8+2). Troll Skeleton: Large Undead, CR 3; 2 claws +8 melee (1d6+6) and bite +3 melee (1d6+3). Chimera Skeleton: Large Undead, CR 4; bite +7 melee (2d6+4) and bite +7 melee (1d8+4) and gore +7 melee (1d8+4) and 2 claws +2 melee (1d6+2). Ettin Skeleton: Large Undead, CR 5; 2 morningstars +10 melee (2d6+6) or 2 claws +10 melee (1d6+6) or 2 javelins +4 ranged (1d8+6), with superior two-weapon fighting. Advanced Megaraptor Skeleton: Huge Undead, CR 6; speed 60 ft.; talons +9 melee (2d8+5) and 2 claws +4 melee (1d8+2) and bite +4 melee (2d6+2). Cloud Giant Skeleton: Huge Undead, CR 7; Gargantuan morningstar +18/+13 melee (4d6+18) or 2 claws +18 melee (1d8+12) or rock +8 ranged (2d8+12), with oversize weapon. Young Adult Red Dragon Skeleton: Huge Undead (Fire), CR 8; bite +17 melee (2d8+10) and 2 claws +12 melee (2d6+5) and 2 wings +12 melee (1d8+5) and tail slap +12 melee (2d6+15); immune to cold and fire. Every one of them carries the same template traits: damage reduction 5/bludgeoning, darkvision 60 ft., immunity to cold, undead traits and Improved Initiative.

lore.summary: Marsh-folk of green, grey and brown scale, taller than a man and heavier, with a long balancing tail and a hide that turns a blade on its own. They hold their reed-and-mud villages by right of ancestry, hunt the shallows, and drown what trespasses. Met in temperate fens, where the water is theirs and the footing is not yours.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Taller than a man and heavier, with a tail near as long as its legs to steady it in the mud.
Durability: Hardy folk. One will stand up to more than a farmhand and keep wading.
Defenses: Scaled hide that serves as armour on its own, and most carry a great shield besides.
Speed: Even afoot; swift and tireless swimming, and able to hold its breath a long while beneath.
Might: Strong arms and a warrior's reach — claws, jaws and a club in the same breath, or a javelin thrown across the water.
Mind: Simple, not stupid. They keep custom, set snares, and remember a wrong for a generation.
Disposition: Neutral folk, neither cruel nor kind. Territorial above all, and murderous to anything that wanders into their claim.
Bane: Draw them onto dry, firm ground. In the reeds their ambushes work and their tails do half the fighting; on hard land the great shield is only weight, and it drags a swimmer down.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They come head-on and all at once, no ranks and no signal, shoving hard to put you in the water where their tails and their breath decide it. Invade their claim, though, and the same folk turn patient: snares in the reeds, javelins from the bank, raids on your camp and your stores by night until you tire of the fen and leave. The older tribes lay better traps than the young ones.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Learn a little Draconic before you enter a fen. It is worth more than a spare blade.
• Never fight them waist-deep. That is their ground, and your footing is the first thing they take.
• Once you cross into their claim they will be setting snares behind you. Walk behind the one watching the ground, not ahead of him.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Words work here, given Draconic and patience. I ate eel with a chief in the Sedge and left with a guide. They want their water and their eggs left be. Say plainly what you seek, offer salt or worked metal, swear to take no fish — and keep the oath, or none of them will speak to you again.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Humanoid (Reptilian)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+5 natural), or 17 (+5 natural, +2 heavy shield); touch 10, flat-footed 15 or 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+2

Full Attack: 2 claws +2 melee (1d4+1) and bite +0 melee (1d4); or club +2 melee (1d6+1) and bite +0 melee (1d4); or javelin +1 ranged (1d6+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Hold breath
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +0
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 10, Con 13, Int 9, Wis 10, Cha 10
Skills: Balance +4, Jump +5, Swim +2
Feats: Multiattack
Environment: Temperate marshes
Organization: Gang (2–3), band (6–10 plus 50% noncombatants plus 1 leader of 3rd–6th level), or tribe (30–60 plus 2 lieutenants of 3rd–6th level and 1 leader of 4th–10th level)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: 50% coins; 50% goods; 50% items
Advancement: By character class (level adjustment +1)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Hold Breath (Ex): A lizardfolk can hold its breath for a number of rounds equal to four times its Constitution score before it risks drowning.

Skills: Because of their tails, lizardfolk have a +4 racial bonus on Jump, Swim, and Balance checks. The skill modifiers given in the statistics block include a –2 armor check penalty (–4 on Swim checks) for carrying a heavy shield.

Tactics: Lizardfolk fight as unorganized individuals. They prefer frontal assaults and massed rushes, sometimes trying to force foes into the water, where the lizardfolk have the advantage. If outnumbered, or if their territory is being invaded, they set snares, plan ambushes, and raid to hinder enemy supplies. Advanced tribes use more sophisticated tactics and better traps.

Lizardfolk as Characters: Racial traits: +2 Strength, +2 Constitution, –2 Intelligence; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet. A lizardfolk begins with two racial levels of humanoid, giving a base attack bonus of +1 and base saves of Fort +0, Ref +3, Will +0, skill points equal to 5 × (2 + Int modifier, minimum 1), and one feat; its class skills are Balance, Jump, and Swim, with a +4 racial bonus on each. It is automatically proficient with simple weapons and shields, has a +5 natural armor bonus, and fights with 2 claws (1d4) and a bite (1d4). Special quality: hold breath. Automatic languages Common and Draconic; bonus languages Aquan, Goblin, Gnoll, Orc. Favored class druid. Level adjustment +1.

lore.summary: Hyena-headed raiders of the warm plains, dirty yellow or rust in the pelt and taller than any man, wandering in loose tribes with their laughing beasts at heel. They hunt by night, eat what they take, and favour prey that can scream. Met on grassland tracks and in hill lairs, where trolls sometimes share the back of the cave.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Taller than a tall man, broad through the shoulder, and heavier than the height leads you to expect.
Durability: About as hard to fell as a soldier, and no harder. They simply seldom come at you alone.
Defenses: Boiled leather, a heavy steel shield and a coarse pelt beneath. Honest steel answers all of it.
Speed: An even pace afoot, and eyes that see in pitch dark as yours see at noon.
Might: Strong enough to split a shield with an axe swung from the hip, with shortbows to open the business.
Mind: Dull and cruel, but not witless. They know a flank when they see one and they take it.
Disposition: Chaotic and wicked. They fall on you when the numbers are theirs and drag off whatever they can carry, prisoners included.
Bane: They come apart without a leader — fell the sergeant and the horde becomes a rabble. And those heavy shields make them clumsy at hiding, so an ambush needs darkness or cover to work. Deny them both and hold your own ranks.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They mass and rush, using weight and numbers to knock a man down and hew him where he lies, loosing a few arrows first if the ground allows. Under a strong sergeant they hold ranks and fight as one body; without one, discipline goes and every gnoll fights for itself. They always want a flank, and they would rather come out of the dark than meet you in the open.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Buy passage with drink and meat. They understand a bargain well enough; they simply do not honour one for long.
• Kill the one giving orders. That is the whole trick of breaking a gnoll war-band.
• Where gnolls den underground, look to the back of the cave for trolls. Carry fire.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk is possible, and treachery is always the nearer thing. I bought passage over the grass with a cask of spirits and a promise that no elf rode with me. Speak to the leader alone, keep your back to nothing, pay in what they can drink or carry — and do not turn to walk away.
