sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Darkvision (Ex): A gnoll sees in total darkness out to 60 feet. Darkvision is black and white only, but is otherwise like normal sight, and gnolls can function with no light at all.

Tactics: Gnolls like to attack when they have the advantage of numbers, using horde tactics and physical strength to overwhelm and knock down opponents. They show little discipline unless they have a strong leader; under one they can hold ranks and fight as a unit. They rarely prepare traps, but they use ambushes and try to attack from a flanking position. Because of its shield, a gnoll’s modifier on Hide checks (untrained) is –2, so gnolls take special care to seek favorable conditions when laying an ambush — darkness, cover, or some other advantage of terrain.

Gnolls as Characters: Racial traits: Strength +4, Constitution +2, Intelligence –2, Charisma –2; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 60 feet; +1 natural armor bonus. A gnoll begins with two racial levels of humanoid, giving a base attack bonus of +1, base saves of Fort +3, Ref +0, Will +0, skill points equal to 5 × (2 + Int modifier), and one feat; its class skills are Listen and Spot. Automatic language Gnoll; bonus languages Common, Draconic, Elven, Goblin, Orc. Favored class ranger. Level adjustment +1.

lore.summary: The largest of the goblin-kin: a shaggy, wedge-headed brute a head taller than a man, that crosses leaf-litter more quietly than you cross a floor in stockings. They den in cold hill and mountain country in gangs and bands, live by ambush and bullying, and keep their morningstars in better repair than their word.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A head taller than a man and a good deal broader — and it still makes less noise entering a room than you do.
Durability: Sturdier than a common raider. It will not go down to the first honest blow.
Defenses: Leather, a light wooden shield and a thick hide under the fur. Nothing your steel cannot answer.
Speed: Ordinary afoot. Its gift is not swiftness but silence.
Might: A morningstar swung with real weight behind it, and javelins for the opening throw.
Mind: Cunning rather than clever. It scouts, it reports, and it comes back with company.
Disposition: Wicked, greedy, a bully by nature — but it thinks before it charges. It would far rather have you surrounded than face you.
Bane: It lives on surprise. Take that away — lanterns, a watched rear, a dog whose nose beats yours — and a bugbear is only a large thug with a club. It smells you long before it sees you, so mind what your camp gives off.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It will not meet you fairly if it can avoid it. Scouts go out ahead of the band; finding prey, they slip back and bring up the rest, and the first you know of any of it is a morningstar coming out of the dark at the man behind you. The attacks are coordinated and the plan is sound, if never brilliant. Rob it of the ambush and it fights like any strong brute, which is to say well enough.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It smells you before it sees you. Wet wool, cook-fires and horses announce a camp for a long way.
• Post a rear guard. Bugbears take the last man in the line, and quietly.
• Pay them and move the same night. A bought bugbear stays bought only while it can still see the purse.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It can be bargained with. It has Common, and it likes coin better than it likes killing. I paid a band to let a caravan through and they took the money and let us by — then followed us three nights to see whether we would grow careless. Pay, keep watch, and be gone before they weigh your strength.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Scent (Ex): A bugbear can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. It notices opponents within 30 feet by scent; if the opponent is upwind the range is 60 feet, downwind 15 feet, and strong scents are noticed at twice those ranges. On detecting a scent the bugbear knows the direction but not the exact location; moving within 5 feet of the source pinpoints it.

Darkvision (Ex): A bugbear sees in total darkness out to 60 feet. Darkvision is black and white only, but is otherwise like normal sight.

Skills: Bugbears have a +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks.

Tactics: Bugbears prefer to ambush opponents whenever possible. When hunting they send scouts ahead of the main group; if the scouts spy prey, they return to report and bring up reinforcements. Bugbear attacks are coordinated, and their tactics are sound if not brilliant. Bugbears speak Goblin and Common.

Bugbears as Characters: Racial traits: +4 Strength, +2 Dexterity, +2 Constitution, –2 Charisma; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision 60 ft. and scent; +3 natural armor bonus; +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks. A bugbear begins with three racial levels of humanoid, giving a base attack bonus of +2, base saves of Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +1, skill points equal to 6 × (2 + Int modifier), and two feats; its class skills are Climb, Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, and Spot. Automatic languages Common and Goblin; bonus languages Draconic, Elven, Giant, Gnoll, Orc. Favored class rogue. Level adjustment +1.

lore.summary: Soldiers, not savages: orange-skinned goblin-kin in dark studded leather and blood-red cloth, drilled into ranks beneath sergeants, lieutenants and a captain. They hold warm hill country in warbands and tribes, keep their weapons polished, and hate elves above every other living thing. You meet them as an army, seldom as a nuisance.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man's height and build, thickset, orange-skinned, with yellow eyes and a blue or red nose on the big males.
Durability: No hardier than a good soldier — and that is rather the point, since you will face a great many of them.
Defenses: Studded leather and a light shield, kept in repair. Their true armour is order.
Speed: A soldier's pace, and they cross broken ground quietly when the order is given.
Might: Longsword and javelin, handled competently. No brute strength; only training, which is worse.
Mind: The sharpest wits among goblin-kin. They grasp strategy, hold to a plan, and carry out orders under pressure.
Disposition: Lawful and cruel. They keep faith with rank and with a struck bargain, and with nothing else. Any elf in your party will be attacked first, without discussion.
Bane: Break the chain of command. Man for man they are ordinary fighters; it is the officer who makes them dangerous. Take the sergeant and the line begins to fray.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They fight as a company — ranks, flanks, a reserve — and the plan holds even when the front bends. Under a good tactician they will feign, envelop, and cut the road behind you before you notice it is gone. Whatever else happens on that field, every elf among your people will find hobgoblins coming for them first; they will leave a nearer foe to reach one.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Deal with the officer. A ranker will not speak for himself, and killing him only starts the fight early.
• Travelling with an elf? Expect her to be the first target and the last. Send her wide of the road.
• A hobgoblin treaty holds. That is worth more than any oath a gnoll ever swore me.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: The most reliable talk among the wicked peoples. They keep a bargain because breaking one is disorder, and disorder they cannot stomach. I bought a road through the red hills from a captain for salt and iron and had it honoured to the last mile. Send no elf to the parley. Send no elf at all.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Darkvision (Ex): A hobgoblin sees in total darkness out to 60 feet. Darkvision is black and white only, but is otherwise like normal sight.

Skills: Hobgoblins have a +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks.

Tactics: These creatures have a strong grasp of strategy and tactics and are capable of carrying out sophisticated battle plans. Under the leadership of a skilled strategist or tactician, their discipline can prove the deciding factor. Hobgoblins hate elves and attack them first, in preference to other opponents.

The Sample Warrior: Most hobgoblins met outside their homes are warriors, and the statistics given are for one of 1st level. The warrior presented here had the following ability scores before racial adjustments: Str 13, Dex 11, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 8.

Hobgoblin Characters: Racial traits: +2 Dexterity, +2 Constitution; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 60 feet; +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks. Automatic languages Common and Goblin; bonus languages Draconic, Dwarven, Infernal, Giant, Orc. Favored class fighter. Level adjustment +1.

lore.summary: Squat reptilian folk of the deep caves, shorter than a man and thicker through the chest, with skin that shifts to the colour of the stone behind them. They live underground in clutches and bands with tame monitor lizards at heel. The first sign of them is never the sight — it is the stink, an oily musk that empties a strong man's stomach.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Shorter than a man and heavier through the chest, with a lizard's head and a low, hunched stance.
Durability: Thickly built and stubbornly hard to put down for something so small.
Defenses: A heavy scaled hide better than any armour they could forge, so they wear none at all.
Speed: Slow and clumsy on its feet. It chases badly and dodges worse.
Might: Claws, jaws and a club all at once, with a javelin thrown first and thrown well.
Mind: Dull, but organised. They post sentries, hide beautifully, and know when a fight has been lost.
Disposition: Chaotic and evil. They raid the dark passages and hoard what they take, and they would rather run than die over it.
Bane: The stench is a poison and nothing more: anyone proof against venom walks through it untroubled, and one who shrugs off a given trog's reek cannot be turned by that same one again for a day and a night. Beyond that they are slow — archers and open floor undo them.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They lie flat against the stone until you are among them, coloured like the wall and perfectly still, and then a volley of javelins comes out of the rock and the smell arrives with it. Those carrying no javelins come in with claws and teeth while you are still retching. Fight sickened and half-blind in a dark passage and you will lose men. When the fight turns against them they scatter and hide rather than sell themselves dearly.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The reek is a venom, not a smell. Anything proof against poison strolls through it laughing.
• Shrug off one trog's stench and that same one cannot turn your gut again for a day and a night. Push through the first rush.
• Watch the wall, not the floor. Their skin takes the colour of the rock and they do not move until you have passed.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Words are possible — they keep Draconic and they covet worked metal — though I would not stand near enough to haggle without something over my nose. I bought a road through a warren for a bundle of iron spearheads. They took it, watched us the whole way out, and did not strike.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Stench (Ex): When a troglodyte is angry or frightened it secretes an oily, musk-like chemical that nearly every form of animal life finds offensive. All living creatures (except troglodytes) within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or be sickened for 10 rounds. The save DC is Constitution-based. A creature that saves cannot be affected by the same troglodyte's stench for 24 hours. A delay poison or neutralize poison spell removes the effect from a sickened creature. Creatures immune to poison are unaffected, and creatures resistant to poison receive their normal bonus on the save.

Darkvision (Ex): A troglodyte sees in total darkness out to 90 feet. Darkvision is black and white only, but is otherwise like normal sight.

Skills: The skin of a troglodyte changes color somewhat, letting it blend with its surroundings like a chameleon and giving a +4 racial bonus on Hide checks. *In rocky or underground settings this bonus improves to +8.

Tactics: Half of any group of troglodytes are armed only with claws and teeth; the rest carry one or two javelins and a club. They normally conceal themselves, loose a volley of javelins, then close to attack. If the battle goes against them they retreat and try to hide. A troglodyte stands about 5 feet tall and weighs about 150 pounds, and troglodytes speak Draconic.

Troglodyte Characters: Racial traits: –2 Dexterity, +4 Constitution, –2 Intelligence; Medium size; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 90 feet; +6 natural armor bonus; natural weapons 2 claws (1d4) and bite (1d4); the stench special attack. A troglodyte begins with two racial levels of humanoid, giving a base attack bonus of +1, base saves of Fort +3, Ref +0, Will +0, skill points equal to 5 × (2 + Int modifier, minimum 1), and one feat, plus Multiattack as a bonus feat; its class skills are Hide and Listen, with a +4 racial bonus on Hide (+8 in rocky or underground surroundings). Automatic language Draconic; bonus languages Common, Giant, Goblin, Orc. Favored class cleric. Level adjustment +2.

lore.summary: Fish-folk of the warm seas, plainly more fish than man: scaled, wide-eyed, finned, and standing about a man's height. They move in companies and patrols under sergeants and captains, craft finely, and are the most civil people you are likely to meet beneath the waves. Met over reefs and warm shallows, longspear in hand.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: About a man's height, and lighter than it looks — all fin, scale and long bone.
Durability: Frail by the measure of the deep. They are not a shark's kin and they do not pretend to be.
Defenses: A layer of tough scale, and nothing besides. They wear no armour.
Speed: Wretched on land, where they hobble. In water they are swift, and can swim flat out without tiring.
Might: Longspear and light crossbow, handled with practice. Bare-handed they have nothing at all: no teeth, no claws, no strength worth the name.
Mind: Bright and thoughtful, the equal of most men — patient crafters, good listeners, better watchers.
Disposition: Neutral and peaceable, and wary of surface folk with good cause. They fight to hold their own water, never to take yours.
Bane: Take the spear and the fight ends: disarmed, a locathah has no natural weapon whatever and will turn and flee. And out of the water it is helpless.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They open with a volley of bolts, and since a crossbow carries poorly under water they loose from nearer than you would like and keep loosing while an ambush holds. Otherwise they close with the longspear — a fishing tool, but they know its use, and they favour it above all. Disarm one and it does not fight on bare-handed. It runs, and I do not blame it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• They keep only Aquan. Without it you are waving your arms at a fisherman.
• Trade iron and worked glass. They craft well but have no forge down there, and they know the worth of both.
• If you must fight, fight in the shallows. In open water you are the slow one.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Talk first, always. They are as sharp as any merchant on the quay and they will trade — pearl and worked shell against iron and glass. I wintered beside a locathah patrol on a warm reef and was fed for it. Bring Aquan, or a ring that grants it; they keep no other tongue.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Aquatic Subtype (Ex): A locathah always has a swim speed and can move through water without making Swim checks. It breathes water and cannot breathe air. Underwater its light crossbow has a range increment of 20 feet.

Skills: A locathah has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Tactics: A battle with locathahs usually opens with volleys of bolts from their crossbows. If they have set an ambush or a trap they keep shooting as long as they can; otherwise they close to bring their longspears into play, and though those spears are primarily fishing gear they make formidable weapons. Locathahs lack teeth, claws, and other natural weapons, so an unarmed one is not especially dangerous and will generally turn and flee.

Appearance and Speech: Although humanoid in shape, locathahs are clearly more fish than human. The average locathah stands 5 feet tall and weighs 175 pounds. Females and males look much alike, though the former can be recognized by the two ochre stripes marking their egg sacs. Locathahs speak Aquan.

lore.summary: Sea people: a man's height and a long fish's tail besides, and heavier than both together. They breathe air as easily as brine, yet they seldom stray more than a few paces from the water's edge, for ashore they are as helpless as a landed salmon. I have met their companies off every warm coast, patrolling reef and wreck.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — as long as a tall man is high, tail and all, and a good deal heavier.
Durability: No hardier than a fisherman. It is the sea that keeps them, not their hide.
Defenses: Boiled leather harness and the water itself; an arrow loses its bite fast in the deep.
Speed: Swift as a porpoise in open water, and near crippled out of it — ashore they drag themselves along a hand's span at a time.
Might: Trident work at close quarters, honest and unfancy; their bolts of shell and blowfish spine carry further underwater than any of ours.
Mind: As quick as any man and far better read in the tides. They keep sergeants, lieutenants and captains, and answer to them.
Disposition: Neutral folk, neither friend nor foe by birth. Wary of surface men because surface men have taught them to be.
Bane: Get them onto land and the whole quarrel is over — they cannot follow you up a beach, and they know it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They see you coming through clear water and open with a barrage of crossbow bolts from the edge of sight, closing only once the water is already reddened. Then it is tridents, in companies, with the current at their backs and porpoises worrying your flanks. They break off freely and slide into the deep rather than die for a stretch of reef.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Talk from the boat, never from the water. In their element the generosity is all yours.
• Never trade shots below the surface. Their bolts fly true down there and yours do not.
• Ask about wrecks. They know every hull on their reef and will sell the knowing for good iron and glass.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Open, and gladly. They speak the sea-tongue and most speak ours besides. Twice I have gone out on the shallows with my blade left behind in the boat and come back with pilotage through a wreck-field. Bring worked goods, name the ship you sail under, and do not lie to them about nets.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Humanoid (Aquatic)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 5 ft. (1 square), swim 50 ft.
Armor Class: 13 (+1 Dex, +2 leather), touch 11, flat-footed 12
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / +2
Attack: Trident +2 melee (1d8+1) or heavy crossbow +2 ranged (1d10/19-20)
Full Attack: Trident +2 melee (1d8+1) or heavy crossbow +2 ranged (1d10/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Amphibious, low-light vision
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +1, Will -1
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 13, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 10
Skills: Listen +3, Spot +3, Swim +9
Feats: Alertness
Environment: Temperate aquatic
Organization: Company (2-4), patrol (11-20 plus 2 3rd-level lieutenants and 1 leader of 3rd-6th level), or band (30-60 plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults, 5 5th-level lieutenants, 3 7th-level captains, and 10 porpoises)
Challenge Rating: 1/2
Alignment: Usually neutral
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Amphibious (Ex): Merfolk can breathe both air and water, although they rarely travel more than a few feet from the water's edge.

Combat: Merfolk favor heavy crossbows of shell and coral that fire bolts fashioned from blowfish spines, with an underwater range increment of 30 feet. Merfolk often barrage their enemies before closing, when they resort to tridents.

Skills: A merfolk has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Merfolk Characters: A merfolk is about 8 feet long from the top of the head to the end of the tail, and weighs about 400 pounds. Merfolk speak Common and Aquan. Most merfolk encountered outside their home are warriors; the statistics above are for one of 1st level. A merfolk's favored class is bard, and the race carries a level adjustment of +1.

lore.summary: Hill folk and raiders: black-haired, red-eyed, ears like a wolf's, dressed in colours that turn a decent man's stomach — blood red, mustard, deep purple, and all of it filthy. They gather in gangs, in squads under sergeants, and in great bands with their broods trailing behind, and they come down on farm and road at the turn of the season.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a head over most men, and broader through the shoulder than any of them.
Durability: Tough enough to keep swinging through a wound that would sit a man down.
Defenses: Studded leather, ill-kept and patched with hide. Nothing about an orc is hard to cut.
Speed: A marching man's pace, kept up all day and half the night after.
Might: Great strength behind a falchion held in both hands. The first stroke is the one meant to finish you.
Mind: Slow of thought and slower of temper, but they lay ambushes well and understand concealment. Do not read dullness as stupidity.
Disposition: Often chaotic and cruel. They keep the rules of war — a truce, a herald, a hostage — exactly as long as keeping them is convenient.
Bane: Daylight. Full sun leaves them dazzled and swearing; an open field at noon is worth a company of spears to you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They fight from cover wherever the ground allows it — a gully, a treeline, a rock above the road — and open the business by flinging javelins before charging in with the falchion high. Every orc goes for the kill on the first stroke and worries about its own guard afterwards. Break that charge and the band frays; put down the sergeants and the whole squad goes to pieces.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Meet them at noon, on open ground. Sun in their eyes is worth more than mail.
• Cut down the sergeant and the band forgets what it came for.
• A truce with an orc holds exactly as long as it pays him. Be over the ridge before it stops.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary. They speak their own tongue and ours, and a chief will hear terms — I bought passage over the Tusk Hills with a keg and a pledge of salt. But the pledge lasts only while it profits him. Take the meeting in daylight, on open ground, and count your party out again as they leave.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Humanoid (Orc)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 13 (+3 studded leather armor), touch 10, flat-footed 13
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / +4
Attack: Falchion +4 melee (2d4+4/18-20) or javelin +1 ranged (1d6+3)
Full Attack: Falchion +4 melee (2d4+4/18-20) or javelin +1 ranged (1d6+3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.

Saves: Fort +3, Ref +0, Will -2

Skills: Listen +1, Spot +1
Feats: Alertness
Environment: Temperate hills
Organization: Gang (2-4), squad (11-20 plus 2 3rd-level sergeants and 1 leader of 3rd-6th level), or band (30-100 plus 150% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 10 adults, 5 5th-level lieutenants, and 3 7th-level captains)
Challenge Rating: 1/2
Alignment: Often chaotic evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Light Sensitivity (Ex): Orcs are dazzled in bright sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell.

Combat: Orcs are proficient with all simple weapons, preferring those that cause the most damage in the least time. Many orcs who take up the warrior or fighter class also gain proficiency with the falchion or the greataxe as a martial weapon. They enjoy attacking from concealment and setting ambushes, and they obey the rules of war (such as honoring a truce) only as long as it is convenient for them.

Orc Traits (Ex): Orcs possess the following racial traits: +4 Strength, -2 Intelligence, -2 Wisdom, -2 Charisma; base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 60 feet; light sensitivity (dazzled in bright sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell). Automatic languages: Common, Orc. Bonus languages: Dwarven, Giant, Gnoll, Goblin, Undercommon. Favored class: barbarian; level adjustment +0.

Orcs As Characters: The language an orc speaks varies slightly from tribe to tribe, but any orc is understandable by someone else who speaks Orc. Some orcs know Goblin or Giant as well. Most orcs encountered away from their homes are warriors; the statistics above are for one of 1st level. An adult male orc is a little over 6 feet tall and weighs about 210 pounds; females are slightly smaller.

lore.summary: Small folk the colour of rust and old blood, dull-eyed, wrapped in soiled dark leather. Bullied since the world began by everything larger than them, they have learned the only lessons on offer: numbers, ambush and the dirty trick. Met on the open plains in gangs and bands, and in warbands astride worgs.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — a child's height, and lighter than the harness makes it look.
Durability: Frail. One honest cut ends one goblin.
Defenses: Leather and a little shield, and the dark, which serves it better than either.
Speed: As quick afoot as you are and quicker away. Astride a worg, quicker than your horse.
Might: Weak in the arm. Morningstar and javelin do their damage by arriving in dozens.
Mind: Ordinary wit put entirely to malicious use. Poor at strategy, splendid at spite. Under a hard captain they will hold a plan together long enough to hurt you.
Disposition: Evil in the small way — thieving, cruel, and frank about it. They flee the moment a battle turns, and they always know it has turned before you do.
Bane: Their nerve. Kill the captain or simply frighten them badly and the band runs; alone, a goblin will surrender before it will fight.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Never a straight fight if they can avoid one. Pits, tripwires, a hail of javelins out of the flank, then the whole gang piling onto whoever went down. In the field they ride worgs, and the mount is the greater danger — the wolves take you while the spears keep you busy. Their tribes keep worgs and dire wolves both. They break early and they break completely.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Buy them off, then shift your camp. Both. Always both.
• Kill the worg first. The rider is a nuisance; the mount is the fight.
• They count better than they fight. Look bigger than you are and they will find another road.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, but worth the attempt. They speak Goblin among themselves and the brighter ones have our tongue as well. I bought a night's safe camp off a gang for a sack of salt pork and the lie that I was expected back by morning. They will take the goods and follow you anyway — so pay, and then move.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Humanoid (Goblinoid)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +2 leather armor, +1 light shield), touch 12, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / -3
Attack: Morningstar +2 melee (1d6) or javelin +3 ranged (1d4)
Full Attack: Morningstar +2 melee (1d6) or javelin +3 ranged (1d4)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft.
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +1, Will -1
Abilities: Str 11, Dex 13, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 6
Skills: Hide +5, Listen +2, Move Silently +5, Ride +4, Spot +2
Feats: Alertness
Environment: Temperate plains
Organization: Gang (4-9), band (10-100 plus 100% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults and 1 leader of 4th-6th level), warband (10-24 with worg mounts), or tribe (40-400 plus 100% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults, 1 or 2 lieutenants of 4th or 5th level, 1 leader of 6th-8th level, 10-24 worgs, and 2-4 dire wolves)
Challenge Rating: 1/3
Alignment: Usually neutral evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Being bullied by bigger, stronger creatures has taught goblins to exploit what few advantages they have: sheer numbers and malicious ingenuity. The concept of a fair fight is meaningless in their society. They favor ambushes, overwhelming odds, dirty tricks, and any other edge they can devise. Goblins have a poor grasp of strategy and are cowardly by nature, tending to flee the field if a battle turns against them. With proper supervision, though, they can implement reasonably complex plans, and in such circumstances their numbers can be a deadly advantage.

Skills: Goblins have a +4 racial bonus on Move Silently and Ride checks. Goblin cavalry (mounted on worgs) usually select the Mounted Combat feat in place of the Alertness feat, which reduces their Spot and Listen check modifiers from +3 to +1.

Challenge Rating: Goblins with levels in NPC classes have a CR equal to their character level -2.

Goblins As Characters: Goblin characters possess the following racial traits: -2 Strength, +2 Dexterity, -2 Charisma; Small size (+1 bonus to Armor Class, +1 bonus on attack rolls, +4 bonus on Hide checks, -4 penalty on grapple checks, lifting and carrying limits three-quarters those of Medium characters); base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 60 feet; +4 racial bonus on Move Silently and Ride checks. Automatic languages: Common, Goblin. Bonus languages: Draconic, Elven, Giant, Gnoll, Orc. Favored class: rogue; level adjustment +0.

Appearance and Speech: A goblin stands 3 to 3-1/2 feet tall and weighs 40 to 45 pounds. Its eyes are usually dull and glazed, varying in color from red to yellow. A goblin's skin color ranges from yellow through any shade of orange to a deep red; usually all members of a single tribe are about the same color. Goblins wear clothing of dark leather, tending toward drab, soiled-looking colors. Goblins speak Goblin; those with Intelligence scores of 12 or higher also speak Common.

lore.summary: Little reptile folk, scaled rusty brown to near black, with glowing red eyes and voices like a yapping dog. They mine, they dig, and above all they trap: no warren of theirs is walked safely, for the floor and the ceiling are as much their weapons as the spear. Cowardly, spiteful, patient, and very clever with a length of cord.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Small — knee to waist on a tall man, and no heavier than a hound.
Durability: The least of any folk I have fought. A blow lands and the matter is settled.
Defenses: Scale hide and rag leather, and a long stretch of tunnel built to kill you before you ever set eyes on one.
Speed: A man's pace on level stone, and much faster than that through their own crawlways.
Might: Feeble. The sling is for softening you at leisure; the spear is for finishing what the trap began.
Mind: As sharp as any common man and far more patient. They quarry, they build, they scheme — and their sorcerers, who come from no particular rank, are the real danger.
Disposition: Orderly in their own fashion and thoroughly cruel. They will not close unless they have two to your one, and they hate gnomes past all reason: a gnome in your party is a fight you cannot talk your way out of.
Bane: Sunlight leaves them dazzled, and their nerve goes the instant the odds even. Break the ambush and the warren empties.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They open with sling-stones out of the dark, from murder-holes and from behind their own pits, and they will keep it up all day rather than close with you. Only when you are staggering do the spears come, and always where a trap has already done half the work. Dire weasels run with their warbands. Even the odds and they melt back into the crawlways to reset everything you sprang.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Probe every floor. They spend more thought on the ground you walk than on the spear they hold.
• Glare in the tunnel mouth — sun or a bright lantern — and their aim falls apart.
• The sorcerer stands behind the smallest of them. Find him, or the ambush never ends.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary. Draconic is their birth-tongue and only some have troubled to learn ours; find one that has and you can bargain — a toll, a guide past their traps, the loan of a shaft. They hold to a bargain longer than an orc does. Never bring a gnome to the meeting. They will not hear a word past the sight of him.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Humanoid (Reptilian)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 15 (+1 size, +1 Dex, +1 natural, +2 leather), touch 12, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / -4
Attack: Spear +1 melee (1d6-1/x3) or sling +3 ranged (1d3-1)
Full Attack: Spear +1 melee (1d6-1/x3) or sling +3 ranged (1d3-1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —

Saves: Fort +2, Ref +1, Will -1
Abilities: Str 9, Dex 13, Con 10, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 8
Skills: Craft (trapmaking) +2, Hide +6, Listen +2, Move Silently +2, Profession (miner) +2, Search +2, Spot +2
Feats: Alertness
Environment: Temperate forests
Organization: Gang (4-9), band (10-100 plus 100% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults and 1 leader of 4th-6th level), warband (10-24 plus 2-4 dire weasels), tribe (40-400 plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 20 adults, 1 or 2 lieutenants of 4th or 5th level, 1 leader of 6th-8th level, and 5-8 dire weasels)
Challenge Rating: 1/4
Alignment: Usually lawful evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Light Sensitivity (Ex): Kobolds are dazzled in bright sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell.

Combat: Kobolds like to attack with overwhelming odds — at least two to one — or trickery; should the odds fall below this threshold, they usually flee. However, they attack gnomes on sight if their numbers are equal. They begin a fight by slinging bullets, closing only when they can see that their foes have been weakened. Whenever they can, kobolds set up ambushes near trapped areas.

Skills: Kobolds have a +2 racial bonus on Craft (trapmaking), Profession (miner), and Search checks.

Challenge Rating: Kobolds with levels in NPC classes have a CR equal to their character level -3.

Kobold Characters: Kobold characters possess the following racial traits: -4 Strength, +2 Dexterity, -2 Constitution; Small size (+1 bonus to Armor Class, +1 bonus on attack rolls, +4 bonus on Hide checks, -4 penalty on grapple checks, lifting and carrying limits three-quarters those of Medium characters); base land speed 30 feet; darkvision out to 60 feet; +1 natural armor bonus; +2 racial bonus on Craft (trapmaking), Profession (miner), and Search checks; light sensitivity. Automatic language: Draconic. Bonus languages: Common, Undercommon. Favored class: sorcerer; level adjustment +0.

Appearance and Speech: Kobolds are short, reptilian humanoids with cowardly and sadistic tendencies. A kobold's scaly skin ranges from dark rusty brown to a rusty black color. It has glowing red eyes, and its tail is nonprehensile. Kobolds wear ragged clothing, favoring red and orange. A kobold is 2 to 2-1/2 feet tall and weighs 35 to 45 pounds. Kobolds speak Draconic with a voice that sounds like that of a yapping dog.

lore.summary: Grey dwarves of the deep roads: bald as river stones, the women as well as the men, dressed in drab that vanishes against rock, their jewellery deliberately kept dull so that nothing of them shines. They hold halls far under the mountains, they make war on their fair-skinned kin, and they take allies among much worse things when the vein they are following requires it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — short, broad, and heavier through the chest than a tall man.
Durability: Very hard to put down. They take punishment the way their mountains do.
Defenses: Mail and a heavy shield, a footing no shove or trip will break, and a bone-deep sourness towards spellcraft. Venom does nothing to them, no charm will freeze them in place, and a phantom conjured to frighten them is simply ignored.
Speed: Short-legged and unhurried, but armour and load cost them nothing at all — they arrive when you do.
Might: Warhammer and crossbow, drilled and patient. And one of them will swell to twice his height at the outset, which is a great deal of grey dwarf to have leaning over you.
Mind: Sober, orderly and grasping. They have the dwarven tongue and the trade-speech of the deep, and they will hear an offer as readily as an insult.
Disposition: Lawful and evil together, which is the worst of the pairings — they keep a contract to the letter and write the letter to ruin you.
Bane: Daylight. Sun, or any conjured equal of it, leaves them dazzled and cursing, and they will not follow you up into it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They fight as a drilled squad and never as a mob: crossbows first, then hammers in a locked line behind heavy shields. Expect one to grow to giant size as the first bolts fly and another to vanish outright and reappear behind your rearmost man, gear and all. Each of those tricks comes once in a day and no more. Weather them and you are fighting ordinary dwarves — which is quite bad enough.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Their word holds under their own roof and nowhere outside it. Do all your business at the table.
• One trick apiece: one grows, one goes unseen. Count them off and the rest is hammer-work.
• Poison, holding-spells and conjured terrors are all wasted here. Bring steel, and bring light.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary — but the deep roads have their law of hospitality and the grey dwarves keep it. Salt, fire and a named price: while you are a guest under that roof the bargain holds. I have sat at a duergar's table over ore he had just refused to sell me and walked out whole. Past the door you are trade goods again.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Humanoid (Dwarf)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. in chainmail (4 squares); base speed 20 ft.
Armor Class: 17 (+5 chainmail, +2 heavy shield), touch 10, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / +2
Attack: Warhammer +2 melee (1d8+1/x3) or light crossbow +1 ranged (1d8/19-20)
Full Attack: Warhammer +2 melee (1d8+1/x3) or light crossbow +1 ranged (1d8/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Duergar traits, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Darkvision 120 ft., duergar traits
Saves: Fort +4*, Ref +0*, Will -1*
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 11, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 9, Cha 4
Skills: Appraise +2, Craft (blacksmithing) +2, Craft (stonemasonry) +2, Listen +3, Move Silently -4, Spot +2
Feats: Toughness
Environment: Underground
Organization: Team (2-4), squad (9-16 plus 3 3rd-level sergeants and 1 leader of 3rd-8th level), or clan (20-80 plus 25% noncombatants plus 1 3rd-level sergeant per 5 adults, 3-6 6th-level lieutenants, and 1-4 9th-level captains)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Often lawful evil
Treasure: Standard coins, double goods, standard items
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day — enlarge person and invisibility, as a wizard of twice the duergar's class level (minimum caster level 3rd). These abilities affect only the duergar and whatever it carries.

Immunities (Ex): Duergar are immune to paralysis, phantasms, and poison. This trait replaces the hill dwarf's +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison. They also gain a +2 racial bonus on saves against spells and spell-like abilities.

Light Sensitivity (Ex): Duergar are dazzled in bright sunlight or within the radius of a daylight spell.

Stability (Ex): Duergar, like all dwarves, are exceptionally stable on their feet. A duergar has a +4 bonus on ability checks made to resist being bull rushed or tripped when standing on the ground (but not when climbing, flying, riding, or otherwise not standing firmly on the ground).

Stonecunning (Ex): A +2 racial bonus on Search checks to notice unusual stonework, such as sliding walls, stonework traps, new construction (even when built to match the old), unsafe stone surfaces, shaky stone ceilings, and the like. Something that isn't stone but is disguised as stone also counts as unusual stonework. A duergar who merely comes within 10 feet of unusual stonework can make a Search check as if actively searching, and can use Search to find stonework traps as a rogue can. A duergar can also intuit depth, sensing his approximate depth underground as naturally as a human senses which way is up.

Duergar Traits (Ex): These traits are in addition to the hill dwarf traits, except where noted: -4 Charisma instead of -2; darkvision out to 120 feet; immunity to paralysis, phantasms, and poison; +2 racial bonus on saves against spells and spell-like abilities; spell-like abilities (1/day enlarge person and invisibility); light sensitivity; +4 racial bonus on Move Silently checks; +1 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks. Automatic languages: Common, Dwarven, Undercommon. Bonus languages: Draconic, Giant, Goblin, Orc, Terran. Favored class: fighter; level adjustment +1. Unlike other dwarves, duergar do not have weapon familiarity with the dwarven waraxe and dwarven urgrosh.

Inherited Dwarf Traits (Ex): +2 Constitution; base land speed 20 feet, which a duergar can maintain even in medium or heavy armor or under a medium or heavy load; +1 racial bonus on attack rolls against orcs (including half-orcs) and goblinoids (including goblins, hobgoblins, and bugbears); +4 dodge bonus to Armor Class against creatures of the giant type (such as ogres, trolls, and hill giants); +2 racial bonus on Appraise checks related to stone or metal items; +2 racial bonus on Craft checks related to stone or metal. The asterisked saving throws above do not include the racial bonuses against poison and against spells and spell-like effects.

Challenge Rating: Duergar with levels in NPC classes have a CR equal to their character level. Duergar with levels in PC classes have a CR equal to their character level +1.

Duergar As Characters: Sometimes called gray dwarves, these evil beings dwell in the underground. Most duergar are bald (even the females), and they dress in drab clothing designed to blend into stone. In their lairs they may wear jewelry, but it is always kept dull. They war with other dwarves, even allying with other underground creatures from time to time. Duergar speak Dwarven and Undercommon. The statistics above are for a 1st-level warrior.

lore.summary: The dark elves: an underground branch of that fair people gone thoroughly bad. Slighter and thinner than their cousins, hair white or some other pale shade, eyes a vivid red. They keep cities in the deep stone, ruled by their women, with the priestesses over the warriors and the warriors over everyone else. You meet them on the lightless roads, in patrols, and in silence.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — slighter than a man, and quieter on bare stone than anything that size has a right to be.
Durability: Slender and easily hurt, if you can once lay a hand on one.
Defenses: A chain shirt and a little shield — and, far more to the point, a natural hostility to spellcraft. Much of what a wizard throws simply slides off them, no sleeping-charm has ever touched one, and charms of the mind fare little better.
Speed: Quick, quiet, and they see further into the black than you will ever see by daylight.
Might: Rapier and hand crossbow, both used with precision rather than force. The killing is done by the venom, not the wound.
Mind: Clever, cultured and cruel: among the sharpest folk I have dealt with, and the finest liars. They have the elven tongue, the trade-speech of the deep, and ours.
Disposition: Usually evil, and quite without warmth. They are not mad and not reckless — everything done to you will have a reason, and the reason will be advantage.
Bane: Light. A sudden brightness blinds a drow outright for a moment and leaves it dazzled while the glare lasts. Carry a covered lantern and know exactly when to uncover it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: A patrol opens the fight before you know it has begun: darkness laid over your torches, a cold glow put on your best-armoured man so that every bolt in the black knows where he stands, then hand crossbows from three sides at once. The bolts are venomed to drop you sleeping rather than dead, which should tell you plainly what they intend afterwards. Whoever is still upright meets the rapiers, and the moment the odds sour they are simply gone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Their knockout venom is no enchantment. It takes elves as readily as men, and it will take you — let no bolt graze anyone you cannot carry out.
• Uncover the lantern at the first bolt. That moment of blindness is the whole of your advantage.
• Everything they tell you will be true and useless. Ask instead what they want; that answer is usually honest.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, and still worth it. Down there guest-right is real: name yourself, offer something of worth, and a patrol leader will hear you out beneath it. I traded a map for my party's passage once and had the passage honoured to the letter — and the letter is precisely where the treachery lives. Concede nothing you cannot afford to lose.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Humanoid (Elf)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 16 (+1 Dex, +4 chain shirt, +1 light shield), touch 11, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +1 / +2
Attack: Rapier +3 melee (1d6+1/18-20) or hand crossbow +2 ranged (1d4/19-20)
Full Attack: Rapier +3 melee (1d6+1/18-20) or hand crossbow +2 ranged (1d4/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison, spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Drow traits, spell resistance 12
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +1, Will -1*
Abilities: Str 13, Dex 13, Con 10, Int 12, Wis 9, Cha 10
Skills: Hide +0, Listen +2, Search +4, Spot +3
Feats: Weapon Focus (rapier)
Environment: Underground
Organization: Squad (2-4), patrol (5-8 plus 2 2nd-level sergeants and 1 leader of 3rd-6th level), or band (20-50 plus 10% noncombatants plus 1 2nd-level sergeant per 5 adults, 2d4 6th-level lieutenants, and 1d4 9th-level captains)
Challenge Rating: 1 (see text)
Alignment: Usually neutral evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Poison (Ex): An opponent struck by a drow's poisoned weapon must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or fall unconscious. After 1 minute, the subject must succeed on another DC 13 Fortitude save or remain unconscious for 2d4 hours. A typical drow carries 1d4-1 doses of drow knockout poison. Drow typically coat arrows and crossbow bolts with this poison, but it can also be applied to a melee weapon. Drow have no special ability to apply poison without risking being poisoned themselves. Since this poison is not a magical effect, drow and other elves are susceptible to it.

Spell-Like Abilities: Drow can use the following spell-like abilities once per day: dancing lights, darkness, faerie fire. Caster level equals the drow's class levels.

Spell Resistance (Ex): A drow has spell resistance equal to 11 + its class levels — spell resistance 12 for the 1st-level warrior above. Drow also gain a +2 racial bonus on Will saves against spells and spell-like abilities.

Light Blindness (Ex): Abrupt exposure to bright light (such as sunlight or a daylight spell) blinds drow for 1 round. On subsequent rounds, they are dazzled as long as they remain in the affected area.

Drow Traits (Ex): These traits are in addition to the high elf traits, except where noted: +2 Intelligence, +2 Charisma; darkvision out to 120 feet (replacing the high elf's low-light vision); spell resistance equal to 11 + class levels; +2 racial bonus on Will saves against spells and spell-like abilities; spell-like abilities (1/day dancing lights, darkness, faerie fire); light blindness. Weapon proficiency: a drow is automatically proficient with the hand crossbow, the rapier, and the short sword. Automatic languages: Common, Elven, Undercommon. Bonus languages: Abyssal, Aquan, Draconic, Drow Sign Language, Gnome, Goblin. Favored class: wizard (male) or cleric (female); level adjustment +2.

Inherited Elf Traits (Ex): +2 Dexterity, -2 Constitution; base land speed 30 feet; immunity to sleep spells and effects, and a +2 racial saving throw bonus against enchantment spells or effects (not reflected in the saving throw modifiers above); +2 racial bonus on Listen, Search, and Spot checks — a drow who merely passes within 5 feet of a secret or concealed door is entitled to a Search check to notice it as if actively looking for it.

Challenge Rating: Drow with levels in NPC classes have a CR equal to their character level. Drow with levels in PC classes have a CR equal to their character level +1.

Drow As Characters: Also known as dark elves, drow are a depraved and evil subterranean offshoot of elvenkind. White is the most common hair color among drow, but almost any pale shade is possible. Drow tend to be smaller and thinner than other sorts of elves, and their eyes are often a vivid red. Drow usually coat their arrows and bolts with a potent venom. The statistics above are for a 1st-level warrior.

lore.summary: Sea devils. Green-scaled, shark-eyed, taller than a man, and lawful in the way a knife is lawful. They raid the shallows in ordered bands with sharks swimming to heel at a thought, and they hate the sea elves above all living things. Any coast within a night's swim of their reefs learns to keep its torches burning.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A tall man's height, lean and green-scaled, darker along the back and pale at the belly.
Durability: No sturdier than a seasoned soldier, until it starts to bleed and stops caring.
Defenses: Scaled hide that turns a glancing cut; it wears little armour and feels no want of it.
Speed: Ordinary afoot, but in the water it swims down anything you can put in the sea.
Might: Trident and talons and a shark's bite together, and when it swims it rakes with its feet as well.
Mind: Sharp as any man and better disciplined; it speaks its own tongue and commonly the trade speech and the water speech besides.
Disposition: Ordered, patient and cruel. It asks no quarter and gives none, and it wars without end on the sea elves and near as bitterly on the tritons.
Bane: The first blaze of sunlight blinds it outright, fresh water sickens it, and hauled from the sea it drowns in open air. Fight them at noon, on a dry deck, or drive them up a river.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They come in ordered teams, half of them casting nets to foul your legs while the rest close with tridents. Sharks arrive soon after, because a sahuagin called them without a word. Cut one deeply and it may go blood-mad, throwing away all guard to claw and bite until one of you is finished. Under the water they need no lantern at all; they feel every movement in the sea around them and will hunt you in perfect black.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight them at noon on a dry deck. Anywhere else you are the one out of your element.
• Half of any band carries nets. Keep a short knife where you can reach it with your arms tangled.
• Wound one and the rest do not scatter. The bleeder goes mad instead, so put the bleeder down first.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: They keep bargains, which is both their use and their danger. I bought passage past a reef once with a cask of good iron and a promise not to fish their water, and they honoured every word of it while plainly hating me. Speak from a boat, in daylight, and never let one get behind you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Monstrous Humanoid (Aquatic)
Initiative: +1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), swim 60 ft.
Armor Class: 16 (+1 Dex, +5 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 15
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+4
Attack: Talon +4 melee (1d4+2) or trident +4 melee (1d8+3) or heavy crossbow +3 ranged (1d10/19-20)
Full Attack: Trident +4 melee (1d8+3) and bite +2 melee (1d4+1); or 2 talons +4 melee (1d4+2) and bite +2 melee (1d4+1); or heavy crossbow +3 ranged (1d10/19-20)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Blood frenzy, rake 1d4+1
Special Qualities: Blindsense 30 ft., darkvision 60 ft., freshwater sensitivity, light blindness, speak with sharks, water dependent

Challenge Rating: 2

Treasure: Standard

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Blood Frenzy: Once per day a sahuagin that takes damage in combat can fly into a frenzy in the following round, clawing and biting madly until either it or its opponent is dead. It gains +2 Constitution and +2 Strength, and takes a -2 penalty to Armor Class. A sahuagin cannot end its frenzy voluntarily.

Rake (Ex): Attack bonus +2 melee, damage 1d4+1. A sahuagin also gains two rake attacks when it attacks while swimming.

Blindsense (Ex): A sahuagin can locate creatures underwater within a 30-foot radius. This ability works only when the sahuagin is underwater.

Speak with Sharks (Ex): Sahuagin can communicate telepathically with sharks up to 150 feet away. The communication is limited to fairly simple concepts such as “food,” “danger,” and “enemy.” Sahuagin can use the Handle Animal skill to befriend and train sharks.

Freshwater Sensitivity (Ex): A sahuagin fully immersed in fresh water must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or become fatigued. Even on a success, it must repeat the save attempt every 10 minutes it remains immersed.

Light Blindness (Ex): Abrupt exposure to bright light (such as sunlight or a daylight spell) blinds sahuagin for 1 round. On subsequent rounds, they are dazzled while operating in bright light.

Water Dependent (Ex): Sahuagin can survive out of the water for 1 hour per 2 points of Constitution (after that, refer to the drowning rules).

Skills: A sahuagin has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered, and it can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line. Underwater, a sahuagin has a +4 racial bonus on Hide, Listen, and Spot checks. It has a +4 racial bonus on Survival and Profession (hunter) checks within 50 miles of its home, and a +4 racial bonus on Handle Animal checks when working with sharks.

Sahuagin Mutants: About one in two hundred sahuagin has four arms. Such creatures can make four claw attacks or use extra weapons, in addition to the claw and bite attacks.

Malenti: If a community of aquatic elves is located within 100 miles of a sahuagin community, about one in one hundred sahuagin looks just like an aquatic elf. These creatures, called malenti, have a swim speed of 40 feet, can remain out of water for 1 hour per point of Constitution, and have freshwater sensitivity and light sensitivity (dazzled in bright light). Malenti have no natural attacks. They are otherwise identical with sahuagin.

lore.summary: Grey folk of the deep caves, smooth-skinned where the eyes should sit, and they have never once missed them. Sound and smell serve a grimlock better than sight serves you; it knows the shape of a chamber and of you standing in it. They hold tribes under the mountains, hunt with stone axes, and are not particular about whose meat they eat.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man's height and heavier in the shoulder, dull grey, with a smooth mask of hide where the eyes ought to be.
Durability: About as hardy as a strong labourer, and rather harder to put down than one.
Defenses: Thick grey hide and no armour worth the name; but no gaze, glamour or trick of the light touches a creature that cannot see.
Speed: It runs and climbs as well as you do, and unlike you it does not slow in the dark.
Might: Strong. It swings a heavy stone axe in both hands and means every blow to end the matter.
Mind: Plain but no fool: a hunter's cunning and poor judgement, kept in order by the tribe. It speaks the trade tongue and its own.
Disposition: Hungry, territorial and cruel. It rushes rather than shoots, and it eats what it kills, kin included when the hunting fails.
Bane: Its whole world is noise and scent. A ringing clamour or a foul enough smoke robs it of both, and past a short cast it cannot find you at all.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hears you before you round the corner and comes at a run with the axe already up, shunning bows because a bow is no use to a blind hunter. In its own tunnels it fights close and in numbers, and grey hide against grey stone means the first you know of a pack is the axe arriving. Deny it sound and smell together and it is simply a blind man in a fight, and it knows it.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Make noise. A ringing pan, a horn, a shrieking spell, anything loud takes its eyes away.
• Stinking smoke does the work of a blade. Carry something foul in a stoppered jar.
• Do not douse your lantern to hide. Save the oil and keep the light; it never had eyes to blind.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: They speak the trade tongue, and a tribe that has eaten recently will listen. I bought a night's passage through a warren with salt and a slaughtered goat, and I believe they smell an honest man out. Arrive loud and empty-handed and they will simply take the meat off you instead.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.body:

Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+4

Full Attack: Battleaxe +4 melee (1d8+3/×3)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Blindsight (Ex): Grimlocks can sense all foes within 40 feet as a sighted creature would. Beyond that range, they treat all targets as having total concealment. Grimlocks are susceptible to sound- and scent-based attacks, however, and are affected normally by loud noises and sonic spells (such as ghost sound or silence) and overpowering odors (such as stinking cloud or incense-heavy air). Negating a grimlock’s sense of smell or hearing reduces this ability to normal Blind-Fight (as the feat). If both these senses are negated, a grimlock is effectively blinded.

Immunities: Grimlocks are immune to gaze attacks, visual effects, illusions, and other attack forms that rely on sight.

Combat: Grimlocks are blind, but their exceptional senses of smell and hearing allow them to notice foes nearby. As a result, they usually shun ranged weapons and rush to the attack, brandishing their stone battleaxes.

Skills: A grimlock’s dull gray skin helps it hide in its native terrain, conferring a +10 racial bonus on Hide checks when in mountains or underground.

Languages: Grimlocks speak Common and Grimlock; some also learn Draconic, Dwarven, Gnome, Terran, or Undercommon.

lore.summary: Serpent-folk, bred long ago out of men and snakes, and proud of every drop of it. Purebloods pass for human and walk your markets as spies; halfbloods wear the serpent openly, with a hooded head or a coiling tail where the legs should be; and the abominations are great venomous snakes with a man's arms and a scholar's mind. All of them scheme, and all of them serve a temple.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: The purebloods and halfbloods stand as a man does. An abomination is a great serpent, longer than a fallen mast, and looks down on both.
Durability: A pureblood dies much as a man dies. The deeper the serpent runs in the blood, the more killing it takes.
Defenses: Scales under good studded leather and a well-used shield, and a stubborn resistance to spellcraft that deepens with the breeding. Save your best incantation for a surer target.
Speed: Quick afoot and quicker of hand. The great ones swim, climb and drive through loose earth besides.
Might: Fine scimitars and good bows, always the best they can obtain, and the blades near always smeared. The serpent-blooded bite as well, with a venom that rots the vigour out of a man, and their skins sweat an acid that eats whatever grips them.
Mind: Genius, every caste of them. The least of them believes itself cleverer than you, and the greatest of them is right.
Disposition: Cold, patient and faithless. They send their least valuable kin forward first and watch carefully how you kill them.
Bane: They will not stand and trade blows. Break the ambush, force close work, and outlast the charms and terrors, which are counted and run dry. Every one of them will spend a lesser kinsman to save itself, and a hunter can use that.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They fight like generals. Purebloods go in first with bow and blade while the halfbloods lie back, their skin turned the colour of the stone, throwing fear and charm and grasping vines out of cover. An abomination stays furthest back of all, reads your company, marks whichever of you it judges most dangerous, and turns that one aside with a loathing of serpents so deep he cannot come within reach of his own fellows; failing that, it takes him in its coils and squeezes. Any of them, hard pressed, drops into the shape of a viper and is gone.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• A handsome, sharp-featured stranger who never seems to blink: look at the tongue.
• Assume every blade and every arrowhead is poisoned. It nearly always is.
• Do not grapple the scaled ones. They sweat acid and you will lose the hand you hold them with.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Words are their favourite weapon, so words will always be offered. I did honest business twice with a pureblood factor in a port city, and both times he was selling out a rival house. One keeps a bargain exactly as long as the bargain pays. Never meet them in their temple, and never alone.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Monstrous Humanoid (pureblood; abominations are Large)
Initiative: +5
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 17 (+1 Dex, +1 natural, +3 masterwork studded leather, +2 masterwork heavy shield), touch 11, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +4/+4
Attack: Masterwork scimitar +5 melee (1d6/18-20) or masterwork longbow +6 ranged (1d8/×3)
Full Attack: Masterwork scimitar +5 melee (1d6/18-20) or masterwork longbow +6 ranged (1d8/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Alternate form, darkvision 60 ft., detect poison, spell resistance 14
Saves: Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +4
Abilities: Str 11, Dex 13, Con 11, Int 12, Wis 10, Cha 12
Skills: Concentration +7, Disguise +4*, Hide +3, Knowledge (any one) +5, Listen +4, Spot +4
Feats: Alertness, Blind-Fight, Dodge, Improved Initiative
Environment: Warm forests
Organization: Solitary, pair, gang (3-4), troupe (2-13 purebloods, 2-5 halfbloods, and 2-4 abominations), or tribe (20-160 purebloods, 10-80 halfbloods, and 10-40 abominations)
Challenge Rating: 3 (pureblood); halfblood 5; abomination 7
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil
Treasure: Double standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Psionics (Sp): Every yuan-ti has innate psionic powers, used at will and available to pureblood, halfblood and abomination alike: alternate form, detect poison, and — for halfbloods and abominations — chameleon power and produce acid. These are psionic abilities, not spells, and are not stopped by the things that stop spellcasting.

Spell-Like Abilities: Pureblood: 1/day—animal trance (DC 13), cause fear (DC 12), charm person (DC 12), darkness, entangle (DC 12). Caster level 4th. Halfblood: 3/day—animal trance (DC 15), cause fear (DC 14), entangle (DC 14); 1/day—deeper darkness, neutralize poison (DC 17), suggestion (DC 16). Caster level 8th. Abomination: at will—animal trance (DC 16), entangle (DC 15); 3/day—deeper darkness, neutralize poison (DC 18), suggestion (DC 17); 1/day—baleful polymorph (DC 19; into snake form only), fear (DC 18). Caster level 10th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Alternate Form (Sp): All yuan-ti can assume the form of a Tiny to Large viper as a psionic ability. The yuan-ti loses its natural weapons (if any) and gains the natural weapon of the viper form it assumes. If the yuan-ti has a poisonous bite of its own, it uses its own or the viper’s poison, whichever is more potent.

Detect Poison (Sp): All yuan-ti have the psionic ability to detect poison as the spell (caster level 6th).

Chameleon Power (Sp): A yuan-ti halfblood or abomination can psionically change the coloration of itself and its equipment to match its surroundings, granting it a +10 circumstance bonus on Hide checks. Purebloods lack this power and rely on disguise instead.

Poison (Ex): Halfbloods and abominations with a serpent’s head bite with venom. Halfblood: injury, Fortitude DC 14, initial and secondary damage 1d6 Con. Abomination: injury, Fortitude DC 17, initial and secondary damage 1d6 Con. The save DCs are Constitution-based. Purebloods have no venomous bite.

Produce Acid (Sp): A halfblood or abomination has the psionic power to exude acid from its body, dealing 3d6 points of acid damage to the next creature it touches, including a creature hit by its bite. If it is grappling, constricting or pinning a foe when it uses this power, its grasp deals 5d6 points of acid damage. The acid becomes inert when it leaves the yuan-ti’s body, and the yuan-ti is immune to its effects.

Aversion (Sp): An abomination can psionically create a compulsion effect targeting one creature within 30 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 22 Will save or gain an aversion to snakes for 10 minutes. Affected creatures must stay at least 20 feet away from any snake or yuan-ti, alive or dead; if already within 20 feet, they move away. A subject unable to move away, or one attacked by snakes or yuan-ti, is overcome with revulsion, reducing its Dexterity score by 4 points until the effect wears off or it is no longer within 20 feet of a snake or yuan-ti. Otherwise similar to antipathy (caster level 16th). The save DC is Charisma-based.

Improved Grab and Constrict (Ex): An abomination that hits a Large or smaller creature with its bite can start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity, and on a won grapple check it constricts for 1d6+6 points of damage. A halfblood with a serpent’s tail constricts for 1d4+3 (with legs) or 1d6+3 (without).

Halfblood and Abomination: Halfblood (CR 5, Medium): Init +5; AC 20 (+1 Dex, +4 natural, +3 masterwork studded leather, +2 masterwork heavy shield), touch 11, flat-footed 19; base attack/grapple +7/+9; masterwork scimitar +10/+5 melee (1d6+2/18-20) and bite +4 melee (1d6+1 plus poison), or masterwork composite longbow (+2 Str) +9/+4 ranged (1d8+2/×3); Fort +3, Ref +6, Will +9; Str 15, Dex 13, Con 13, Int 18, Wis 18, Cha 16; scent, darkvision 60 ft., spell resistance 16. Roughly two in five have snake arms instead of a snake head (two bites, 1d4+2 plus poison), a serpent’s tail alongside human legs (swim 15 ft., constrict Small or smaller), or a serpent’s tail in place of legs (speed 20 ft., climb 15 ft., swim 15 ft., constrict Medium or smaller). Abomination (CR 7, Large): Init +5; speed 30 ft., burrow 20 ft.; AC 22 (-1 size, +1 Dex, +10 natural, +2 masterwork heavy shield), touch 10, flat-footed 21; base attack/grapple +9/+17; masterwork scimitar +13/+8 melee (1d8+4/18-20) and bite +7 melee (2d6+3 plus poison), or masterwork composite longbow (+4 Str) +10/+5 ranged (2d6+4/×3); space/reach 10 ft./10 ft.; Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +11; Str 19, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 20, Wis 20, Cha 18; spell resistance 18; aversion, constrict, improved grab. Abominations rule the temples; halfbloods lead the war-bands; purebloods pass for human and do the talking.

Skills: A pureblood gains a +5 racial bonus on Disguise checks when impersonating a human. Yuan-ti using chameleon power gain a +10 circumstance bonus on Hide checks. An abomination can always take 10 on Climb checks and has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard.

Source: Yuan-ti are Wizards of the Coast product identity and are not part of the Open Game Content SRD. This block reconstructs the Yuan-ti, Pureblood entry from the 3.5 Monster Manual (p. 263, with the halfblood and abomination on p. 264), cross-checked against the Forgotten Realms wiki and the dndtools.one and realmshelps.net 3.5 mirrors.

lore.summary: Fish-men of the lightless lakes, silver-grey and slick, with bulging silver-black eyes that swivel apart and a reek of rotting fish that arrives before they do. They are ancient, mad and devout: whole cities of them under the earth, kneeling at drowning-pools to a lobster-headed goddess, ruled by priest-kings and driven by their whips.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A little shorter than a man and paunchy in the body, on willowy limbs that end in broad flipper hands.
Durability: Tougher than its soft shape suggests, though nothing remarkable.
Defenses: Heavy natural scale and a great wooden shield finished in a glue of their own making. Lightning barely troubles them, and no poison nor palsy-magic touches them at all. Their skin oils are so slippery that webs and snares are wasted, and no grip holds them.
Speed: Shuffling and slow on dry stone; in water it becomes another creature entirely.
Might: Shortspear and a mouthful of sharp teeth. The veterans carry a long pincer-staff that snatches a man from well beyond his own reach and crushes him while he hangs there.
Mind: Clever, watchful and quite mad. Nothing hides from those swivelling eyes: a man gone invisible, or walking the ghost-road, is seen the moment he moves.
Disposition: Sinister, greedy and treacherous; it will sell its own brother to the priests. They trade with almost anything that walks, save the mind-eaters, whom they fall upon without warning.
Bane: Daylight blinds them at the first flash, which is why they never come far up. And their shields are a trap, not a wall: strike one and your sword stays in it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They fight in ranks, throwing spears and then closing. Hack at a shield and your blade is glued fast and torn out of your hands, so thrust past it or bring an arm you can afford to lose. Where two or more of their whips stand together they will join hands and hurl lightning down the length of your company, so never let your people bunch. The nets, harpoons and pincer-staves are not there to kill you; they are there to take you alive for the drowning-pool, which is a worse end.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bring pearls and shells, not coin. They value them above gold and will trade you the gold for them.
• Never strike the shield. The shield keeps whatever touches it.
• Spread your line. Two of their priests hand in hand means lightning down the middle of you.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: They will trade with anyone, and they mean it while it lasts. I bought a ferry across a black lake with a sack of pearls and shells, which they prize far above gold. But madness runs through a shoal of them like fire in thatch. Deal quickly, in the open, and be gone before a priest finds a use for you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Monstrous Humanoid (Aquatic)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), swim 50 ft.
Armor Class: 18 (+6 natural, +2 heavy wooden shield), touch 10, flat-footed 18; or 16 (+6 natural), touch 10, flat-footed 16
Base Attack/Grapple: +2/+3
Attack: Shortspear +3 melee (1d6+1) or bite +3 melee (1d4+1)
