Challenge Rating: 2
Alignment: Often neutral evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Adhesive (Ex): Kuo-toas use their own body oil and other materials to give their shields a finish almost like flypaper, holding fast any creatures or items touching them. Anyone who makes an unsuccessful melee attack against a kuo-toa must succeed on a DC 14 Reflex save, or the attacker’s weapon sticks to the shield and is yanked out of the wielder’s grasp. Creatures using natural weapons are automatically grappled if they get stuck. A kuo-toa requires 1 hour and special materials costing 20 gp to coat a shield with adhesive. The adhesive remains good for up to three days or until it actually catches someone or something, in which case the shield can trap no more. Pulling a stuck weapon or limb from a shield requires a DC 20 Strength check.

Lightning Bolt (Su): Two or more kuo-toa clerics (known as whips) operating together can generate a stroke of lightning every 1d4 rounds. The whips must join hands to launch the bolt but need merely be within 30 feet of one another while it builds. The lightning bolt deals 1d6 points of electricity damage per whip, but a successful Reflex save (DC 13 + number of whips) halves this amount.

Pincer Staff: Many kuo-toa fighters and all whips of 7th level or higher carry this Large exotic weapon. A pincer staff deals 1d10 points of bludgeoning damage, threatens a critical hit on a natural 20, and deals double damage on a critical hit. It has a 10-foot reach and cannot be used against an adjacent opponent. A wielder that hits an opponent of at least Small but no larger than Large size can attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If the wielder wins the grapple check, the staff establishes a hold and deals 1d10 points of damage each round the hold is maintained.

Keen Sight (Ex): Kuo-toas have excellent vision thanks to their two independently focusing eyes. Their eyesight is so keen that they can spot a moving object or creature even if it is invisible or ethereal. Only by remaining perfectly still can such objects or creatures avoid their notice. Their keen sight also detects figments for what they are.

Slippery (Ex): All kuo-toas secrete an oily film that makes them difficult to grapple or snare. Webs, magical or otherwise, do not affect kuo-toas, and they usually can wriggle free from most other forms of confinement.

Immunities (Ex): Kuo-toas are immune to poison and paralysis, and the various hold spells have no effect on them. They also have resistance to electricity 10.

Light Blindness (Ex): Abrupt exposure to bright light (such as sunlight or a daylight spell) blinds kuo-toas for 1 round. On subsequent rounds, they are dazzled while operating in bright light.

Amphibious (Ex): Although kuo-toas breathe by means of gills, they can survive indefinitely on land.

Skills: Kuo-toas have a +8 racial bonus on Escape Artist checks and a +4 racial bonus on Spot and Search checks. A kuo-toa has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard, can always take 10 on a Swim check even if distracted or endangered, and can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Tactics and Faith: Kuo-toa tactics and weapons vary greatly with the training of the individual. A group of kuo-toa fighters usually fights in formation, throwing spears before closing to melee range. Their clerics, the whips, drive the worship of the Sea Mother; every community keeps at least one shrine to her, and most are open to drow traders, who are both feared and hated.

Source: Kuo-toa are Wizards of the Coast product identity and are not part of the Open Game Content SRD. This block reconstructs the Kuo-toa entry from the 3.5 Monster Manual (p. 163), cross-checked against the Forgotten Realms wiki and the dndtools.one and realmshelps.net 3.5 mirrors.

lore.summary: Small, blue-white and mad. The derro are a degenerate kin of the deep places, made out of dwarf and human stock by some nameless god of darkness, and not one of them is sane nor can be made so. They keep no clans and raise no cities; they infest warrens beneath other folk's floors, raid upward for captives, and carry them home to be broken slowly.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Shorter than a dwarf and stockier, with coarse white hair, a drooping moustache, and blank white eyes without iris or pupil.
Durability: Slight. One honest blow generally settles a derro, if you can land one.
Defenses: Studded leather over a tough little hide. Its true armour is that spells slide off it more often than not, so do not waste your best working on the small mad thing.
Speed: Short-legged and no runner. It makes up the difference by never being where you last looked.
Might: Feeble of arm. It kills with a crossbow that shoots and shoots without pausing to load, the bolts smeared with venom, and with a short sword put in from behind.
Mind: Cunning, inventive and deranged past mending. Delusions of grandeur laid over a plain appetite for the pain of other creatures. It reasons perfectly well and wants nothing you would recognise as a want.
Disposition: Malicious without profit in it. They will hold a truce with other folk for a few weeks at the outside, and then the madness comes back up and takes them.
Bane: Sunlight is a slow poison to them; an hour of it wastes a derro and a day of it kills. Nothing that muddles a mind will bite, either, for there is no sanity left in there to disturb.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It never meets you fairly. Derro lay careful traps, wait in the dark, and shoot poisoned bolts from cover, choosing a venom that cripples rather than kills because they want you breathing when they carry you off. Then a knife in the back while your attention is on the noise they made elsewhere, for they can throw darkness across a passage, cast a voice into an empty corner, and loose a burst of sound that leaves a man reeling. Break the ambush and they are pitiful. Let it run its course and they will take your whole company alive.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight them where the sun can reach. The sky does half the work for you.
• Their bolts cripple rather than kill. That is not mercy, it is a shopping list.
• Charms and confusions are wasted breath here. You cannot madden the mad.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing in there to bargain with. I tried twice. The second truce held the better part of a month before the little wretch who swore it woke one morning and had my guide flayed for the pleasure of watching. No derro can know that it is mad. Strike first, and strike all of them.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Small Monstrous Humanoid
Initiative: +6
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares)
Armor Class: 19 (+1 size, +2 Dex, +2 natural, +3 studded leather armor, +1 buckler), touch 13, flat-footed 17
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/-1
Attack: Short sword +4 melee (1d4/19-20) or repeating light crossbow +6 ranged (1d6/19-20 plus poison)
Full Attack: Short sword +4 melee (1d4/19-20) or repeating light crossbow +6 ranged (1d6/19-20 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison use, spell-like abilities, sneak attack +1d6
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., madness, spell resistance 15, vulnerability to sunlight
Saves: Fort +2, Ref +5, Will +6
Abilities: Str 11, Dex 14, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 5*, Cha 16*
Skills: Bluff +5, Hide +10, Listen +1, Move Silently +8
Feats: Blind-Fight, Improved Initiative
Environment: Underground
Organization: Team (2-4), squad (5-8 plus 1 3rd-level sorcerer), or band (11-20 plus 30% noncombatants plus 3 3rd-level sorcerers and 1 sorcerer of 5th-8th level)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually chaotic evil
Treasure: Standard coins; double goods; standard items
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Madness (Ex): Derro use their Charisma modifier on Will saves instead of their Wisdom modifier, and have immunity to confusion and insanity effects. A derro cannot be restored to sanity by any means short of a miracle or wish spell. The racial madness of the derro provides a +6 bonus to their Charisma scores and a -6 penalty to their Wisdom scores (both already figured into the numbers above); a derro restored to sanity gains 6 points of Wisdom and loses 6 points of Charisma.

Poison Use (Ex): Derro typically carry 2d4 doses of greenblood oil or Medium monstrous spider venom, applying it to their crossbow bolts. Derro are not at risk of poisoning themselves when handling poison.

Sneak Attack (Ex): Any time a derro’s opponent is denied his Dexterity bonus to AC, or if a derro flanks his opponent, the derro deals an extra 1d6 points of damage. This ability is just like the rogue’s sneak attack and is subject to the same limitations.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will—darkness, ghost sound; 1/day—daze (DC 13), sound burst (DC 15). Caster level 3rd. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Vulnerability to Sunlight (Ex): A derro takes 1 point of Constitution damage for every hour it is exposed to sunlight, and it dies if its Constitution score reaches 0. Lost Constitution points are recovered at the rate of 1 per every 24-hour period spent underground or otherwise sheltered from the sun.

Skills: Derro have a +4 racial bonus on Hide and Move Silently checks.

Combat: Derro are stealthy and bloodthirsty. They like to carefully arrange cruel traps and deadly ambushes, and strike savagely from hiding. They delight in taking captives who can be tortured to death later, and favor traps and poisons that disable without killing.

Source: Derro appear in the 3.5 Monster Manual (p. 49) and, unlike yuan-ti and kuo-toa, the entry was released as Open Game Content — this block follows the SRD text at d20srd.org and dandwiki, cross-checked against the dndtools.one Monster Manual v.3.5 mirror and the Forgotten Realms wiki.

lore.summary: A spider's face set on a gaunt man's frame, grey and sour-smelling, squatting in the warm forests where the paths run quiet. The ettercap does not hunt so much as build: nets strung between trunks, great sheets pitched overhead to catch whatever flies, and monstrous spiders kept at heel like a shepherd's dogs. Where the wood goes still, look up.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-high and thin, long in the limb, with a swollen spider's head atop it.
Durability: Frail enough. It dies much as a man dies, and knows it.
Defenses: Little more than a leathery hide and a quick step; it trusts its snares, never its skin.
Speed: Brisk afoot and brisker on a wall, and it walks its own webbing as easily as level ground.
Might: Keen claws and a venomous bite whose poison unstrings the limbs and leaves a man slack and fumbling.
Mind: Dull, but cunning at craft — it lays traps a veteran poacher would envy, and it has the Common tongue.
Disposition: Cowardly and cruel, wicked by habit; it keeps monstrous spiders about it and lets them close first.
Bane: Fire. Its webbing burns twice as eagerly as anything else in that wood, and stripped of its webs it is only a nervous thing with a bad bite.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It will not meet you honestly. First the trap: a sheet you never saw until you were hanging in it. Failing that, it casts a net of web from cover to pin you where you stand, then keeps its distance while its spiders work, and closes to bite and rake only once you have stopped moving. Hurt it and it flees along the strands overhead, where you cannot follow.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Torch before sword. The webbing goes up like dry straw, and its courage goes with it.
• Look up. The killing sheet is always overhead, and the spinner is above that.
• Kill its spiders first, or you fight a whole household at once.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: It has the Common tongue, and that is precisely the trap. I have heard one calling a child's name out of a thicket in a stolen voice, plain as a neighbour over a fence. Answer nothing. Words with an ettercap are bait, never bargain; the only speech it keeps is the snare above the path.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Aberration
Initiative: +3
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares), climb 30 ft.
Armor Class: 14 (+3 Dex, +1 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 11
Base Attack/Grapple: +3/+5
Attack: Bite +5 melee (1d8+2 plus poison)
Full Attack: Bite +5 melee (1d8+2 plus poison) and 2 claws +3 melee (1d3+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Poison, web
Special Qualities: Low-light vision
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +6
Abilities: Str 14, Dex 17, Con 13, Int 6, Wis 15, Cha 8
Skills: Climb +10, Craft (trapmaking) +4, Hide +9, Listen +4, Spot +8
Feats: Great Fortitude, Multiattack
Environment: Warm forests
Organization: Solitary, pair, or troupe (1-2 plus 2-4 Medium monstrous spiders)
Challenge Rating: 3
Alignment: Usually neutral evil
Treasure: Standard
Advancement: 6-7 levels (Medium); 8-15 levels (Large)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Ettercaps are not brave creatures, but their cunning traps often ensure that the enemy never draws a weapon. When an ettercap does engage its enemies, it attacks with its keen-edged claws and venomous bite. It usually will not come within melee reach of any foe that is still able to move.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 15, initial damage 1d6 Dex, secondary damage 2d6 Dex. The save DC is Constitution based and includes a +2 racial bonus.

Web (Ex): An ettercap can throw a web eight times per day. This is similar to an attack with a net but has a maximum range of 50 feet, with a range increment of 10 feet, and is effective against targets of up to Medium size. The web anchors the target in place, allowing no movement. An entangled creature can escape with a DC 13 Escape Artist check or burst the web with a DC 17 Strength check. The check DCs are Constitution-based, and the Strength check DC includes a +4 racial bonus. The web has hardness 0, is destroyed by 6 points of damage, and takes double damage from fire. Ettercaps can also create sheets of sticky webbing from 5 to 60 feet square. They usually position these to snare flying creatures but can also try to trap prey on the ground. Approaching creatures must succeed on a DC 20 Spot check to notice a web, or they stumble into it and become trapped as though by a successful web attack. Attempts to escape or burst the webbing receive a +5 bonus if the trapped creature has something to walk on or grab while pulling free. Each 5-foot-square section has hardness 0, is destroyed by 6 points of damage, and takes double damage from fire. An ettercap can move across its own sheet web at its climb speed and can determine the exact location of any creature touching the web.

Skills: Ettercaps have a +4 racial bonus on Craft (trapmaking), Hide, and Spot checks. They have a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks and can always choose to take 10 on Climb checks, even if rushed or threatened.

lore.summary: Corpses walked by another's will. Any body with bones in it can be raised so — a commoner from a plague pit, a kobold, a troglodyte, and if the necromancer is ambitious, an ogre, a minotaur, a wyvern, a gray render. What rises is not the dead man. It is a slow grey errand in his shape, obeying whatever simple order it was given, in any land and under it.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Whatever the corpse was. Most are man-sized; the worst I have met stood as tall as an ogre and had been one.
Durability: It will not stop for pain, shock, or a wound that would drop the living, and it feels nothing you do to it.
Defenses: Dead meat closes on a thrust — points and picks sink in and accomplish little. Nothing aimed at the mind touches it: no fear, no charm, no sleep, no poison, no plague, no sapping of strength or spirit, and no cunning stroke to a vital place, for it keeps none.
Speed: Slow and stiff, and it cannot run. It either shuffles or it swings, never both, unless it comes straight at you in a charge.
Might: Cold heavy hands, stronger than the man was in life, and whatever club or blade he was still holding when he fell.
Mind: None whatever. No will, no wit, no memory of the face it is wearing.
Disposition: Wicked the way a loosed arrow is wicked. It does what it was told, in the plainest words its maker could manage.
Bane: The edge, never the point — hew it apart. And a priest with his holy symbol raised will scatter or unmake a whole shambling row of them at a stroke.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It walks at you in a straight line and swings, and that is the whole of its art. It cannot flank, cannot feint, cannot be talked into a bad position because it was never in a good one. Give ground and it can only follow or strike, not both; the danger is never one of them but the dozen behind it, and the man in the dark who counted them out.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Axe, not rapier. Hew, don't pierce — a point only makes another hole in the meat.
• Walk backwards. It must choose between coming and swinging; a patient bowman can empty a barrow alone.
• Burn the parts after. A whole corpse left lying is a gift to the next necromancer along the road.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Nothing looks out of those eyes. I have tried it — stood in a barn and spoke the name of a man I had drunk with a season before, and got the same slack hands at my throat. If you want a parley, go and find the necromancer. The corpse is only his sentence, said aloud.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor foe, alone

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead
Initiative: -1
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares; can't run)
Armor Class: 11 (-1 Dex, +2 natural), touch 9, flat-footed 11
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/+2
Attack: Slam +2 melee (1d6+1) or club +2 melee (1d6+1)
Full Attack: Slam +2 melee (1d6+1) or club +2 melee (1d6+1)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: —
Special Qualities: Single actions only, damage reduction 5/slashing, darkvision 60 ft., undead traits
Saves: Fort +0, Ref -1, Will +3
Abilities: Str 12, Dex 8, Con —, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 1
Skills: —
Feats: Toughness
Environment: Any
Organization: Any
Challenge Rating: 1/2
Alignment: Always neutral evil
Treasure: None
Advancement: None

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Reference Block: The statistics above are those of the Human Commoner Zombie, the standard example of the template. "Zombie" is an acquired template that can be added to any corporeal creature (other than an undead) that has a skeletal system. Zombies are corpses reanimated through dark and sinister magic. Because of their utter lack of intelligence, the instructions given to a newly created zombie must be very simple.

Creating a Zombie: The base creature's type changes to undead. It retains any subtypes except alignment subtypes and subtypes that indicate kind, and does not gain the augmented subtype. Drop any levels gained from character classes (to a minimum of one), then double the monster levels that remain and raise their die type to d12. A base creature with more than ten monster levels (not counting those gained through experience) cannot be made into a zombie with the animate dead spell. If the base creature can fly, its maneuverability rating drops to clumsy. Base attack bonus equals one-half the zombie's total levels; base saves are Fort +1/3, Ref +1/3, and Will +1/2 per level, with an extra +2 to Will. Strength increases by 2, Dexterity decreases by 2, the zombie has no Constitution or Intelligence score, Wisdom becomes 10, and Charisma becomes 1. A zombie has no skills, loses all of the base creature's feats and gains Toughness, and keeps none of the base creature's special attacks. It loses most special qualities, retaining only extraordinary qualities that improve its melee or ranged attacks. Environment is any land and underground; organization is any; treasure is none; alignment is always neutral evil. Advancement is as the base creature but with double the monster levels (maximum twenty), or by character class if the base creature advances that way.

Natural Armor by Size: A zombie's natural armor bonus increases according to its size: Tiny or smaller +0; Small +1; Medium +2; Large +3; Huge +4; Gargantuan +7; Colossal +11.

Slam Attack: A zombie retains all the natural weapons, manufactured weapon attacks, and weapon proficiencies of the base creature, and also gains a slam attack. Slam damage by size: Fine 1; Diminutive 1d2; Tiny 1d3; Small 1d4; Medium 1d6; Large 1d8; Huge 2d6; Gargantuan 2d8; Colossal 4d6. Use the base creature's slam damage instead if it is better. Natural and manufactured weapons deal damage normally.

Single Actions Only (Ex): Zombies have poor reflexes and can perform only a single move action or attack action each round. A zombie can move up to its speed and attack in the same round, but only if it attempts a charge.

Damage Reduction (Ex): A zombie has damage reduction 5/slashing. Zombies are lumbering masses of flesh.

Undead Traits: A zombie has no Constitution score and darkvision out to 60 feet. It is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects), and to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, and death effects. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability drain, or energy drain, and is immune to damage to its physical ability scores as well as to fatigue and exhaustion. Because it has no Intelligence score it cannot heal damage on its own, though it can be healed by others, and negative energy such as an inflict spell heals it. It is immune to any effect requiring a Fortitude save unless that effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not at risk of death from massive damage, but is destroyed outright once its wounds overwhelm it. It is not affected by raise dead or reincarnate; resurrection and true resurrection turn it back into the living creature it was. Zombies do not breathe, eat, or sleep.

Challenge Rating: A zombie's Challenge Rating depends on its total levels: one-half level, CR 1/8; 1 level, CR 1/4; 2 levels, CR 1/2; 4 levels, CR 1; 6 levels, CR 2; 8-10 levels, CR 3; 12-14 levels, CR 4; 15-16 levels, CR 5; 18-20 levels, CR 6.

Sample Zombies: Kobold zombie: Small, CR 1/2, slam +1 melee (1d4-1). Human commoner zombie: Medium, CR 1/2, slam +2 melee (1d6+1). Troglodyte zombie: Medium, CR 1, slam +3 melee (1d6+1). Bugbear zombie: Medium, CR 2, slam +6 melee (1d6+3). Ogre zombie: Large, CR 3, slam +9 melee (1d8+9). Minotaur zombie: Large, CR 4, slam +10 melee (1d8+5). Wyvern zombie: Large, CR 4, slam +11 melee (2d6+7); it keeps a fly speed of 60 ft. (poor). Gray render zombie: Large, CR 6, slam +16 melee (1d8+10). Every one of them shares the same package: single actions only, damage reduction 5/slashing, darkvision 60 ft., undead traits, no skills, and Toughness.

lore.summary: Not a beast but a weather. A swarm is a mass of small hungers moving as one body and fought as one foe: spiders in the warm forests, rats in any cellar, bats out of the desert dark, centipedes underground, locusts over the plains, and hellwasps that come from a wicked plane and are worse than all of them together. It pours through any gap one of its number could pass.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Each creature small enough to crush under a thumb; together they fill a corner of a room and shape themselves to whatever they must cross.
Durability: You cannot stab a cloud. Blade, arrow and haft pass through and kill almost nothing — save among rats and their like, which are big enough that cut and thrust take some little toll.
Defenses: No throat, no flank, no vital place; a spell shaped for a single foe finds nothing to fasten on. The hellwasps go further, shrugging off common steel and caring little for flame.
Speed: As quick as a walking man where it crawls, quicker still on walls, and quickest of all where it takes to the air.
Might: It does not strike, it covers you, and every part of it bites at once. Spiders and centipedes and hellwasps carry venom, rats carry a filthy fever, and a bat cloud leaves you bleeding until the wound is bound.
Mind: Witless vermin, most of them. The hellwasps are the exception: while the mass is thick they think together with a cold infernal cunning, and thin them and the wit simply goes out.
Disposition: Hungry, and nothing else. It surrounds whatever lives and stays until it is scattered or sated. The hellwasps hate, which is far worse.
Bane: Fire, and anything that fills a space rather than seeking a target — a flask of oil, a swung torch, a lantern thrown to break at their feet, a wizard's burst. Such things bite the whole mass at once, and harder than they would a single foe.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes into the space you are standing in and crawls over every inch of you, and there is no parrying that. Standing in it turns the stomach so badly that a man can scarcely lift his arms, which is how most die: retching while it eats them. It cannot be grappled, tripped, or held, and it will not punish you for walking away — so walk, and throw fire from where it is not.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Oil and a torch. Steel is for whatever sent it.
• Don't stand and swing. It has to be on you to hurt you, and it cannot hold you there — move, then burn the space you left.
• If a man's skin crawls beneath his shirt, he is not a man any more. Hellwasps wear the helpless and the dead alike.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: I do not parley with weather. There is nothing behind those thousand eyes to take an offer, and a swarm has never once heard a word I said. The hellwasp cloud alone could answer — and it answers in the voice of the dead man it is wearing, which is reason enough not to stay and hear it out.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser terror, and a swift one

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Diminutive Vermin (Swarm)
Initiative: +3
Speed: 20 ft. (4 squares), climb 20 ft.
Armor Class: 17 (+4 size, +3 Dex), touch 17, flat-footed 14
Base Attack/Grapple: +1/—
Attack: Swarm (1d6 plus poison)
Full Attack: Swarm (1d6 plus poison)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./0 ft.
Special Attacks: Distraction, poison
Special Qualities: Darkvision 60 ft., immune to weapon damage, swarm traits, tremorsense 30 ft., vermin traits
Saves: Fort +3, Ref +3, Will +0
Abilities: Str 1, Dex 17, Con 10, Int —, Wis 10, Cha 2
Skills: Climb +11, Listen +4, Spot +4
Feats: —
Environment: Warm forests
Organization: Solitary, tangle (2-4 swarms), or colony (7-12 swarms)
Challenge Rating: 1
Alignment: Always neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: None

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Reference Block: The statistics above are those of the Spider Swarm, the standard example of the form. A swarm is a dense mass of Fine, Diminutive, or Tiny creatures that would not be dangerous in small groups but is a terrible foe in sufficient numbers. For game purposes a swarm is a single creature with a space of 10 feet; gigantic hordes are actually many swarms in close proximity. The swarm's type varies with the nature of the component creature (most are animals or vermin), but every swarm has the swarm subtype.

Combat: A spider swarm seeks to surround and attack any living prey it encounters. A swarm deals 1d6 points of damage to any creature whose space it occupies at the end of its move. To attack, a swarm moves into an opponent's space, which provokes an attack of opportunity. It can occupy the same space as a creature of any size, since it crawls all over its prey, but it remains a creature with a 10-foot space. Swarms never make attacks of opportunity, though they can provoke them. Unlike other creatures with a 10-foot space, a swarm is shapeable: it can occupy any four contiguous squares, and it can squeeze through any space large enough to contain one of its component creatures.

Distraction (Ex): Any living creature that begins its turn with a spider swarm in its space must succeed on a DC 11 Fortitude save or be nauseated for 1 round. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Poison (Ex): Injury, Fortitude DC 11, initial and secondary damage 1d3 Str. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Skills: A spider swarm has a +4 racial bonus on Hide and Spot checks and a +8 racial bonus on Climb checks. It uses its Dexterity modifier instead of its Strength modifier for Climb checks. It can always choose to take 10 on a Climb check, even if rushed or threatened.

Swarm Attack: Creatures with the swarm subtype do not make standard melee attacks. Instead they deal automatic damage to any creature whose space they occupy at the end of their move, with no attack roll needed, and swarm attacks are not subject to a miss chance for concealment or cover. The stat block lists "swarm" in the Attack and Full Attack entries with no attack bonus. Damage scales with the swarm's power: 1d6 for a weak swarm, rising through 2d6, 3d6 and 4d6 to 5d6 for the mightiest. A swarm's attacks are nonmagical unless its description says otherwise, so damage reduction sufficient to reduce a swarm attack to nothing, being incorporeal, and similar defences usually grant immunity or resistance. Swarms do not threaten creatures in their square and do not make attacks of opportunity.

Swarm Traits: A swarm has no clear front or back and no discernable anatomy, so it is not subject to critical hits or flanking. A swarm made up of Tiny creatures takes half damage from slashing and piercing weapons; one composed of Fine or Diminutive creatures is immune to all weapon damage. Once its wounds overwhelm it a swarm simply breaks up, though damage taken until that point does not degrade its ability to attack or resist attack. Swarms are never staggered or reduced to a dying state by damage, and they cannot be tripped, grappled or bull rushed, nor can they grapple an opponent. A swarm is immune to any spell or effect that targets a specific number of creatures, with the exception of mind-affecting effects if the swarm has an Intelligence score and a hive mind, and it takes half again as much damage (+50%) from spells or effects that affect an area. Swarms of Diminutive or Fine creatures are susceptible to high winds such as a gust of wind spell, treating the swarm as a creature of the same size as its constituent creatures. A swarm knocked out by nonlethal damage becomes disorganized and dispersed and does not re-form until it has recovered from that nonlethal damage.

Vulnerabilities of Swarms: Swarms are extremely difficult to fight with physical attacks, but they have a few special vulnerabilities. A lit torch swung as an improvised weapon deals 1d3 points of fire damage per hit. A weapon with a special ability such as flaming or frost deals its full energy damage with each hit, even if the weapon's normal damage cannot affect the swarm. A lit lantern can be thrown, dealing 1d4 points of fire damage to all creatures in squares adjacent to where it breaks.

Other Swarms: Bat swarm: Diminutive Animal (Swarm), CR 2, swarm 1d6 plus wounding, distraction DC 11, blindsense 20 ft., fly 40 ft. (good); anything it damages keeps bleeding for 1 point per round until stopped by a DC 10 Heal check or any cure spell. Rat swarm: Tiny Animal (Swarm), CR 2, swarm 1d6 plus disease, distraction DC 12, scent, climb 15 ft.; its bite carries filth fever (Fortitude DC 12, incubation 1d3 days, damage 1d3 Dex and 1d3 Con), and being made of Tiny creatures it takes half damage from slashing and piercing weapons instead of ignoring weapons entirely. Centipede swarm: Diminutive Vermin (Swarm), CR 4, swarm 2d6 plus poison, distraction DC 13, tremorsense 30 ft., climb 20 ft.; poison is injury, Fortitude DC 13, initial and secondary damage 1d4 Dex. (good); poison is injury, Fortitude DC 18, initial and secondary damage 1d6 Dex, its attacks count as evil-aligned magic weapons, a hive mind gives the intact swarm an Intelligence of 6, and it can inhabit a helpless or dead body over 1 minute to puppet it, dealing 2d4 Constitution damage per hour to a living host until a remove disease or heal spell drives it out. Note that bat and rat swarms are Animals in the SRD, not Vermin, and so are not mindless in the way spider, centipede and locust swarms are.

lore.summary: Lycanthropy is a sickness of people, not of beasts, and the werewolf is its cruellest strain. A man or a woman wears three shapes: his own, a heavy grey wolf, and the shaggy-shouldered thing that stands between them. Born to it or bitten into it, he keeps the temperate forests, and true wolves run at his heel.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized in all three shapes — the wolf is only a large and heavy wolf, and the between-shape stands as a tall man stands.
Durability: As hardy as a seasoned warrior, and it does not tire the way a warrior does.
Defenses: In wolf or between-shape, honest steel closes on it and does almost nothing; silver alone bites true. In its own skin it is merely a man, and dies like one.
Speed: Very swift on four legs — it will run down a horse over broken ground — and no slower than a man on two.
Might: Jaws that fell a standing man and worry him on the ground; in the between-shape, claws and teeth together, or a weapon in a hand that still works.
Mind: A man's wits kept whole beneath the fur. It plans, it lies, it lays ambush, and it remembers a face.
Disposition: Cruel and lawless without exception. It kills for the pleasure of killing, and passes on its curse to have company in it.
Bane: Silver, and nothing else. For one freshly bitten, belladonna eaten within the hour — the herb is poison in its own right, so warn the poor soul first — or the removing of curses spoken over him on one of the three days of the full moon. That mercy works only on the afflicted; one born to the curse can never be cured of it.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It picks the shape that suits the ground: a wolf among dark trees, the between-shape when it means to hold a doorway. On four legs it lunges low, takes the legs and drags a man down for the pack to finish; in the between-shape it fights claw, claw and bite, and will keep a blade in hand out of pure malice. It knows ordinary weapons cannot hurt it, and fights without fear until silver comes out. Wounded, it does not withdraw — it circles and comes again from the dark.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver, or nothing. A silvered dagger in the boot has saved me more often than my sword ever did.
• Belladonna within the hour, or the bite keeps. The herb may cripple the man you are saving; tell him the price before he swallows.
• The one you are hunting may be asleep in a farmhouse bed, guilty of nothing he can remember. Ask, before you burn.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, and I mean wary. The wits are a man's, the tongue is a man's, the appetite is a wolf's. I once bought a night's passage from a pack-leader with a heifer and two casks of ale. He kept the bargain until dawn, then came for us anyway. Talk, if you must — but talk while you are backing towards the light.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor peril

Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft.
Special Attacks: Curse of lycanthropy

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Other Forms: The block above is the hybrid shape. In human form the werewolf is Medium, initiative +0, speed 30 ft., Armor Class 17 (+2 natural, +4 chain shirt, +1 light shield), touch 10, flat-footed 17; it fights with a longsword +3 melee (1d8+1/19-20) or a light crossbow +2 ranged (1d8/19-20), has Str 13, Dex 11, Con 12, saves Fort +6, Ref +3, Will +2, and carries no damage reduction. In wolf form it is Medium, initiative +6, speed 50 ft., Armor Class 16 (+2 Dex, +4 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 14, and attacks with a bite +5 melee (1d6+3) that can trip; it has damage reduction 10/silver, Str 15, Dex 15, Con 16, and saves Fort +8, Ref +5, Will +2. Werewolves in human shape have no distinguishing traits.

Alternate Form (Su): A werewolf can assume the form of a wolf or a bipedal wolf-humanoid hybrid. Changing to or from animal or hybrid form is a standard action. A slain lycanthrope reverts to its humanoid shape, although it remains dead; severed body parts keep their animal form. Natural lycanthropes have full control over this power; afflicted ones find it difficult to command.

Curse of Lycanthropy (Su): Any humanoid or giant struck by a werewolf's bite attack in animal or hybrid form must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or contract lycanthropy. A victim whose size is not within one size category of the lycanthrope cannot catch the curse from it. Only natural lycanthropes pass on the curse; afflicted lycanthropes cannot.

Trip (Ex): A werewolf in wolf form that hits with its bite may attempt to trip the opponent (+2 check modifier) as a free action without making a touch attack and without provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react by trying to trip the werewolf.

Damage Reduction (Ex): In animal or hybrid form a natural lycanthrope has damage reduction 10/silver; an afflicted lycanthrope has damage reduction 5/silver. The samples given here are natural lycanthropes. In humanoid form a lycanthrope has no damage reduction at all — steel bites it as it bites any person.

Wolf Empathy (Ex): In any form the lycanthrope can communicate and empathize with wolves and dire wolves, conveying simple concepts and — if the animal is friendly — commands such as "friend," "foe," "flee," and "attack." It also gains a +4 racial bonus on Charisma-based checks made to influence them.

Lycanthrope Traits (Ex): A lycanthrope keeps the type of its base creature and gains the shapechanger subtype. In every one of its three shapes it has low-light vision, the scent ability, and a +2 bonus to natural armor, and it receives Iron Will as a bonus feat. It also keeps the skills, feats, and special qualities of both the person and the beast, using whichever set fits the shape it currently wears.

Skills: A werewolf in wolf or hybrid form gains a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent.

Afflicted and Natural Lycanthropes: A natural lycanthrope is born to the curse and commands its shapes at will. An afflicted lycanthrope caught the curse from a bite: no symptom shows until the first night of the next full moon, when it changes involuntarily, forgets its own identity, and acts by the alignment of its animal form until dawn. It recalls nothing of the episode unless it succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom check, in which case it becomes aware of its condition. Thereafter it transforms involuntarily under the full moon and whenever it is wounded in combat unless it succeeds on a Control Shape check. Each change to animal form forces a Will save (DC 15 + the number of times it has already worn the beast) or the animal's alignment becomes its own permanently, in all shapes; any voluntary change to animal or hybrid form makes that alignment change at once.

A victim who eats a sprig of belladonna (wolfsbane) within 1 hour of the attack may attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save to shake off the affliction — one attempt only, and the herb must have been picked within the last week. Otherwise only remove curse or break enchantment cast during one of the three days of the full moon will serve, followed by a DC 20 Will save by the victim; if the save fails the whole process must be repeated. Those undergoing the cure are commonly kept bound or caged until it takes.

lore.summary: In the cold forests, where the pines go on for days, there are folk who also wear a bear's shape. Stout, bearded, thick-haired, dressed in plain stuff that is easy to shed — they keep the wild places, they hold to their given word, and of everything in this book they stand highest on the list of things I would rather have at my back than before me.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A broad man in his own skin; in bear shape and in the between-shape, a great deal larger — head and shoulders above any of us, and reaching further than you judge.
Durability: Enormously tough and slow to tire. It will outlast your whole company and be fresh at the end of it.
Defenses: A hide that turns ordinary weapons in bear or between-shape — silver alone gets through. It swims strongly besides, which matters more often than you would think in that country.
Speed: Lumbering to the eye, faster than it looks, and it simply does not stop coming.
Might: Terrible. In bear shape it catches a man in both forepaws and holds him, and a man held is a man finished. In the between-shape it swings a great axe one-handed and claws and bites around it.
Mind: Sound sense, long memory, plain honesty. It speaks as a man speaks, because it is one.
Disposition: Lawful and good, without a single exception in my experience. It guards its forest, its family and its promises. Provoke it and you are in the wrong, and it will know that you are.
Bane: Silver, if it ever comes to that — and it should not; the better weapon is an apology. Remember that its bite passes the curse even when it wishes you no harm: belladonna within the hour, or the removing of curses at the full moon, and only for the afflicted.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not start fights, and it ends them quickly. In bear shape it closes the distance, hooks you with a forepaw and grapples, and a man in a bear's arms goes nowhere; in the between-shape it keeps a great axe working in one hand and uses claws and teeth with the rest. It fights to drive you off rather than to kill, gives ground it does not need, and will let you go the moment you go. Should you press it past that, it stops being merciful and there is no second warning.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• If a werebear tells you to leave the valley, leave the valley. He is right and you are not.
• They take care not to bite, because they know what the bite carries. Do not make one bite you.
• Bring salt, iron nails and good thread. Better currency in the northern pines than coin ever was.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Open, and gladly. The one cursed kind I name friend. Old Hafgrim in the northern pines has fed me, splinted my arm and walked me out of a storm, and asked only that I leave his elk be. Come in daylight, weapons slung, and say plainly who you are and what you want.

sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

lore.summary: Down in the wet dark beneath any city of size, the wererat keeps his own counsel. In his own skin he is a thin, wiry man with darting eyes and a ragged moustache; as a great rat he is a grey shadow along a rafter; between the two he walks upright with a rapier in his fist. They are found anywhere men are, and they keep guilds, ledgers and grudges.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A man of less than common height, and a rat rather smaller than a man — but the between-shape stands full man-height.
Durability: Slight. One stout blow ends it, provided the blow lands and the blade is the right metal.
Defenses: In rat or between-shape, honest steel scarcely marks it; silver undoes that at once. Add that it climbs anything it can get a claw into and swims the sewers happily — defence enough, most nights.
Speed: Quick on two legs, quicker on four, and it goes up a wall as easily as it walks a floor.
Might: Little strength of its own. Its harm lies in a rapier, a light crossbow shot from a dark gallery, and the filth in its teeth.
Mind: Sharp, patient and orderly. These are the ones who keep written accounts of the people they have ruined.
Disposition: Lawful in the worst manner — organised, oath-bound to its own kind, and wicked to everyone else. It would far rather watch, spy and extort than fight you.
Bane: Silver, and light. Take away the dark and the low roof and half its courage goes with them. For the bitten: belladonna within the hour, or the removing of curses at the full moon, and only for the afflicted.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not want the fight. In rat shape it is there to listen and to slip away, not to bite; forced to it, it takes the between-shape, keeps the rapier moving and the crossbow loaded, and works the ceiling beams and the drain mouths so that you are always the one standing in the open. Its teeth carry a foul wasting fever on top of the curse, so even a small wound is a debt that comes due days later. Press it hard and it pours itself into a hole no man can follow.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver — even a silvered eating knife. They know the difference the instant you draw it.
• The bite gives two gifts: the curse and a filthy fever. Wash the wound out first, then take the herb.
• Never chase one into the drains. Wait at the outfall with a lamp; they hate an open sky worse than they hate you.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary — yet of all the cursed kinds these are the likeliest to deal honestly, because a bargain is worth coin to them. I bought a map of an under-city from a guild's ratcatcher, paid in silver he could not bear to touch and carried in a purse instead. He honoured it to the letter. He also had me followed for a month.

lore.summary: Out where the temperate forest meets the last of the farms, and nobody is friendly, you find the wereboar. A stocky, short-tempered soul who goes about as a man, as a great tusked boar, or as a bristled thing upright between the two. He is not wicked. He is simply the worst neighbour you will ever have, and he was there before the fences were.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-sized in all three shapes — a heavy, thick-set man and a heavy, thick-set boar.
Durability: Very hardy, and worse than that: hurt it past the point where a man would fall and it keeps fighting as though nothing had happened to it at all.
Defenses: Ordinary steel means little against the boar and the between-shape; silver does not. Nothing else about it is armoured but muscle and bristle, and whatever mail it was wearing when it changed.
Speed: Trots faster than you expect on four legs; on two it is no swifter than a man in mail.
Might: Tusks. It gores, and with this kind alone it is the gore rather than the bite that carries the curse.
Mind: Plain wits, plain speech, no cunning worth the name, and a temper with no fuse on it whatever.
Disposition: Neither good nor wicked — territorial, proud, and quick to take offence. Most of the killing it does began as an argument that went too far.
Bane: Silver, and its own temper: it will charge a braced spear rather than give ground. For those it has gored, belladonna within the hour, or the removing of curses at the full moon, and only for the afflicted.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It charges. That is most of the plan and nearly all of the subtlety. In boar shape it comes head-down through the undergrowth and tries to open you from hip to ribs; in the between-shape it keeps a heavy weapon in its hands and still puts the tusks in. Wounds do not slow it — a wereboar goes on fighting long after it should be lying down, and good men die because they stopped guarding something they had judged finished.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It keeps fighting after it ought to be dead. Do not turn your back on one to loot.
• The tusks carry the curse, not the teeth. Being bitten is the least of your troubles.
• Ask what the quarrel was. Half the time you can settle it with a pig and an apology.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary, but far from hopeless. A wereboar will talk if you speak first, keep your hand off your hilt and do not stand upon his ground. I shared a fire with one over a boundary stone and we settled it; he walked me back to the road himself. His brother tried to gore me a fortnight later over the very same stone.

sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.body:

Alternate Form (Su): A wereboar can assume the form of a boar or a bipedal boar-humanoid hybrid. Changing to or from animal or hybrid form is a standard action. A slain lycanthrope reverts to its humanoid shape, although it remains dead; severed body parts keep their animal form. Natural lycanthropes have full control over this power; afflicted ones find it difficult to command.

Curse of Lycanthropy (Su): Any humanoid or giant struck by a wereboar's gore attack in animal or hybrid form must succeed on a DC 15 Fortitude save or contract lycanthropy. A victim whose size is not within one size category of the lycanthrope cannot catch the curse from it. Only natural lycanthropes pass on the curse; afflicted lycanthropes cannot.

Ferocity (Ex): A wereboar is so tenacious a combatant that it fights on without penalty even while disabled or dying.

Damage Reduction (Ex): In animal or hybrid form a natural lycanthrope has damage reduction 10/silver; an afflicted lycanthrope has damage reduction 5/silver. The samples given here are natural lycanthropes. In humanoid form a lycanthrope has no damage reduction at all — steel bites it as it bites any person.

Boar Empathy (Ex): In any form the lycanthrope can communicate and empathize with boars and dire boars, conveying simple concepts and — if the animal is friendly — commands such as "friend," "foe," "flee," and "attack." It also gains a +4 racial bonus on Charisma-based checks made to influence them.

Lycanthrope Traits (Ex): A lycanthrope keeps the type of its base creature and gains the shapechanger subtype. In every one of its three shapes it has low-light vision, the scent ability, and a +2 bonus to natural armor, and it receives Iron Will as a bonus feat. It also keeps the skills, feats, and special qualities of both the person and the beast, using whichever set fits the shape it currently wears.

Combat: In any shape wereboars are as ferocious as ordinary boars. In hybrid form they fight with a weapon and their dangerous gore attack; note that it is the gore, not a bite, that carries the curse.

Afflicted and Natural Lycanthropes: A natural lycanthrope is born to the curse and commands its shapes at will. An afflicted lycanthrope caught the curse from a bite: no symptom shows until the first night of the next full moon, when it changes involuntarily, forgets its own identity, and acts by the alignment of its animal form until dawn. lore.summary: Warm forests, alone or in pairs, and always at a distance. The weretiger is a tall, sleek, unhurried person who is also a tiger and also the thing between the two. Proud past all reason, and wholly certain that the wood belongs to it. You will not see one until it has already decided whether you are worth the trouble.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Tall and lithe as a person; as a tiger, and in the between-shape, a good deal larger than any man and longer in the reach.
Durability: Strong and enduring, though not so mulish about it as a bear or a boar.
Defenses: Silver, or nothing — ordinary blades scarcely trouble it in cat or between-shape. Add a stillness in cover that comes very near to invisibility, and in tall grass it is worse still.
Speed: Fast, and worse than fast: quiet. It crosses tall grass without moving the grass.
Might: It springs the whole distance and lands with everything at once — claws, claws and teeth — takes hold, and rakes with the hind feet while it has you down.
Mind: Clever, vain and given to long silences. It thinks carefully about what it is doing, which is more than most quarry can manage.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor kind. Territory and pride govern it entirely. It will let a respectful traveller pass and kill an insolent one for the insolence alone.
Bane: Silver, open ground and daylight. Deny it cover and you have taken half of it away. For the bitten: belladonna within the hour, or the removing of curses at the full moon, and only for the afflicted.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hunts rather than fights. It circles, chooses its moment, and comes out of the cover in one leap that arrives as a whole flurry of blows — you are struck, gripped, dragged down and opened by the hind claws in the same breath. The spring and the raking belong to the cat shape alone; in the between-shape it stands and works with its claws instead, and will carry a weapon if the mood takes it. Ordinary steel gives no answer, and it knows that perfectly well.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver, and stand where the grass is short. In cover you are not the hunter.
• The leap comes from behind and above. Watch the branches, not the path.
• Praise the forest, never the tiger. Flattery it can smell; respect it cannot.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary. It has every wit you have and none of your hurry. Stand still, speak first, do not look away, and offer to leave. I have talked my way out of a weretiger's clearing twice; the second time she asked after the first one by name, and I understood I had been let go both times as a courtesy.

lore.summary: Break a bargain you swore freely and, some day, a courteous figure in banded mail will greet you by name. The kolyarut is law wearing clockwork flesh — gold and silver, gears where a man has sinew, eyes lit from within. It comes for oath-breakers, often carrying a copy of the broken contract, and it never sets the trail down.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Man-high and dressed like a man of rank — heavy mail, a cloak, a good sword at the hip.
Durability: Wrought metal that mends itself as you watch; the wound you gave it is closing before your next swing.
Defenses: Gold-chased plate and clockwork turn honest steel aside, and a great many spells simply slide off it unfelt.
Speed: Unhurried, and slowed by its own armour — but it walks while you sleep, and it knows where you are going.
Might: A touch that draws the life out of a man and pours it into the machine, a black ray at bowshot that leaves you hollow and weak, and a swordarm past any duellist's.
Mind: It thinks, learns and remembers. The most talkative of its kin: it will greet you properly, name your oath, and hear your answer before it moves.
Disposition: Fixed wholly upon the oath-breaker and nobody else. Bystanders it steps around — but those who sheltered its quarry it counts as party to the crime.
Bane: Chaos. A weapon of riot and misrule cuts it truly and those cuts are slow to knit; nothing else lastingly marks it. Failing that, settle the debt — it can commute a sentence, and would rather see the wronged party made whole than see you dead.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It studies you first — wearing another face, in your own tavern, sometimes for weeks. Then it walks in unseen and tries to end the matter in a breath, laying that life-stealing hand on you before you know it stands there. Denied surprise, it works at range with the hollowing ray, nails the room down with terror and holdings, and will happily drain one of your own companions to feed itself. It fights to finish, not to make a spectacle, and it does not linger over the dead.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• It knows your face before you know its name. Assume it has watched you a fortnight.
• Nothing dull and lawful will bite. Bring a chaos-touched blade, or bring an apology.
• It will drink a friend of yours to heal itself. Fight it spread wide, or do not fight it.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Speak — but do not lie, for it hears falsehood the way you hear a shout. One met me on the coast road and named a bargain I had struck drunk and forgotten. It heard me out. Offer to make the wronged party whole and it may take that instead of your life, though it will lay a binding on you to be sure of you.

sections.body: Dire — A dire reckoning

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Enervation Ray (Su): A kolyarut can fire a black enervation ray at targets within 200 feet. The effect is identical with the enervation spell (caster level 13th), draining levels from the creature it strikes.

Vampiric Touch (Su): As a melee touch attack, a kolyarut can steal life force from its foe, as the vampiric touch spell (caster level 13th), dealing 5d6 damage and taking that stolen vigour into itself as temporary vitality. A kolyarut has no compunctions about using this ability on its own allies to strengthen itself, if doing so helps it complete its mission.

Disguise Self (Sp): A kolyarut can use disguise self at will to appear as almost any kind of humanoid — useful when it must go undercover to reach its quarry. Paired with invisibility, this is its favourite opening: walk in unremarked, then finish the deal-breaker with a vampiric touch before it can react. It has a +4 racial bonus on Disguise checks.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will — discern lies (DC 17), disguise self, fear (DC 17), hold person (DC 16), invisibility, locate creature, suggestion (DC 16); 1/day — hold monster (DC 17), mark of justice; 1/week — geas/quest. Caster level 13th. The save DCs are Charisma-based. Its Quickened Spell-Like Ability feat lets it cast suggestion as a swift action.

Fast Healing (Ex): A kolyarut heals 5 points of damage each round for as long as it has not yet been destroyed. Damage dealt by chaotic weapons, however, heals only at the normal rate.

Construct Traits: An inevitable is a construct. It has no Constitution score and is never fatigued or exhausted. It is immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, morale effects, patterns and phantasms), and to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and necromancy. It is immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, ability drain, energy drain, or damage to its physical ability scores. It cannot heal wounds on its own (though the inevitables' fast healing does so for them), and it is destroyed outright once its wounds overcome it, leaving nothing that raise dead or resurrection can restore. It does not eat, sleep or breathe. It has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision. Unlike most constructs, an inevitable has an Intelligence score and can think, learn and remember.

Lawful Weapons (Ex): An inevitable's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Skills: A kolyarut has a +4 racial bonus on Disguise, Gather Information, and Sense Motive checks.

lore.summary: The grave sends a collector. Taller than any man, plated in gold and iron, bald as a bell and perfectly calm, the marut walks toward those who have bought themselves years they were never owed — liches, the deathless, all who keep cheating the ferryman. It does not run and it does not rest. It arrives, and it brings with it the death you dodged.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Half again the height of a tall man and broad as a doorway, in full plate the colour of old coin.
Durability: Immense, and it knits itself whole faster than most companies can wound it.
Defenses: Armour and clockwork hide turn all but the fiercest steel, and it shrugs off sorcery that would fell a giant.
Speed: Steady rather than swift afoot — but it walks upon the air, steps through space at a whim, and will follow you to another world.
Might: Two fists like falling towers: the left bursts with thunder and leaves you deaf, the right with lightning and leaves you blind. Beyond them it calls down forked storm, a ring of killing dark, walls of hard air, and the shudder of the earth itself.
Mind: Clever and lettered, deep in the lore of gods and graves. It judges before it strikes and can be reasoned with, briefly.
Disposition: Implacable and without heat. It has one name to collect and no interest in yours; those who merely defile the dead may earn a binding and a brand rather than a killing.
Bane: Chaos-forged arms, and little else. After that, dispersal — stand clustered and its ring of dark and its lightning take the whole company in one stroke.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It shuts the doors first, walling every road out with hard air, then opens with forked lightning as it closes the ground. In reach it simply hits you: thunder in one hand, storm in the other, deafening and blinding as it works. Crowd it and a ring of killing dark falls over the lot of you. Against spellcasters it strips wards methodically until they stand bare. Run, and it finds you by sorcery and steps after you — through walls, through worlds.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• If a marut is on your patron's trail, ask what he has been drinking these past years. Then leave him.
• Never bunch up. Its ring of dark and its lightning both love a crowd.
• Deaf in one round and blind in the next is how good hunters die. Stopper your ears and learn to fight by feel.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: You may speak with it; it is lettered and courteous in its cold way. But there is only one plea it truly hears — that you never bought a year you were not owed. I watched a hedge-necromancer argue his case for the better part of an hour and walk away branded, bound and breathing. That is more than most manage.

lore.summary: Flee a lawful sentence and one day you will hear hoofbeats on ground that carries no horse. The zelekhut is built in the shape of a centaur, gold and silver and faceless, and at first sight it looks almost harmless — until spiked chains spring from its forearms and golden wings unfold from its back. It hunts fugitives from justice, and it is very good at finding them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Horse-bodied and man-torsoed, taller than a rider and heavier than the horse he sits.
Durability: Hard-wrought and self-mending; open it and the metal closes over while you watch.
Defenses: Barded head to flank in gold plate, proof against ordinary arms, and difficult to touch with magic.
Speed: Faster than a good horse on the road and faster still on the wing — and it seals the sky and the roads behind you both before it shows itself.
Might: Twin spiked chains that leap out of its arms crackling with lightning. It prefers to trip, disarm and bind, but it can break a man in half if the man insists.
Mind: It thinks and remembers, tracks by skill and by sorcery together, and sees through every glamour, shadow and borrowed face you own.
Disposition: Cold, correct, set upon one runaway. It holds your friends still rather than killing them and steps carefully around the innocent — and it would far rather take you living, to answer to the court that sentenced you.
Bane: Chaos-forged steel, and nothing else worth the name. Do not run and do not hide: settle with the magistrate, or make your stand somewhere it cannot use the air.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It arrives with the exits already covered — a listening ear laid on your bolt-holes, a sealing that ruins any escape by magic — then comes in on the wing. It frightens or freezes whoever stands between, takes care not to spill the innocent, and closes on the fugitive with both chains, tripping and disarming rather than killing. Charge past it and it charges back, weight and speed and chain together, and that is a blow you feel through your boots.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• You cannot hide from it. Glamours, shadow, a borrowed face — it sees the man underneath.
• It shuts the way out before it lets you see it. If you mean to run, run early.
• Rushing it earns you both chains at once. Let it come to you, and fight it under a low roof.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk is possible; surrender is better. It bears no malice and feels no hurry, and its charge is to deliver the guilty to a court, not to a grave. I asked one to let a boy answer to the magistrate rather than to itself. It agreed — then branded him, so that he could not run a second time.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Large Construct (Extraplanar, Lawful)
Initiative: +0
Speed: 35 ft. in plate barding (7 squares), fly 40 ft. (average) in plate barding (8 squares); base speed 50 ft., fly 60 ft. (average)
Armor Class: 27 (–1 size, +10 natural, +8 plate barding), touch 9, flat-footed 27
Base Attack/Grapple: +6/+15
Attack: Spiked chain +10 melee (2d6+5 plus 1d6 electricity)
Full Attack: 2 spiked chains +10 melee (2d6+5 plus 1d6 electricity)
Space/Reach: 10 ft./10 ft.
Special Attacks: Spell-like abilities
Special Qualities: Construct traits, damage reduction 10/chaotic, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 5, low-light vision, spell resistance 20
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +2, Will +5
Abilities: Str 21, Dex 11, Con —, Int 10, Wis 17, Cha 15
Skills: Diplomacy +4, Listen +9, Search +9, Sense Motive +12, Spot +9, Survival +3 (+5 following tracks)
Feats: Great Fortitude, Ride-By Attack, Spirited Charge
Environment: A lawful-aligned plane
Organization: Solitary
Challenge Rating: 9
Alignment: Always lawful neutral
Treasure: None
Advancement: 9–16 levels (Large); 17–24 levels (Huge)

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spiked Chains and Wings (Ex): A zelekhut may initially appear rather non-threatening — but when it is about to enter combat it can cause two spiked chains to spring forth from its forearms as a free action. In similar fashion it can cause a pair of golden metallic wings to emerge from its back, granting it flight. Retracting the chains or the wings is also a free action. In battle it apprehends its fugitive with the chains, tripping or disarming as needed.

Spell-Like Abilities: At will — clairaudience/clairvoyance, dimensional anchor, dispel magic, fear (DC 16), hold person (DC 15), locate creature, true seeing; 3/day — hold monster (DC 17), mark of justice; 1/week — lesser geas (DC 16). Caster level 8th. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Fast Healing (Ex): A zelekhut heals 5 points of damage each round for as long as it has not yet been destroyed. Damage dealt by chaotic weapons, however, heals only at the normal rate.

Construct Traits: An inevitable is a construct. It has no Constitution score and is never fatigued or exhausted. It is immune to mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, morale effects, patterns and phantasms), and to poison, sleep effects, paralysis, stunning, disease, death effects and necromancy. It is immune to any effect that requires a Fortitude save unless the effect also works on objects or is harmless. It is not subject to critical hits, nonlethal damage, ability damage, ability drain, energy drain, or damage to its physical ability scores. It cannot heal wounds on its own (though the inevitables' fast healing does so for them), and it is destroyed outright once its wounds overcome it, leaving nothing that raise dead or resurrection can restore. It does not eat, sleep or breathe. It has darkvision 60 ft. and low-light vision. Unlike most constructs, an inevitable has an Intelligence score and can think, learn and remember.

Lawful Weapons (Ex): An inevitable's natural weapons, as well as any weapons it wields, are treated as lawful-aligned for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Skills: A zelekhut has a +4 racial bonus on Search and Sense Motive checks.

Feats: Due to its centaur-like construction, a zelekhut qualifies for feats as if it had the Mounted Combat feat.

lore.summary: In the burning wastes of the fire-plane, things drift on the heat like carrion birds. A rast is a hovering horror with a head near as large as its body, fringed underneath by clawed limbs it never once sets on the ground — more of them than it can ever use at once. Its stare stops the blood; then it fastens on and drinks. Where one drifts, others are usually near.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: A body about the bulk of a big hound, with a head nearly as large again, and a hanging fringe of claws below.
Durability: Middling. It is a predator, not a fortress, and a solid blow tells on it.
Defenses: A tough hide and nothing more. Its safety lies in the air and in the stare, not in armour.
Speed: Wretched on the ground — it barely creeps — but it flies well and nimbly, and it would rather never come down at all.
Might: Raking claws or a heavy bite, never both in the same breath. Once its jaws are set it clamps on and drinks the blood out of you while you lie stiff and awake.
Mind: Little more than a clever animal. No speech, no bargains, no cunning worth the name — only appetite.
Disposition: A pure predator. It freezes everything it can, eats whatever has stopped moving, and takes its time about it.
Bane: Cold. It is born of fire and laughs at flame, but frost bites it worse than steel does. And keep your eyes off it — the stiffening comes from meeting its gaze, not from any touch.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes in on the air and meets every eye it can, hanging back while the stare does the work for it. Whoever still moves it rakes with those hanging claws; whoever has gone rigid it takes in its jaws, clamps down and drains at leisure. A cluster of them will strip a caravan bare while half the drivers stand upright, watching, and cannot so much as blink.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Fight it blindfolded if you can stomach it. Half my company learned that lesson stiff as fence-planks.
• Anything frost-touched — a chilled blade, a flask of rime — hurts it worse than your best steel.
• Fire is wasted on it. Utterly wasted. Save the oil for the road home.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing in there to talk to. I have tried — in the fire-tongue, in signs, with good meat laid out on a stone — and got the stare for my trouble and a fortnight of bad dreams after. Treat it as a wolf that flies and can nail you to the spot. Strike first, and strike cold.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Formidable — A formidable foe

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Paralyzing Gaze (Su): Paralysis for 1d6 rounds, 30 feet, Fortitude DC 13 negates. The save DC is Charisma-based. Rasts paralyse as many of their foes as possible, then set upon any that are still moving.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a rast must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Blood Drain (Ex): A rast drains blood from a grabbed opponent, dealing 1 point of Constitution damage each round it maintains the hold.

Flight (Su): A rast can cease or resume flight as a free action. A rast that loses this ability falls and can perform only a single action (either a move action or an attack action) each round.

Fire and Cold (Ex): A rast is immune to fire and vulnerable to cold, taking half again as much damage (+50%) from cold attacks regardless of whether a saving throw is allowed or the save succeeds.

Combat: A rast has anywhere from ten to fifteen claws, though it can use only four at once. It can claw or bite, but cannot do both during the same round.

lore.summary: Silver-skinned folk of the deep water, scaled blue below the waist, blue-green of hair, and reclusive by nature. Tritons keep their own cities far out beneath the temperate seas and want nothing from the dry world but to be left alone in it. Meet them at the edge of their waters, riding porpoises in a loose company, and you will be questioned courteously long before you are threatened.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Of a height and weight with a man, and built much the same above the waist.
Durability: About as hardy as a seasoned soldier. The scales help; underneath, they are flesh like yours.
Defenses: Heavy silver scale over the lower body turns a glancing blade, and that is the whole of it — no warding sorcery, no proof against honest steel.
Speed: Swift and tireless in the water, and all but helpless out of it; ashore a triton can barely drag itself along.
Might: The trident, used from the back of a porpoise with real horsemanship, and a heavy crossbow that carries well below the surface. At need they call up the sea's own — elementals of water, and whatever great swimming thing answers — to fight beside them.
Mind: Sharp, lettered, craftsmen nearly to a soul; they keep the trade tongue as well as the water tongue.
Disposition: Good-hearted and proud, wary of surface folk, slow to draw and unyielding once drawn. They give up not one length of their own halls.
Bane: Get one on dry land and the matter is already settled. In their own water their weakness is number — they are few, and defending a home they cannot afford to lose, they hold nothing in reserve.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: They avoid a fight wherever there is a way round it, and they never skirmish for sport. Pressed, they meet you mounted: riding down with the trident at the charge, wheeling off before you can answer, loosing bolts between the passes. Threaten a hall of theirs and they call the sea itself — elementals and great beasts of the deep — and from that point nobody withdraws and nobody is spared.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Come with no blade drawn and speak first. They will hear you out; they nearly always do.
• They cannot follow you ashore — but neither can they run from you at sea. Think hard on which of those helps you.
• Do not raid a triton hall for its treasure. The sea comes when they call it, and it comes quickly.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: The easiest good folk under the water to speak with, if you come open-handed. Name the sharkfolk of the sahuagin as your enemy and you have friends for life; that hatred is old and patient. I wintered in a triton hall once, ate their bitter green bread, and was sent home with a pilot and a blessing.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A lesser danger

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Spell-Like Abilities: 1/day — summon nature's ally IV. Caster level 7th. Tritons often choose water elementals for their companions.

Skills: A triton has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard. It can always choose to take 10 on a Swim check, even if distracted or endangered. It can use the run action while swimming, provided it swims in a straight line.

Combat: The reclusive tritons prefer to avoid combat, but they fiercely defend their homes. They attack with either melee or ranged weapons as the circumstances warrant. When encountered outside their lair, they are 90% likely to be mounted on friendly sea creatures such as porpoises. A triton has silvery skin fading into silver-blue scales on the lower half of its body, and deep blue or blue-green hair; it is about the same size and weight as a human, and speaks Common and Aquan.

lore.summary: Somewhere back along the blood a celestial stooped to love a mortal, and the debt is still being paid in silver hair and golden eyes. Aasimar are folk, not monsters — tall, comely, unsettlingly steady of gaze. They are born and buried among men, keep the temples and the toll-roads, and carry a lamp in the marrow that they can kindle at need.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a person, and usually a tall handsome one.
Durability: As hardy as any healthy soldier, no more.
Defenses: Nothing but honest mail; the blood turns aside a bite of acid, a bite of frost, a bite of the storm, and no more than that.
Speed: A soldier's walk, slowed by whatever scale he chose to wear.
Might: Sword and crossbow, plainly taught. The strength of a man in good years.
Mind: A whole and reasoning mind. Speaks the common tongue and the tongue of the higher planes from the cradle, and often the speech of elves or dwarves besides.
Disposition: Decidedly good, most of them, and forward about it — they will argue you out of a wickedness before they draw. A rare few take on the judging, vengeful cast of their forebear.
Bane: Mortal as you are, and the celestial spark buys nothing against fire, steel, or poison. Set an evil in front of one and he will fight to the death rather than withdraw — that pride kills more of them than any monster does.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights like a decent man-at-arms and wants the fight fair — declared, front to front, no ambush. Once a day it can call down a standing pool of true daylight, which it uses to strip the dark from things that need the dark; then it closes with the sword. Set it against something plainly evil and the caution goes out of it entirely: it will not break off, it will not run, it will die on its feet arguing.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Not quarry. Put your book away and buy the man a drink.
• The eyes give it away before the hair does — gold, and they do not blink enough.
• If you must brawl one, do it over money. Give it a cause and it will fight until one of you is dead.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: These are people, and better people than most. I have wintered with an aasimar toll-keeper who fed me and would take no coin for it. Speak plainly, do not lie — they have an unpleasant knack for the smell of a lie — and name your business. Half of them will offer to come along.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Minor — A minor threat

Organization: Solitary, pair, or team (3-4)
