sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Planetouched: Planetouched is a general word for someone who can trace his or her bloodline back to an outsider, usually a fiend or a celestial. The effects of a supernatural being in one's heritage last for many generations. Although not as dramatically altered as a half-celestial, an aasimar still retains some special qualities. The block above is a typical aasimar 1st-level warrior.

Daylight (Sp): An aasimar can use daylight once per day as a 1st-level caster, or as a caster of its class levels, whichever is higher.

Resistances (Ex): An aasimar has resistance to acid 5, cold 5, and electricity 5, and darkvision out to 60 feet.

Skills: An aasimar has a +2 racial bonus on Spot and Listen checks.

Aasimar Racial Traits: +2 Wisdom, +2 Charisma. Medium size; base land speed 30 feet. Darkvision 60 ft. +2 racial bonus on Spot and Listen checks. Feats according to class levels. Special attack: daylight. Special qualities: resistance to acid 5, cold 5, and electricity 5. Automatic languages Common and Celestial; bonus languages Draconic, Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, Halfling, Sylvan. Favored class paladin. Level adjustment +1.

Appearance and Temper: Aasimars are usually tall, good-looking, and generally pleasant. Some have a minor physical trait suggesting their heritage, such as silver hair, golden eyes, or an unnaturally intense stare. Most are decidedly good-aligned, fighting evil causes and swaying others to do right; occasionally one takes on the vengeful, judgmental aspect of its celestial ancestor, but this is rare. In a fight an aasimar usually likes a fair, straightforward contest, but against a particularly evil foe it fights with utter conviction and to the death.

lore.summary: A fiend got into the family line some generations back and the family has been paying rent ever since. Tieflings are people — born of women, buried in churchyards — but no two are marked alike: little horns, red eyes, pointed teeth, a cloven foot, a whiff of brimstone. Many pass wholly for human, and the towns that raise them usually treat them badly.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a person, and often a slight, quick one.
Durability: A person's toughness, no better.
Defenses: Leather and a buckler if it can afford them. The infernal drop shrugs off a lick of flame, of frost, and of lightning — a lick, no more.
Speed: Quick on its feet and quicker with its hands; a fine sneak and a fine liar.
Might: A rapier held well, or a crossbow from a doorway. Nimble rather than strong.
Mind: Sharp — sharper than most men. Speaks the common tongue and the infernal one, and picks up others readily.
Disposition: More often crooked than not, though I have known upright ones and would not hang a man on his horns. Conniving, subtle, disinclined to a fair contest.
Bane: Flesh and blood like the rest of us, thin in the chest and short of temper. It relies on ambush; take that away — open ground, good light, a companion at your back — and it has nothing left but a thin sword and bad odds.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It will not meet you fairly if it can help it. Expect the alley, the drawn shutter, the friend behind you. Once a day it can pull a smothering darkness over a room and it will spend that at the worst moment for you — then work with the rapier while you grope, since it sees in the black perfectly well and you do not. Cut off the exit and it turns to bargaining fast.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Bring your own light — a light that is not a flame it can smother. Its dark falls once, and it falls on you.
• It sees in the pitch. You do not. Never let the fight go to the cellar.
• Not all of them are wicked, and the ones that are got there by being hounded. Ask before you accuse.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Talk, always — but count your purse after. They are folk, not fiends, and most of the crimes laid at their door were laid there by neighbours who did not like the horns. I have hired two as guides and been robbed by one of them. That is a fair average, and better than I have had from men.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Planetouched: Planetouched is a general word for someone who can trace his or her bloodline back to an outsider, usually a fiend or a celestial. The effects of a supernatural being in one's heritage last for many generations. Although not as dramatically altered as a half-fiend, a tiefling still retains some special qualities. The block above is a typical tiefling 1st-level warrior.

Darkness (Sp): A tiefling can use darkness once per day, at a caster level equal to its class levels.

Resistances (Ex): A tiefling has resistance to cold 5, electricity 5, and fire 5, and darkvision out to 60 feet.

Special attack: darkness. Special qualities: resistance to cold 5, electricity 5, and fire 5. Automatic languages Common and Infernal; bonus languages Draconic, Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, Orc. Favored class rogue. Level adjustment +1.

Appearance and Temper: Many tieflings are indistinguishable from humans. Others have small horns, pointed teeth, red eyes, a whiff of brimstone about them, or even cloven feet. No two tieflings are the same. They are sneaky, subtle, and generally conniving; they prefer to strike from ambush and usually avoid a fair fight if they can.

lore.summary: A hunched grey mountain of muscle, taller than two men and near as broad, with a mouth that opens the whole width of its head and six small keen eyes above it. It walks the temperate marshes alone — always alone; each one bears a single young in a belly pouch and then abandons it. Strangest of all, it adopts. It picks some creature or band of creatures and shadows them for life.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — hunched, and still it looks down at you.
Durability: Appalling. It is a wall of gristle and it does not tire and it does not stop for wounds that would fell a bear.
Defenses: No trick to it, only hide like layered rope over slabs of muscle. Blades turn or stick.
Speed: A man's pace, no faster, and it neither climbs nor swims well. It does not need to hurry.
Might: Enormous. It bites, holds on, and then tears — that tearing is the thing that kills, and there is no defence against it once the jaws are set.
Mind: Dim, near an animal's, and yet it can track a scent for days and it plainly loves what it has adopted.
Disposition: Not wicked — neutral as weather. Left alone it hunts, hides, and lays fresh meat at the feet of whatever it has taken into its keeping, whether that creature wants the gift or not.
Bane: It cannot be talked to and it cannot be fooled by ground, but it is slow, it fights alone, and it will never be joined by another of its kind. Wear it down at reach, or from a boat, or from a tree. And it will retreat from those it has adopted if they turn on it — which is a door, if you can find who it loves.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It hides in the reeds and the grey water — better than a thing that size has any right to — and waits for you to come close. Then it charges, shoulders through the line, and bites. If the bite holds it drags you in and rends, and that second grip is the one that opens a man from collar to hip. It attacks to kill, always, whether hunting or guarding, and it will follow a scent for a very long way to finish what it started.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Six eyes. You will not sneak up on it in daylight, and it sees in the dark besides.
• Once the jaws close it tears, and the tearing is what kills. Break the grip or die in it.
• Find out what it has adopted. Threaten that and it comes at you; harm it and the render will not fight you at all. Choose which sort of man you are.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing in there to talk to — the mind is a beast's, and it has no speech. I tried meat, I tried song, I tried standing very still. It came anyway. The only bargain a render keeps is with whatever it has decided to love, and that will never be you.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a gray render must hit with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Rend (Ex): A gray render that wins a grapple check after a successful bite attack establishes a hold, latching onto the opponent's body and tearing the flesh. This attack automatically deals 2d6+9 points of damage.

Skills: Gray renders have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks due to their six keen eyes.

Adoption: A unique quality of the gray render is its tendency to bond with, protect, and provide for another creature (or group of creatures) native to its surroundings. Whether accepted or not, the render always attempts to remain fairly close, watching over its adopted charges and daily bringing an offering of meat. It never willingly harms adopted creatures and retreats if they attack it. Gray renders are never found in groups: each of these asexual creatures produces one offspring and carries it for a time in a pouch, but thereafter the young render must fend for itself.

Combat: A gray render stands about 9 feet tall in spite of its hunched posture, is about 4 feet wide, and weighs about 4,000 pounds. It attacks to kill, whether to bring down prey or to protect itself or those it has adopted. When hunting, it sometimes attempts to hide and wait for prey to wander close.

lore.summary: In the deep places, some of the stone is hungry. A roper is a tapering pillar of grey flesh, thick at the foot and narrow at the crown, that shifts its colour and even its chill to match the cave around it. One eye and one wide maw open when it has decided to eat. It stands among honest stalagmites for years without moving, and it is patient, cruel, and entirely aware of what it is doing.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a pillar as tall as a lance stood on end.
Durability: Very tough, and its rind is hard as the rock it apes.
Defenses: Stone-hard hide; magic slides off it more often than it bites; lightning does nothing at all and cold barely troubles it.
Speed: Wretched. It creeps. Its reach, however, crosses a whole chamber.
Might: Half a dozen sticky cords lash out across the dark, fasten, and haul you in — and everything they touch goes weak, the arms first, until you cannot lift your own shield. What arrives at the maw is bitten in half.
Mind: As clever as a man and far more patient. It speaks the tongue of the earth-folk and the trade speech of the deep roads, and it listens to everything you say while you walk past it.
Disposition: Chaotic and cruel. It hunts alone or in small clusters and it enjoys the waiting.
Bane: Fire. It has no answer to fire at all — flame hurts it worse than it hurts anything else down there. Beyond that: it is nearly rooted, so anything it cannot reach is safe, and cutting a cord costs it nothing but a moment.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It stands still and lets you walk into the middle of the chamber. Then the cords come — several at once, from a pillar you had already dismissed — and they neither cut nor burn but stick, and reel, and sap the strength out of the limb they touch. It drags a man to the maw while he is still trying to work out where the attack came from, bites him, and starts on the next cord. Cut a strand and it simply grows another.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Burn it. Oil, pitch, a torch on a spear — nothing in that cave fears fire more.
• Count the stalagmites on your way in. If one of them is warm, or the wrong grey, back out of the room.
• The cords steal your strength, not your blood. Once your sword arm goes slack, no amount of courage brings it back — retreat then, not later.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: It has words — the earth-tongue and the deep-road trade speech — and it will use them, mostly to keep you talking until the cords are close enough. I bargained with one across a chasm it could not span, and learned two good roads from it. Never speak to one you could walk to.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Drag (Ex): If a roper hits with a strand attack, the strand latches onto the opponent's body. This deals no damage but drags the stuck opponent 10 feet closer each subsequent round (provoking no attack of opportunity) unless that creature breaks free, which requires a DC 23 Escape Artist check or a DC 19 Strength check. The check DCs are Strength-based, and the Escape Artist DC includes a +4 racial bonus. A roper can draw in a creature within 10 feet of itself and bite with a +4 attack bonus in the same round. A strand can be attacked by making a successful sunder attempt, and is severed once it has taken enough damage (10 points); attacking a roper's strand does not provoke an attack of opportunity. If the strand is currently attached to a target, the roper takes a -4 penalty on its opposed attack roll to resist the sunder attempt. Severing a strand deals no damage to a roper.

Strands (Ex): Most encounters with a roper begin when it fires strong, sticky strands. The creature can have up to six strands at once, and they can strike up to 50 feet away (no range increment). If a strand is severed, the roper can extrude a new one on its next turn as a free action.

Weakness (Ex): A roper's strands can sap an opponent's strength. Anyone grabbed by a strand must succeed on a DC 18 Fortitude save or take 2d8 points of Strength damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Skills: Ropers have a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks in stony or icy areas.

Combat: A roper stands some 9 feet tall and tapers from 3 or 4 feet in diameter at the base to 1 foot across at the top; it weighs 2,200 pounds, and its coloration and temperature change to match the surrounding cave. It hunts by standing very still and imitating a bit of rock, which often lets it attack with surprise. When prey comes within reach it lashes out with its strands, and in melee it bites adjacent opponents with its powerful maw. Ropers speak Terran and Undercommon.

lore.summary: Take an eagle, make it the size of a cart-horse, and give it a mind that can hold a conversation — that is the great eagle of the high crags. They keep the temperate mountains in ones, in mated pairs, and now and then in a whole cliff-face eyrie of them. They speak the common tongue and the speech of the air, they judge a stranger honestly, and they are good folk in feathers.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — as tall as a man and wider across the wings than a barn door.
Durability: A bird's build; hollow-boned and not made to trade blows. It can be brought down.
Defenses: Only its feathers and its wits — but it slips a blast or a bursting flame so cleanly that it walks away untouched where a man would be scorched.
Speed: Grand in the air, swift and sure. On the ground it is a shuffling, awkward thing and knows it.
Might: Two great talons and a slashing beak, brought down at the end of a dive with all that weight behind them. It goes for the head and the eyes.
Mind: As bright as a man and sharper of sight than anything I have hunted with. It reads a stranger's intent well; you will not easily lie to one.
Disposition: Good-hearted and neutral in its dealings — a solitary bird patrolling near its nest ignores anyone who does not look like trouble. Threaten the nest and a mated pair will die defending it.
Bane: Ground it and it is nearly helpless — nets, a covered gorge, a narrow cave. Its heart is the nest: everything it does can be predicted from where the eggs are.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights from height. It climbs, turns, and comes down out of the sun in a dive, striking with both talons in passing and beating up again before you have your guard round — and it will do that again and again rather than land. Denied the dive it works the head and eyes with beak and claws. A pair strikes in concert, driving intruders off by turns; over a nest, neither will break away.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Do not go near the eyrie. Everything else about them is reasonable; that is not.
• It will slip your fire and your lightning clean — use the bow, and lead it far more than feels right.
• Earn one and it will carry you, but it wants six weeks of courtship and a proper saddle. Do not try to break it like a horse; it will remember.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Talk first, always. They speak our tongue and the tongue of the air, and they are better-natured than most men in a tavern. I have shared a ledge and a goat with a mated pair and been carried over a pass for it. Announce yourself from below, keep well off the nest, and offer meat.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Evasion (Ex): With a successful Reflex save against an attack that allows a Reflex save for half damage, a giant eagle takes no damage.

Skills: Giant eagles have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks.

Combat: A typical giant eagle stands about 10 feet tall, has a wingspan of up to 20 feet, and weighs about 500 pounds. It typically attacks from a great height, diving earthward at tremendous speed; when it cannot dive it uses its powerful talons and slashing beak to strike at its target's head and eyes. A solitary giant eagle is usually hunting or patrolling near its nest and generally ignores creatures that do not appear threatening. A mated pair attacks in concert, making repeated diving attacks to drive away intruders, and fights to the death to defend the nest or hatchlings. Giant eagles speak Common and Auran.

Training a Giant Eagle: Although intelligent, a giant eagle requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. To be trained it must have a friendly attitude toward the trainer (achievable with a successful Diplomacy check). Training a friendly giant eagle requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding one requires an exotic saddle; a giant eagle can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Eggs are worth 2,500 gp apiece on the open market and chicks 4,000 gp each; professional trainers charge 1,000 gp to rear or train one.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a giant eagle is up to 300 pounds; a medium load, 301-600 pounds; and a heavy load, 601-900 pounds.

lore.summary: Waist-high and feather-quick, the deinonychus is the cleverest hunter in any warm forest, and it never comes alone. Bright green along the back, pale beneath, dappled with dark stripes, it carries its stiff tail straight out behind and runs on two legs faster than a good horse. You will hear the pack answering one another long before you see the first of them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: No taller than a man, and lighter — which is the only kindness in it.
Durability: Slight for a thing so savage; a solid blow tells on it at once.
Defenses: Pebbled hide and nothing further, but it is seldom standing where your blade was aimed.
Speed: Frighteningly swift over open ground, and it leaps as readily as it runs.
Might: The ripping talons on the hind legs do the killing; the grasping forearms and the teeth only hold you still for them.
Mind: Dull as men reckon wit, yet bright for a dinosaur — the pack hunts with genuine cunning, cutting one traveller away from the rest.
Disposition: A hunter, plainly and only. You are meat that has wandered into its wood.
Bane: Alone it is a hard morning's work and no more; the whole horror is the pack. Put your back to stone, break the flankers first, and never run — it is faster than you and it hunts what flees.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It stalks under cover until it can reach you at a rush, then leaps and brings everything at once — both hind talons ripping down, the forearms gripping, the jaws worrying at whatever they find. Its nose finds you long before its eyes do. The pack works this together: one comes at your front to hold your shield, and the moment you commit to that charge the others are in behind your knees.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Count the calls before you draw. If a fourth voice answers, walk backward, slowly.
• They come from where you are not looking. Fight in a doorway or a cleft, never in the open.
• Downwind, always. It has your scent long before you have any sign of it.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. I have talked a manticore out of a meal and an annis out of a bargain, but this is a beast with a beast's wants and no words in it at all. It hears the cunning in your voice and reads only prey standing still. Draw first, and speak after, if you must speak.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A deinonychus is bright green along its back and flanks, with a much lighter shade of the same colour on its underside, and darker spots or stripes over the body. Its tail extends straight out behind it, held aloft by an intricate structure of bony supports, so that its weight is carried entirely by the back legs; it weighs about 600 pounds. A deinonychus uses a combination of speed, grasping forearms, large teeth, and hind legs with ripping talons. It hunts by running at prey, leaping, and ripping with its rear talons as it claws and bites. The talons count as one attack. A deinonychus has a relatively large brain for a dinosaur, and its pack hunts with cunning tactics.

Pounce (Ex): If a deinonychus charges, it can make a full attack — talons, both foreclaws and bite — at the end of the charge.

Skills: A deinonychus has a +8 racial bonus on Hide, Jump, Listen, Spot, and Survival checks.

lore.summary: The great predator, and it knows no other trade. Longer than a river barge from nose to tail-tip, it walks the warm plains on two pillar legs at a pace no horse will hold, its head alone longer than a tall man's stride and its teeth the length of daggers. It pursues and eats near enough anything it sees. There is no more to it than that.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a walking hill with a mouth at the front of it.
Durability: Vast and heavy-bodied. You will be a long, loud while cutting it down.
Defenses: Thick pebbled hide, and nothing else. It has never needed anything else.
Speed: A swift runner for all its bulk. Do not lay plans that require outpacing it across open grass.
Might: One bite, and the one bite suffices — it seizes you, holds you fast off your feet, and swallows you down whole into a gullet that burns as it grinds.
Mind: A dull brute with a keen nose. It hunts by scent and appetite, never by plan.
Disposition: Hungry, and incurious about anything else. It walks alone or with a mate; it keeps no herd and shares no kill.
Bane: No wits and no guile — its whole art is to charge in and bite. Break the line of that charge and it blunders past you. Kill it from a distance, or from above, where the great head cannot reach.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Simple, and terrible for it: the beast charges, and the beast bites. If those jaws close on anything smaller than itself it will not let go — it worries you off the ground and down its throat, and once inside you must cut your own way out through the gizzard while the juices take your skin. It will not stop to be fought while it is feeding. Reach a swallowed friend quickly, or do not reach him at all.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• If it has you in its teeth, stop hitting the head. Cut, and keep cutting, and be ready to fall out wet.
• Carry a short blade where your hand can find it with both arms pinned. That is the whole of the plan.
• It comes straight at you. Stand where straight will not serve it — rocks, a ravine, a stand of old trees.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. It has no more mind than a landslide and no more mercy. I once stood still and silent before one, as a man does for a bear, on the reasoning that it hunted by movement. I was wrong about that, and I carry the scars in a ring about my middle to prove how wrong.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Despite its enormous size and 6-ton weight, a tyrannosaurus is a swift runner. Its head is nearly 6 feet long and its teeth are from 3 to 6 inches in length; it is slightly more than 30 feet long from nose to tail. A tyrannosaurus pursues and eats just about anything it sees, and its tactics are simple — charge in and bite.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a tyrannosaurus must hit an opponent of up to one size smaller with its bite attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity. If it wins the grapple check, it establishes a hold and can try to swallow the foe the following round.

Swallow Whole (Ex): A tyrannosaurus can try to swallow a grabbed opponent of up to two sizes smaller by making a successful grapple check. The swallowed creature takes 2d8+8 points of bludgeoning damage and 8 points of acid damage per round from the tyrannosaurus's gizzard. A swallowed creature can cut its way out by using a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 points of damage to the gizzard (AC 12); once the creature exits, muscular action closes the hole, so another swallowed opponent must cut its own way out. A Huge tyrannosaurus's gizzard can hold 2 Medium, 8 Small, 32 Tiny, or 128 Diminutive or smaller opponents.

Skills: A tyrannosaurus has a +2 racial bonus on Listen and Spot checks.

lore.summary: A living rampart: three horns, a great bony shield of a frill above the shoulders, and more weight behind them than a laden wagon train. The triceratops crops the temperate grasslands in herds and wants nothing whatever from you — but it will run a horn through any rival of its own bulk that sets foot on its ground, and walk over anything smaller without breaking stride.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — a body the length of a longhouse, and heavier than you will credit until it moves.
Durability: Enormously tough. There is little on the grasslands harder to put down.
Defenses: Hide like layered shield-boards, and that vast frill standing guard over neck and shoulder.
Speed: Unhurried at the graze, but its charge crosses ground faster than you will step out of it.
Might: The gore, and the gore alone, and it is dreadful — taken at the charge it will lift a warhorse clean off the earth.
Mind: Dimmer than a cow, and no likelier to be reasoned with.
Disposition: A grazer, content to be one. Anything of its own bulk that crowds its ground it takes for a rival and skewers; anything smaller it simply tramples into the turf and grazes on.
Bane: Its wits are as narrow as its charge is straight. Keep off its ground and it wants nothing of you at all; crowd it, and nothing you carry will turn that horn — so give the charge a boulder, an old oak or a gully to spend itself upon, and step aside.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It gives you warning, and the warning is the head coming down. Then it comes in one long straight rush and puts a horn through whatever it has settled on, a rush that will break a shield-wall and the horse behind it in the same breath. Smaller foes it does not trouble to gore; it walks them under. And it seldom grazes alone — reckon on the herd, not on the beast, and make certain you have angered only the one.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Nothing you carry will turn that horn. Do not test the matter. Move.
• Break the line of the charge with anything solid. Once it is committed it cannot correct.
• If it is only grazing, walk wide and let it graze. This one has never wanted you.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never — not for malice, but for want of any mind to talk to. I have offered fodder to a herd bull with my hands open and my voice low, and it came at me all the same. It does not hate you. It simply will not have you standing there.

sections.body:

lore.summary: Big as a warhorse and wholly silent on the wing, the giant owl keeps the old temperate forests by night. It stands head and shoulders above a tall man, spreads wings broader than a barn door, and sees by starlight what you could not see by lamp. It speaks the common tongue and the fey one both, and it thinks before it speaks, which is more than most.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — taller than a tall man, with a wingspan that fills a clearing.
Durability: Light-boned and no hardier than it looks. It cannot afford a long fight, and it knows that better than you do.
Defenses: Feather and hollow bone, and nothing else whatever. Its defence is that you never hear it coming.
Speed: Ungainly and hobbling afoot; on the wing, swift and beautifully turned.
Might: Both talons and a hooked beak, driven by the whole weight of a stoop out of the dark.
Mind: As clever as a man, and considerably better mannered. It knows its wood, its weather and every beast that walks in it.
Disposition: Good-hearted as a rule, and suspicious by nature. It will watch you a long while before it consents to be seen, and it keeps company with good folk when it keeps company at all.
Bane: Frail, and near helpless once it is grounded — it hobbles where it does not fly. Take away its air or its silence and it has nothing left. I would rather you did not.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not brawl. It glides a hand's breadth above the treetops, silent as falling snow, and drops the moment it is directly overhead — both talons in, the beak after — and is gone up into the black before you have finished turning. It fights that way or not at all. If the first stoop does not settle the matter it breaks off and waits for a better one rather than stand and trade blows.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• You will not hear it. Watch the stars instead, for the gap where they go out.
• Speak first, in the common tongue or the fey one. Nine times in ten there is no fight to be had here.
• It knows the wood better than your maps do. Ask it about the road before you ask it about your quarry.

sections.title: Parley (open)
sections.body: Open, and gladly. Ask any owl-company of the north wood about the winter I spent among them: I gave them warning of the axes coming up the valley, and they gave me the safe roads and a dry place to sleep. Be patient — they are suspicious by nature and will study you a good while first. And never lie to one twice.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: Giant owls are nocturnal birds of prey, feared for their ability to hunt and attack in near silence. They are intelligent, and though naturally suspicious, sometimes associate with good creatures. A typical giant owl stands about 9 feet tall, has a wingspan of up to 20 feet, and resembles its smaller cousins in nearly every way except size. Giant owls speak Common and Sylvan. A giant owl attacks by gliding silently just a few feet above its prey and plunging to strike when directly overhead.

Superior Low-Light Vision (Ex): A giant owl can see five times as far as a human can in dim light.

Skills: Giant owls have a +8 racial bonus on Listen checks and a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks. *When in flight, giant owls gain a +8 bonus on Move Silently checks.

Training a Giant Owl: Although intelligent, a giant owl requires training before it can bear a rider in combat. To be trained, a giant owl must have a friendly attitude toward the trainer (this can be achieved through a successful Diplomacy check). Training a friendly giant owl requires six weeks of work and a DC 25 Handle Animal check. Riding a giant owl requires an exotic saddle. A giant owl can fight while carrying a rider, but the rider cannot also attack unless he or she succeeds on a Ride check. Giant owl eggs are worth 2,500 gp apiece on the open market, while chicks are worth 4,000 gp each; professional trainers charge 1,000 gp to rear or train a giant owl.

Carrying Capacity: A light load for a giant owl is up to 300 pounds; a medium load, 301–600 pounds; and a heavy load, 601–900 pounds.

lore.summary: The true vampire, and the oldest terror in this book — not the swollen thing riding a monstrous host on an earlier page, but a man or woman remade by another's kiss. It looks as it looked in life, only hardened, with the predatory set of a wolf about the face. It loves finery and titles. It casts no shadow, throws no reflection, and speaks every tongue it knew before it died.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Whatever it was in life. A man, a woman; no larger.
Durability: It cannot be worn down. Cut it and the wound closes while you watch it close; beat it past all bearing and it does not fall — it bursts into mist and streams away for its coffin, and is whole again by the following night.
Defenses: Dead flesh that shrugs off poison, plague, weariness and terror alike; cold and lightning trouble it barely at all; and any steel that is neither silvered nor ensorcelled bites into it as into wet clay. It stands its ground under a priest's rebuke that would scatter lesser dead like leaves.
Speed: Quick as a wolf and quicker of hand. It walks up sheer walls the way a spider does, wears the shape of bat or wolf when being a man no longer suits, and as vapour it goes wherever a draught goes.
Might: Strength no living man has in the blow — and the blow itself takes the living years out of you. Struck once you are lessened; struck often enough you are a corpse that gets up again and calls it master. Pinned beneath it, you feel the fangs go in, and it drinks you empty.
Mind: Sharper than it was in life, and it had a lifetime's cunning before it started. Add to that long ages of practice at being liked.
Disposition: Evil without exception, whatever manners it has put on. It commands the lesser things of the night — rats, bats, a pack of wolves called up out of nowhere — and the spawn it has made of your neighbours answer it and cannot be freed until it is destroyed.
Bane: It keeps a coffin, and it keeps rules, and the rules are its undoing. It cannot cross your threshold unless it is invited; it cannot cross running water; it recoils from garlic, from a mirror, from a holy symbol held up boldly. Sunlight unmakes it where it stands. Running water unmakes it as surely. A wooden stake through the heart slays it outright — and it rises again the moment that stake is drawn, so take the head afterward and fill the mouth with holy bread.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It fights like something that cannot lose and has all night to prove the point. First the eyes: it catches and holds your gaze and turns one of your own company against you where they stand. Then the night comes indoors — rats, bats, wolves at the door. It strikes with a strength no living arm has, and every blow takes something out of a man that a night's rest will not give back; get within its reach and it pins you and feeds. Wound it and the wound knits. Hurt it past enduring and it still does not die: it becomes a ribbon of mist and pours away through the keyhole, and from that moment you have only the hours before dawn to find the coffin it is running for.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Silver in one hand, something blessed in the other. Plain steel is a courtesy call.
• Never invite it in. Not as a jest, not to be clever, not to save the friend it is holding at your door.
• Kill it at noon, in its box. Anything else is a chase, and it knows every cellar in the county.

sections.title: Parley (wary)
sections.body: Wary — but talk, because it will talk. It is proud, it is bored, and it remembers being a person. I have taken wine with one across a table for the better part of a night and walked out at dawn with what I came for. It lied through every word of it. Accept no invitation, offer none, and be gone before it needs to feed.

sections.title: Threat
sections.body: Grave — A grave peril

sections.title: Stat block (SRD)
sections.body:
Size/Type: Medium Undead (Augmented Humanoid) — the sample vampire, a 5th-level human fighter
Initiative: +7
Speed: 30 ft. (6 squares)
Armor Class: 23 (+3 Dex, +6 natural, +4 masterwork chain shirt), touch 13, flat-footed 20
Base Attack/Grapple: +5/+11
Attack: Slam +11 melee (1d6+9 plus energy drain) or +1 spiked chain +13 melee (2d4+12) or masterwork shortbow +9 ranged (1d6/×3)
Full Attack: Slam +11 melee (1d6+9 plus energy drain) or +1 spiked chain +13 melee (2d4+12) or masterwork shortbow +9 ranged (1d6/×3)
Space/Reach: 5 ft./5 ft. (10 ft. with spiked chain)
Special Attacks: Blood drain, children of the night, create spawn, dominate, energy drain
Special Qualities: +4 turn resistance, alternate form, damage reduction 10/silver and magic, darkvision 60 ft., fast healing 5, gaseous form, resistance to cold 10 and electricity 10, spider climb, undead traits, vampire weaknesses
Saves: Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +4
Abilities: Str 22, Dex 17, Con —, Int 12, Wis 16, Cha 12
Skills: Bluff +9, Climb +10, Hide +10, Listen +17, Move Silently +10, Ride +11, Search +9, Sense Motive +11, Spot +17
Feats: Alertness, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Exotic Weapon Proficiency (spiked chain), Improved Initiative, Lightning Reflexes, Mobility, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (spiked chain), Weapon Specialization (spiked chain)

Organization: Solitary, pair, gang (3–5), or troupe (1–2 plus 2–5 vampire spawn)
Challenge Rating: 7 (the base creature's rating +2)
Alignment: Always evil (any)
Treasure: Double standard; this one carries a +1 spiked chain, a masterwork chain shirt, a masterwork shortbow and a potion of haste
Advancement: By character class

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
The Vampire Template: “Vampire” is an acquired template that can be added to any humanoid or monstrous humanoid creature (the base creature). The vampire uses all the base creature's statistics and special abilities except as noted: its type changes to undead (augmented humanoid or monstrous humanoid) with no recalculation of base attack bonus, saves or skill points; its size is unchanged; its natural armour bonus improves by +6; it gains a slam attack if it did not already have one (1d6 for a Medium vampire, 1d4 Small, 1d8 Large, 2d6 Huge), and keeps any weapon use and natural weapons it had in life. Its abilities increase by Str +6, Dex +4, Int +2, Wis +2 and Cha +4, and as an undead creature it has no Constitution score. It gains Alertness, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Improved Initiative and Lightning Reflexes as bonus feats where it qualifies, a +8 racial bonus on Bluff, Hide, Listen, Move Silently, Search, Sense Motive and Spot checks, double standard treasure, and an alignment of always evil (any). Save DCs for its special attacks are 10 + half the vampire's levels + its Charisma modifier unless noted otherwise; for the sample vampire above that is DC 13. Vampires appear just as they did in life, though their features are often hardened and feral, with the predatory look of wolves. Like liches they frequently embrace finery and decadence and may assume the guise of nobility — but they cast no shadow and throw no reflection in a mirror. They speak any languages they knew in life.

Blood Drain (Ex): A vampire can suck blood from a living victim with its fangs by making a successful grapple check. If it pins the foe, it drains blood, dealing 1d4 points of Constitution drain each round the pin is maintained. On each such successful attack the vampire is briefly strengthened by the blood it has taken.

Children of the Night (Su): Vampires command the lesser creatures of the world and once per day can call forth 1d6+1 rat swarms, 1d4+1 bat swarms, or a pack of 3d6 wolves as a standard action. (If the base creature is not terrestrial, this power might summon other creatures of similar power.) These creatures arrive in 2d6 rounds and serve the vampire for up to 1 hour.

Dominate (Su): A vampire can crush an opponent's will just by looking into his or her eyes. This is similar to a gaze attack, except that the vampire must use a standard action, and those merely looking at it are not affected. Anyone the vampire targets must succeed on a Will save (DC 13 for the sample vampire) or fall instantly under the vampire's influence as though by a dominate person spell (caster level 12th). The ability has a range of 30 feet.

Create Spawn (Su): A humanoid or monstrous humanoid slain by a vampire's energy drain rises as a vampire spawn 1d4 days after burial. If the vampire instead drains the victim's Constitution to 0 or lower, the victim returns as a spawn if it was of 4th level or lower and as a full vampire if it was of 5th level or higher. In either case the new vampire or spawn is under the command of the vampire that created it and remains enslaved until its master's destruction. At any given time a vampire may have enslaved spawn totalling no more than twice its own levels; any spawn it creates beyond that limit are created free-willed. An enslaved vampire may create and enslave spawn of its own, so a master vampire can command a whole hierarchy of lesser vampires. A vampire may voluntarily free an enslaved spawn in order to enslave a new one, but once freed, a vampire or vampire spawn cannot be enslaved again.

Energy Drain (Su): Living creatures hit by a vampire's slam attack (or any other natural weapon the vampire might possess) gain two negative levels. For each negative level so bestowed, the vampire is briefly strengthened. A vampire can use its energy drain ability once per round.

Alternate Form (Su): A vampire can assume the shape of a bat, dire bat, wolf, or dire wolf as a standard action. While in its alternate form the vampire loses its natural slam attack and its dominate ability, but it gains the natural weapons and extraordinary special attacks of its new form. It can remain in that form until it assumes another or until the next sunrise. (If the base creature is not terrestrial, this power might allow other forms.)

Damage Reduction (Su): A vampire has damage reduction 10/silver and magic. A vampire's natural weapons are treated as magic weapons for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction.

Fast Healing (Ex): A vampire recovers 5 points of damage each round so long as it has not been beaten down. If reduced to the point of collapse in combat, it automatically assumes gaseous form and attempts to escape. It must reach its coffin home within 2 hours or be utterly destroyed (it can travel up to nine miles in 2 hours). Any additional damage dealt to a vampire forced into gaseous form has no effect. Once at rest in its coffin the vampire is helpless; it recovers slightly after 1 hour, is then no longer helpless, and resumes healing at the rate of 5 points of damage per round.

Gaseous Form (Su): As a standard action, a vampire can assume gaseous form at will as the spell (caster level 5th), but it can remain gaseous indefinitely and has a fly speed of 20 feet with perfect manoeuvrability.

Resistances (Ex): A vampire has resistance to cold 10 and electricity 10.

Spider Climb (Ex): A vampire can climb sheer surfaces as though with a spider climb spell.

Turn Resistance (Ex): A vampire has +4 turn resistance: anyone attempting to turn, rebuke, command or bolster it treats the vampire as though it were four levels more powerful than it actually is.

Vampire Weaknesses — Repelling a Vampire: For all their power, vampires have a number of weaknesses. They cannot tolerate the strong odour of garlic and will not enter an area laced with it; they recoil likewise from a mirror or a strongly presented holy symbol. These things do not harm the vampire — they merely keep it at bay: a recoiling vampire must stay at least 5 feet away from a creature holding the mirror or holy symbol and cannot touch or make melee attacks against that creature for the rest of the encounter, and holding a vampire at bay takes a standard action. Vampires are also unable to cross running water, although they can be carried over it while resting in their coffins or aboard a ship. And they are utterly unable to enter a home or other building unless invited in by someone with the authority to do so; public places, being by definition open to all, they may enter freely.

Vampire Weaknesses — Slaying a Vampire: Beating a vampire down in combat incapacitates it but does not always destroy it (see fast healing). Certain attacks, however, can slay one outright. Exposing any vampire to direct sunlight disorients it: it can take only a single move action or attack action and is destroyed utterly in the next round if it cannot escape. Immersing a vampire in running water robs it of one-third of its remaining vitality each round until it is destroyed at the end of the third round of immersion. Driving a wooden stake through a vampire's heart instantly slays the monster — though it returns to life if the stake is removed, unless the body is destroyed. A popular tactic is to cut off the creature's head and fill its mouth with holy wafers or their equivalent.

Vampire Characters: Vampires are always evil, which causes characters of certain classes to lose some class abilities. Vampire clerics lose their ability to turn undead but gain the ability to rebuke undead — an ability that does not affect the vampire's own controller or any other vampires that a master controls — and have access to two of the following domains: Chaos, Destruction, Evil, or Trickery. Vampire sorcerers and wizards retain their class abilities, but if such a character has a familiar other than a rat or bat, the link between them is broken and the familiar shuns its former companion; the character may summon another familiar, but it must be a rat or bat.

lore.summary: A serpent's neck set upon a barrel body, rowed through warm shallows by four great paddles. For all its sea-craft it breathes air as you do, and hunts with its head held clear of the swell, snapping down on whatever swims, wades or trails a hand over the gunwale. Mariners who glimpse only neck or tail swear afterwards they met a sea-serpent.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Huge — longer than a war-galley's beam, and half of that length is neck and tail.
Durability: Deep in the chest and dreadfully hardy; it will wear out a boatful of spearmen before it tires.
Defenses: Nothing but pebbled hide. No armour worth the name, no venom, no trickery — it simply endures.
Speed: A superb and nimble swimmer, quick to wheel and lunge. Ashore it can only shuffle and heave.
Might: A single crushing bite carried on the whole weight of that neck; it seizes prey and bears it under.
Mind: Beast-dull. It knows hunger, movement, and the taste of blood, and nothing else at all.
Disposition: Aggressive without provocation. It attacks anything it notices, be that a fish, a swimmer, or an oar.
Bane: The water is its whole world. Reach a bank, a reef, a deck it cannot reach, and it is beaten — and out of the water it cannot conceal itself at all, though beneath the surface it vanishes like a shadow.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It cruises with the head up, sights you, and strikes downward — that neck crosses more water in a heartbeat than you credit, and the head arrives before the body ever does. It seizes, hauls its catch under, and thrashes. Wounded, it does not flee; it circles and comes again from the blind side, and it will take the smallest swimmer in a party first because the smallest swims slowest.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Watch the water, not the neck. The body tells you where the head will be.
• Boat-hooks and long spears. Anything short means letting it get within reach of you.
• It must surface to breathe. Wait it out from the shallows; it cannot wait you out on land.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is nothing behind those eyes to bargain with. I tried the dragon-turtle's courtesy on one off the coral coast — meat held out over the rail, slow words, open hands. It took the meat, the rail, and most of the arm that offered them. Row, and keep rowing.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: An elasmosaurus is aggressive and attacks anything it notices. The creature is strong, fast, and highly maneuverable, able to turn quickly and lunge at prey. When hunting, it travels with its head out of the water, snapping down quickly to seize prey.

Amphibious Habit: Though it resides primarily in the water, an elasmosaurus only breathes air. It has a total length of some 30 feet, including a tail half as long as its entire body, and weighs about 5,000 pounds. Observers who see only its head or tail might easily mistake it for a massive snake.

Scent (Ex): An elasmosaurus can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell, noticing opponents within 30 feet (60 feet upwind, 15 feet downwind) and twice those distances for strong scents.

Skills: An elasmosaurus has a +8 racial bonus on Hide checks in water. It has a +8 racial bonus on any Swim check to perform some special action or avoid a hazard, and may always take 10 on a Swim check even when distracted or endangered; it can use the run action while swimming in a straight line.

lore.summary: The hunting lizard grown to the height of a mounted rider — same shape as the lesser raptor, same habits, and a great deal more of it. It runs down prey in the warm forests on two long legs, kills with the hooked talon of the hind foot, and hunts in small, patient packs that will follow a blood-trail for days.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — it stands taller than a man on horseback, and most of the length behind it is stiff, balancing tail.
Durability: Rangy but hard-wearing; it takes a great deal of steel to put one down before it reaches you.
Defenses: Tough hide and nothing more. It relies on never being where the blow falls.
Speed: Frighteningly swift over open ground, and a prodigious leaper. You will not outrun it. Do not try.
Might: It leaps and rips with the great hind talons, tearing with the smaller forelimb claws and biting all the while.
Mind: Bright for a beast — brighter than a hound. The pack co-ordinates, drives, and flanks with real cunning.
Disposition: A confident hunter that treats a traveller as meat and a mule as a feast. Neither shy nor easily frightened off.
Bane: It closes at a run, and a running beast can be spitted. Set spears, use narrow ground, and it loses the charge that is its whole art — and it hunts by nose, so foul water or wind in your favour buys you distance.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It stalks in cover until the ground is right, then charges, and when it charges it brings everything at once — it lands upon its quarry and rips with the hind talons while the small claws hold and the jaws work. The pack does not swarm; it spreads. Two show themselves and drive you, the rest wait where you are being driven. Whichever of you is slowest or last will be the one they take.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• They drive you somewhere. Stop and look where they are not, and you will find the rest of them.
• Spear-butt in the earth, point at chest height. Let its own rush do the work.
• It can track by nose for days. Wade, cross running water, and take the long way home.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: You may bribe a hungry wolf and part on terms. Not this one. I have thrown a whole deer's haunch to a pack and watched two eat while the third circled behind me. They are clever enough to divide the labour and far too dull to be reasoned with. Trees, water, or spears.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Pounce (Ex): If a megaraptor charges, it can make a full attack.

Combat: A megaraptor is a larger version of the deinonychus, standing about 12 feet tall with a total length of 24 feet, and has the same appearance, habits, and abilities as the smaller version. It uses a combination of speed, grasping forearms, large teeth, and hind legs with ripping talons: it runs at prey, leaps, and rips with its rear talons as it claws and bites. The talons count as one attack. A megaraptor has a relatively large brain for a dinosaur, and its pack hunts with cunning tactics.

Scent (Ex): A megaraptor can detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell, noticing opponents within 30 feet (60 feet upwind, 15 feet downwind) and twice those distances for strong scents.

Skills: A megaraptor has a +8 racial bonus on Hide, Jump, Listen, Spot, and Survival checks.

lore.summary: A patient carnivore of the temperate woods, standing the height of a horse and folding its barbed forelimbs as if at prayer. It waits perfectly still among the green — hours, days — until something walks close enough to be taken. It hunts alone. There is no hive, no mate hunting beside it, only the one green thing that was a branch until it moved.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — long-limbed and lanky, taller than the man it is watching.
Durability: Not much meat on it. Land a solid blow and it goes down quickly enough.
Defenses: A hard shell over the back, and better than that, a colouring that makes it part of the foliage until it strikes.
Speed: Slow and stilting afoot. It can fly, but only badly — a heavy, clattering flight, not a pursuit.
Might: The barbed forelimbs snatch and pin, and once you are held it eats you where you stand, at leisure.
Mind: None whatever. It has no thought to read, to frighten, or to trick.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor angry. It is hungry and it is patient, and it does not care in the least what you are.
Bane: Take it out of the leaves and it is a clumsy thing on stilts — in bare ground or on stone you will see it coming a long way off, and it can neither run you down nor fly after you.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It does not fight so much as harvest. It stands motionless until you are within reach, then the forelimbs come out and close, and it holds you fast while the jaws start their work — the biting only begins once it has you gripped. It fights whoever is nearest and does not manoeuvre, does not retreat, and does not know enough to be discouraged. Cut the arm that holds and the rest is easy.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Beat the brush ahead with a pole. Better a stick finds it than your face does.
• Free the held one first. Everything it does begins with the grip.
• In leaf-cover you will never see it. On open ground it is a clumsy, gangling joke.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: There is no one home. I have spoken to spiders that at least turned to listen; this one is a set of shears with an appetite behind them. I have stood a spear's length from a mantis and watched it wait, and it was waiting still when I struck. Words are wasted breath here.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a giant praying mantis must hit with its claws attack. If it wins the ensuing grapple check, it establishes a hold and makes a bite attack as a primary attack (at its full +6 attack bonus). Holding an opponent this way, the mantis folds the prey into its raking forelimbs and squeezes it against the bite — it need not move into the victim's square, and each round the hold is maintained it may bite again.

Combat: This patient carnivore remains completely still as it waits for prey to come near, then seizes it with a strike of the spined forelimbs. It flies, but only clumsily, and prefers to ambush from cover rather than pursue.

Vermin Traits: A giant praying mantis is mindless: it has no Intelligence score and is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects). It has darkvision out to 60 feet, is proficient with its natural weapons only, wears no armor, and breathes, eats, and sleeps.

Skills: A giant praying mantis has a +4 racial bonus on Hide and Spot checks. *Because of its camouflage, the Hide bonus increases to +12 when a mantis is surrounded by foliage.

lore.summary: A dog-sized beetle of the warm forests that lives on carrion and offal, heaping the rotting stuff into mounds to nest and lay in. They are found in small clusters, sometimes in whole clicking companies. Left alone they are harmless middens on legs; disturbed, they turn the tail towards you and spray a scalding vapour that eats cloth, skin and eyes.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — about as long as a big hound, and a good deal broader.
Durability: Small and soon killed, though the shell must be cracked first.
Defenses: A thick chitin case over the back that turns a glancing cut. Its true defence is the spray.
Speed: A brisk scuttling trot, no faster than a walking man. It does not chase.
Might: The bite is nothing to speak of. The burning vapour it vents behind is the whole of its danger, and it can vent again and again.
Mind: Mindless. It eats filth and defends its nest, and that is the sum of it.
Disposition: Peaceable. It attacks only to protect itself, its nest, or its eggs — a great many hunters have died learning where the nest was.
Bane: The spray goes where the tail points, and it is a short, wide gout, not a hurled thing. Come at the head, spread out, and stay off the line of the tail.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It gives ground rather than advancing, swinging the abdomen round to bring the vent to bear, and lets go a scalding cloud at whoever crowds it — then again, and again, for as long as it is pressed. If several are together every one of them turns and answers at once, and a narrow gully full of beetles becomes a fog that strips the skin. The bite is an afterthought it uses only when cornered.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Never stand behind it. That is where the harm comes from — the wrong end is the dangerous end.
• It will not follow. Back off a few paces and the fight is simply over.
• The shell and the venting sac fetch good coin from alchemists. Cut the sac out last, and cut it carefully.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: No mind to parley with — but of all mindless things this is the one you may most easily leave in peace. It wants your camp's offal, not you. I have shared a clearing with a whole click of them by the simple courtesy of never walking towards their midden. Give way and no blood is spilled.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Acid Spray (Ex): When attacked or disturbed, the creature can release a 10-foot cone of acidic vapor once per round. Those within the cone must succeed on a DC 13 Fortitude save or take 1d4+2 points of acid damage. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Combat: Giant bombardier beetles feed primarily on carrion and offal, gathering heaps of the stuff in which to build nests and lay eggs. One is about 6 feet long. They normally attack only to defend themselves, their nests, or their eggs — and open with the acid spray before closing to bite.

Vermin Traits: A giant bombardier beetle is mindless: it has no Intelligence score and is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects). It has darkvision out to 60 feet, is proficient with its natural weapons only, wears no armor, and breathes, eats, and sleeps.

lore.summary: Grown to the size of a large dog, and for all that no different in temper from the bees in a cottage garden. They work the temperate grasslands, navigate unerringly home over great distances, and keep hives whose combs hold honey by the barrelful. They sting only in defence of themselves or the hive — but the hive is defended by all of them at once.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a hound's bulk on wings, furred gold and black.
Durability: Slight and easily killed; a good swat with a staff will do it.
Defenses: None to speak of. It trusts to flight and to numbers.
Speed: Very fast on the wing and beautifully handled in the air. Afoot it is an awkward crawler.
Might: One sting, driving a venom that saps the strength out of a body over the following hours, and may kill a weak man outright.
Mind: Mindless as all its kind, though the hive together behaves with a purpose no single bee possesses.
Disposition: Not aggressive. It goes about its foraging and ignores you utterly unless you or your smoke come near the comb.
Bane: The sting stays in the wound and the bee dies of the giving — each can strike you only the once. Stand your ground, let a few spend themselves, and the swarm thins as fast as it gathers.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It comes on fast and straight, drives the sting home, and tears itself free to die — so the danger is never one bee but the host behind it, arriving from every quarter at once. They fight only until the intruder is gone from the hive's ground and then break off entirely; nothing pursues a fleeing man far. The venom does its worst long after, and it is the venom, not the wound, that puts hunters in the ground.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Each bee has one sting and dies giving it. Count what has spent itself and you will know when it is over.
• Smoke at the comb-mouth quiets the whole hive. Wet green wood, upwind, and take the honey slowly.
• The venom keeps working after the fight. Carry the antidote, or carry the man.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Mindless, and yet the easiest neighbour in this book. I have robbed three hives and been stung twice, and both times it was my own haste. Move slowly, keep the smoke between you and the comb, take a share and not the whole, and they will let you walk out with it.

Combat: Although many times larger, growing to a length of about 5 feet, giant bees behave generally the same as their smaller cousins. They are usually not aggressive except when defending themselves or their hive — and every sting they land costs them their life.

Vermin Traits: A giant bee is mindless: it has no Intelligence score and is immune to all mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects). It has darkvision out to 60 feet, is proficient with its natural weapons only, wears no armor, and breathes, eats, and sleeps.

Skills: Giant bees have a +4 racial bonus on Spot checks. *They also have a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks to orient themselves.

lore.summary: Bad-tempered and territorial, the brown bear owns whatever ground he happens to be standing on. He is the grizzly and every great bear of that kind: a mountain of muscle over a humped shoulder, reared taller than a tall man, met alone or in pairs through the cold forests. He swims strongly and he outlasts you.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — a mountain of fur and shoulder, and taller than a tall man when he rears.
Durability: Enormously tough; he soaks up punishment and keeps coming forward.
Defenses: No craft and no magic — only a thick pelt, heavy fat, and slabbed muscle beneath.
Speed: Faster afoot than anything that heavy has any right to be, and a strong swimmer besides.
Might: Two raking claws with a jaw behind them; when a claw lands he takes hold and hauls you in.
Mind: Beast-witted but far from stupid — a long memory for grudges and a superb nose.
Disposition: Bad-tempered, territorial, quick to take offence. He does not bluff you twice.
Bane: He comes straight on with no cunning in it, and he cannot climb after you into a good tree.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He attacks mainly by tearing at you with his claws, and the moment a claw takes hold he is upon you — grappling, bearing you down under all that weight while the jaws go to work. There is no circling and no feint in him. Noise does not turn him and neither does a wound; he simply keeps arriving.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Back away speaking low and level. Never run — over short ground he is faster than you are.
• Between a bear and her cubs is the same place as between a bear and his kill. Leave it.
• A tree will save you from this one. It will not save you from his black cousin, who climbs.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. He has no words and wants none — he wants you off his ground or off his kill. Twice I have talked my way clear of a bear, and both times the talking was only my own voice kept low and slow while my feet went backwards. That is not parley. That is retreat with manners.

sections.title: Special abilities
sections.body:
Combat: A brown bear attacks mainly by tearing at opponents with its claws.

Improved Grab (Ex): To use this ability, a brown bear must hit with a claw attack. It can then attempt to start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity.

Scent (Ex): This ability lets the creature detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. It can detect opponents within 30 feet by smell; if the opponent is upwind the range increases to 60 feet, and if downwind it drops to 15 feet. Strong scents such as smoke or rotting garbage can be detected at twice those ranges, and overpowering scents at triple. Detecting a scent reveals only that a source is present somewhere within range; the creature can take a move action to note the direction, and it pinpoints the source when it comes within 5 feet of it. A creature with the Track feat and the scent ability can follow tracks by smell, making a Survival check to find or follow a trail — DC 10 for a fresh trail, increased by 2 for each hour the trail is cold, and modified by how strong the quarry's odor is and how many creatures made the trail. Creatures tracking by scent ignore the effects of surface conditions and poor visibility.

Low-Light Vision (Ex): The creature can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. It retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

Skills: A brown bear has a +4 racial bonus on Swim checks.

lore.summary: Long, lean, and a shade taller than his brown cousin, the white bear holds the cold plains and the water between the floes. His coat makes him a drift of snow until the drift turns and looks at you. He swims as easily as he walks and thinks nothing of taking to the sea to reach you. Met alone, or with a mate.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer and leaner than the brown bear, and a little the taller of the two.
Durability: Hardier even than his brown cousin; the cold has made him thick and patient.
Defenses: Fat and fur against the killing cold, and a white coat that hides him utterly in snow.
Speed: Quick across the ice and quicker in the water, where he swims without ever seeming to tire.
Might: Claws that open a seal like a purse, and a grip that follows the claw. Then come the jaws.
Mind: Beast-witted, but the finest stalker of all the bears; he will wait an age at a breathing hole.
Disposition: Neither cruel nor kind. He is hungry, and the ice is a thin larder.
Bane: On bare rock or dark ground his coat betrays him utterly, and he must still come at you straight.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: He fights as the brown bear fights — straight in, claws first, and a grip that turns the whole affair into a wrestle he cannot lose. What is his own is the approach: he comes up out of the water at the floe's edge, or out of the white ground itself, and the first you know of him is the weight of him.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Watch the open water at the ice edge. He comes up through it, and he comes up fast.
• In snow you will not see him. Look for the black of the nose and the eye — that is all he cannot hide.
• Wet furs draw him from a long way off. Never sleep in the clothes you butchered in.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. There is nothing behind that white face but distance and hunger. I once shared a floe with one for the better part of a night, each of us pretending the other was elsewhere. That is the whole of the diplomacy on offer. Give him the seal and go quietly.

lore.summary: Pack hunters, known for persistence and cunning, and the finest trackers I have ever walked beside — a wolf runs a quarry to exhaustion rather than beat it. Met in the temperate forests alone, in pairs, or in a pack of a dozen and more. Small folk ride them to war. I have hunted them, and I have hunted with them.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — a big dog, no more, and rarely as heavy as the winter coat makes him look.
Durability: Slight. A solid blow ends a wolf, and the pack knows it better than you do.
Defenses: Nothing but a thick coat and the good sense to be somewhere else.
Speed: Very fast and quite tireless. You will not outrun one and you will not outlast the pack.
Might: A single bite — and the bite is not the point. The point is that it takes your legs from under you.
Mind: Sharp for a beast: patient, cunning, and it reads a limping man better than most men can.
Disposition: Wary of us by nature. A wolf that comes at a person is starving, sick, or guarding young.
Bane: Alone it is very little. Take ground they cannot flank and the pack loses half its craft.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: The pack sends a few against your front to hold your eyes while the rest circle to the flanks and the rear. The bite is a lever: one that lands will pull you off your feet, and a man on the ground with wolves about him is a dead man. They will not press a losing fight — they break off, follow at a distance, and try you again when you are tired.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Count them, then count again. The one you can see is watching you for the ones you cannot.
• Never turn and never fall. Everything else about a wolf fight follows from those two.
• Leave a flank open on purpose, with a spear standing in it. They take the opening every time.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never, in the way this book means the word — there are no words in a wolf. But a wolf is read, and read easily: the ears, the tail, whether the pack is spread or gathered. Stand tall, keep the fire, do not run. I have shared a hillside with a pack all night and come down unbitten.

Combat: Wolves are pack hunters known for their persistence and cunning. A favorite tactic is to send a few individuals against the foe's front while the rest of the pack circles and attacks from the flanks or rear.

Trip (Ex): A wolf that hits with a bite attack can attempt to trip the opponent (+1 check modifier) as a free action without making a touch attack or provoking an attack of opportunity. If the attempt fails, the opponent cannot react to trip the wolf.

Scent (Ex): This ability lets the creature detect approaching enemies, sniff out hidden foes, and track by sense of smell. It can detect opponents within 30 feet by smell; if the opponent is upwind the range increases to 60 feet, and if downwind it drops to 15 feet. Strong scents such as smoke or rotting garbage can be detected at twice those ranges, and overpowering scents at triple. Detecting a scent reveals only that a source is present somewhere within range; the creature can take a move action to note the direction, and it pinpoints the source when it comes within 5 feet of it. Skills: *Wolves have a +4 racial bonus on Survival checks when tracking by scent.

lore.summary: The great cat of the warm plains, hunting in prides of half a score, though a male will keep alone or take a single companion. The lionesses do the work and the maned one comes to the kill. In tall grass she is not there at all until the grass moves, and by then the charge is already upon you.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — heavy through chest and shoulder. The maned male is the bigger, not the better hunter.
Durability: Tough as a big cat is tough; she can take a wound and still finish the charge.
Defenses: Only hide and hair. What guards her is that you never see her coming.
Speed: Swift over open ground in a short burst, and near silent through the approach.
Might: A charge that arrives as claws, jaws and both hind feet together; the jaws take hold, then the raking begins.
Mind: Beast-witted, yet a pride hunts with an understanding between its members that looks a great deal like a plan.
Disposition: She hunts to eat and she defends the kill. A lion that has learned to eat men will not unlearn it.
Bane: The charge is the whole of it — blunt the first rush and she will often abandon the affair. Fire and noise still turn a pride.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: She charges out of cover and arrives with everything at once: claws, bite, and the raking hind feet. The jaws take hold, she drags you down, and the back claws work at you while you are on the ground. A pride encircles first and charges after, from the side you were not watching.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• The grass moves against the wind. That is your only warning, and you get it once.
• Watch the lionesses, never the mane. The mane arrives when the fighting is finished.
• Face it standing and make yourself large. Crouch, and you have taken the shape of prey.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. She is a cat, and you are meat that happens to be standing up. Whatever can be done is done before the charge: face her, spread your cloak wide, shout, and never crouch or run. I have backed away from a whole pride at a waterhole doing exactly that, and I kept the water skin.

It can detect opponents within 30 feet by smell; if the opponent is upwind the range increases to 60 feet, and if downwind it drops to 15 feet. Strong scents such as smoke or rotting garbage can be detected at twice those ranges, and overpowering scents at triple. lore.summary: The greatest of the cats, and always alone. He keeps to the warm forests, striped so that the light coming through the leaves eats his outline entirely; he swims well and will cross a river to reach a hunting ground. Where the lion has a pride to help her, the tiger has never needed one.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Large — longer and heavier than the lion, and far stronger in the forequarters.
Durability: Very hard to put down. He absorbs a great deal and stays on his feet.
Defenses: His stripes. In dappled forest or standing grass he is not there until he is.
Speed: A blinding rush across a short distance, a fine swimmer, and quiet as falling cloth.
Might: The strongest stroke of any cat I have met. Either paw or the jaws can take hold, and then the hind claws open you.
Mind: Beast-witted, solitary, and careful. He will study a camp for several nights before he tries it.
Disposition: Solitary and territorial. He does not share, and he gives no warning at all.
Bane: He hunts alone — there is no pack to cut your retreat. Deny him the ambush and you face only half a tiger.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: Everything is the ambush. He watches, chooses the man at the back or the edge of the line, and comes in a single silent rush that lands as claws, jaws and raking hind feet together. A claw will do as well as the bite for taking hold; once you are down, the back feet do the work. If the rush fails he withdraws into cover and tries again — the same night, the same party, a different man.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Sleep in the middle. He takes the edge of a camp, every time, without exception.
• Paint a pair of eyes on the back of your hood. He wants the face that is turned away.
• He crosses rivers without a thought. Water at your back is not a wall.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never — and take no comfort in his being a mere beast. He has watched your fire for nights already and has settled which of you sleeps nearest the edge. The only argument he has ever accepted from me was a thorn wall and a watch kept honestly until dawn.

lore.summary: Smallest of the great cats and the likeliest of them to kill you, because it hunts by night and it hunts from above. The same page serves for the jaguar, the panther and the mountain lion. It climbs like a squirrel, hauls its kill up the trunk after it, and drops on whatever passes beneath the branch.

sections.title: Hunter's assessment
sections.body:
Size: Medium — no bigger than a large hound, and a good deal heavier than it looks.
Durability: Slight. It cannot trade blows with you, and it has no intention of trying.
Defenses: Speed, a dappled hide, and height. It fights from wherever you are not looking.
Speed: Very quick, a prodigious leaper, and it climbs as readily as it runs. No ground is out of its reach.
Might: Modest for a cat, and quite sufficient — the bite takes hold and the hind claws finish the argument.
Mind: Beast-witted and thoroughly nocturnal. It will watch a road for a night or two before using it.
Disposition: Shy of daylight and of company. It wants a straggler, in the dark, alone.
Bane: The least of the cats in strength, and it will not fight once surprised — light, noise and company send it up a tree.

sections.title: How it fights
sections.body: It waits on a branch or a ledge above the path and drops. The bite takes hold and the hind feet rake while you are still working out what has happened to you. It never takes on a group, never presses a fight it is losing, and goes straight up the nearest trunk — with its kill if it can, without it if it must.

sections.title: Margin notes
sections.body:
• Look up. Then look up again. It is always the branch that overhangs the path.
• Never walk the night road at the back of the line. That is the place it takes.
• It drags its kill into the tree. Meat overhead means you are standing in its larder.

sections.title: Parley (never)
sections.body: Never. There is nothing to say to it and no moment in which to say it. Your whole defence is arranged beforehand: a fire, a companion at your back, and the settled habit of looking upward. Once, I looked up in time. That is the entire art of surviving one.
